qs.q: A rectangular patio measures \(8\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}\) long and \(5\frac{1}{3}\text{ m}\) wide. A triangular garden with a base of \(3\frac{3}{4}\text{ m}\) and a height of \(2\frac{2}{5}\text{ m}\) is built inside the patio. What is the remaining area of the patio?
qs.s: The patio area is \(\frac{17}{2} \times \frac{16}{3} = \frac{136}{3} = 45\frac{1}{3}\text{ m}^2\), and the garden area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{15}{4} \times \frac{12}{5} = \frac{9}{2} = 4\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}^2\). Subtracting gives \(45\frac{1}{3} - 4\frac{1}{2} = 40\frac{5}{6}\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A craftsperson makes a banner consisting of \(5\) identical triangular flags. Each flag has a base of \(3\frac{3}{4}\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(2\frac{2}{5}\text{ cm}\). What is the total area of all \(5\) flags?
qs.s: The area of one flag is \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{15}{4} \times \frac{12}{5} = \frac{9}{2}\text{ cm}^2\). Multiplying by \(5\) flags gives \(5 \times \frac{9}{2} = \frac{45}{2} = 22\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A trapezoidal panel has parallel bases of \(3\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}\) and \(4\frac{5}{6}\text{ m}\), and a height of \(2\frac{1}{4}\text{ m}\). What is the area of the panel?
qs.s: The sum of the parallel bases is \(3\frac{1}{2} + 4\frac{5}{6} = \frac{25}{3}\text{ m}\). The area of the trapezoid is \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{25}{3} \times \frac{9}{4} = \frac{75}{8} = 9\frac{3}{8}\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular billboard has a length of \(6\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\) and a height of \(3\frac{3}{8}\text{ m}\). A painter charges \(\$4\frac{1}{2}\) per square meter to paint it. What is the total cost to paint the billboard?
qs.s: The area of the billboard is \(\frac{20}{3} \times \frac{27}{8} = \frac{45}{2}\text{ m}^2\). Multiplying by the rate gives \(\frac{45}{2} \times \frac{9}{2} = \frac{405}{4} = \$101\frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage crate has a length of \(2\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\), a width of \(1\frac{1}{4}\text{ m}\), and a height of \(1\frac{5}{7}\text{ m}\). What is the volume of the crate?
qs.s: Convert the dimensions to improper fractions: \(\frac{8}{3}\text{ m}\), \(\frac{5}{4}\text{ m}\), and \(\frac{12}{7}\text{ m}\). Multiply the dimensions to find the volume: \(\frac{8}{3} \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{12}{7} = \frac{40}{7} = 5\frac{5}{7}\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: A shipping carton measures \(7\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\) long, \(4\frac{2}{3}\text{ cm}\) wide, and \(2\frac{1}{4}\text{ cm}\) high. What is the volume of the carton?
qs.s: Convert the dimensions to improper fractions: \(\frac{15}{2} \times \frac{14}{3} \times \frac{9}{4}\). Canceling common factors gives \(\frac{5 \times 7 \times 9}{4} = \frac{315}{4} = 78\frac{3}{4}\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: An aquarium measures \(10\frac{1}{2}\text{ in}\) long, \(8\frac{2}{7}\text{ in}\) wide, and \(5\frac{1}{3}\text{ in}\) high. What is the volume of the aquarium?
qs.s: Write each mixed fraction as an improper fraction: \(\frac{21}{2} \times \frac{58}{7} \times \frac{16}{3}\). Since \(21\) cancels with \(7 \times 3\), simplify to \(\frac{58 \times 16}{2} = 58 \times 8 = 464\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage bin measures \(8\frac{1}{3}\text{ m}\) long, \(4\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}\) wide, and \(2\frac{2}{5}\text{ m}\) high. What is the volume of the storage bin?
qs.s: Convert each dimension to an improper fraction: \(\frac{25}{3} \times \frac{9}{2} \times \frac{12}{5}\). Multiplying and simplifying common factors yields \(\frac{25 \times 9 \times 12}{3 \times 2 \times 5} = 5 \times 3 \times 6 = 90\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular planter box has a length of \(6\frac{2}{3}\text{ ft}\), a width of \(3\frac{3}{4}\text{ ft}\), and a depth of \(1\frac{1}{2}\text{ ft}\). What is the volume of the planter box?
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions: \(\frac{20}{3} \times \frac{15}{4} \times \frac{3}{2}\). Canceling common factors gives \(\frac{5 \times 15 \times 1}{1 \times 1 \times 2} = \frac{75}{2} = 37\frac{1}{2}\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular block of wood measures \(4\frac{4}{5}\text{ cm} \times 3\frac{1}{8}\text{ cm} \times 2\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\). What is the volume of the block?
qs.s: Convert the mixed fractions to improper fractions: \(\frac{24}{5} \times \frac{25}{8} \times \frac{7}{3}\). Canceling common factors leaves \(1 \times 5 \times 7 = 35\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular bin measures \(15\frac{3}{4}\text{ ft} \times 9\frac{1}{3}\text{ ft} \times 6\frac{2}{7}\text{ ft}\). It is completely filled with mulch that weighs \(2\frac{1}{11}\text{ lb}\) per cubic foot. What is the total weight of the mulch in the bin?
qs.s: Express all four values as improper fractions: \(\frac{63}{4} \times \frac{28}{3} \times \frac{44}{7} \times \frac{23}{11}\). Canceling common factors leaves \(3 \times 28 \times 1 \times 23 = 1932\text{ lb}\).

qs.q: A solid rectangular block of metal measures \(21\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm} \times 13\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm} \times 8\frac{3}{4}\text{ cm}\). A machinist cuts out a rectangular piece measuring \(5\frac{1}{4}\text{ cm} \times 4\frac{2}{7}\text{ cm} \times 3\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\). What is the volume of the remaining metal?
qs.s: The original volume is \(\frac{64}{3} \times \frac{27}{2} \times \frac{35}{4} = 2520\text{ cm}^3\), and the cutout volume is \(\frac{21}{4} \times \frac{30}{7} \times \frac{10}{3} = 75\text{ cm}^3\). Subtracting gives \(2520 - 75 = 2445\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage crate measures \(12\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 6\frac{2}{5}\text{ m} \times 3\frac{3}{4}\text{ m}\). If the material filling the crate has a density of \(1\frac{1}{3}\text{ tonnes/m}^3\), what is the total mass of the material in the crate?
qs.s: Multiply the three dimensions and the density as improper fractions: \(\frac{25}{2} \times \frac{32}{5} \times \frac{15}{4} \times \frac{4}{3}\). Canceling common factors yields \(5 \times 16 \times 5 \times 1 = 400\text{ tonnes}\).

qs.q: A delivery truck has two cargo compartments. The front compartment measures \(14\frac{2}{5}\text{ ft} \times 7\frac{1}{2}\text{ ft} \times 6\frac{1}{4}\text{ ft}\), and the rear compartment measures \(16\frac{2}{3}\text{ ft} \times 8\frac{1}{4}\text{ ft} \times 7\frac{1}{5}\text{ ft}\). What is the total combined cargo volume of the two compartments?
qs.s: The front volume is \(\frac{72}{5} \times \frac{15}{2} \times \frac{25}{4} = 675\text{ ft}^3\), and the rear volume is \(\frac{50}{3} \times \frac{33}{4} \times \frac{36}{5} = 990\text{ ft}^3\). Summing them gives \(675 + 990 = 1665\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: A warehouse manager is comparing two rectangular storage units. Unit A measures \(14\frac{2}{5}\text{ m} \times 8\frac{1}{3}\text{ m} \times 4\frac{1}{6}\text{ m}\), and Unit B measures \(8\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 5\frac{1}{4}\text{ m} \times 3\frac{1}{3}\text{ m}\). How much greater is the volume of Unit A than Unit B?
qs.s: The volume of Unit A is \(\frac{72}{5} \times \frac{25}{3} \times \frac{25}{6} = 500\text{ m}^3\), and Unit B is \(\frac{17}{2} \times \frac{21}{4} \times \frac{10}{3} = \frac{595}{4} = 148\frac{3}{4}\text{ m}^3\). Subtracting gives \(500 - 148\frac{3}{4} = 351\frac{1}{4}\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular patio measures \(14\frac{2}{3}\text{ m} \times 8\frac{1}{4}\text{ m}\). If outdoor tiles will cover \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the patio, what is the area of the tiled section in square meters?
qs.s: The total area of the patio is \(\frac{44}{3} \times \frac{33}{4} = 121\text{ m}^2\). The tiled section covers \(121 \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{363}{4} = 90\frac{3}{4}\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A community park measures \(20\frac{1}{4}\text{ m} \times 15\frac{5}{9}\text{ m}\). If a playground occupies \(\frac{3}{7}\) of the park, how many square meters does the playground occupy?
qs.s: The total area of the park is \(\frac{81}{4} \times \frac{140}{9} = 315\text{ m}^2\). The playground covers \(315 \times \frac{3}{7} = 135\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A flat rooftop measures \(22\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 10\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\). If solar panels cover \(\frac{5}{6}\) of the roof, how many square meters will the solar panels cover?
qs.s: The total area of the roof is \(\frac{45}{2} \times \frac{32}{3} = 240\text{ m}^2\). The solar panels cover \(240 \times \frac{5}{6} = 200\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular vegetable garden measures \(18\frac{3}{4}\text{ m} \times 12\frac{2}{5}\text{ m}\). If tomato plants will cover \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the garden, how many square meters will the tomato plants cover?
qs.s: The total area of the garden is \(\frac{75}{4} \times \frac{62}{5} = \frac{465}{2}\text{ m}^2\). The tomato plants cover \(\frac{465}{2} \times \frac{4}{5} = 186\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: An outdoor billboard measures \(16\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 7\frac{1}{3}\text{ m}\). If an advertisement covers \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the billboard, what is the area of the advertisement in square meters?
qs.s: The billboard's total area is \(\frac{33}{2} \times \frac{22}{3} = 121\text{ m}^2\). The advertisement covers \(121 \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{363}{5} = 72\frac{3}{5}\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular water storage tank has a base measuring \(4\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 3\frac{1}{3}\text{ m}\) and a height of \(2\frac{2}{5}\text{ m}\). If the tank is filled to \(\frac{5}{8}\) of its total capacity, how many cubic meters of water are in the tank?
qs.s: The capacity of the tank is \(\frac{9}{2} \times \frac{10}{3} \times \frac{12}{5} = 36\text{ m}^3\). The volume of water is \(36 \times \frac{5}{8} = \frac{45}{2} = 22\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: A backyard measures \(31\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 18\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\). A swimming pool covers \(\frac{2}{7}\) of the yard, and a stone patio covers \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the yard. How many square meters of the yard remain uncovered?
qs.s: The total yard area is \(\frac{63}{2} \times \frac{56}{3} = 588\text{ m}^2\). Subtracting the pool area (\(588 \times \frac{2}{7} = 168\text{ m}^2\)) and patio area (\(588 \times \frac{1}{6} = 98\text{ m}^2\)) leaves \(588 - (168 + 98) = 322\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular commercial lot measures \(37\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 26\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\). A developer paves a parking area that occupies \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the lot, and builds a store that occupies \(2\frac{1}{2}\) times the area of the parking area. How many square meters of the lot remain unoccupied?
qs.s: The total area is \(\frac{75}{2} \times \frac{80}{3} = 1000\text{ m}^2\), where the parking area is \(1000 \times \frac{1}{5} = 200\text{ m}^2\) and the store is \(200 \times \frac{5}{2} = 500\text{ m}^2\). The remaining area is \(1000 - (200 + 500) = 300\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular farm field measures \(42\frac{2}{3}\text{ m} \times 27\frac{3}{4}\text{ m}\). The farmer plants corn on \(\frac{5}{8}\) of the field and soybeans on \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the field. How many more square meters are planted with corn than with soybeans?
qs.s: The total field area is \(\frac{128}{3} \times \frac{111}{4} = 1184\text{ m}^2\). The difference in fractions is \(\frac{5}{8} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{8}\), so corn covers \(1184 \times \frac{3}{8} = 444\text{ m}^2\) more than soybeans.

qs.q: A school is paving sections of two rectangular grounds. Ground A measures \(18\frac{3}{4}\text{ m} \times 10\frac{2}{5}\text{ m}\), and \(\frac{2}{3}\) of it will be paved. Ground B measures \(12\frac{1}{2}\text{ m} \times 8\frac{4}{5}\text{ m}\), and \(\frac{3}{5}\) of it will be paved. What is the total paved area of both grounds combined in square meters?
qs.s: Paved Ground A is \(\left(\frac{75}{4} \times \frac{52}{5}\right) \times \frac{2}{3} = 195 \times \frac{2}{3} = 130\text{ m}^2\), and paved Ground B is \(\left(\frac{25}{2} \times \frac{44}{5}\right) \times \frac{3}{5} = 110 \times \frac{3}{5} = 66\text{ m}^2\). The total paved area is \(130 + 66 = 196\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: An industrial oil vat is \(11\frac{1}{4}\text{ yards long}\), \(4\frac{2}{3}\text{ yards wide}\), and \(2\frac{1}{7}\text{ yards deep}\). If the vat is currently \(\frac{5}{6}\) full of oil, how many cubic yards of oil are in the vat?
qs.s: Convert each mixed number to an improper fraction and multiply: \(\frac{45}{4} \times \frac{14}{3} \times \frac{15}{7} \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{375}{4} = 93\frac{3}{4}\text{ cubic yards}\).

qs.q: A rectangular retention pond is \(18\frac{1}{3}\text{ meters long}\), \(6\frac{1}{2}\text{ meters wide}\), and has an average depth of \(2\frac{2}{5}\text{ meters}\). If the pond is \(\frac{3}{4}\) full of rainwater, how many cubic meters of water are in the pond?
qs.s: Convert each dimension to an improper fraction and multiply: \(\frac{55}{3} \times \frac{13}{2} \times \frac{12}{5} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{429}{2} = 214\frac{1}{2}\text{ cubic meters}\).

qs.q: A rectangular aquarium is \(14\frac{2}{5}\text{ inches long}\), \(8\frac{1}{3}\text{ inches wide}\), and \(7\frac{1}{4}\text{ inches high}\). If the aquarium is filled \(\frac{3}{4}\) full with water, how many cubic inches of water are in the aquarium?
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions and multiply by the fraction full: \(\frac{72}{5} \times \frac{25}{3} \times \frac{29}{4} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{1305}{2} = 652\frac{1}{2}\text{ cubic inches}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage bin is \(12\frac{1}{2}\text{ feet long}\), \(6\frac{2}{3}\text{ feet wide}\), and \(2\frac{1}{4}\text{ feet deep}\). If the bin is \(\frac{5}{6}\) full of grain, how many cubic feet of grain are in the bin?
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions and multiply: \(\frac{25}{2} \times \frac{20}{3} \times \frac{9}{4} \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{625}{4} = 156\frac{1}{4}\text{ cubic feet}\).

qs.q: A rectangular greenhouse planter box is \(14\frac{1}{2}\text{ feet long}\), \(5\frac{1}{3}\text{ feet wide}\), and \(3\frac{3}{4}\text{ feet deep}\). If it is filled \(\frac{5}{8}\) full with compost, how many cubic feet of compost are in the planter box?
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions and multiply: \(\frac{29}{2} \times \frac{16}{3} \times \frac{15}{4} \times \frac{5}{8} = \frac{725}{4} = 181\frac{1}{4}\text{ cubic feet}\).

qs.q: A water district manages two rectangular reservoirs. Reservoir A is \(22\frac{1}{2}\text{ meters long}\), \(12\frac{2}{3}\text{ meters wide}\), and \(3\frac{1}{5}\text{ meters deep}\), and is \(\frac{3}{4}\) full. Reservoir B is \(18\frac{3}{4}\text{ meters long}\), \(14\frac{2}{5}\text{ meters wide}\), and \(4\frac{1}{6}\text{ meters deep}\), and is \(\frac{5}{8}\) full. How many more cubic meters of water are in Reservoir B than in Reservoir A?
qs.s: Water in Reservoir A is \(\frac{45}{2} \times \frac{38}{3} \times \frac{16}{5} \times \frac{3}{4} = 684\text{ m}^3\), and water in Reservoir B is \(\frac{75}{4} \times \frac{72}{5} \times \frac{25}{6} \times \frac{5}{8} = \frac{5625}{8} = 703\frac{1}{8}\text{ m}^3\). The difference is \(703\frac{1}{8} - 684 = 19\frac{1}{8}\text{ cubic meters}\).

qs.q: A rectangular cargo container is \(18\frac{3}{4}\text{ feet long}\), \(8\frac{2}{5}\text{ feet wide}\), and \(6\frac{2}{3}\text{ feet high}\). The container is \(\frac{3}{4}\) full of grain. If each cubic foot of grain weighs \(1\frac{3}{10}\text{ pounds}\), what is the total weight, in pounds, of the grain in the container?
qs.s: Find the volume of the grain by multiplying \(\frac{75}{4} \times \frac{42}{5} \times \frac{20}{3} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{1575}{2}\text{ ft}^3\). Multiply by the density \(\frac{13}{10}\) to find the weight: \(\frac{1575}{2} \times \frac{13}{10} = \frac{4095}{4} = 1023\frac{3}{4}\text{ pounds}\).

qs.q: A public pool has two connected rectangular sections. The shallow section is \(12\frac{1}{2}\text{ yards long}\), \(8\frac{2}{3}\text{ yards wide}\), and \(1\frac{1}{5}\text{ yards deep}\). The deep section is \(15\frac{3}{4}\text{ yards long}\), \(8\frac{2}{3}\text{ yards wide}\), and \(3\frac{1}{3}\text{ yards deep}\). If the entire pool is filled to \(\frac{5}{6}\) of its total capacity, how many cubic yards of water are in the pool?
qs.s: The shallow volume is \(\frac{25}{2} \times \frac{26}{3} \times \frac{6}{5} = 130\text{ yd}^3\), and the deep volume is \(\frac{63}{4} \times \frac{26}{3} \times \frac{10}{3} = 455\text{ yd}^3\). Total water is \((130 + 455) \times \frac{5}{6} = 585 \times \frac{5}{6} = 487\frac{1}{2}\text{ cubic yards}\).

qs.q: A large rectangular reservoir is \(33\frac{1}{3}\text{ yards long}\), \(12\frac{1}{2}\text{ yards wide}\), and \(4\frac{1}{5}\text{ yards deep}\). Water is pumped into the empty reservoir until it is \(\frac{7}{10}\) full. Later, evaporation causes a loss of \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the water that was pumped in. How many cubic yards of water remain in the reservoir?
qs.s: The total capacity is \(\frac{100}{3} \times \frac{25}{2} \times \frac{21}{5} = 1750\text{ yd}^3\), and the water pumped in is \(1750 \times \frac{7}{10} = 1225\text{ yd}^3\). After \(\frac{1}{6}\) is lost, \(\frac{5}{6}\) remains: \(1225 \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{6125}{6} = 1020\frac{5}{6}\text{ cubic yards}\).

qs.q: A rectangular swimming pool is \(20\frac{1}{4}\text{ meters long}\), \(10\frac{2}{3}\text{ meters wide}\), and \(2\frac{1}{2}\text{ meters deep}\). Initially, the pool is \(\frac{7}{8}\) full of water. After some water is drained, the pool is \(\frac{1}{3}\) full. How many cubic meters of water were drained from the pool?
qs.s: The pool's total volume is \(\frac{81}{4} \times \frac{32}{3} \times \frac{5}{2} = 540\text{ m}^3\), and the fraction drained is \(\frac{7}{8} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{13}{24}\). Multiplying gives \(540 \times \frac{13}{24} = \frac{585}{2} = 292\frac{1}{2}\text{ cubic meters}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{7}{9}\).
qs.s: Exchanging the numerator and the denominator of \(\frac{7}{9}\) gives \(\frac{9}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{4}{7}\).
qs.s: Exchanging the numerator and the denominator of \(\frac{4}{7}\) gives \(\frac{7}{4}\), since \(\frac{4}{7} \times \frac{7}{4} = 1\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{3}{8}\).
qs.s: Exchanging the numerator and the denominator gives \(\frac{8}{3}\), since \(\frac{3}{8} \times \frac{8}{3} = 1\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{2}{5}\).
qs.s: Exchanging the numerator and the denominator of \(\frac{2}{5}\) gives \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{11}\).
qs.s: Exchanging the numerator and the denominator of \(\frac{5}{11}\) gives \(\frac{11}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{5}\).
qs.s: First add the fractions using a common denominator: \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{5} = \frac{5}{15} + \frac{6}{15} = \frac{11}{15}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{11}{15}\) is \(\frac{15}{11}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{4}{9} \div \frac{2}{3}\).
qs.s: First evaluate the division: \(\frac{4}{9} \div \frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{2}{3}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{2}{3}\) is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{5}\).
qs.s: First calculate the product: \(1\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{2}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{2}\) is \(\frac{2}{1} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(4\frac{2}{3}\).
qs.s: First convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(4\frac{2}{3} = \frac{14}{3}\). The reciprocal is found by exchanging the numerator and denominator, which gives \(\frac{3}{14}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{\frac{3}{5}}{\frac{7}{10}}\).
qs.s: First simplify the complex fraction: \(\frac{\frac{3}{5}}{\frac{7}{10}} = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{10}{7} = \frac{6}{7}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{6}{7}\) is \(\frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(11\).
qs.s: Write \(11\) as \(\frac{11}{1}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal, \(\frac{1}{11}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(8\).
qs.s: Write \(8\) as the fraction \(\frac{8}{1}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal, \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{8}\).
qs.s: Exchange the numerator and denominator of \(\frac{5}{8}\) to get the reciprocal, \(\frac{8}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{9}\).
qs.s: Exchange the numerator and denominator of \(\frac{1}{9}\) to get \(\frac{9}{1}\), which simplifies to \(9\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{3}{7}\).
qs.s: Exchange the numerator and denominator of \(\frac{3}{7}\) to get the reciprocal, \(\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of the complex fraction \(\frac{\frac{2}{5}}{\frac{8}{15}}\).
qs.s: Simplify the complex fraction by dividing: \(\frac{2}{5} \div \frac{8}{15} = \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{15}{8} = \frac{3}{4}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{3}{4}\) is \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{6} \div \frac{2}{3}\).
qs.s: Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor to get \(\frac{5}{6} \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{5}{4}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{4}\) is \(\frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of the product \(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{4}{5}\).
qs.s: Multiply the fractions to get \(\frac{2 \times 4}{3 \times 5} = \frac{8}{15}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{8}{15}\) is \(\frac{15}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(5\frac{3}{4}\).
qs.s: Convert \(5\frac{3}{4}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{23}{4}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal, \(\frac{4}{23}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(3\frac{2}{5}\).
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{2}{5}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{17}{5}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal, \(\frac{5}{17}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{3}\).
qs.s: The reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{3}\) is found by inverting the fraction to get \(\frac{3}{1} = 3\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{10}\).
qs.s: Inverting the numerator and denominator of \(\frac{1}{10}\) yields \(\frac{10}{1} = 10\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{8}\).
qs.s: Exchanging the numerator and denominator of \(\frac{1}{8}\) gives \(\frac{8}{1} = 8\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{7}\).
qs.s: Exchanging the numerator and denominator of \(\frac{1}{7}\) gives \(\frac{7}{1} = 7\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{6}\).
qs.s: To find the reciprocal of a fraction, exchange the numerator and denominator. The reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{6}\) is \(\frac{6}{1} = 6\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(8 \div \frac{4}{5}\).
qs.s: First evaluate the division: \(8 \div \frac{4}{5} = 8 \times \frac{5}{4} = 10\). The reciprocal of \(10\) is \(\frac{1}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{9}{10}\).
qs.s: First compute the quotient: \(\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{9}{10} = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{10}{9} = \frac{5}{6}\). Taking the reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{6}\) gives \(\frac{6}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(4\frac{3}{8}\).
qs.s: First rewrite \(4\frac{3}{8}\) as the improper fraction \(\frac{35}{8}\). Inverting the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal, \(\frac{8}{35}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(2\frac{5}{7}\).
qs.s: First convert \(2\frac{5}{7}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{19}{7}\). The reciprocal is found by exchanging the numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{7}{19}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{13}{6}\).
qs.s: To find the reciprocal of a fraction, exchange the numerator and the denominator. The reciprocal of \(\frac{13}{6}\) is \(\frac{6}{13}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{7}{12}\).
qs.s: To find the reciprocal of a fraction, exchange the numerator and the denominator. The reciprocal of \(\frac{7}{12}\) is \(\frac{12}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{8}{5}\).
qs.s: To find the reciprocal of a fraction, exchange the numerator and the denominator. The reciprocal of \(\frac{8}{5}\) is \(\frac{5}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{11}{4}\).
qs.s: To find the reciprocal of a fraction, exchange the numerator and the denominator. The reciprocal of \(\frac{11}{4}\) is \(\frac{4}{11}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{9}\).
qs.s: To find the reciprocal of a fraction, exchange the numerator and the denominator. The reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{9}\) is \(\frac{9}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(5\frac{3}{7}\).
qs.s: First convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(5\frac{3}{7} = \frac{38}{7}\). Then exchange the numerator and denominator to get the reciprocal, \(\frac{7}{38}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of the complex fraction \(\frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{8}{9}}\).
qs.s: Simplify the complex fraction: \(\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{8}{9} = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{8} = \frac{3}{4}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{3}{4}\) is \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{10}\).
qs.s: Multiply and simplify to get \(\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{10} = \frac{2}{15}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{2}{15}\) is \(\frac{15}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{28}{42}\).
qs.s: Exchange the numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{42}{28}\), then divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 14, to obtain \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{3}{5}\).
qs.s: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(1\frac{3}{5} = \frac{1 \times 5 + 3}{5} = \frac{8}{5}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives \(\frac{5}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(3\frac{1}{2}\).
qs.s: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(3\frac{1}{2} = \frac{3 \times 2 + 1}{2} = \frac{7}{2}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives \(\frac{2}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{5}{6}\).
qs.s: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(1\frac{5}{6} = \frac{1 \times 6 + 5}{6} = \frac{11}{6}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives \(\frac{6}{11}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(2\frac{2}{3}\).
qs.s: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(2\frac{2}{3} = \frac{2 \times 3 + 2}{3} = \frac{8}{3}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives \(\frac{3}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(2\frac{1}{4}\).
qs.s: First convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(2\frac{1}{4} = \frac{2 \times 4 + 1}{4} = \frac{9}{4}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal, \(\frac{4}{9}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{5}{6} \div 1\frac{1}{4}\).
qs.s: First perform the division: \(\frac{5}{6} \div 1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{6} \div \frac{5}{4} = \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{2}{3}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{2}{3}\) is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{1}{2} \times 2\frac{2}{3}\).
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions and multiply: \(1\frac{1}{2} \times 2\frac{2}{3} = \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{8}{3} = 4\). The reciprocal of \(4\) is \(\frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{1}{2} + 1\frac{1}{4}\).
qs.s: First add the mixed numbers: \(1\frac{1}{2} + 1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{2} + \frac{5}{4} = \frac{6}{4} + \frac{5}{4} = \frac{11}{4}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{11}{4}\) is \(\frac{4}{11}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(8\frac{5}{12}\).
qs.s: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: \(8\frac{5}{12} = \frac{8 \times 12 + 5}{12} = \frac{101}{12}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal, \(\frac{12}{101}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{\frac{3}{4}}{6}\).
qs.s: Simplify the complex fraction: \(\frac{\frac{3}{4}}{6} = \frac{3}{4} \div 6 = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{8}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{1}{8}\) is \(8\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{7}{9}\).
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{7}{9}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{16}{9}\). The reciprocal is found by swapping the numerator and denominator to get \(\frac{9}{16}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(5\frac{2}{7}\).
qs.s: Write \(5\frac{2}{7}\) as the improper fraction \(\frac{37}{7}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{37}{7}\) is \(\frac{7}{37}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(3\frac{5}{6}\).
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{5}{6}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{23}{6}\). Exchanging the numerator and denominator gives the reciprocal \(\frac{6}{23}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(2\frac{4}{5}\).
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{4}{5}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{14}{5}\). The reciprocal is found by inverting the fraction to get \(\frac{5}{14}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{2}{3} + 2\frac{1}{4}\).
qs.s: First add the mixed numbers: \(\frac{5}{3} + \frac{9}{4} = \frac{20}{12} + \frac{27}{12} = \frac{47}{12}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{47}{12}\) is \(\frac{12}{47}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(\frac{1\frac{1}{3}}{\frac{8}{9}}\).
qs.s: Simplify the complex fraction: \(\frac{4}{3} \div \frac{8}{9} = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{9}{8} = \frac{3}{2}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{3}{2}\) is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(1\frac{1}{4} \times 2\frac{2}{3}\).
qs.s: First calculate the product: \(\frac{5}{4} \times \frac{8}{3} = \frac{10}{3}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{10}{3}\) is \(\frac{3}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(14\frac{5}{12}\).
qs.s: Convert \(14\frac{5}{12}\) to an improper fraction: \(\frac{14 \times 12 + 5}{12} = \frac{173}{12}\). Inverting gives the reciprocal \(\frac{12}{173}\).

qs.q: Find the reciprocal of \(2\frac{1}{2} \div 3\frac{3}{4}\).
qs.s: Evaluate the quotient: \(\frac{5}{2} \div \frac{15}{4} = \frac{5}{2} \times \frac{4}{15} = \frac{2}{3}\). The reciprocal of \(\frac{2}{3}\) is \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{1}{5}\) of a circle is divided into 4 equal pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{1}{5}\) by 4 by multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{1}{5} \div 4 = \frac{1}{5} \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{20}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a circle is divided into 4 equal pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{2}{3}\) by 4 and simplify: \(\frac{2}{3} \div 4 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{1}{2}\) of a circle is divided into 5 equal pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{1}{2}\) by 5 by multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{1}{2} \div 5 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{10}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{1}{4}\) of a circle is divided into 3 equal pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{1}{4}\) by 3 by multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{1}{4} \div 3 = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{12}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a circle is divided into 6 equal pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{3}{4}\) by 6 and simplify: \(\frac{3}{4} \div 6 = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{24} = \frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: If \(3\frac{1}{3}\) circles are divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a circle, how many pieces are obtained?
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{1}{3}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{10}{3}\), then divide by \(\frac{2}{3}\): \(\frac{10}{3} \div \frac{2}{3} = \frac{10}{3} \times \frac{3}{2} = 5\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a circle is divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{1}{16}\) of the circle, how many pieces are formed?
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{3}{4}\) by \(\frac{1}{16}\): \(\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{1}{16} = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{16}{1} = 12\) pieces.

qs.q: A sector representing \(\frac{2}{5}\) of a circle is removed. If the remaining portion is divided into 9 equal pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: The remaining portion of the circle is \(1 - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{5}\). Dividing this by 9 gives \(\frac{3}{5} \div 9 = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{1}{9} = \frac{1}{15}\).

qs.q: If \(2\frac{2}{5}\) circles are divided equally into 8 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{2}{5}\) to \(\frac{12}{5}\) and divide by 8: \(\frac{12}{5} \div 8 = \frac{12}{5} \times \frac{1}{8} = \frac{12}{40} = \frac{3}{10}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{9}{10}\) of a circle is divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{3}{20}\) of the circle, how many pieces are formed?
If \(\frac{4}{7}\) of a circle is divided into 6 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Dividing \(\frac{4}{7}\) by 6 is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{4}{7} \div 6 = \frac{4}{7} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{2}{21}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a circle is divided into 5 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Dividing \(\frac{2}{3}\) by 5 is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{2}{3} \div 5 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{5} = \frac{2}{15}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{5}{8}\) of a circle is divided into 3 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Dividing \(\frac{5}{8}\) by 3 is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{5}{8} \div 3 = \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{5}{24}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{3}{5}\) of a circle is divided into 4 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Dividing \(\frac{3}{5}\) by 4 is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{3}{5} \div 4 = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{20}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{5}{6}\) of a circle is divided into 7 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Dividing \(\frac{5}{6}\) by 7 is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{5}{6} \div 7 = \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{1}{7} = \frac{5}{42}\).

qs.q: A circle has \(\frac{3}{10}\) removed. If the remaining part is divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{7}{40}\) of a circle, find the number of pieces.
qs.s: The remaining part of the circle is \(1 - \frac{3}{10} = \frac{7}{10}\). Dividing by the piece size gives \(\frac{7}{10} \div \frac{7}{40} = \frac{7}{10} \times \frac{40}{7} = 4\).

qs.q: If \(3\frac{1}{3}\) circles are divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{5}{12}\) of a circle, find the number of pieces.
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{1}{3}\) to \(\frac{10}{3}\), then divide by the piece size: \(\frac{10}{3} \div \frac{5}{12} = \frac{10}{3} \times \frac{12}{5} = 8\).

qs.q: If \(2\frac{1}{4}\) circles are divided into 6 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{1}{4}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{9}{4}\), then divide by 6: \(\frac{9}{4} \div 6 = \frac{9}{4} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{8}\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{8}{9}\) of a circle is divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{2}{27}\) of a circle, find the number of pieces.
qs.s: Divide the fraction of the circle by the size of each piece: \(\frac{8}{9} \div \frac{2}{27} = \frac{8}{9} \times \frac{27}{2} = 12\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{1}{6}\) of a circle is removed and the remaining part is divided into 10 pieces, find the size of each piece.
qs.s: The remaining part of the circle is \(1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}\). Dividing by 10 gives \(\frac{5}{6} \div 10 = \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{1}{10} = \frac{1}{12}\).

qs.q: If a whole pie is divided into fifths, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Dividing a whole pie into fifths is calculated as \(1 \div \frac{1}{5} = 1 \times 5 = 5\) pieces.

qs.q: If a circular cake is divided equally among 3 people, find the fraction of the cake that each person receives.
qs.s: Dividing 1 whole cake equally among 3 people gives \(1 \div 3 = \frac{1}{3}\) of the cake per person.

qs.q: If a circular pizza is cut into slices that are each \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the pizza, find the number of slices obtained.
qs.s: Dividing the whole pizza into slices of size \(\frac{1}{6}\) gives \(1 \div \frac{1}{6} = 1 \times 6 = 6\) slices.

qs.q: If a circular disk is divided into 10 equal sectors, find the fraction of the disk that each sector represents.
qs.s: Dividing the whole disk into 10 equal parts gives \(1 \div 10 = \frac{1}{10}\) of the disk per sector.

qs.q: If a whole circle is divided into eighths, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Dividing a whole circle into eighths is calculated as \(1 \div \frac{1}{8} = 1 \times 8 = 8\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(3\frac{1}{3}\) circular fruit tarts are cut into servings that are each \(\frac{2}{9}\) of a tart, find the number of servings obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{1}{3}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{10}{3}\), then divide by \(\frac{2}{9}\) to get \(\frac{10}{3} \times \frac{9}{2} = 15\) servings.

qs.q: If \(\frac{4}{5}\) of a circular pie is divided into slices that are each \(\frac{2}{15}\) of the whole pie, find the number of slices obtained.
qs.s: Dividing \(\frac{4}{5}\) by \(\frac{2}{15}\) gives \(\frac{4}{5} \times \frac{15}{2} = \frac{60}{10} = 6\) slices.

qs.q: If \(\frac{4}{5}\) of a circular cake is shared equally among 6 people, find the fraction of the whole cake that each person receives.
qs.s: Dividing \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the cake by 6 gives \(\frac{4}{5} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{4}{30} = \frac{2}{15}\) of the cake.

qs.q: If \(3\frac{1}{2}\) circular quiches are cut into pieces that are each \(\frac{1}{4}\) of a quiche, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{1}{2}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{7}{2}\), then divide by \(\frac{1}{4}\) to get \(\frac{7}{2} \times 4 = 14\) pieces.

qs.q: If 10 whole pizzas are divided into portions that are each \(\frac{2}{5}\) of a pizza, find the number of portions obtained.
qs.s: Dividing 10 by \(\frac{2}{5}\) gives \(10 \times \frac{5}{2} = \frac{50}{2} = 25\) portions.

qs.q: If each of 5 whole circles is divided into halves, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Dividing 5 circles into halves is calculated as \(5 \div \frac{1}{2} = 5 \times 2 = 10\) pieces.

qs.q: If each of 3 whole circles is divided into fourths, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Dividing 3 circles into fourths is calculated as \(3 \div \frac{1}{4} = 3 \times 4 = 12\) pieces.

qs.q: If each of 4 whole circles is divided into fifths, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Dividing 4 circles into fifths is calculated as \(4 \div \frac{1}{5} = 4 \times 5 = 20\) pieces.

qs.q: If each of 2 whole circles is divided into eighths, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Dividing 2 circles into eighths is calculated as \(2 \div \frac{1}{8} = 2 \times 8 = 16\) pieces.

qs.q: If each of 6 whole circles is divided into thirds, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Dividing 6 circles into thirds is calculated as \(6 \div \frac{1}{3} = 6 \times 3 = 18\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a circle is divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{1}{12}\) of the whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Divide the fraction of the circle by the piece size: \(\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{12} = \frac{2}{3} \times 12 = 8\) pieces.

qs.q: If 3 whole circles are divided into fourths and 2 whole circles are divided into thirds, find the total number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Find the pieces from each set and add them: \(\left(3 \div \frac{1}{4}\right) + \left(2 \div \frac{1}{3}\right) = 12 + 6 = 18\) pieces.

qs.q: If 6 whole circles are divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Divide the total number of circles by the size of each piece: \(6 \div \frac{2}{3} = 6 \times \frac{3}{2} = 9\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(2\frac{2}{3}\) whole circles are divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{1}{6}\) of a circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{2}{3}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{8}{3}\) and divide by \(\frac{1}{6}\): \(\frac{8}{3} \div \frac{1}{6} = \frac{8}{3} \times 6 = 16\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(\frac{3}{5}\) of a whole circle is divided equally into 9 pieces, what fraction of the whole circle is each piece?
qs.s: Divide the fractional part of the circle by 9: \(\frac{3}{5} \div 9 = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{1}{9} = \frac{1}{15}\) of the whole circle.

qs.q: If \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a circle is divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{3}{4}\) by \(\frac{1}{8}\) by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{3}{4} \times 8 = 6\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a circle is divided into pieces which are \(\frac{2}{9}\) of the whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{2}{3}\) by \(\frac{2}{9}\) by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{2} = 3\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(\frac{5}{6}\) of a circle is divided into pieces which are \(\frac{5}{12}\) of the whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{5}{6}\) by \(\frac{5}{12}\) by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{5}{6} \times \frac{12}{5} = 2\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(\frac{4}{5}\) of a circle is divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{10}\) of the whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{4}{5}\) by \(\frac{1}{10}\) by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{4}{5} \times 10 = 8\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(\frac{1}{2}\) of a circle is divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{10}\) of the whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{1}{2}\) by \(\frac{1}{10}\) by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{1}{2} \times 10 = 5\) pieces.

qs.q: One circle has \(\frac{5}{6}\) of its area shaded and a second identical circle has \(\frac{3}{4}\) of its area shaded. If the total shaded area from both circles is divided into pieces that are each \(\frac{1}{12}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Add the two shaded areas to get \(\frac{5}{6} + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{19}{12}\), then divide by \(\frac{1}{12}\) to get \(\frac{19}{12} \times 12 = 19\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(4\frac{2}{3}\) circles are divided into pieces which are each \(\frac{2}{9}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(4\frac{2}{3}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{14}{3}\), then divide by \(\frac{2}{9}\) by multiplying by its reciprocal to get \(\frac{14}{3} \times \frac{9}{2} = 21\) pieces.

qs.q: A circular design has \(\frac{11}{12}\) of its area colored. If \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the whole circle is removed from the colored area, and the remainder is divided into sections that are each \(\frac{1}{15}\) of the whole circle, find the number of sections obtained.
qs.s: Subtract to find the remaining colored area: \(\frac{11}{12} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}\). Then divide by \(\frac{1}{15}\) to get \(\frac{2}{3} \times 15 = 10\) sections.

qs.q: If \(2\frac{5}{8}\) circles are divided equally into 7 pieces, what fraction of a whole circle is each piece?
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{5}{8}\) to \(\frac{21}{8}\), then divide by 7 by multiplying by \(\frac{1}{7}\) to get \(\frac{21}{8} \times \frac{1}{7} = \frac{3}{8}\) of the whole circle.

qs.q: If \(\frac{7}{9}\) of a circle is divided into pieces which are each \(\frac{2}{15}\) of the whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained, expressed as a mixed number.
qs.s: Divide \(\frac{7}{9}\) by \(\frac{2}{15}\) by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{7}{9} \times \frac{15}{2} = \frac{35}{6} = 5\frac{5}{6}\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(1\frac{2}{3}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{9}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{2}{3}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{5}{3}\). Then divide: \(\frac{5}{3} \div \frac{1}{9} = \frac{5}{3} \times 9 = 15\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(1\frac{3}{5}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{10}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{3}{5}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{8}{5}\). Then divide: \(\frac{8}{5} \div \frac{1}{10} = \frac{8}{5} \times 10 = 16\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(2\frac{1}{4}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{8}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{1}{4}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{9}{4}\). Then divide: \(\frac{9}{4} \div \frac{1}{8} = \frac{9}{4} \times 8 = 18\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(2\frac{1}{3}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{6}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{1}{3}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{7}{3}\). Then divide: \(\frac{7}{3} \div \frac{1}{6} = \frac{7}{3} \times 6 = 14\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(1\frac{1}{2}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{6}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{1}{2}\) to the improper fraction \(\frac{3}{2}\). Then divide: \(\frac{3}{2} \div \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{2} \times 6 = 9\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(2\frac{2}{3}\) circles are divided equally into 12 pieces, find what fraction of a whole circle each piece represents.
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{2}{3}\) to \(\frac{8}{3}\) and divide by 12: \(\frac{8}{3} \div 12 = \frac{8}{3} \times \frac{1}{12} = \frac{2}{9}\) of a whole circle.

qs.q: If \(3\frac{1}{2}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{4}\) of a whole circle, and 5 of these pieces are then removed, how many pieces remain?
qs.s: First find the total number of pieces: \(3\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{4} = \frac{7}{2} \times 4 = 14\) pieces. Then subtract the 5 pieces removed: \(14 - 5 = 9\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(4\frac{2}{3}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{2}{9}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(4\frac{2}{3}\) to \(\frac{14}{3}\), then divide by multiplying by the reciprocal: \(\frac{14}{3} \div \frac{2}{9} = \frac{14}{3} \times \frac{9}{2} = 21\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(2\frac{1}{2}\) circles and an additional \(1\frac{3}{4}\) circles are combined and then divided into pieces which are \(\frac{1}{8}\) of a whole circle, find the total number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: First add the circles: \(2\frac{1}{2} + 1\frac{3}{4} = \frac{10}{4} + \frac{7}{4} = \frac{17}{4}\). Then divide by \(\frac{1}{8}\): \(\frac{17}{4} \times 8 = 34\) pieces.

qs.q: If \(3\frac{3}{4}\) circles are divided into pieces which are \(\frac{2}{5}\) of a whole circle, find the number of pieces obtained.
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{3}{4}\) to \(\frac{15}{4}\), then divide: \(\frac{15}{4} \div \frac{2}{5} = \frac{15}{4} \times \frac{5}{2} = \frac{75}{8} = 9\frac{3}{8}\) pieces.
