qs.q: If \(m \cdot n \cdot p\) is positive and \(m\) is negative, what must be true of \(n\) and \(p\)?
qs.s: Since \(m\) is negative and \(m \cdot (n \cdot p)\) is positive, the product \(n \cdot p\) must be negative, which means \(n\) and \(p\) must have opposite signs.

qs.q: If \((-2) \cdot (-a) \cdot b \cdot (-c)\) is negative, what must be true of the product \(a \cdot b \cdot c\)?
d: \(a \cdot b \cdot c\) can be positive or negative
qs.s: Simplifying the expression gives \((-2) \cdot (-a) \cdot b \cdot (-c) = -2 \cdot (a \cdot b \cdot c)\). For this to be negative, the product \(a \cdot b \cdot c\) must be positive.

qs.q: If \(p\) is negative, what must be true of \(q\) if \(p(-q)\) is negative?
qs.s: Since \(p\) is negative, for \(p(-q)\) to be negative, the factor \((-q)\) must be positive. If \(-q > 0\), then \(q\) must be negative.

qs.q: If \(m\) is positive, what must be true of \(n\) if \(-m \cdot n\) is negative?
qs.s: Since \(m\) is positive, \(-m\) is negative. For a negative number multiplied by \(n\) to produce a negative result, \(n\) must be positive.

qs.q: What must be true of the signs of \(a\) and \(b\) if \(-a \cdot b\) is positive?
d: They must have the same sign
qs.s: For \(-a \cdot b\) to be positive, the product \(a \cdot b\) must be negative. Therefore, \(a\) and \(b\) must have opposite signs.

qs.q: What must be true of the signs of \(x\) and \(y\) if \((-x)(-y)\) is positive?
qs.a: They must have the same sign
d: At least one must be zero
qs.s: Since \((-x)(-y) = x \cdot y\), the expression is positive whenever \(x \cdot y > 0\). This means \(x\) and \(y\) must have the same sign.

qs.q: What must be true of \(u\) and \(v\) if \(-u \cdot v = 0\)?
qs.a: At least one of \(u\) or \(v\) must be zero
qs.s: A product of two factors equals zero if and only if at least one of the factors is zero, so \(u = 0\) or \(v = 0\).

qs.q: If \(a\) is positive and \(b\) is negative, what must be true of \(c\) if \(-4a(-b)(-2c)\) is negative?
qs.s: Since \(a > 0\), \(-4a < 0\), and since \(b < 0\), \(-b > 0\), so \((-4a)(-b)\) is negative. For the total product with \((-2c)\) to remain negative, \((-2c)\) must be positive, which means \(c\) must be negative.

qs.q: If \(x\) is negative and \(y\) is negative, what must be true of \(z\) if \((-2x)(3y)(-z)\) is positive?
qs.s: Since \(x < 0\), \(-2x > 0\), and since \(y < 0\), \(3y < 0\), making \((-2x)(3y)\) negative. For this negative product times \((-z)\) to be positive, \((-z)\) must be negative, which means \(z\) must be positive.

qs.q: If \(k\) is negative, what must be true of the signs of \(m\) and \(n\) if \((-k)(-m)(n)\) is positive?
d: \(m\) and \(n\) must have the same sign
qs.s: Since \(k < 0\), the factor \(-k\) is positive, so the remaining product \((-m)(n) = -(mn)\) must also be positive. For \(-(mn)\) to be positive, \(mn\) must be negative, meaning \(m\) and \(n\) must have opposite signs.

qs.q: If \(w\) is positive and \(x\) is negative, what must be true of the signs of \(y\) and \(z\) if \((-w)(x)(-y)(-z)\) is positive?
qs.a: \(y\) and \(z\) must have the same sign
qs.s: Since \(w > 0\) and \(x < 0\), \((-w)(x) = (\text{negative})(\text{negative})\) is positive. The product simplifies to a positive number times \((-y)(-z) = yz\), so \(yz\) must be positive, meaning \(y\) and \(z\) must have the same sign.

qs.q: If \(p\) and \(q\) have the same sign, what must be true of \(r\) if \((-2p)(3q)(-r)\) is negative?
qs.s: Because \(p\) and \(q\) have the same sign, their product \(pq\) is positive. The expression simplifies to \((-2)(3)(-1)pqr = 6pqr\), so for \(6pqr\) to be negative, \(r\) must be negative.

exercises.name: Conditions on signs of variables in products

qs.q: If \((-u) \cdot (-v) \cdot w\) is positive and \(w < 0\), what must be true about the signs of \(u\) and \(v\)?
d: \(u\) and \(v\) must have the same sign
qs.s: The expression simplifies to \(u \cdot v \cdot w > 0\). Since \(w < 0\), the product \(u \cdot v\) must be negative, which means \(u\) and \(v\) must have opposite signs.

qs.q: If \(a \cdot (-b) \cdot c\) is positive and both \(a\) and \(c\) are negative, what must be true of \(b\)?
qs.s: The expression simplifies to \(-(a \cdot b \cdot c) > 0\), so \(a \cdot b \cdot c < 0\). Since \(a \cdot c\) is positive (negative times negative), \(b\) must be negative (\(b < 0\)).

qs.q: If \(-a \cdot b \cdot c\) is positive and all three variables are non-zero, how many of the variables \(a, b,\) and \(c\) must be negative?
qs.s: For \(-a \cdot b \cdot c\) to be positive, the product \(a \cdot b \cdot c\) must be negative. A product of three non-zero integers is negative if an odd number of them are negative, so 1 or 3 variables must be negative.

qs.q: If \(-x \cdot y \cdot z\) is negative, and it is known that \(x > 0\) and \(y > 0\), what must be true of \(z\)?
qs.s: Since \(-x \cdot y \cdot z < 0\), the product \(x \cdot y \cdot z\) must be positive. Because \(x\) and \(y\) are both positive, \(z\) must also be positive (\(z > 0\)).

qs.q: If \(-p \cdot q \cdot r = 0\), which condition must be true?
qs.a: At least one of \(p, q,\) or \(r\) must be 0
d: All of \(p, q,\) and \(r\) must be 0
Exactly one of \(p, q,\) or \(r\) must be 0
None of \(p, q,\) or \(r\) can be 0
qs.s: A product of integers equals zero if and only if at least one factor is zero, so at least one of \(p, q,\) or \(r\) must equal 0.

qs.q: If the product \((-w)(-x)(-y)(-z)\) is negative and none of the variables are zero, how many of the variables \(w, x, y,\) and \(z\) must be negative?
qs.s: Simplifying gives $(-w)(-x)(-y)(-z) = wxyz < 0$. A product of four non-zero integers is negative only when an odd number of them are negative, so there must be 1 or 3 negative variables.

qs.q: If \((-x)(2y)(-z)(w)(-v) < 0\) and the variables \(x, y, z,\) and \(w\) are all negative, what must be true of \(v\)?
qs.s: The numerical coefficients multiply to \((-1)(2)(-1)(1)(-1) = -2\), giving $-2xyzwv < 0$, so $xyzwv > 0$. Since $xyzw = (-)(-)(-)(-) = +$, \(v\) must be positive (\(v > 0\)).
Multiplying the coefficients yields \((-3)(-1)(2)(-4)(1) = -24\), so $-24abcde < 0$, which means $abcde > 0$. Since $abce = (+)(-)(-)(+) = +$, it follows that \(d > 0\).

qs.q: If \((-2a)(3b)(-c)(-d)\) is positive, and \(a < 0\), \(b > 0\), and \(c < 0\), what must be true of \(d\)?
qs.s: The coefficients multiply to \((-2)(3)(-1)(-1) = -6\), so $-6abcd > 0$, which means $abcd < 0$. Since \(abc = (-)(+)(-) = +\), \(d\) must be negative (\(d < 0\)).

qs.q: Suppose \(p, q, r,\) and \(s\) are non-zero integers such that \(-p \cdot q \cdot (-r) \cdot s > 0\). If \(p\) and \(q\) have the same sign, what must be true about the signs of \(r\) and \(s\)?
qs.a: \(r\) and \(s\) must have the same sign
qs.s: The expression simplifies to $pqrs > 0$. Because \(p\) and \(q\) have the same sign, \(pq > 0\), which forces \(rs > 0\), meaning \(r\) and \(s\) must have the same sign.

qs.q: What must be true of the non-zero integers \(x\) and \(y\) if \(-x \cdot y > 0\)?
d: \(x\) and \(y\) must have the same sign
qs.s: For \(-x \cdot y\) to be positive, the product \(x \cdot y\) must be negative. Two non-zero integers yield a negative product if and only if they have opposite signs.

qs.q: If \(a \cdot b \cdot c > 0\), and it is known that \(a < 0\) and \(b < 0\), what must be true of \(c\)?
qs.s: Since \(a < 0\) and \(b < 0\), their product \(a \cdot b\) is positive. For \((a \cdot b) \cdot c\) to remain positive, \(c\) must also be positive (\(c > 0\)).

qs.q: What must be true of the variables \(u\), \(v\), and \(w\) if \(-3 \cdot u \cdot v \cdot w = 0\)?
qs.a: At least one of \(u\), \(v\), or \(w\) must be zero
d: All three of \(u\), \(v\), and \(w\) must be zero
Exactly one of \(u\), \(v\), or \(w\) must be zero
None of \(u\), \(v\), or \(w\) can be zero
qs.s: Since the constant factor \(-3\) is non-zero, the product can only equal zero if at least one of the variables \(u\), \(v\), or \(w\) is zero.

qs.q: If the product \(x \cdot y \cdot z = 0\) and neither \(x\) nor \(y\) is equal to \(0\), what must be true of \(z\)?
qs.s: A product of factors is zero if and only if at least one factor is zero. Since \(x \ne 0\) and \(y \ne 0\), \(z\) must equal \(0\).

qs.q: If \(p \cdot q \cdot r < 0\), and both \(p\) and \(q\) are positive, what must be true of \(r\)?
qs.s: Since \(p > 0\) and \(q > 0\), their product \(p \cdot q\) is positive. For \((p \cdot q) \cdot r\) to be negative, \(r\) must be negative (\(r < 0\)).

qs.q: If \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), and \(d\) are non-zero integers such that \((-a) \cdot (-b) \cdot (-c) \cdot d > 0\), and it is known that \(a < 0\), \(b > 0\), and \(c < 0\), what must be true of \(d\)?
qs.s: Evaluating the signs of the first three factors gives \(-a > 0\), \(-b < 0\), and \(-c > 0\), so their product is negative. For this negative result multiplied by \(d\) to be positive, \(d\) must also be negative (\(d < 0\)).

qs.q: If \((-2) \cdot x \cdot (-5) \cdot y \cdot (-1) = -70\), which statement must be true about the non-zero integers \(x\) and \(y\)?
qs.a: \(x\) and \(y\) must have the same sign
qs.s: Multiplying the numerical coefficients gives \((-2) \cdot (-5) \cdot (-1) = -10\). Thus \(-10 \cdot x \cdot y = -70\), which simplifies to \(x \cdot y = 7 > 0\), meaning \(x\) and \(y\) must share the same sign.

qs.q: If \(a \cdot b \cdot c \cdot d > 0\) and \(a \cdot b < 0\), which condition must be true for \(c\) and \(d\)?
qs.s: Grouping the product as \((a \cdot b) \cdot (c \cdot d) > 0\), since \(a \cdot b\) is negative, \(c \cdot d\) must also be negative (\(c \cdot d < 0\)) for the overall product of the two groups to be positive.

qs.q: The product of five non-zero integers \(a \cdot b \cdot c \cdot d \cdot e\) is negative. What is the maximum number of these five integers that can be negative?
qs.s: A product of non-zero integers is negative if and only if an odd number of factors are negative. The possible numbers of negative factors are 1, 3, or 5, so the maximum is 5.

qs.q: If the product of four non-zero integers \(w \cdot x \cdot y \cdot z\) is negative, what is the maximum number of these integers that can be positive?
qs.s: For the product to be negative, there must be an odd number of negative factors (either 1 or 3). To maximize positive factors, exactly 1 factor must be negative, leaving at most \(4 - 1 = 3\) positive factors.

qs.q: If \(x\) is a negative integer and \(y\) is a positive integer, what must be true of \(z\) if \(-x \cdot y \cdot z\) is negative?
qs.s: Since \(x < 0\), \(-x\) is positive, making \((-x) \cdot y\) positive. For the entire product to be negative, \(z\) must be multiplied by this positive quantity to yield a negative, so \(z\) must be negative.

qs.q: What must be true of the integers \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) if \(-a \cdot b \cdot c = 0\)?
qs.a: At least one of the variables must be 0
d: Exactly one of the variables must be 0
None of the variables can be negative
qs.s: If a product of integers equals zero, at least one of the factors must be zero. Therefore, at least one of \(a\), \(b\), or \(c\) must equal 0.

qs.q: If \(m\) is a negative integer and \(n\) is a positive integer, what must be true of \(k\) if \((-m) \cdot n \cdot k\) is positive?
qs.s: Because \(m\) is negative, \(-m\) is positive, so \((-m) \cdot n\) is the product of two positive integers, which is positive. For the entire product to remain positive, \(k\) must also be positive.

qs.q: What must be true of the non-zero integers \(p\), \(q\), and \(r\) if \((-p)(-q)r\) is positive?
qs.a: All three are positive, or exactly two are negative
d: All three are negative, or exactly one is negative
All three are negative, or exactly two are negative
qs.s: Since \((-p)(-q) = p \cdot q\), the expression simplifies to \(p \cdot q \cdot r > 0\). A product of three non-zero integers is positive when an even number of factors are negative, meaning all three are positive or exactly two are negative.

qs.q: What must be true of the non-zero integers \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) if \(-a \cdot b \cdot c\) is positive?
qs.a: All three are negative, or exactly one is negative
d: All three are positive, or exactly two are negative
All three are negative, or exactly two are negative
All three are positive, or exactly one is positive
qs.s: Since \(-a \cdot b \cdot c > 0\), multiplying by \(-1\) gives \(a \cdot b \cdot c < 0\). For the product of three non-zero integers to be negative, there must be an odd number of negative factors, so either all three are negative or exactly one is negative.

qs.q: If \(a, b,\) and \(c\) are non-zero integers such that \(-a \cdot b > 0\) and \(-b \cdot c > 0\), what must be true of the product \(a \cdot c\)?
d: \(a \cdot c\) can be positive or negative depending on the sign of \(b\)
qs.s: From \(-a \cdot b > 0\) and \(-b \cdot c > 0\), we have \(a \cdot b < 0\) and \(b \cdot c < 0\), so both \(a\) and \(c\) have the opposite sign of \(b\). Since \(a\) and \(c\) have the same sign as each other, their product \(a \cdot c\) must be positive.

qs.q: What must be true about the number of negative variables among the non-zero integers \(w, x, y,\) and \(z\) if \((-2w)(3x)(-y)(-4z)\) is positive?
qs.a: Exactly 1 or 3 of the variables are negative
d: Exactly 0, 2, or 4 of the variables are negative
Exactly 2 of the variables are negative
All 4 of the variables must be negative
qs.s: Multiplying the coefficients gives \((-2)(3)(-1)(-4) = -24\), so the expression is $-24wxyz > 0$, which means $wxyz < 0$. For a product of four non-zero integers to be negative, an odd number of factors must be negative, so exactly 1 or 3 variables are negative.

qs.q: If \(a < 0\), \(b > 0\), and \(c < 0\), what must be true of the non-zero integer \(d\) if \((-2a)(-3b)(4c)(-d)\) is negative?
qs.s: The signs of the first three factors are \(-2a > 0\), \(-3b < 0\), and \(4c < 0\), giving a product of \((\text{positive})(\text{negative})(\text{negative}) = \text{positive}\). For the total product to be negative, the last factor \(-d\) must be negative, meaning \(d\) must be positive.

qs.q: If \(x, y,\) and \(z\) are non-zero integers such that \((-x) \cdot y \cdot y \cdot (-z) < 0\), what must be true about the signs of \(x\) and \(z\)?
d: \(x\) and \(z\) must have the same sign
qs.s: Since \(y\) is non-zero, \(y \cdot y\) is always positive, and \((-x)(-z) = x \cdot z\), so the expression simplifies to \((x \cdot z)(y \cdot y) < 0\). Because \(y \cdot y > 0\), we must have \(x \cdot z < 0\), which means \(x\) and \(z\) have opposite signs.

qs.q: A hiker was at an elevation of \(820\text{ m}\). As he walked down a mountain trail, his elevation decreased by \(45\text{ m}\) every hour for \(6\) hours. What was his elevation at the end of the hike?
qs.s: The total decrease in elevation is \(6 \times (-45\text{ m}) = -270\text{ m}\). The final elevation is \(820\text{ m} + (-270\text{ m}) = 550\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Marcus had $250 in his savings account. An automated service fee of $8 was deducted from his account each month for \(9\) months, with no other deposits or withdrawals. How much money was in his account at the end of the \(9\) months?
qs.s: The total amount deducted is \(9 \times (-\)8) = -\(72\). The final balance is \(250 + (-\)72) = \(178\).

qs.q: A scuba diver is at an elevation of \(-14\text{ m}\) relative to sea level. She descends at a rate of \(3\text{ m}\) per minute for \(7\) minutes. What is her elevation at the end of the descent?
qs.s: The change in elevation is \(7 \times (-3\text{ m}) = -21\text{ m}\). Adding this to her initial elevation gives \(-14\text{ m} + (-21\text{ m}) = -35\text{ m}\).

qs.q: At 8:00 p.m., the temperature was \(6^\circ\text{C}\). The temperature dropped by \(3^\circ\text{C}\) each hour for the next \(5\) hours. What was the temperature at 1:00 a.m.?
qs.s: The total change in temperature is \(5 \times (-3^\circ\text{C}) = -15^\circ\text{C}\). Adding this to the initial temperature gives \(6^\circ\text{C} + (-15^\circ\text{C}) = -9^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The water level in a storage tank was initially \(140\text{ cm}\). Due to a leak, the water level dropped by \(5\text{ cm}\) each day for \(16\) days. What was the water level in the tank after \(16\) days?
qs.s: The total change in water level is \(16 \times (-5\text{ cm}) = -80\text{ cm}\). The final water level is \(140\text{ cm} + (-80\text{ cm}) = 60\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A small business bank account had a balance of $1450. Over the next \(8\) weeks, the company paid a weekly utility fee of $65. During the same period, a client made \(4\) bi-weekly payments of \(120\) into the account. What was the account balance at the end of the \(8\) weeks?
qs.s: The deductions total \(8 \times (-\)65) = -\(520\) and the deposits total $4 \times $120 = \(480\). The final balance is \(1450 + (-\)520) + $480 = \(1410\).

qs.q: A deep-freeze storage unit starts at \(-5^\circ\text{C}\). During a rapid cooling cycle, its temperature decreases by \(4^\circ\text{C}\) per hour for \(6\) hours. A defrost cycle then increases the temperature by \(2^\circ\text{C}\) per hour for \(3\) hours. Finally, it cools down at \(3^\circ\text{C}\) per hour for \(4\) hours. What is the final temperature of the storage unit?
qs.s: The temperature changes are \(6 \times (-4^\circ\text{C}) = -24^\circ\text{C}\), \(3 \times 2^\circ\text{C} = 6^\circ\text{C}\), and \(4 \times (-3^\circ\text{C}) = -12^\circ\text{C}\). Combining these gives \(-5^\circ\text{C} + (-24^\circ\text{C}) + 6^\circ\text{C} + (-12^\circ\text{C}) = -35^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: In a trivia tournament, a team starts with \(350\) points. In Round 1, they answer \(8\) questions incorrectly, losing \(25\) points for each. In Round 2, they answer \(12\) questions correctly, gaining \(40\) points for each. In Round 3, they answer \(6\) questions incorrectly, losing \(35\) points for each. What is the team's final score?
qs.s: The points changes are \(8 \times (-25) = -200\), \(12 \times 40 = 480\), and \(6 \times (-35) = -210\). The final score is \(350 + (-200) + 480 + (-210) = 420\).

qs.q: A research submarine begins at an elevation of \(-320\text{ m}\). It descends at a rate of \(25\text{ m}\) per minute for \(12\) minutes, stops for an hour, and then ascends at a rate of \(18\text{ m}\) per minute for \(15\) minutes. What is the submarine's final elevation?
qs.s: The descent gives \(12 \times (-25\text{ m}) = -300\text{ m}\) and the ascent gives \(15 \times 18\text{ m} = 270\text{ m}\). The final elevation is \(-320\text{ m} + (-300\text{ m}) + 270\text{ m} = -350\text{ m}\).

qs.q: At midnight, the temperature on a mountain summit was \(-8^\circ\text{C}\). Over the next \(6\) hours, the temperature fell at a constant rate of \(3^\circ\text{C}\) per hour. Then, as the sun rose, the temperature increased at a rate of \(4^\circ\text{C}\) per hour for the following \(5\) hours. What was the temperature at 11:00 a.m.?
qs.s: The changes in temperature are \(6 \times (-3^\circ\text{C}) = -18^\circ\text{C}\) and \(5 \times 4^\circ\text{C} = 20^\circ\text{C}\). The final temperature is \(-8^\circ\text{C} + (-18^\circ\text{C}) + 20^\circ\text{C} = -6^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: In a trivia game, Liam started the bonus round with 450 points. In this round, he lost 35 points for each incorrect answer. If he gave 8 incorrect answers, what was his final score?
qs.s: The change in score from incorrect answers is \(8 \times (-35) = -280\text{ points}\). His final score is \(450 + (-280) = 170\text{ points}\).

qs.q: Marcus had a balance of $1850 in his savings account. He withdrew $45 each week for 20 weeks to pay for music lessons. What was his bank balance at the end of the 20 weeks?
qs.s: The total amount withdrawn is \(20 \times (-\$45) = -\$900\). Adding this to the initial balance gives $1850 + (-$900) = $950.

qs.q: At midnight, the temperature on a mountain summit was 8°C. Over the next 6 hours, the temperature dropped at a steady rate of 3°C per hour. What was the temperature at 6:00 a.m.?
qs.s: The total temperature drop is \(6 \times (-3^\circ\text{C}) = -18^\circ\text{C}\). The final temperature is \(8^\circ\text{C} + (-18^\circ\text{C}) = -10^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A research submarine was at a depth of -140 m relative to sea level. It then descended at a rate of 18 m per minute for 10 minutes. What was its new depth?
qs.s: Descending at 18 m per minute is represented as \(-18\text{ m/min}\), so the change in depth is \(10 \times (-18\text{ m}) = -180\text{ m}\). The new depth is \(-140\text{ m} + (-180\text{ m}) = -320\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A water reservoir contains 3200 L of water. A leak causes it to lose 60 L of water each hour for 24 hours. How much water is left in the reservoir after 24 hours?
qs.s: The total amount of water lost is \(24 \times (-60\text{ L}) = -1440\text{ L}\). The remaining water is \(3200\text{ L} + (-1440\text{ L}) = 1760\text{ L}\).

qs.q: At 6:00 a.m., the temperature at a polar research station was -14°C. During a storm, the temperature dropped at a rate of 4°C per hour for 5 hours. Then, the storm passed and the temperature rose at a rate of 3°C per hour for 7 hours. What was the temperature at 6:00 p.m.?
qs.s: The change during the storm is \(5 \times (-4^\circ\text{C}) = -20^\circ\text{C}\) and the change during the warming is \(7 \times (+3^\circ\text{C}) = +21^\circ\text{C}\). The final temperature is \(-14^\circ\text{C} + (-20^\circ\text{C}) + 21^\circ\text{C} = -13^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A small business had an operating balance of -$4200 at the beginning of the year. Over the next 6 months, it lost $850 each month. Over the following 4 months, it made a profit of $2100 each month. What was the business's balance at the end of the 10 months?
qs.s: The total loss is \(6 \times (-\$850) = -\$5100\) and the total profit is \(4 \times \$2100 = \$8400\). The final balance is \(-\$4200 + (-\$5100) + \$8400 = -\$900\).

qs.q: A drone's fully charged battery has an energy capacity of 4800 mAh. In cruising mode, it consumes 175 mAh per minute for 18 minutes. In high-speed mode, it consumes 240 mAh per minute for 5 minutes. What is the remaining battery capacity after these two flights?
qs.s: The energy consumed is \(18 \times (-175\text{ mAh}) = -3150\text{ mAh}\) in cruising mode and \(5 \times (-240\text{ mAh}) = -1200\text{ mAh}\) in high-speed mode. The remaining capacity is \(4800\text{ mAh} - 3150\text{ mAh} - 1200\text{ mAh} = 450\text{ mAh}\).

qs.q: A deep-sea exploration vehicle was at a depth of -280 m. It descended at a rate of 16 m per minute for 15 minutes, and then ascended at a rate of 22 m per minute for 10 minutes. What was the vehicle's depth at the end of this trip?
qs.s: The descent gives a change of \(15 \times (-16\text{ m}) = -240\text{ m}\), and the ascent gives \(10 \times (+22\text{ m}) = +220\text{ m}\). The final depth is \(-280\text{ m} + (-240\text{ m}) + 220\text{ m} = -300\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Elena had $3150 in her bank account. For 14 weeks, she withdrew $65 each week for groceries. Then, for the next 8 weeks, she deposited $120 each week from tutoring. What was her bank balance at the end of these 22 weeks?
qs.s: The withdrawals total \(14 \times (-\$65) = -\$910\) and the deposits total \(8 \times \$120 = \$960\). Her final balance is $3150 + (-$910) + $960 = $3200.

qs.q: A hot-air balloon descending to the ground loses \(65\text{ meters}\) per minute in altitude. If the balloon took \(14\text{ minutes}\) to land, at what height was the balloon when it first started its descent?
qs.s: Multiply the rate of descent by the time: \(65\text{ m/min} \times 14\text{ min} = 910\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: An account balance decreases by \(\$320\) each month due to recurring service fees. If it took \(14\text{ months}\) for the balance to reach \(\$0\), what was the account balance before the fees began?
qs.s: Multiply the rate of decrease by the number of months: \(\$320/\text{month} \times 14\text{ months} = \$4{,}480\).

qs.q: A laboratory freezer cools a liquid sample, lowering its temperature by \(4^\circ\text{C}\) per minute. If it took \(18\text{ minutes}\) for the sample to cool down to \(0^\circ\text{C}\), what was its temperature when it first started cooling?
qs.s: Multiply the rate of temperature decrease by the time: \(4^\circ\text{C/min} \times 18\text{ min} = 72^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A water reservoir is drained at a constant rate of \(250\text{ liters}\) per minute. If it took \(35\text{ minutes}\) to completely empty the reservoir, how many liters of water were in the reservoir before it started draining?
qs.s: Multiply the rate of water loss by the total time: \(250\text{ L/min} \times 35\text{ min} = 8{,}750\text{ liters}\).

qs.q: A construction elevator descends to ground level at a constant rate of \(5\text{ meters}\) per second. If the elevator took \(26\text{ seconds}\) to reach the ground, at what height was the elevator when it first started descending?
qs.s: Multiply the rate of descent by the time taken: \(5\text{ m/s} \times 26\text{ s} = 130\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: A scientific space probe enters a planetary atmosphere, losing \(125\text{ meters}\) of altitude per second. If the descent lasts for \(4\text{ minutes}\) (\(60\text{ seconds}\) per minute) before the probe reaches its target landing site, how many meters did the probe descend in total?
qs.s: Convert time to seconds and multiply the three factors: \(125 \times 60 \times 4 = 125 \times 240 = 30{,}000\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: A commercial jet cruising at an altitude of \(11{,}500\text{ meters}\) begins its descent. It loses altitude at \(720\text{ meters}\) per minute for \(10\text{ minutes}\), flies level for \(5\text{ minutes}\) losing \(0\text{ meters}\) per minute, and then descends at \(650\text{ meters}\) per minute for \(6\text{ minutes}\). What is the altitude of the jet at the end of this period?
qs.s: The total descent is \((10 \times 720) + (5 \times 0) + (6 \times 650) = 7{,}200 + 0 + 3{,}900 = 11{,}100\text{ meters}\), leaving an altitude of \(11{,}500 - 11{,}100 = 400\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: A plane begins its descent towards an airport. For the first \(12\text{ minutes}\), it loses altitude at a rate of \(650\text{ meters}\) per minute. For the next \(8\text{ minutes}\), it slows its descent to lose \(420\text{ meters}\) per minute before touching down on the runway. At what altitude was the plane when it first started its descent?
qs.s: Calculate the descent in each stage and add them together: \((12 \times 650) + (8 \times 420) = 7{,}800 + 3{,}360 = 11{,}160\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: Starting from sea level (\(0\text{ meters}\)), Submarine A dives at a rate of \(24\text{ meters}\) per minute for \(15\text{ minutes}\). From the same starting point, Submarine B dives at a rate of \(38\text{ meters}\) per minute for \(12\text{ minutes}\). How many meters deeper is Submarine B than Submarine A?
qs.s: Submarine A reaches \(24 \times 15 = 360\text{ m}\) and Submarine B reaches \(38 \times 12 = 456\text{ m}\), so Submarine B is \(456 - 360 = 96\text{ meters}\) deeper.

qs.q: A hiker descends from a mountain peak towards a base camp located at an elevation of \(0\text{ meters}\). She descends at a rate of \(85\text{ meters}\) per hour for \(6\text{ hours}\), climbs uphill over a ridge at a rate of \(40\text{ meters}\) per hour for \(2\text{ hours}\), and finally descends at a rate of \(95\text{ meters}\) per hour for \(5\text{ hours}\) to reach base camp. What was the elevation of the mountain peak?
qs.s: Calculate the net change in altitude: \((6 \times -85) + (2 \times 40) + (5 \times -95) = -510 + 80 - 475 = -905\text{ meters}\), so the starting elevation was \(905\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: A small business lost $1250 each week for 6 weeks. If the company's bank balance is now $32 400, what was the balance 6 weeks ago?
qs.s: The total change in balance was \(6 \times (-\$1250) = -\$7500\). Therefore, the balance 6 weeks ago was \(\$32\,400 - (-\$7500) = \$39\,900\).

qs.q: A piece of industrial machinery depreciated by $2150 per year for 4 years. If the machinery is currently valued at $68 000, what was its value 4 years ago?
qs.s: The total depreciation was \(4 \times (-\$2150) = -\$8600\). Its value 4 years ago was \(\$68\,000 - (-\$8600) = \$76\,600\).

qs.q: A used car dropped $340 in value per month for 7 months. If the car is now worth $12 500, what was the value of the car 7 months ago?
qs.s: The total decrease in value was \(7 \times (-\$340) = -\$2380\). The value 7 months ago was \(\$12\,500 - (-\$2380) = \$14\,880\).

qs.q: Due to a leak, the volume of water in a storage tank dropped 180 L per hour for 9 hours. If the tank now contains 4350 L of water, how much water was in the tank 9 hours ago?
qs.s: The total change in volume was \(9 \times (-180\text{ L}) = -1620\text{ L}\). The volume 9 hours ago was \(4350\text{ L} - (-1620\text{ L}) = 5970\text{ L}\).

qs.q: An investment portfolio lost $420 per week for 8 weeks. If the portfolio is now worth $18 600, what was its value 8 weeks ago?
qs.s: The total loss over 8 weeks was \(8 \times (-\$420) = -\$3360\). Thus, the portfolio value 8 weeks ago was \(\$18\,600 - (-\$3360) = \$21\,960\).

qs.q: A company's reserve fund gained $1400 per month for 5 months, but then lost $2100 per month for the following 4 months. If the fund now has $58 500, what was the fund's balance 9 months ago?
A tech stock dropped $350 in value per month for 4 months, and then dropped $520 per month for the next 3 months. If the stock is now worth $4100, what was its value 7 months ago?

A research submarine started at an unknown elevation. It descended at a rate of 45 m per minute for 8 minutes, ascended at 20 m per minute for 5 minutes, and then descended at 35 m per minute for 6 minutes. If the submarine ended at an elevation of \(-720\text{ m}\), what was its elevation before these maneuvers began?
qs.s: The net elevation change was \(8(-45) + 5(20) + 6(-35) = -360 + 100 - 210 = -470\text{ m}\). The initial elevation was \(-720 - (-470) = -250\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A commercial building's value changed over an 18-month period: it dropped $2400 per month for the first 6 months, gained $1500 per month for the next 8 months, and dropped $3100 per month for the last 4 months. If the building is currently valued at $815 000, what was its value 18 months ago?

Over a 12-hour period, the temperature at a weather station dropped \(4^\circ\text{C}\) per hour for the first 5 hours, and then dropped \(2^\circ\text{C}\) per hour for the remaining 7 hours. If the temperature is now \(-18^\circ\text{C}\), what was the temperature 12 hours ago?
qs.s: The total change was \(5(-4^\circ\text{C}) + 7(-2^\circ\text{C}) = -20^\circ\text{C} - 14^\circ\text{C} = -34^\circ\text{C}\). The initial temperature was \(-18^\circ\text{C} - (-34^\circ\text{C}) = 16^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: During an 8-week monitoring period, Glacier Alpha receded by an average of 45 meters per week. Glacier Beta receded by an average of 6 meters per day. By how many meters did Glacier Alpha's total recession exceed Glacier Beta's total recession over the 8 weeks? (Assume 1 week = 7 days.)
qs.s: Glacier Alpha receded by 8 * (-45 m) = -360 m, and Glacier Beta receded by 56 * (-6 m) = -336 m over 56 days. Glacier Alpha's recession exceeded Glacier Beta's by 360 - 336 = 24 meters.

qs.q: Elena's catering business averaged a loss of $65 per week for a year. Marcus's food truck averaged a loss of $270 per month for a year. How much more money did Elena's business lose than Marcus's business over the year? (Assume 1 year = 52 weeks = 12 months.)
qs.s: Elena's total annual loss was 52 * (-\(65) = -\)3,380, while Marcus's total loss was 12 * (-\(270) = -\)3,240. Elena's business lost $3,380 - $3,240 = $140 more than Marcus's business.

qs.q: Over the course of a year, Investment Fund P lost an average of $35 per week. Investment Fund Q lost an average of $160 per month. How much more money did Investment Fund Q lose than Investment Fund P over the year? (Assume 1 year = 52 weeks = 12 months.)
qs.s: Fund P lost 52 * (-\(35) = -\)1,820, while Fund Q lost 12 * (-\(160) = -\)1,920. Fund Q lost $1,920 - $1,820 = $100 more than Fund P.

qs.q: During a drought, Reservoir X's water level dropped by an average of 14 cm per week for a year. Reservoir Y's water level dropped by an average of 55 cm per month for a year. By how many centimeters did Reservoir X's total drop exceed Reservoir Y's total drop over the year? (Assume 1 year = 52 weeks = 12 months.)
qs.s: Reservoir X dropped by 52 * (-14 cm) = -728 cm, and Reservoir Y dropped by 12 * (-55 cm) = -660 cm. The drop in Reservoir X exceeded Reservoir Y by 728 - 660 = 68 cm.

qs.q: Liam's small retail shop averaged a loss of $80 per week for a year. Sophia's online boutique averaged a loss of $330 per month for a year. How much more money did Liam's shop lose than Sophia's boutique over the year? (Assume 1 year = 52 weeks = 12 months.)
qs.s: Liam's shop lost 52 * (-\(80) = -\)4,160, and Sophia's boutique lost 12 * (-\(330) = -\)3,960. Liam's shop lost $4,160 - $3,960 = $200 more than Sophia's boutique.

qs.q: Marcus and Chloe both tracked their investment losses over a 2-year period. Marcus lost an average of $60 per week for the entire 2 years. Chloe lost an average of $220 per month for the first year. In the second year, Chloe lost an equal amount each month such that her total 2-year loss equaled Marcus's total 2-year loss. What was Chloe's average monthly loss during the second year? (Assume 1 year = 52 weeks = 12 months.)
qs.s: Marcus's total 2-year loss was 104 * (-\(60) = -\)6,240. Chloe lost 12 * (-\(220) = -\)2,640 in Year 1, leaving -\(6,240 - (-\)2,640) = -$3,600 to lose across Year 2, which gives an average monthly loss of -\(3,600 / 12 = -\)300 ($300 per month).

qs.q: Over a 3-year period, Company Alpha averaged a loss of $120 per week in Year 1, $85 per week in Year 2, and $40 per week in Year 3. Over the same 3-year period, Company Beta averaged a loss of $410 per month throughout all 3 years. By how many dollars did Company Beta's total 3-year loss exceed Company Alpha's total 3-year loss? (Assume 1 year = 52 weeks = 12 months.)
qs.s: Company Alpha's 3-year loss was 52(-$120 - $85 - \(40) = 52(-\)245) = -$12,740, and Company Beta's 3-year loss was 36(-\(410) = -\)14,760. Company Beta's total loss exceeded Company Alpha's by $14,760 - $12,740 = $2,020.

qs.q: Drill Rig X descended at an average rate of 14 meters per hour for 18 hours, then ascended at 6 meters per hour for 5 hours. Drill Rig Y descended at an average rate of 9 meters per hour for 24 hours, then ascended at 4 meters per hour for 8 hours. By how many meters was Drill Rig X deeper than Drill Rig Y at the end of these operations?
qs.s: Rig X reached a depth of 18(-14) + 5(6) = -252 + 30 = -222 m (222 m deep), and Rig Y reached 24(-9) + 8(4) = -216 + 32 = -184 m (184 m deep). Rig X was deeper by 222 - 184 = 38 meters.

qs.q: Over a 2-year period, Division A lost an average of $135 per week, Division B lost an average of $580 per month, and Division C lost an average of $18 per day. By how many dollars did the greatest total 2-year loss exceed the least total 2-year loss? (Assume 1 year = 52 weeks = 12 months = 365 days.)
qs.s: Over 2 years, Division A lost 104 * (-\(135) = -\)14,040, Division B lost 24 * (-\(580) = -\)13,920, and Division C lost 730 * (-\(18) = -\)13,140. The greatest loss exceeded the least loss by $14,040 - $13,140 = $900.

qs.q: Over a 52-week year, Investor A lost $65 per week for 36 weeks and gained $110 per week for the remaining 16 weeks. Investor B lost $175 per month for 8 months and gained $90 per month for the remaining 4 months. How much greater was Investor B's net loss than Investor A's net loss over the year?
qs.s: Investor A's net change was 36(-\(65) + 16(\)110) = -$2,340 + \(1,760 = -\)580 (a $580 loss), and Investor B's net change was 8(-\(175) + 4(\)90) = -$1,400 + \(360 = -\)1,040 (a $1,040 loss). Investor B's net loss exceeded Investor A's by $1,040 - $580 = $460.

qs.q: A scuba diver records two depth changes of \(-4\text{ m}\) and \(-9\text{ m}\). Which is larger: the product \((-4)(-9)\) or the sum \((-4) + (-9)\), and why?
qs.s: The product is \((-4)(-9) = 36\) and the sum is \((-4) + (-9) = -13\). Because a positive number is always greater than a negative number, \(36 > -13\), so the product is larger.

qs.q: Is the product of two negative integers always, sometimes, or never larger than their sum? Why?
qs.a: Always, because the product is always positive and the sum is always negative.
d: Sometimes, because the product is only larger when both integers are less than -2.

qs.s: Dividing two negative fractions gives a positive result: \(\left(-\frac{7}{12}\right) \times (-2) = \frac{14}{12} = \frac{7}{6} = 1\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.s: Multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{5}{6} \times \left(-\frac{9}{4}\right) = -\frac{45}{24} = -\frac{15}{8}\). Converting to a mixed fraction yields \(-1\frac{7}{8}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right) \div \frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor: \(\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right) \times \frac{4}{3} = -\frac{20}{18} = -\frac{10}{9}\). In mixed fraction form, this is \(-1\frac{1}{9}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-\frac{8}{9}\right) \div \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: A negative divided by a negative yields a positive result: \(\left(-\frac{8}{9}\right) \times \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = \frac{24}{18} = \frac{4}{3} = 1\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\frac{7}{10} \div \left(-\frac{2}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{7}{10} \times \left(-\frac{5}{2}\right) = -\frac{35}{20} = -\frac{7}{4}\). Converting to a mixed fraction gives \(-1\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-3\frac{1}{3}\right) \div 1\frac{1}{4}\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions and multiply by the reciprocal: \(\left(-\frac{10}{3}\right) \div \frac{5}{4} = \left(-\frac{10}{3}\right) \times \frac{4}{5} = -\frac{8}{3} = -2\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-4\frac{1}{2}\right) \div \left(-1\frac{5}{7}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert each mixed number to an improper fraction: \(\left(-\frac{9}{2}\right) \div \left(-\frac{12}{7}\right) = \left(-\frac{9}{2}\right) \times \left(-\frac{7}{12}\right) = \frac{21}{8} = 2\frac{5}{8}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\frac{3}{4} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{8}\right) \div \frac{2}{5}\)
qs.s: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction and evaluate left to right: \(\frac{3}{4} \times \left(-\frac{8}{9}\right) \times \frac{5}{2} = -\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{5}{2} = -\frac{5}{3} = -1\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(2\frac{2}{5} \div \left(-3\frac{3}{7}\right) \div \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions and multiply by reciprocals: \(\frac{12}{5} \times \left(-\frac{7}{24}\right) \times (-3) = \frac{21}{10} = 2\frac{1}{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-4\frac{1}{6}\right) \div 1\frac{7}{8}\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions: \(\left(-\frac{25}{6}\right) \div \frac{15}{8} = \left(-\frac{25}{6}\right) \times \frac{8}{15} = -\frac{20}{9} = -2\frac{2}{9}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(18 \div \left(-2\frac{1}{4}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert \(-2\frac{1}{4}\) to \(-\frac{9}{4}\) and multiply by the reciprocal: \(18 \div \left(-\frac{9}{4}\right) = 18 \times \left(-\frac{4}{9}\right) = -8\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-24 \div \left(-1\frac{3}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert \(-1\frac{3}{5}\) to \(-\frac{8}{5}\) and multiply by the reciprocal: \(-24 \div \left(-\frac{8}{5}\right) = -24 \times \left(-\frac{5}{8}\right) = 15\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-14 \div 1\frac{1}{3}\)
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{1}{3}\) to \(\frac{4}{3}\) and multiply by the reciprocal: \(-14 \div \frac{4}{3} = -14 \times \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{21}{2}\). Converting to a mixed number gives \(-10\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-15 \div 3\frac{1}{3}\)
qs.s: Convert \(3\frac{1}{3}\) to \(\frac{10}{3}\) and multiply by the reciprocal: \(-15 \div \frac{10}{3} = -15 \times \frac{3}{10} = -\frac{9}{2}\). Converting to a mixed number gives \(-4\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-20 \div 1\frac{1}{2}\)
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{1}{2}\) to \(\frac{3}{2}\) and multiply by the reciprocal: \(-20 \div \frac{3}{2} = -20 \times \frac{2}{3} = -\frac{40}{3}\). Converting to a mixed number gives \(-13\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-30 \div 2\frac{1}{2} \div 1\frac{3}{5}\)
qs.s: Working from left to right, first calculate \(-30 \div 2\frac{1}{2} = -30 \times \frac{2}{5} = -12\). Then compute \(-12 \div 1\frac{3}{5} = -12 \times \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{15}{2} = -7\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-6\frac{2}{5} \div \left(-1\frac{7}{15}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert both mixed numbers to improper fractions to obtain \(-\frac{32}{5} \div \left(-\frac{22}{15}\right) = -\frac{32}{5} \times \left(-\frac{15}{22}\right)\). Simplifying the product yields \(\frac{48}{11} = 4\frac{4}{11}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-75 \div 2\frac{2}{9}\)
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{2}{9}\) to \(\frac{20}{9}\) and multiply by the reciprocal: \(-75 \div \frac{20}{9} = -75 \times \frac{9}{20} = -\frac{135}{4}\). In mixed fraction form, this is \(-33\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-18 \div 2\frac{1}{4} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Working from left to right, first compute \(-18 \div 2\frac{1}{4} = -18 \times \frac{4}{9} = -8\). Then divide by the next term: \(-8 \div \left(-1\frac{1}{5}\right) = -8 \times \left(-\frac{5}{6}\right) = \frac{20}{3} = 6\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-5\frac{1}{4} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{8}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert both mixed numbers to improper fractions to get \(-\frac{21}{4} \div \left(-\frac{9}{8}\right) = -\frac{21}{4} \times \left(-\frac{8}{9}\right)\). Simplifying the product yields \(\frac{14}{3} = 4\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-8\frac{1}{3} \div \left(-3\frac{4}{7}\right)\)
qs.s: A negative divided by a negative is positive, giving \(\frac{25}{3} \div \frac{25}{7} = \frac{25}{3} \times \frac{7}{25}\). Canceling the common factor of \(25\) results in \(\frac{7}{3} = 2\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(4\frac{1}{6} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{4}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to obtain \(\frac{25}{6} \div \left(-\frac{5}{4}\right) = \frac{25}{6} \times \left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)\). Multiplying and simplifying yields \(-\frac{10}{3} = -3\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-5\frac{5}{8} \div \left(-2\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Dividing two negative numbers yields a positive result: \(\frac{45}{8} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{9}{4}\). Converting \(\frac{9}{4}\) to a mixed fraction gives \(2\frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-6\frac{2}{3} \div 1\frac{7}{9}\)
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions to get \(-\frac{20}{3} \div \frac{16}{9} = -\frac{20}{3} \times \frac{9}{16}\). Simplifying the fraction gives \(-\frac{15}{4} = -3\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(3\frac{3}{5} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Write the mixed numbers as improper fractions to get \(\frac{18}{5} \div \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\left(\frac{18}{5} \times \frac{2}{3}\right)\). Simplifying produces \(-\frac{12}{5} = -2\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-2\frac{1}{4} \times \left(-3\frac{1}{3}\right) \div \left(-2\frac{1}{7}\right)\)
qs.s: With three negative values, the result is negative: \(-\left(\frac{9}{4} \times \frac{10}{3} \times \frac{7}{15}\right)\). Multiplying and canceling common factors gives \(-\frac{7}{2} = -3\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-14\frac{2}{5} \div \left(-3\frac{3}{8}\right)\)
qs.s: A negative divided by a negative is positive: \(\frac{72}{5} \times \frac{8}{27}\). Canceling the common factor of \(9\) between \(72\) and \(27\) gives \(\frac{64}{15} = 4\frac{4}{15}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(5\frac{1}{4} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{8}\right) \div 1\frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: Working from left to right, first divide \(\frac{21}{4} \times \left(-\frac{8}{9}\right) = -\frac{14}{3}\). Next, divide \(-\frac{14}{3} \times \frac{4}{7} = -\frac{8}{3} = -2\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-11\frac{1}{4} \div \left(-4\frac{2}{7}\right)\)
qs.s: A negative divided by a negative is positive, giving \(\frac{45}{4} \div \frac{30}{7} = \frac{45}{4} \times \frac{7}{30}\). Dividing \(45\) and \(30\) by their common factor \(15\) gives \(\frac{21}{8} = 2\frac{5}{8}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-6\frac{2}{3}\right) \div 1\frac{7}{9} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Dividing from left to right, first compute \(-\frac{20}{3} \times \frac{9}{16} = -\frac{15}{4}\). Then divide \(-\frac{15}{4} \div \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = \frac{15}{4} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{5}{2} = 2\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-3\frac{1}{2} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{4}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to get \(-\frac{7}{2} \div \left(-\frac{5}{4}\right) = -\frac{7}{2} \times \left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) = \frac{14}{5}\). In mixed fraction form, this is \(2\frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(4\frac{4}{5} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to obtain \(\frac{24}{5} \div \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) = \frac{24}{5} \times \left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) = -\frac{18}{5}\). Converting to a mixed fraction yields \(-3\frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-5\frac{1}{4} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions: \(-\frac{21}{4} \div \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{21}{4} \times \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{7}{2}\). In mixed fraction form, this is \(3\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-3\frac{3}{8} \div \left(-1\frac{7}{8}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions: \(-\frac{27}{8} \div \left(-\frac{15}{8}\right) = -\frac{27}{8} \times \left(-\frac{8}{15}\right) = \frac{9}{5}\). Converting to a mixed fraction gives \(1\frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-2\frac{5}{8} \div 1\frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: Convert each mixed number to an improper fraction: \(-\frac{21}{8} \div \frac{7}{4} = -\frac{21}{8} \times \frac{4}{7} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Written as a mixed fraction, this is \(-1\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\frac{\left(-1\frac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(-2\frac{2}{5}\right)}{\left(-1\frac{1}{5}\right) \times 1\frac{7}{8}}\)
qs.s: With three negative factors, the final result is negative. Multiply the numerator to get \(\frac{18}{5}\) and the denominator to get \(-\frac{9}{4}\); then divide: \(\frac{18}{5} \div \left(-\frac{9}{4}\right) = \frac{18}{5} \times \left(-\frac{4}{9}\right) = -\frac{8}{5} = -1\frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\frac{\left(-2\frac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(-1\frac{1}{3}\right)}{-1\frac{1}{4}}\)
qs.s: An odd number of negative factors (3) means the result is negative. Simplify the numerator to \(\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right) \times \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) = \frac{10}{3}\), then divide by \(-\frac{5}{4}\) to get \(\frac{10}{3} \times \left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) = -\frac{8}{3} = -2\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-4\frac{1}{2} \div 1\frac{1}{4} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Evaluate from left to right: \(-\frac{9}{2} \div \frac{5}{4} = -\frac{9}{2} \times \frac{4}{5} = -\frac{18}{5}\), and then \(-\frac{18}{5} \div \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) = -\frac{18}{5} \times \left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) = \frac{27}{10} = 2\frac{7}{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-6\frac{2}{3}\right) \div \left(-3\frac{1}{3}\right) \div \left(-1\frac{1}{4}\right) \times \left(-2\frac{1}{4}\right)\)
qs.s: Evaluate from left to right: \(\left(-\frac{20}{3}\right) \times \left(-\frac{3}{10}\right) = 2\), then \(2 \times \left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) = -\frac{8}{5}\), and finally \(-\frac{8}{5} \times \left(-\frac{9}{4}\right) = \frac{18}{5} = 3\frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\left(-3\frac{3}{4}\right) \times 1\frac{3}{5} \div \left(-1\frac{7}{8}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to get \(\left(-\frac{15}{4}\right) \times \frac{8}{5} \div \left(-\frac{15}{8}\right)\). Multiplying the first two gives \(-6\), and dividing by \(-\frac{15}{8}\) gives \(-6 \times \left(-\frac{8}{15}\right) = \frac{16}{5} = 3\frac{1}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-3\frac{1}{4} \div 1\frac{2}{5}\)
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions to get \(-\frac{13}{4} \div \frac{7}{5}\). Multiply by the reciprocal: \(-\frac{13}{4} \times \frac{5}{7} = -\frac{65}{28} = -2\frac{9}{28}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-3\frac{3}{7} \div 2\frac{1}{2}\)
qs.s: Convert each mixed number to an improper fraction: \(-\frac{24}{7} \div \frac{5}{2}\). Multiply by the reciprocal to find \(-\frac{24}{7} \times \frac{2}{5} = -\frac{48}{35} = -1\frac{13}{35}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-4\frac{1}{2} \div \left(-1\frac{5}{7}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers into improper fractions to get \(-\frac{9}{2} \div \left(-\frac{12}{7}\right)\). Dividing two negatives yields a positive result: \(\frac{9}{2} \times \frac{7}{12} = \frac{21}{8} = 2\frac{5}{8}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-1\frac{5}{6} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{8}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to obtain \(-\frac{11}{6} \div \left(-\frac{9}{8}\right)\). Since a negative divided by a negative is positive, multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{11}{6} \times \frac{8}{9} = \frac{44}{27} = 1\frac{17}{27}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(2\frac{2}{5} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to get \(\frac{12}{5} \div \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)\). Multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{12}{5} \times \left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) = -\frac{9}{5} = -1\frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\frac{-4\frac{2}{3}}{-1\frac{1}{6} \times 1\frac{3}{5}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the denominator first: \(\left(-\frac{7}{6}\right) \times \frac{8}{5} = -\frac{28}{15}\). Then divide the numerator by the denominator: \(\left(-\frac{14}{3}\right) \div \left(-\frac{28}{15}\right) = \left(-\frac{14}{3}\right) \times \left(-\frac{15}{28}\right) = \frac{5}{2} = 2\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-3\frac{1}{3} \div \left(-1\frac{1}{4}\right) \div 1\frac{5}{7}\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions: \(-\frac{10}{3} \div \left(-\frac{5}{4}\right) \div \frac{12}{7}\). Evaluating from left to right, \(\left(-\frac{10}{3}\right) \times \left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) = \frac{8}{3}\), and then \(\frac{8}{3} \times \frac{7}{12} = \frac{14}{9} = 1\frac{5}{9}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(\frac{-3\frac{1}{8} \times \left(-1\frac{3}{5}\right)}{-1\frac{7}{8}}\)
qs.s: Multiply the factors in the numerator to get \(\left(-\frac{25}{8}\right) \times \left(-\frac{8}{5}\right) = 5\). Then divide by the denominator: \(5 \div \left(-\frac{15}{8}\right) = 5 \times \left(-\frac{8}{15}\right) = -\frac{8}{3} = -2\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-4\frac{1}{2} \div \left(-1\frac{2}{7}\right) \div 2\frac{5}{8}\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions: \(\left(-\frac{9}{2}\right) \div \left(-\frac{9}{7}\right) \div \frac{21}{8}\). Working from left to right, \(\left(-\frac{9}{2}\right) \times \left(-\frac{7}{9}\right) = \frac{7}{2}\), and then \(\frac{7}{2} \times \frac{8}{21} = \frac{4}{3} = 1\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Simplify. Leave answer in mixed fraction form: \(-1\frac{5}{7} \times \left(-2\frac{4}{5}\right) \div \left(-1\frac{7}{9}\right)\)
qs.s: Convert each term to an improper fraction: \(\left(-\frac{12}{7}\right) \times \left(-\frac{14}{5}\right) \div \left(-\frac{16}{9}\right)\). Multiply the first two factors to get \(\frac{24}{5}\), then multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor to get \(\frac{24}{5} \times \left(-\frac{9}{16}\right) = -\frac{27}{10} = -2\frac{7}{10}\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-4 \cdot (-7) \cdot 5}{-14}\)
qs.s: There are three negative integers (an odd count), so the answer is negative: \(\frac{-4 \cdot (-7) \cdot 5}{-14} = \frac{140}{-14} = -10\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{8 \cdot (-3) \cdot (-5)}{-20}\)
qs.s: There are three negative integers (an odd count), so the answer is negative: \(\frac{8 \cdot (-3) \cdot (-5)}{-20} = \frac{120}{-20} = -6\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-6 \cdot 5 \cdot (-4)}{-15}\)
qs.s: There are three negative integers (an odd count), so the answer is negative: \(\frac{-6 \cdot 5 \cdot (-4)}{-15} = \frac{120}{-15} = -8\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-8 \cdot (-7) \cdot (-2)}{-28}\)
qs.s: There are four negative integers (an even count), so the answer is positive: \(\frac{-8 \cdot (-7) \cdot (-2)}{-28} = \frac{-112}{-28} = 4\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-9 \cdot (-4) \cdot 2}{-24}\)
qs.s: There are three negative integers (an odd count), so the answer is negative: \(\frac{-9 \cdot (-4) \cdot 2}{-24} = \frac{72}{-24} = -3\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-24 \cdot 35 \cdot (-18) \cdot (-5)}{-27 \cdot 28}\)
qs.s: There are four negative factors, so the result is positive. Simplifying the magnitudes gives \(\frac{24 \cdot 35 \cdot 18 \cdot 5}{27 \cdot 28} = \frac{75600}{756} = 100\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-4 \cdot (-9) \cdot (-10) \cdot 14}{-7 \cdot (-12)}\)
qs.s: There are five negative factors, so the result is negative. Dividing out common factors gives \(\frac{4 \cdot 9 \cdot 10 \cdot 14}{7 \cdot 12} = \frac{5040}{84} = 60\), so the answer is \(-60\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-12 \cdot (-15) \cdot (-14)}{-9 \cdot 20}\)
qs.s: There are four negative factors (even count), making the result positive. Simplifying the magnitudes gives \(\frac{12 \cdot 15 \cdot 14}{9 \cdot 20} = \frac{2520}{180} = 14\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-18 \cdot (-25) \cdot (-8)}{-15 \cdot (-12)}\)
qs.s: There are five negative factors (odd count), making the result negative. Simplifying the magnitudes gives \(\frac{18 \cdot 25 \cdot 8}{15 \cdot 12} = \frac{3600}{180} = 20\), so the answer is \(-20\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{-16 \cdot (-21) \cdot (-30)}{-8 \cdot (-7) \cdot (-15)}\)
qs.s: There are six negative factors, so the result is positive. Cancelling terms directly gives \(\frac{16}{8} \cdot \frac{21}{7} \cdot \frac{30}{15} = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 = 12\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{(-7) \cdot (-12) \cdot 5}{(-10) \cdot 6}\)
qs.s: There are 3 negative integers (an odd number), so the result is negative. Simplifying the absolute values gives \(\frac{7 \cdot 12 \cdot 5}{10 \cdot 6} = \frac{420}{60} = 7\), giving \(-7\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{(-4) \cdot 9 \cdot (-10)}{(-6) \cdot 5}\)
qs.s: There are 3 negative integers (an odd number), so the result is negative. Simplifying the absolute values gives \(\frac{4 \cdot 9 \cdot 10}{6 \cdot 5} = \frac{360}{30} = 12\), so the answer is \(-12\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{6 \cdot (-8) \cdot (-5)}{(-4) \cdot (-15)}\)
qs.s: There are 4 negative integers (an even number), so the result is positive. Simplifying the absolute values gives \(\frac{6 \cdot 8 \cdot 5}{4 \cdot 15} = \frac{240}{60} = 4\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{(-3) \cdot (-16) \cdot 5}{(-6) \cdot (-8)}\)
qs.s: There are 4 negative integers (an even number), so the result is positive. Simplifying the absolute values gives \(\frac{3 \cdot 16 \cdot 5}{6 \cdot 8} = \frac{240}{48} = 5\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{(-2) \cdot (-18) \cdot (-4)}{(-8) \cdot (-3)}\)
qs.s: There are 5 negative integers (an odd number), so the result is negative. Simplifying the absolute values gives \(\frac{2 \cdot 18 \cdot 4}{8 \cdot 3} = \frac{144}{24} = 6\), giving \(-6\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{(-16) \cdot (-21) \cdot (-10) \cdot (-18)}{(-20) \cdot 14 \cdot (-27)}\)
qs.s: There are 6 negative integers (an even number), so the product is positive. Simplifying the absolute values gives \(\frac{16 \cdot 21 \cdot 10 \cdot 18}{20 \cdot 14 \cdot 27} = \frac{60480}{7560} = 8\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\frac{(-48) \cdot 25 \cdot (-27)}{(-15) \cdot (-36) \cdot (-20)}\)
qs.s: There are 5 negative integers (an odd number), so the answer is negative. Cancelling common factors gives \(\frac{48 \cdot 25 \cdot 27}{15 \cdot 36 \cdot 20} = \frac{32400}{10800} = 3\), giving a final answer of \(-3\).

qs.s: The first fraction evaluates to \(\frac{\text{negative}}{\text{positive}} = \text{negative}\), and the second fraction evaluates to \(\frac{\text{positive}}{\text{positive}} = \text{positive}\). Multiplying a negative by a positive yields a negative result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(x\) is negative, \(y\) is positive, and \(z\) is negative: \(\frac{-(-x \cdot y)}{-(-z)} \cdot \frac{-(-(-x))}{y \cdot (-z)}\)
qs.s: The first fraction simplifies to \(\frac{\text{negative}}{\text{negative}} = \text{positive}\), and the second fraction simplifies to \(\frac{\text{positive}}{\text{positive}} = \text{positive}\). The product of two positive values is positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a\) is negative, \(b\) is positive, \(c\) is negative, \(d\) is negative, \(e\) is positive, and \(f\) is negative: \(\frac{-a \cdot (-b) \cdot c}{-d \cdot e \cdot (-f)}\)
qs.s: The numerator \((-a) \cdot (-b) \cdot c\) has two negative factors (\((-b)\) and \(c\)), making it positive. The denominator \((-d) \cdot e \cdot (-f)\) has all positive factors, so dividing a positive by a positive yields a positive result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(u\) is negative, \(v\) is negative, and \(w\) is negative: \(\frac{u \cdot (-v)}{-w \cdot u \cdot v}\)
qs.s: The numerator contains one negative factor (\(u\)), and the denominator contains two negative factors (\(u\) and \(v\)), totaling three negative factors. Since three is odd, the expression is negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a\) is positive, \(b\) is negative, \(c\) is negative, and \(d\) is positive: \(\frac{-a \cdot b}{(-c) \cdot d \cdot (-b)}\)
qs.s: The numerator has two negative factors (\(-a\) and \(b\)), while all factors in the denominator (\(-c\), \(d\), and \(-b\)) are positive. Two negative factors is an even number, so the expression is positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(p\) is positive, \(q\) is negative, and \(r\) is positive: \(\frac{-p \cdot (-q)}{-r \cdot q}\)
qs.s: The numerator has one negative factor (\(-p\)), and the denominator has two negative factors (\(-r\) and \(q\)), giving three negative factors in total. Since an odd number of negative factors yields a negative result, the expression is negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(m\) is negative, \(n\) is positive, and \(k\) is negative: \(\frac{m \cdot n \cdot k}{(-n) \cdot (-k)}\)
qs.s: The numerator has two negative factors (\(m\) and \(k\)), while the denominator has one negative factor (\(-n\)), for a total of three negative factors. Because the number of negative factors is odd, the expression is negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(w\) is negative, \(x\) is positive, \(y\) is negative, and \(z\) is negative: \(\frac{w \cdot (-x) \cdot y}{(-w) \cdot z}\)
qs.s: The numerator has three negative factors (\(w\), \(-x\), and \(y\)), and the denominator has one negative factor (\(z\)). With four negative factors in total, the even count ensures the expression evaluates to positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(x\) is negative, \(y\) is positive, and \(z\) is negative: \(\frac{(-x) \cdot (-x) \cdot (-x) \cdot (-y) \cdot z}{(-y) \cdot (-y) \cdot (-z) \cdot x}\)
qs.s: The numerator contains two negative factors (\(-y\) and \(z\)) since \(-x\) is positive. The denominator contains three negative factors (two copies of \(-y\), and \(x\)) since \(-z\) is positive. Across the entire expression there are five negative factors, which is an odd number, so the result is negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(w\) is negative, \(x\) is negative, \(y\) is negative, and \(z\) is positive: \(\left(\frac{-x \cdot y}{-z}\right) \div \left(\frac{-(-w) \cdot (-x)}{y \cdot (-z)}\right)\)
qs.s: The first fraction simplifies to \(\frac{(+)\cdot(-)}{(-)} = +\), while the second fraction simplifies to \(\frac{(-)\cdot(+)}{(-)\cdot(-)} = -\). Dividing a positive value by a negative value results in a negative expression.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a\) is negative, \(b\) is positive, \(c\) is negative, \(d\) is negative, and \(e\) is positive: \(\frac{-2a \cdot (-b) \cdot (-(-c))}{-d \cdot 3e \cdot (-a)}\)
qs.s: In the numerator, \(-b\) and \(-(-c)\) are negative while \(-2a\) is positive (giving two negative factors). In the denominator, \(-d\), \(3e\), and \(-a\) are all positive, so the entire expression contains two negative factors (an even number), making it positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a\) is positive, \(b\) is negative, \(c\) is negative, \(d\) is positive, \(e\) is negative, and \(f\) is positive: \(\frac{-(-a) \cdot (-b) \cdot (-(-(-c)))}{-d \cdot (-e) \cdot (-f)}\)
qs.s: All three numerator factors (\(-(-a)\), \(-b\), and \(-(-(-c))\)) evaluate to positive, while the denominator contains two negative factors (\(-d\) and \(-f\)). Because there are two negative factors in total (an even count), the expression evaluates to positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a\) is negative, \(b\) is negative, \(c\) is positive, and \(d\) is negative: \(-\frac{-a \cdot (-b) \cdot (-c) \cdot d}{-(-a) \cdot (-d) \cdot c}\)
qs.s: Inside the fraction, the numerator has two negative factors (\(-c\) and \(d\)) and the denominator has one (\(-(-a)\)), making the fraction itself negative. The negative sign outside the fraction negates this negative value, giving a positive result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(x\) is negative, \(y\) is negative, \(z\) is positive, and \(w\) is negative: \(\frac{(-x) \cdot (-(y))}{-(z) \cdot w}\)
qs.s: The numerator \((-x)(-(y))\) is \((+)(+) = +\), and the denominator \(-(z) \cdot w\) is \((-)(-) = +\). Dividing a positive by a positive gives a positive result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(p\) is positive, \(q\) is negative, and \(r\) is positive: \(\frac{-(-p) \cdot (-q)}{-r}\)
qs.s: The factor \(-(-p)\) is positive, \(-q\) is positive, and the denominator \(-r\) is negative. Thus, \(\frac{(+) \cdot (+)}{-} = -\), which is negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(u\) is positive, \(v\) is positive, \(w\) is negative, and \(t\) is negative: \(\frac{-(-u) \cdot (-v)}{-w \cdot (-(-t))}\)
qs.s: The numerator is \((+) \cdot (-) = -\), and the denominator is \((+) \cdot (-) = -\). Dividing a negative by a negative yields a positive result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(m\) is negative, \(n\) is negative, and \(k\) is positive: \(\frac{-m \cdot (-(-n))}{-(-k)}\)
qs.s: Here, \(-m\) is positive, \(-(-n)\) is negative, and \(-(-k)\) is positive. Therefore, the expression evaluates to \(\frac{(+) \cdot (-)}{+} = -\), which is negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(z\) is positive and \(u, v, w, x, y\) are negative: \(\frac{-(-x) \cdot (-2y) \cdot (-(-(-z)))}{-(-w) \cdot 3u \cdot (-(-v))}\)
qs.s: The numerator simplifies to \((-) \cdot (+) \cdot (-) = +\), while the denominator contains three negative factors: \((-) \cdot (-) \cdot (-) = -\). A positive divided by a negative gives a negative result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(x\) is negative, \(y\) is positive, and \(z\) is negative: \(\frac{-5 \cdot (-(-x)) \cdot (-3y)}{-(-2) \cdot (-z) \cdot (-4)}\)
qs.s: The numerator has three negative factors, so it is negative: \((-) \cdot (-) \cdot (-) = -\). The denominator has one negative factor, so it is also negative: \((+) \cdot (+) \cdot (-) = -\). A negative divided by a negative is positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a\) is negative, \(b\) is positive, \(c\) is negative, \(d\) is positive, and \(e\) is negative: \(\frac{-(-(-a)) \cdot (-b) \cdot c}{-(-d) \cdot (-(-e))}\)
qs.s: The numerator evaluates to \((+) \cdot (-) \cdot (-) = +\) and the denominator evaluates to \((+) \cdot (-) = -\). Dividing a positive by a negative gives a negative result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a, b, c\) are negative and \(d, e\) are positive: \([-(-a) \cdot (-b) \cdot (-(-c))] \div [-(-(-d)) \cdot (-e)]\)
qs.s: The dividend evaluates to \((-) \cdot (+) \cdot (-) = +\), and the divisor evaluates to \((-) \cdot (-) = +\). Dividing a positive number by a positive number results in a positive value.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(p, q, s, u\) are negative and \(r, t\) are positive: \(\frac{-(-p) \cdot (-(q)) \cdot (-(-r))}{-(-(-s)) \cdot (-t) \cdot u}\)
qs.s: There are 13 negative factors in total (9 explicit negative signs and 4 negative variables). Since 13 is odd, the expression evaluates to a negative value.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(u\) is positive, \(v\) is negative, \(w\) is positive, and \(z\) is negative: \(\frac{-(u) \cdot v}{(-w) \cdot (-(z))}\)
qs.s: The numerator has two negative factors, \(-(u)\) and \(v\), making it positive. The denominator has one negative factor, \(-w\), because \(-(z)\) is positive, so dividing the positive numerator by the negative denominator yields a negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(w\) is negative, \(x\) is positive, \(y\) is negative, and \(z\) is positive: \(\frac{-w \cdot (-x)}{y \cdot (-z)}\)
qs.s: Since \(w < 0\), \(-w\) is positive, and since \(x > 0\), \(-x\) is negative, making the numerator negative. In the denominator, \(y\) is negative and \(-z\) is negative, which gives a positive product, so dividing a negative by a positive results in a negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(p\) is negative, \(q\) is negative, \(r\) is positive, and \(s\) is negative: \(\frac{-(p) \cdot q}{(-r) \cdot (-s)}\)
qs.s: The numerator is a positive times a negative, which is negative, while the denominator is a negative times a positive, which is also negative. Dividing a negative by a negative results in a positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(m\) is positive, \(n\) is negative, \(p\) is negative, and \(q\) is negative: \(\frac{(-m) \cdot (-n)}{(-p) \cdot q}\)
qs.s: The numerator evaluates to \((-m) \cdot (-n) = (-) \cdot (+) = -\), and the denominator evaluates to \((-p) \cdot q = (+) \cdot (-) = -\). Dividing a negative by a negative gives a positive result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(u\) is negative, \(v\) is negative, \(w\) is positive, \(x\) is positive, \(y\) is negative, and \(z\) is positive: \(\frac{-(-u) \cdot (-v) \cdot w}{-(x) \cdot (-y) \cdot (-z)}\)
qs.s: In the numerator, \(-(-u)\) is negative while \(-v\) and \(w\) are positive; in the denominator, \(-(x)\) and \(-z\) are negative while \(-y\) is positive. With a total of 3 negative factors (an odd number), the entire expression evaluates to a negative.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(a\) is positive, \(b\) is negative, \(c\) is positive, and \(d\) is positive: \(\frac{-15 \cdot (-a) \cdot (-b)}{-4 \cdot c \cdot (-d)}\)
qs.s: The numerator has two negative factors, \(-15\) and \(-a\) (since \(-b > 0\)), making it positive. The denominator also has two negative factors, \(-4\) and \(-d\) (since \(c > 0\)), making it positive, so dividing gives a positive result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(w\) is negative, \(x\) is negative, \(y\) is positive, and \(z\) is negative: \(\frac{-w}{-(-x)} \cdot \frac{-(y)}{-(-z)}\)
qs.s: The first fraction simplifies to \(\frac{+}{-} = -\), and the second fraction simplifies to \(\frac{-}{-} = +\). Multiplying a negative by a positive gives a negative result.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(m\) is negative, \(n\) is positive, \(p\) is negative, and \(q\) is negative: \(-\left( \frac{-(-m) \cdot n}{-p \cdot (-q)} \right)\)
qs.s: Inside the parentheses, the numerator is negative because \(-(-m) < 0\) and the denominator is positive because \(-p > 0\) and \(-q > 0\), making the fraction negative. The outer negative sign then negates this value, resulting in a positive.

qs.q: Determine the sign of the expression if \(r\) is positive, \(s\) is negative, \(t\) is positive, and \(u\) is negative: \(\frac{-(-r) \cdot (-s)}{-(t)} \div \frac{-u}{-(-t)}\)
qs.s: The first fraction evaluates to \(\frac{(+) \cdot (+)}{-} = -\), and the second fraction evaluates to \(\frac{+}{+} = +\). Dividing a negative by a positive results in a negative.

exercises.name: Rate of Change and Integer Division Word Problems

qs.q: During a cold front, the temperature drops by \(4^\circ\text{C}\) each hour. The total change in temperature over the period is \(-28^\circ\text{C}\). For how many hours has the temperature been dropping?
qs.s: Divide the total temperature change by the hourly rate of change: \(\frac{-28}{-4} = 7\) hours.

qs.q: A reservoir's water level decreases by 6 centimeters each day. The total change in the water level is -144 centimeters. Over how many days did the water level decrease?
qs.s: Divide the total change in water level by the daily decrease: \(\frac{-144}{-6} = 24\) days.

qs.q: A social media page loses 150 followers each day. Over a certain period, the total change in followers is -1,350. How many days were involved?
qs.s: Divide the total change in followers by the daily change: \(\frac{-1350}{-150} = 9\) days.

qs.q: A research submarine descends at a constant rate of 45 meters per minute. Its total change in depth is -360 meters. For how many minutes has the submarine been descending?
qs.s: Divide the total change in depth by the rate of descent per minute: \(\frac{-360}{-45} = 8\) minutes.

qs.q: A charity reserve fund is reduced by $75 each week to purchase supplies. If the total change in the fund balance is -$975, how many weeks of purchases were made?
qs.s: Divide the total change in the fund by the weekly expense: \(\frac{-975}{-75} = 13\) weeks.

qs.q: An online store lost $320 per day during the first 5 days of an advertising campaign. For the remainder of the campaign, it lost $480 per day. If the total loss over the entire campaign was $4,480, how many days did the second part of the campaign last?
qs.s: The loss for the first 5 days was \(5 \times (-320) = -1600\) dollars, leaving a remaining loss of \(-4480 - (-1600) = -2880\) dollars. Dividing by the second rate gives \(\frac{-2880}{-480} = 6\) days.

qs.q: At 8:00 a.m., the temperature in an arctic town was \(14^\circ\text{F}\). By 5:00 p.m. on the same day, a storm caused the temperature to drop steadily to \(-31^\circ\text{F}\). What was the hourly rate of change in temperature, in \(^\circ\text{F}\) per hour?
qs.s: The 9 hours elapsed produced a temperature change of \(-31 - 14 = -45^\circ\text{F}\). Divide by the time to find the hourly rate: \(\frac{-45}{9} = -5^\circ\text{F}\) per hour.

qs.q: An undersea research vehicle begins at a depth of -450 meters relative to sea level. It descends at a constant rate of 75 meters per hour until it reaches a depth of -2,400 meters. How many hours did the descent take?
qs.s: The total change in depth is \(-2400 - (-450) = -1950\) meters. Dividing by the rate of descent gives \(\frac{-1950}{-75} = 26\) hours.

qs.q: A group of 6 business partners shared equally in a business venture. Over a period of 4 months, the venture suffered a steady loss of $2,550 each month. By how many dollars did each partner's account balance change in total over the 4 months?
qs.s: The total venture loss was \(4 \times (-2550) = -10200\) dollars. Dividing equally among 6 partners gives \(\frac{-10200}{6} = -1700\) dollars.

qs.q: A weather balloon at an altitude of 1,450 meters descends at a constant rate of 65 meters per minute until it reaches an altitude of 280 meters. For how many minutes did the balloon descend?
qs.s: Find the total change in altitude, \(280 - 1450 = -1170\) meters, and divide by the rate of descent: \(\frac{-1170}{-65} = 18\) minutes.

exercises.name: Rate of Change and Integer Division Word Problems

qs.q: During an extended dry season, the water level of a reservoir dropped by a total of 144 centimetres over 9 weeks. What was the average weekly change in the water level?
qs.s: The drop is represented as -144 centimetres. Dividing by 9 weeks gives -144 / 9 = -16 centimetres per week.

qs.q: Over a period of 7 years, the thickness of a glacier decreased by 168 metres. Find the average annual change in the glacier's thickness.
qs.s: A decrease is represented as a negative integer, -168 metres. Dividing the total change by the number of years gives -168 / 7 = -24 metres per year.

qs.q: Over an 8-hour period, the temperature in a freezer dropped by 56 degrees Celsius. Find the average hourly change in temperature.
qs.s: Represent the temperature drop as -56 degrees Celsius. Dividing by 8 hours gives -56 / 8 = -7 degrees Celsius per hour.

qs.q: The population of an industrial town decreased by 11 400 people over a span of 6 years. Find the average annual change in population.
qs.s: Represent the population decrease as -11 400. The average annual change is -11 400 / 6 = -1900 people per year.

qs.q: A small business accumulated a debt of $18 900. The owner pays off the debt in equal monthly installments of $630. How many payments are needed to pay off the debt completely?
qs.s: Owing debt is represented as -$18 900 and each payment reduction is -$630. Dividing the debt by the installment amount gives -18 900 / -630 = 30 payments.

qs.q: Over the course of a year (12 months), an investment fund recorded four quarterly changes in value: -\(23 000, -\)17 000, -\(31 000, and -\)25 000. What was the average monthly change in the fund's value?
qs.s: The total annual change is (-23 000) + (-17 000) + (-31 000) + (-25 000) = -$96 000. Dividing by 12 months gives -\(96 000 / 12 = -\)8000 per month.

qs.q: At 9:00 AM, the temperature on a mountain summit was 15 degrees Celsius. By 3:00 PM on the same day (6 hours later), the temperature had dropped to -21 degrees Celsius. What was the average hourly change in temperature?
qs.s: The total change in temperature is -21 - 15 = -36 degrees Celsius. Dividing by the 6 hours gives -36 / 6 = -6 degrees Celsius per hour.

qs.q: Over a 7-year period, City X's population changed by -15 400. Over an 8-year period, City Y's population changed by -14 400. What is the difference between City X's average annual change in population and City Y's average annual change in population (City X's rate minus City Y's rate)?
qs.s: City X's rate is -15 400 / 7 = -2200, and City Y's rate is -14 400 / 8 = -1800. The difference is -2200 - (-1800) = -400.

qs.q: A deep-sea research probe starts at an elevation of -200 metres relative to sea level. It descends at a constant average rate of -40 metres per minute until it reaches an elevation of -1400 metres. How many minutes did the probe take to complete this descent?
qs.s: The total change in elevation is -1400 - (-200) = -1200 metres. Dividing by the rate of change gives -1200 / -40 = 30 minutes.

qs.q: A submarine descended 450 metres during its first dive session and another 750 metres during its second dive session. If the total descent took 15 minutes, what was the submarine's average change in elevation per minute over the entire period?
qs.s: The total change in elevation is (-450) + (-750) = -1200 metres. Dividing by 15 minutes gives -1200 / 15 = -80 metres per minute.

exercises.name: Rate of Change and Integer Division Word Problems

qs.q: The water level in a reservoir dropped from \(735\text{ cm}\) to \(465\text{ cm}\) over a period of \(15\text{ days}\). At what rate did the water level change per day?
qs.s: The change in water level is \(465 - 735 = -270\text{ cm}\). Dividing by time gives \(-270 \div 15 = -18\text{ cm/day}\).

qs.q: A submarine's elevation changed from \(-140\text{ m}\) to \(-860\text{ m}\) in \(18\text{ minutes}\). What was its average rate of change in elevation per minute?
qs.s: The elevation change is \(-860 - (-140) = -720\text{ m}\). Dividing by time gives \(-720 \div 18 = -40\text{ m/min}\).

qs.q: The temperature in an industrial freezer decreased from \(16^\circ\text{C}\) to \(-14^\circ\text{C}\) over a period of \(6\text{ hours}\). What was the average rate of change in temperature per hour?
qs.s: The change in temperature is \(-14 - 16 = -30^\circ\text{C}\). Dividing by the time gives \(-30 \div 6 = -5^\circ\text{C/h}\).

qs.q: A diver descends from the surface at a constant rate of change in elevation of \(-8\text{ m/min}\). How many minutes will it take the diver to reach an elevation of \(-120\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: Divide the target elevation by the rate of change: \(-120 \div (-8) = 15\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A weather balloon's altitude decreased from \(2450\text{ m}\) to \(830\text{ m}\) in \(45\text{ seconds}\). At what rate did its altitude change per second?
qs.s: The change in altitude is \(830 - 2450 = -1620\text{ m}\). Dividing by time gives \(-1620 \div 45 = -36\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: A retail corporation reported a total quarterly loss of \(-\$540{,}000\). The loss was shared equally among \(15\) regional districts, and each district distributed its loss equally among \(9\) branch stores. By how much did each branch store's account balance change?
qs.s: Each district incurred a loss of \(-540{,}000 \div 15 = -36{,}000\) dollars. Dividing equally among \(9\) branches gives \(-36{,}000 \div 9 = -\$4{,}000\) per branch.

qs.q: A club with \(16\) members incurred an unexpected shared debt of \(-\$3840\). The members agreed to split the debt equally, and each member pays off their share in equal monthly installments of \(-\$40\). How many months will it take each member to pay off their share?
qs.s: Each member's share is \(-3840 \div 16 = -\$240\). Dividing each share by the monthly payment gives \(-240 \div (-40) = 6\text{ months}\).

qs.q: An automated ocean probe is at an elevation of \(-180\text{ m}\). It first ascends \(60\text{ m}\) to transmit data, and then dives at a constant rate of change in elevation of \(-40\text{ m/min}\). How many minutes after starting the dive will it take to reach an elevation of \(-1520\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: The dive starts at \(-180 + 60 = -120\text{ m}\), so the change in elevation is \(-1520 - (-120) = -1400\text{ m}\). The time required is \(-1400 \div (-40) = 35\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: During a lab experiment, the temperature of a sample was initially \(20^\circ\text{C}\). For the first \(8\text{ hours}\), the temperature dropped at a steady rate of \(-3^\circ\text{C/h}\). Over the next \(14\text{ hours}\), the sample cooled to a final temperature of \(-74^\circ\text{C}\). What was the rate of change in temperature per hour during the final \(14\text{ hours}\)?
