qs.s: The surface area of a cube is \(\text{SA} = 6S^2 = 6(5a)^2 = 6(25a^2) = 150a^2\).

qs.q: In a table of measurements for a cube (with columns \(S\), \(\text{SA}\), and \(V\)), find the surface area \(\text{SA}\) given that the side length is \(S = 2x\).
qs.s: The surface area of a cube is \(\text{SA} = 6S^2 = 6(2x)^2 = 6(4x^2) = 24x^2\).

qs.q: In a table of measurements for a cube (with columns \(S\), \(\text{SA}\), and \(V\)), find the volume \(V\) given that the side length is \(S = 6y\).
qs.s: The volume of a cube is \(V = S^3 = (6y)^3 = 216y^3\).

qs.q: In a table of measurements for a cube (with columns \(S\), \(\text{SA}\), and \(V\)), find the surface area \(\text{SA}\) given that the volume is \(V = 64k^3\).
qs.s: Since \(V = S^3 = 64k^3\), the side length is \(S = 4k\). The surface area is then \(\text{SA} = 6S^2 = 6(4k)^2 = 96k^2\).

qs.q: In a table of measurements for a cube (with columns \(S\), \(\text{SA}\), and \(V\)), find the surface area \(\text{SA}\) given that the volume is \(V = \frac{1}{27}w^3\).
qs.s: Since \(V = S^3 = \frac{1}{27}w^3\), the side length is \(S = \frac{1}{3}w\). Thus, \(\text{SA} = 6S^2 = 6\left(\frac{1}{3}w\right)^2 = 6\left(\frac{1}{9}w^2\right) = \frac{2}{3}w^2\).

qs.q: In a table of measurements for a cube (with columns \(S\), \(\text{SA}\), and \(V\)), find the surface area \(\text{SA}\) given that the side length is \(S = \frac{2}{3}b\).
qs.s: The surface area is \(\text{SA} = 6S^2 = 6\left(\frac{2}{3}b\right)^2 = 6\left(\frac{4}{9}b^2\right) = \frac{8}{3}b^2\).

qs.q: In a table of measurements for a cube (with columns \(S\), \(\text{SA}\), and \(V\)), find the volume \(V\) given that the surface area is \(\text{SA} = 150x^2\).
qs.s: Since \(\text{SA} = 6S^2 = 150x^2\), the side length is \(S = \sqrt{25x^2} = 5x\). The volume is then \(V = S^3 = (5x)^3 = 125x^3\).

qs.q: In a table of measurements for a cube (with columns \(S\), \(\text{SA}\), and \(V\)), find the volume \(V\) given that the side length is \(S = 2n^2\).
qs.s: The volume of the cube is \(V = S^3 = (2n^2)^3 = 2^3 \cdot (n^2)^3 = 8n^6\).

exercises.name: Volume of a right prism from a diagram

qs.q: Find the volume of the right triangular prism shown in the figure.
qs.s: The base is a right triangle with an area of B = (1/2) × 6 cm × 4 cm = 12 cm². The volume of the prism is V = B × h = 12 cm² × 9 cm = 108 cm³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the right trapezoidal prism shown in the figure.
qs.s: The area of the trapezoidal base is B = ((10 cm + 6 cm) / 2) × 4 cm = 32 cm². The volume of the prism is V = B × h = 32 cm² × 8 cm = 256 cm³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the right rectangular prism shown in the figure.
qs.s: The area of the rectangular base is B = 7 m × 5 m = 35 m². The volume of the prism is V = B × h = 35 m² × 4 m = 140 m³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the right prism with a parallelogram base shown in the figure.
qs.s: The area of the parallelogram base is B = base × height = 9 m × 5 m = 45 m² (the slant side length of 6 m is not the perpendicular height). The volume is V = B × h = 45 m² × 14 m = 630 m³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the right prism shown in the figure.
qs.s: The pentagonal base consists of a rectangle and a triangle: B = (8 m × 5 m) + (1/2 × 8 m × 3 m) = 40 m² + 12 m² = 52 m². The volume of the prism is V = 52 m² × 12 m = 624 m³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the right L-shaped prism shown in the figure.
qs.s: Partition the L-shaped base into two rectangles: a vertical rectangle of 2 cm × 7 cm = 14 cm² and a horizontal rectangle of (6 - 2) cm × 3 cm = 12 cm², giving a base area of B = 26 cm². The volume is V = 26 cm² × 10 cm = 260 cm³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the right prism shown in the diagram.
qs.s: The base is a right triangle with base 9 m and height 4 m, so B = (1/2) × 9 m × 4 m = 18 m². Thus, the volume is V = 18 m² × 11 m = 198 m³.

qs.q: Use the diagram to find the volume of the right triangular prism.
qs.s: The base is a right triangle with area B = (1/2) × 6 cm × 8 cm = 24 cm². Multiplying by the prism length gives V = 24 cm² × 10 cm = 240 cm³.

qs.q: Use the dimensions in the diagram to find the volume of the triangular right prism.
qs.s: The triangular base has an area of B = (1/2) × 8 cm × 5 cm = 20 cm². The volume is V = B × h = 20 cm² × 12 cm = 240 cm³.

qs.q: Calculate the volume of the right trapezoidal prism shown in the diagram.
qs.s: The area of the trapezoidal base is B = ((8 + 4) / 2) × 5 = 30 cm². Multiplying by the prism length gives V = 30 cm² × 6 cm = 180 cm³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the rectangular right prism shown in the diagram.
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is given by V = l × w × h = 7 cm × 4 cm × 5 cm = 140 cm³.

qs.q: Find the volume of the L-shaped right prism shown in the diagram.
qs.s: Split the base into two rectangles: a 3 cm × 7 cm vertical section and a 3 cm × 3 cm horizontal section, giving B = 21 + 9 = 30 cm². The volume is V = 30 cm² × 8 cm = 240 cm³.

qs.q: The base of the right prism is an isosceles triangle with sides 10 cm, 10 cm, and 16 cm. Find the volume of the prism.
qs.s: The altitude bisects the 16 cm base into two 8 cm segments. The height is √(10² - 8²) = 6 cm. The base area is (1/2) × 16 cm × 6 cm = 48 cm², so V = 48 cm² × 18 cm = 864 cm³.

qs.q: The base of the right prism is an isosceles trapezoid. Calculate the volume of the prism.
qs.s: The horizontal leg of each right triangle in the trapezoid is (14 - 8) / 2 = 3 cm, giving height h = √(5² - 3²) = 4 cm. The base area is ((14 + 8) / 2) × 4 = 44 cm², so V = 44 cm² × 15 cm = 660 cm³.

qs.q: The diagram shows a house-shaped right prism consisting of a rectangular body and a triangular roof. Calculate its volume.
qs.s: The base area is the sum of the rectangle (8 m × 5 m = 40 m²) and the triangle ((1/2) × 8 m × 3 m = 12 m²), which is 52 m². The volume is V = 52 m² × 10 m = 520 m³.

qs.q: Use the diagram to calculate the volume of the right triangular prism.
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean theorem on the base triangle, the missing leg is √(13² - 5²) = 12 cm. The base area is (1/2) × 5 cm × 12 cm = 30 cm², so V = 30 cm² × 14 cm = 420 cm³.

exercises.name: Weight of an object from proportional volume

qs.q: A marble slab with dimensions 50 cm, 30 cm, and 20 cm weighs 81.0 kg. A second slab made of the same marble has dimensions 40 cm, 25 cm, and 24 cm. What does the second piece weigh?
qs.s: The first slab has a volume of \(50 \times 30 \times 20 = 30{,}000\text{ cm}^3\) and the second has a volume of \(40 \times 25 \times 24 = 24{,}000\text{ cm}^3\). The second slab weighs \(81.0 \times \frac{24{,}000}{30{,}000} = 64.8\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A copper block with dimensions 12 cm, 8 cm, and 5 cm weighs 4.08 kg. A second copper block made of the same alloy has dimensions 15 cm, 10 cm, and 4 cm. What does the second piece weigh?
qs.s: The first block has a volume of \(12 \times 8 \times 5 = 480\text{ cm}^3\) and the second has a volume of \(15 \times 10 \times 4 = 600\text{ cm}^3\). The second block weighs \(4.08 \times \frac{600}{480} = 5.10\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: An acrylic block with dimensions 20 cm, 15 cm, and 12 cm weighs 2.70 kg. A second acrylic block made of the same material has dimensions 16 cm, 15 cm, and 10 cm. What does the second piece weigh?
qs.s: The first block's volume is \(20 \times 15 \times 12 = 3600\text{ cm}^3\) and the second block's volume is \(16 \times 15 \times 10 = 2400\text{ cm}^3\). The second block weighs \(2.70 \times \frac{2400}{3600} = 1.80\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A block of stone with dimensions 25 cm, 16 cm, and 10 cm weighs 5.60 kg. A second block made of the same stone has dimensions 20 cm, 12 cm, and 15 cm. What does the second piece weigh?
qs.s: The volume of the first block is \(25 \times 16 \times 10 = 4000\text{ cm}^3\) and the second is \(20 \times 12 \times 15 = 3600\text{ cm}^3\). The second block weighs \(5.60 \times \frac{3600}{4000} = 5.04\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A steel bar with dimensions 40 cm, 15 cm, and 10 cm weighs 7.20 kg. A second steel bar made of the same steel has dimensions 25 cm, 20 cm, and 18 cm. What does the second piece weigh?
qs.s: The volume of the first bar is \(40 \times 15 \times 10 = 6000\text{ cm}^3\) and the second is \(25 \times 20 \times 18 = 9000\text{ cm}^3\). Since weight is proportional to volume, the second bar weighs \(7.20 \times \frac{9000}{6000} = 10.80\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A stone block in the shape of a rectangular prism with dimensions 30 cm by 20 cm by 15 cm weighs 21.6 kg. A second stone block made of the same material is a right trapezoidal prism with a length of 40 cm. The trapezoidal base has parallel sides of lengths 12 cm and 18 cm, and a perpendicular distance of 10 cm between them. What does the second stone block weigh?
qs.s: The volume of the rectangular block is \(30 \times 20 \times 15 = 9000\text{ cm}^3\), and the volume of the trapezoidal prism is \(\frac{1}{2}(12 + 18)(10) \times 40 = 6000\text{ cm}^3\). The second block weighs \(21.6 \times \frac{6000}{9000} = 14.4\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A block of cast iron measuring 50 cm by 30 cm by 20 cm weighs 216 kg. A manufacturer casts 15 identical smaller machine parts from the same iron, each in the shape of a prism with a right triangular base of legs 8 cm and 5 cm, and a height of 12 cm. What is the total weight of the 15 machine parts?
qs.s: The large block has volume \(50 \times 30 \times 20 = 30{,}000\text{ cm}^3\). The 15 parts have total volume \(15 \times (\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 \times 12) = 3600\text{ cm}^3\), so their total weight is \(216 \times \frac{3600}{30{,}000} = 25.92\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A solid metal rectangular prism with dimensions 24 cm by 15 cm by 10 cm weighs 8.64 kg. A second solid piece made of the same metal is a right triangular prism whose base is a right triangle with legs 18 cm and 20 cm, and whose length is 25 cm. What does the second piece weigh?
qs.s: The volume of the rectangular prism is \(24 \times 15 \times 10 = 3600\text{ cm}^3\), and the volume of the triangular prism is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 20 \times 25 = 4500\text{ cm}^3\). The second piece weighs \(8.64 \times \frac{4500}{3600} = 10.80\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A solid brass rectangular block with dimensions 40 cm by 25 cm by 20 cm weighs 54.0 kg. A hollow sleeve made of the same brass has the same outer dimensions of 40 cm by 25 cm by 20 cm, but has an inner rectangular hole of 15 cm by 10 cm running all the way through its 40 cm length. What does the hollow sleeve weigh?
qs.s: The volume of the solid block is \(40 \times 25 \times 20 = 20{,}000\text{ cm}^3\). The hollow sleeve has volume \(20{,}000 - (15 \times 10 \times 40) = 14{,}000\text{ cm}^3\), so it weighs \(54.0 \times \frac{14{,}000}{20{,}000} = 37.8\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A solid oak beam with dimensions 1.5 m by 20 cm by 12 cm weighs 25.2 kg. A second wooden block from the same oak is a 50 cm long prism whose base is an L-shape formed by cutting a 6 cm by 5 cm rectangle out of the corner of a 14 cm by 10 cm rectangle. What does the second block weigh?
qs.s: Converting the beam's length gives \(150\text{ cm}\), so its volume is \(150 \times 20 \times 12 = 36{,}000\text{ cm}^3\). The second prism's base area is \((14 \times 10) - (6 \times 5) = 110\text{ cm}^2\) and its volume is \(110 \times 50 = 5500\text{ cm}^3\), so it weighs \(25.2 \times \frac{5500}{36{,}000} = 3.85\text{ kg}\).

exercises.name: Cost based on rectangular prism volume

qs.q: A rectangular foundation measuring 25 m by 16 m has cement poured to a thickness of 12 cm. If cement costs $110 per cubic metre, what is the total cost of the cement?
qs.s: The volume of cement is \(25 \text{ m} \times 16 \text{ m} \times 0.12 \text{ m} = 48 \text{ m}^3\). The total cost is \(48 \times \$110 = \$5280\).

qs.q: A rectangular concrete patio measuring 12 m by 5 m is poured to a thickness of 10 cm. If concrete costs $95 per cubic metre, how much will the concrete cost?
qs.s: The volume of the concrete is \(12 \text{ m} \times 5 \text{ m} \times 0.10 \text{ m} = 6 \text{ m}^3\). Multiplying by the cost per cubic metre gives \(6 \times \$95 = \$570\).

qs.q: A rectangular garden bed measuring 15 m by 4 m is covered with topsoil to a depth of 8 cm. If topsoil costs $45 per cubic metre, what will the topsoil cost?
qs.s: The volume of topsoil is \(15 \text{ m} \times 4 \text{ m} \times 0.08 \text{ m} = 4.8 \text{ m}^3\). The cost is \(4.8 \times \$45 = \$216\).

qs.q: A rectangular parking pad measuring 10 m by 8 m is filled with crushed gravel to a depth of 15 cm. If crushed gravel costs $36 per cubic metre, how much will the gravel cost?
qs.s: The volume of gravel needed is \(10 \text{ m} \times 8 \text{ m} \times 0.15 \text{ m} = 12 \text{ m}^3\). The cost is \(12 \times \$36 = \$432\).

qs.q: A rectangular driveway measuring 20 m by 6 m is paved with asphalt to a thickness of 5 cm. If asphalt costs $80 per cubic metre, what is the total cost of the asphalt?
qs.s: The volume is \(20 \text{ m} \times 6 \text{ m} \times 0.05 \text{ m} = 6 \text{ m}^3\). The total cost is \(6 \times \$80 = \$480\).

qs.q: A contractor preparing a rectangular slab measuring 24 m by 15 m considers two options: a thickness of 8 cm at $120 per cubic metre, or a thickness of 10 cm using a mix costing $92 per cubic metre. How much money is saved by choosing the cheaper option?
qs.s: The base area is \(24 \times 15 = 360 \text{ m}^2\). The 8 cm option costs \(360 \times 0.08 \times 120 = \$3456\), while the 10 cm option costs \(360 \times 0.10 \times 92 = \$3312\), saving \(\$3456 - \$3312 = \$144\).

qs.q: A concrete walkway 2 m wide is poured around a rectangular swimming pool measuring 12 m by 6 m. The walkway is poured to a thickness of 10 cm. If concrete costs $115 per cubic metre, what is the total cost of the concrete?
qs.s: The outer dimensions are \(16 \text{ m} \times 10 \text{ m} = 160 \text{ m}^2\), so the walkway area is \(160 - (12 \times 6) = 88 \text{ m}^2\). The volume is \(88 \times 0.10 = 8.8 \text{ m}^3\), giving a total cost of \(8.8 \times \$115 = \$1012\).

qs.q: A rectangular driveway measuring 18 m by 5 m is constructed with a 10 cm layer of crushed gravel topped with an 8 cm layer of concrete. If crushed gravel costs $35 per cubic metre and concrete costs $125 per cubic metre, what is the total cost of these materials?
qs.s: The base area is \(18 \times 5 = 90 \text{ m}^2\). Gravel costs \(90 \times 0.10 \times \$35 = \$315\) and concrete costs \(90 \times 0.08 \times \$125 = \$900\), for a total cost of \(\$315 + \$900 = \$1215\).

qs.q: An L-shaped concrete patio has an overall length of 14 m and width of 10 m, with a rectangular corner section measuring 6 m by 4 m removed. Concrete is poured to a thickness of 15 cm. If concrete costs $120 per cubic metre, how much will the concrete cost?
qs.s: The base area is \((14 \times 10) - (6 \times 4) = 140 - 24 = 116 \text{ m}^2\), giving a volume of \(116 \times 0.15 = 17.4 \text{ m}^3\). The cost is \(17.4 \times \$120 = \$2088\).

qs.q: A drainage trench is shaped like a right prism whose cross-section is a trapezoid. The trapezoid has parallel bases of 2.5 m and 1.5 m and a height of 1.2 m. If the trench is 40 m long and filled completely with gravel costing $42 per cubic metre, what is the total cost of the gravel?
qs.s: The base area of the trapezoid is \(\frac{2.5 + 1.5}{2} \times 1.2 = 2.4 \text{ m}^2\), so the volume is \(2.4 \times 40 = 96 \text{ m}^3\). The total cost is \(96 \times \$42 = \$4032\).

exercises.name: Dimensions of a rectangular solid from volume relations

qs.q: The length of a rectangular solid is six times its width, and its height is three times its width. If the volume of the solid is \(144\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the solid?
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width. The volume is \(V = (6w)(w)(3w) = 18w^3 = 144\), which simplifies to \(w^3 = 8\) and \(w = 2\text{ cm}\), so the height is \(3w = 3(2) = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular solid is three times its height, and its width is twice its height. If the volume of the solid is \(750\text{ cm}^3\), what is the width of the solid?
qs.s: Let \(h\) be the height. The volume is \(V = (3h)(2h)(h) = 6h^3 = 750\), so \(h^3 = 125\) and \(h = 5\text{ cm}\), meaning the width is \(2h = 2(5) = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular solid is twice its width, and its height is equal to its width. If the volume of the solid is \(128\text{ cm}^3\), what is the length of the solid?
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width. The volume is \(V = (2w)(w)(w) = 2w^3 = 128\), giving \(w^3 = 64\) and \(w = 4\text{ cm}\), so the length is \(2w = 2(4) = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular solid is twice its width, and its height is five times its width. If the volume of the solid is \(270\text{ cm}^3\), what is the length of the solid?
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width. The volume is \(V = (2w)(w)(5w) = 10w^3 = 270\), which gives \(w^3 = 27\) and \(w = 3\text{ cm}\), so the length is \(2w = 2(3) = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular solid is five times its width, and its height is twice its width. If the volume of the solid is \(640\text{ cm}^3\), what is the width of the solid?
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width. The volume is \(V = (5w)(w)(2w) = 10w^3 = 640\), which simplifies to \(w^3 = 64\) and gives \(w = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The width of a rectangular solid is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of its length, and its height is \(\frac{1}{2}\) of its width. If the volume of the solid is \(1296\text{ cm}^3\), what is the length of the solid?
qs.s: Letting \(h\) be the height, width is \(2h\) and length is \(3h\). The volume is \(V = (3h)(2h)(h) = 6h^3 = 1296\), yielding \(h^3 = 216\), \(h = 6\text{ cm}\), and length \(l = 3(6) = 18\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular solid is \(2.5\) times its width, and its height is \(1.2\) times its length. If the volume of the solid is \(60{,}000\text{ cm}^3\), what is the length of the solid?
qs.s: Expressing dimensions via width \(w\), length is \(2.5w\) and height is \(1.2(2.5w) = 3w\). The volume is \(V = w(2.5w)(3w) = 7.5w^3 = 60{,}000\), which gives \(w^3 = 8000\), \(w = 20\text{ cm}\), and length \(l = 2.5(20) = 50\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular solid is \(1.5\) times its width, and its height is \(4\) times its length. If the volume of the solid is \(72{,}000\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the solid?
qs.s: In terms of the width \(w\), length is \(1.5w\) and height is \(4(1.5w) = 6w\). The volume is \(V = w(1.5w)(6w) = 9w^3 = 72{,}000\), giving \(w^3 = 8000\), so \(w = 20\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 6(20) = 120\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length, width, and height of a rectangular solid are in the ratio \(4 : 3 : 2\). If the volume of the solid is \(3000\text{ cm}^3\), what is the sum of its three dimensions?
qs.s: Let the dimensions be \(4x\), \(3x\), and \(2x\). The volume is \((4x)(3x)(2x) = 24x^3 = 3000\), so \(x^3 = 125\) and \(x = 5\text{ cm}\), making the sum of dimensions \(4(5) + 3(5) + 2(5) = 20 + 15 + 10 = 45\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The base of a rectangular solid has a length that is four times its width. The height of the solid is twice its width. If the volume of the solid is \(1728\text{ cm}^3\), what is the area of the base of the solid?
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width, so length is \(4w\) and height is \(2w\). Then \(V = (4w)(w)(2w) = 8w^3 = 1728\), giving \(w^3 = 216\) and \(w = 6\text{ cm}\), which means the base area is \((4w)(w) = 24 \times 6 = 144\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A decorative stone is submerged in a rectangular glass tank that has a base measuring \(40\text{ cm}\) by \(25\text{ cm}\). If the stone causes the water level to rise by \(2\text{ cm}\), what is the volume of the stone?
qs.s: The volume of the stone equals the volume of the displaced water: \(\text{Volume} = 40\text{ cm} \times 25\text{ cm} \times 2\text{ cm} = 2000\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A ceramic figurine is submerged in a rectangular tank measuring \(30\text{ cm}\) by \(10\text{ cm}\). The figurine causes the water to rise by \(5\text{ cm}\). What is the volume of the figurine?
qs.s: The volume of the submerged figurine is \(\text{Base Area} \times \text{Rise} = (30\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm}) \times 5\text{ cm} = 1500\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A heavy iron weight is placed in a rectangular aquarium with a base of \(45\text{ cm}\) by \(20\text{ cm}\). If the weight completely sinks and raises the water level by \(6\text{ cm}\), what is the volume of the iron weight?
qs.s: The volume of the weight equals the volume of the displaced rectangular prism of water: \(45\text{ cm} \times 20\text{ cm} \times 6\text{ cm} = 5400\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A solid metal part is placed into a rectangular container measuring \(20\text{ cm}\) long and \(15\text{ cm}\) wide. If this causes the water level to rise by \(4\text{ cm}\), what is the volume of the metal part?
qs.s: The volume of the displaced water is found by multiplying the base area by the rise in water level: \(20\text{ cm} \times 15\text{ cm} \times 4\text{ cm} = 1200\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A solid brick is lowered into a rectangular trough with a base of \(60\text{ cm}\) by \(20\text{ cm}\). The water level increases by \(1.5\text{ cm}\). What is the volume of the brick?
qs.s: The volume of the brick is equal to the displaced volume of water: \(60\text{ cm} \times 20\text{ cm} \times 1.5\text{ cm} = 1800\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular tank with a base of \(60\text{ cm}\) by \(45\text{ cm}\) is filled with water to a depth of \(28\text{ cm}\). The tank itself has a total height of \(30\text{ cm}\). When a statue is lowered into the tank, the water level rises to the top brim and an additional \(1800\text{ cm}^3\) of water spills over the edge. What is the total volume of the statue?
qs.s: The volume needed to reach the brim is \(60 \times 45 \times (30 - 28) = 5400\text{ cm}^3\). Adding the \(1800\text{ cm}^3\) that overflowed gives a total statue volume of \(5400 + 1800 = 7200\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular container has a base measuring \(48\text{ cm}\) by \(25\text{ cm}\). When 5 identical lead weights are fully submerged in the water, the water level increases from \(15.2\text{ cm}\) to \(18.7\text{ cm}\). What is the volume of a single lead weight?
qs.s: The rise in height is \(18.7 - 15.2 = 3.5\text{ cm}\), giving a total displaced volume of \(48 \times 25 \times 3.5 = 4200\text{ cm}^3\). Dividing by 5 yields \(840\text{ cm}^3\) per weight.

qs.q: Eight identical solid metal spheres are completely submerged in a rectangular tank measuring \(40\text{ cm}\) by \(30\text{ cm}\). If the water level rises by \(6\text{ cm}\), what is the volume of ONE metal sphere?
qs.s: The total displaced volume for all 8 spheres is \(40 \times 30 \times 6 = 7200\text{ cm}^3\), so the volume of one sphere is \(7200 \div 8 = 900\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A machine part is submerged into a rectangular tank with a base of \(35\text{ cm}\) by \(24\text{ cm}\). Before the part is placed inside, the water depth is \(12.5\text{ cm}\), and after it is fully submerged, the water depth is \(16.5\text{ cm}\). What is the volume of the machine part?
qs.s: The rise in water level is \(16.5\text{ cm} - 12.5\text{ cm} = 4\text{ cm}\). The volume of the part is the displaced volume: \(35\text{ cm} \times 24\text{ cm} \times 4\text{ cm} = 3360\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular tank has a base of \(50\text{ cm}\) by \(40\text{ cm}\). Submerging a rock causes the water level to rise by \(2.5\text{ cm}\). When a metal sculpture is also submerged into the tank, the water rises an additional \(4\text{ cm}\). How much greater is the volume of the sculpture than the volume of the rock?
qs.s: The difference in water rise caused by the sculpture compared to the rock is \(4\text{ cm} - 2.5\text{ cm} = 1.5\text{ cm}\). Thus, the sculpture's volume is greater by \(50 \times 40 \times 1.5 = 3000\text{ cm}^3\).

exercises.name: Height of a triangular prism from volume

qs.q: A concrete block is in the shape of an isosceles right triangular prism where the legs of the base equal the height. If the volume of the block is \(13.5\text{ m}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Setting the volume formula \(\frac{1}{2}h^3 = 13.5\) gives \(h^3 = 27\), so the height is \(h = 3\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A wooden wedge is shaped as an isosceles right triangular prism whose base legs are equal to its height. If the volume of the wedge is \(256\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Since the base legs equal the height, \(V = \frac{1}{2}h^3\). Setting \(\frac{1}{2}h^3 = 256\) gives \(h^3 = 512\), so \(h = \sqrt[3]{512} = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A decorative glass trophy is crafted as an isosceles right triangular prism whose base legs are equal in length to its height. If its volume is \(62.5\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(\frac{1}{2}h^3 = 62.5\), which simplifies to \(h^3 = 125\), giving a height of \(h = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The base of an isosceles right triangular prism has legs equal to its height. If the volume of the prism is \(500\text{ mm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Using the volume formula \(V = \frac{1}{2}h^3\), we set \(\frac{1}{2}h^3 = 500\), which gives \(h^3 = 1000\) and \(h = 10\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: The base of an isosceles right triangular prism has legs equal to its height. If the volume of the prism is \(32\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: The volume of the prism is \(V = \frac{1}{2}h^2 \times h = \frac{1}{2}h^3\). Setting \(\frac{1}{2}h^3 = 32\) gives \(h^3 = 64\), so \(h = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The legs of the base of an isosceles right triangular prism are each twice its height. If the volume of the prism is \(432\text{ m}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Let the height be \(h\text{ m}\), so each leg of the base is \(2h\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{1}{2}(2h)^2(h) = 2h^3 = 432\), giving \(h^3 = 216\) and \(h = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The height of an isosceles right triangular prism is 4 times the length of each leg of its base. If the volume of the prism is \(250\text{ mm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Let each leg be \(x\text{ mm}\), so the height is \(h = 4x\text{ mm}\). Then \(V = \frac{1}{2}x^2(4x) = 2x^3 = 250\), giving \(x^3 = 125\), so \(x = 5\text{ mm}\) and \(h = 4(5) = 20\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: Each leg of the base of an isosceles right triangular prism is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the height of the prism. If the volume of the prism is \(162\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Let the height be \(h\text{ cm}\), so each leg is \(\frac{2}{3}h\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2}{3}h\right)^2(h) = \frac{2}{9}h^3 = 162\), which yields \(h^3 = 729\) and \(h = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The height of an isosceles right triangular prism is 3 times the length of each leg of its base. If the volume of the prism is \(96\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Let each leg be \(x\text{ cm}\), so the height is \(h = 3x\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{1}{2}x^2(3x) = \frac{3}{2}x^3 = 96\), which gives \(x^3 = 64\), so \(x = 4\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 3(4) = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The height of an isosceles right triangular prism is twice the length of each leg of its base. If the volume of the prism is \(125\text{ cm}^3\), what is the height of the prism?
qs.s: Let each leg be \(x\text{ cm}\), so the height is \(h = 2x\text{ cm}\). Then \(V = \frac{1}{2}x^2(2x) = x^3 = 125\), which gives \(x = 5\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 2(5) = 10\text{ cm}\).

exercises.name: Volume of subdivided sections of a rectangular solid

qs.q: A rectangular solid is cut into six pieces as shown. What is the volume of the middle-left piece labeled E?
qs.s: Piece E has a length of 7 cm, a height of 4 cm, and a depth of 8 cm. Its volume is V = 7 cm × 4 cm × 8 cm = 224 cm³.

qs.q: A rectangular solid is sliced into six pieces as shown. Use the diagram to find the volume of piece B.
qs.s: Piece B has a length of 3 m, a height of 3 m, and a depth of 5 m. Its volume is V = 3 m × 3 m × 5 m = 45 m³.

qs.q: The rectangular block shown is divided into six smaller prisms. Find the volume of piece D, located in the upper-right corner.
qs.s: Piece D has a length of 3 in, a height of 3 in, and a depth of 4 in. Its volume is V = 3 in × 3 in × 4 in = 36 in³.

qs.q: The rectangular solid shown is cut into six pieces. What is the volume of the shaded front piece labeled C?
qs.s: Piece C has a length of 4 cm, a height of 5 cm, and a depth of 2 cm. Its volume is V = 4 cm × 5 cm × 2 cm = 40 cm³.

qs.q: The rectangular solid shown is divided into six smaller rectangular prisms. Use the diagram to find the volume of the shaded piece A.
qs.s: Piece A has a length of 5 cm, a height of 4 cm, and a depth of 6 cm. Its volume is V = 5 cm × 4 cm × 6 cm = 120 cm³.

qs.q: A rectangular block is divided into 12 smaller rectangular prisms by planes parallel to its faces, as shown. What is the volume of the shaded piece P located at the front-bottom-center?
qs.s: Piece P has a length of 3 cm, a height of 6 cm, and a depth of 4 cm. Its volume is V = 3 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm = 72 cm³.

qs.q: A rectangular marble block is sliced into six sections. The shaded corner piece labeled Discarded is removed. What is the remaining volume of the marble block?
qs.s: The total volume is (9 + 6) cm × (4 + 3 + 5) cm × 8 cm = 15 cm × 12 cm × 8 cm = 1440 cm³. The discarded piece has volume 6 cm × 5 cm × 8 cm = 240 cm³. The remaining volume is 1440 cm³ - 240 cm³ = 1200 cm³.

qs.q: Two corner pieces, A (bottom-left) and B (top-right), are removed from the rectangular solid shown. What is the total combined volume of the two removed pieces?
qs.s: Piece A has volume 8 cm × 5 cm × 10 cm = 400 cm³. Piece B has volume 6 cm × 7 cm × 10 cm = 420 cm³. Their combined volume is 400 cm³ + 420 cm³ = 820 cm³.

qs.q: A rectangular wooden block with a total length of 14 cm is cut into eight smaller blocks by three slicing planes, as shown. Find the volume of the shaded block S located at the front-top-right.
qs.s: The length of block S is 14 cm - 6 cm = 8 cm. Its height is 3 cm and its depth is 4 cm. Its volume is V = 8 cm × 3 cm × 4 cm = 96 cm³.

qs.q: The rectangular prism shown is divided into six smaller prisms. What is the difference in volume between the largest piece and the smallest piece?
qs.s: The largest piece has dimensions 4.5 cm × 3.5 cm × 6 cm = 94.5 cm³. The smallest piece has dimensions 2.5 cm × 2.5 cm × 6 cm = 37.5 cm³. The difference is 94.5 cm³ - 37.5 cm³ = 57 cm³.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length and width are both doubled, while its height remains unchanged?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V_{\text{new}} = (2l)(2w)(h) = 4lwh = 4V\), so the volume is multiplied by a factor of 4.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if each of the three dimensions is halved?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V_{\text{new}} = \left(\frac{1}{2}l\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}w\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}h\right) = \frac{1}{8}lwh = \frac{1}{8}V\), so the volume is multiplied by a factor of \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if each of the three dimensions is quadrupled?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V_{\text{new}} = (4l)(4w)(4h) = 64lwh = 64V\), meaning the volume is multiplied by a factor of 64.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if each of the three dimensions is tripled?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V_{\text{new}} = (3l)(3w)(3h) = 27lwh = 27V\), so the volume is multiplied by a factor of 27.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length is doubled, its width is tripled, and its height remains unchanged?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V_{\text{new}} = (2l)(3w)(h) = 6lwh = 6V\), so the volume is multiplied by a factor of 6.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). If its length is multiplied by \(2x\), its width is multiplied by \(3x\), and its height is multiplied by \(5x\), by what factor is its volume multiplied in terms of \(x\)?
qs.s: Multiplying the three dimension factors together gives \((2x)(3x)(5x) = (2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5)(x \cdot x \cdot x) = 30x^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length is multiplied by \(\frac{5}{2}\), its width is halved, and its height is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{5}\)?
qs.s: The volume scale factor is \(\frac{5}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{15}{20}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has an initial volume of \(45\text{ cm}^3\). If its length is doubled, its width is multiplied by 5, and its height is multiplied by 3, what is the new volume of the prism, in cubic centimeters?
qs.s: The overall volume scale factor is \(2 \times 5 \times 3 = 30\). Multiplying the original volume by this factor gives \(45 \times 30 = 1350\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l = 6\text{ cm}\), \(w = 4\text{ cm}\), and \(h = 5\text{ cm}\). If each dimension is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{2}\), by how many cubic centimeters does the volume increase?
qs.s: The original volume is \(6 \times 4 \times 5 = 120\text{ cm}^3\), and the new volume is \(120 \times \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = 120 \times \frac{27}{8} = 405\text{ cm}^3\). The increase in volume is \(405 - 120 = 285\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has length \(l\), width \(w\), and height \(h\). Its length is multiplied by 4, its width is multiplied by 3, and its height is doubled. If the new volume of the prism is \(720\text{ cm}^3\), what was its original volume, in cubic centimeters?
qs.s: The volume changes by a factor of \(4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24\), giving \(24V = 720\text{ cm}^3\). Dividing by 24 gives an original volume of \(V = 30\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does multiplying each dimension by 10 have on its volume?
qs.s: Multiplying each dimension by 10 gives \(V' = (10l)(10w)(10h) = 1000lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 1000.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does doubling each dimension have on its volume?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Doubling each dimension gives \(V' = (2l)(2w)(2h) = 8lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 8.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does halving each dimension have on its volume?
qs.s: Halving each dimension gives \(V' = \left(\frac{1}{2}l\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}w\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}h\right) = \frac{1}{8}lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does multiplying each dimension by 5 have on its volume?
qs.s: Multiplying each dimension by 5 gives \(V' = (5l)(5w)(5h) = 125lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 125.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does quadrupling each dimension have on its volume?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Quadrupling each dimension gives \(V' = (4l)(4w)(4h) = 64lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 64.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does multiplying the length by 6, the width by \(\frac{1}{2}\), and the height by \(\frac{2}{3}\) have on its volume?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = (6l)\left(\frac{1}{2}w\right)\left(\frac{2}{3}h\right) = \left(6 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3}\right)lwh = 2lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 2.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does multiplying the length by \(\frac{3}{4}\), the width by \(\frac{2}{3}\), and the height by \(\frac{1}{2}\) have on its volume?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = \left(\frac{3}{4}l\right)\left(\frac{2}{3}w\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}h\right) = \left(\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{2}\right)lwh = \frac{1}{4}lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does multiplying the length by 5, the width by 6, and the height by 12 have on its volume?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = (5l)(6w)(12h) = (5 \times 6 \times 12)lwh = 360lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 360.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does doubling the length, tripling the width, and quadrupling the height have on its volume?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = (2l)(3w)(4h) = (2 \times 3 \times 4)lwh = 24lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 24.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does multiplying each dimension by \(\frac{2}{3}\) have on its volume?
qs.s: Scaling each dimension by \(\frac{2}{3}\) results in \(V' = \left(\frac{2}{3}l\right)\left(\frac{2}{3}w\right)\left(\frac{2}{3}h\right) = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 lwh = \frac{8}{27}lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{8}{27}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: quadrupling the length and tripling the height?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). If the length is quadrupled and the height is tripled, the new volume is \((4l)(w)(3h) = 12lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 12.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: tripling the length and tripling the width?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). If the length and width are both tripled, the new volume is \((3l)(3w)(h) = 9lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 9.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: multiplying the width by 5 and doubling the length?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). If the length is doubled and the width is multiplied by 5, the new volume is \((2l)(5w)(h) = 10lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 10.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: doubling the length and quadrupling the height?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). With the new dimensions, the volume becomes \((2l)(w)(4h) = 8lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 8.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: doubling the length and doubling the width?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). If the length and width are both doubled, the new volume is \((2l)(2w)(h) = 4lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 4.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: halving the length, halving the width, and tripling the height?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Scaling the dimensions gives \((\frac{1}{2}l)(\frac{1}{2}w)(3h) = \frac{3}{4}lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 3/4.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: multiplying the length by 12, halving the width, and dividing the height by 3?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Scaling the dimensions gives \((12l)(\frac{1}{2}w)(\frac{1}{3}h) = 2lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 2.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: multiplying the length by 6, multiplying the width by 5, and halving the height?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Scaling the dimensions gives \((6l)(5w)(\frac{1}{2}h) = 15lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 15.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: doubling the length, tripling the width, and quadrupling the height?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Scaling all three dimensions gives \((2l)(3w)(4h) = 24lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 24.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). What effect does the following condition have on its volume: tripling the length, tripling the width, and tripling the height?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). Tripling each dimension gives \((3l)(3w)(3h) = 27lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by 27.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length, width, and height are all halved?
qs.s: The new volume is \(\left(\frac{1}{2}l\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}w\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}h\right) = \frac{1}{8}lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length is doubled and its width is tripled, while its height remains unchanged?
qs.s: The new volume is \((2l)(3w)(h) = 6lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by a factor of \(6\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its width is halved and its height is reduced to one-third of its original value, while its length remains unchanged?
qs.s: The new volume is \((l)\left(\frac{1}{2}w\right)\left(\frac{1}{3}h\right) = \frac{1}{6}lwh\), which multiplies the original volume by \(\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length, width, and height are all doubled?
qs.s: The new volume is \((2l)(2w)(2h) = 8lwh\), which means the volume is multiplied by \(8\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length is halved and its height is quadrupled, while its width remains unchanged?
qs.s: The new volume is \(\left(\frac{1}{2}l\right)(w)(4h) = 2lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by \(2\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). If the length is multiplied by \(8\) and the width is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{4}\), by what factor must the height be multiplied so that the new volume is \(3\) times the original volume?
qs.s: The product of the scale factors for length and width is \(8 \times \frac{3}{4} = 6\). For the volume to scale by \(3\), the height factor \(k\) must satisfy \(6k = 3\), so \(k = \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: A rectangular box has an initial volume of \(144\text{ cm}^3\). If its length is doubled, its width is tripled, and its height is reduced to one-fourth of its original size, by how many cubic centimeters does the volume increase?
qs.s: The volume scaling factor is \(2 \times 3 \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\), making the new volume \(144 \times \frac{3}{2} = 216\text{ cm}^3\). The increase is \(216 - 144 = 72\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has an initial volume of \(450\text{ cm}^3\). If its length is multiplied by \(4\), its width is divided by \(3\), and its height is halved, what is the new volume of the prism?
qs.s: The volume scale factor is \(4 \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{3}\). Multiplying the initial volume gives \(450\text{ cm}^3 \times \frac{2}{3} = 300\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length is multiplied by \(\frac{4}{3}\), its width is multiplied by \(\frac{9}{8}\), and its height is multiplied by \(\frac{2}{5}\)?
qs.s: Multiplying the scale factors gives \(\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{9}{8} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{72}{120} = \frac{3}{5}\), so the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has a square base of side length \(s\) and a height of \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if the side length of the square base is tripled and the height is divided by \(6\)?
qs.s: Tripling the side length multiplies the base area by \(3^2 = 9\). Combining this with the height factor gives \(9 \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if the length is quadrupled, the width is divided by 3, and the height is halved?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = (4l)\left(\frac{1}{3}w\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}h\right) = \left(4 \cdot \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\right)lwh = \frac{2}{3}V\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if the length is tripled, the width is doubled, and the height is divided by 4?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = (3l)(2w)\left(\frac{1}{4}h\right) = \left(3 \cdot 2 \cdot \frac{1}{4}\right)lwh = \frac{3}{2}V\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if the length is halved, the width is halved, and the height is quadrupled?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = \left(\frac{1}{2}l\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}w\right)(4h) = \left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot 4\right)lwh = 1V\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 1.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if the length is doubled, the width is doubled, and the height is halved?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = (2l)(2w)\left(\frac{1}{2}h\right) = \left(2 \cdot 2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\right)lwh = 2V\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 2.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if the length is quadrupled, the width is tripled, and the height is halved?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = (4l)(3w)\left(\frac{1}{2}h\right) = \left(4 \cdot 3 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\right)lwh = 6V\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by 6.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). If the length is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{4}\) and the width is multiplied by \(\frac{8}{5}\), by what factor must the height be multiplied so that the volume is doubled?
qs.s: Let \(k\) be the scale factor for the height. Setting \(\left(\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{8}{5} \cdot k\right)V = 2V\) gives \(\frac{6}{5}k = 2\), so \(k = 2 \cdot \frac{5}{6} = \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). If the length is tripled and the width is halved, by what factor must the height be multiplied so that the volume is multiplied by 6?
qs.s: Let \(k\) be the scale factor for the height. Then \(\left(3 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot k\right)V = 6V\), which simplifies to \(\frac{3}{2}k = 6\), giving \(k = 6 \cdot \frac{2}{3} = 4\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has a length of \(5\text{ cm}\), a width of \(4\text{ cm}\), and a height of \(3\text{ cm}\). If the length is doubled, the width is tripled, and the height is halved, by how many cubic centimeters does the volume increase?
qs.s: The original volume is \(V = 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 = 60\text{ cm}^3\), and the new volume is \(V' = (2 \cdot 5)(3 \cdot 4)\left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot 3\right) = 180\text{ cm}^3\). The increase in volume is \(180 - 60 = 120\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if its length is multiplied by \(\frac{4}{3}\), its width is multiplied by \(\frac{5}{6}\), and its height is multiplied by \(\frac{9}{8}\)?
qs.s: The new volume is \(V' = \left(\frac{4}{3}l\right)\left(\frac{5}{6}w\right)\left(\frac{9}{8}h\right) = \left(\frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{9}{8}\right)lwh = \frac{5}{4}lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of \(108\text{ cm}^3\). If its length is doubled, its width is divided by 4, and its height is multiplied by \(\frac{5}{3}\), what is its new volume in cubic centimeters?
qs.s: The overall scale factor for the volume is \(2 \cdot \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{5}{3} = \frac{5}{6}\). The new volume is \(108 \cdot \frac{5}{6} = 90\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). If each dimension is multiplied by a factor of \(k\), by what factor is the volume multiplied?
qs.s: Multiplying each dimension by \(k\) gives \((kl)(kw)(kh) = k^3lwh\). Hence, the volume is multiplied by a factor of \(k^3\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if each dimension is multiplied by \(\frac{1}{2}\)?
qs.s: Multiplying each dimension by \(\frac{1}{2}\) gives a new volume of \((\frac{1}{2}l)(\frac{1}{2}w)(\frac{1}{2}h) = \frac{1}{8}lwh\). Thus, the volume is multiplied by a factor of \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if each dimension is multiplied by \(\frac{2}{3}\)?
qs.s: Scaling each dimension by \(\frac{2}{3}\) results in a volume of \((\frac{2}{3}l)(\frac{2}{3}w)(\frac{2}{3}h) = \frac{8}{27}lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by \(\frac{8}{27}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if each dimension is doubled?
qs.s: The volume of a rectangular prism is \(V = lwh\). When each dimension is multiplied by 2, the new volume is \((2l)(2w)(2h) = 8lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by a factor of 8.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). By what factor is its volume multiplied if each dimension is multiplied by 5?
qs.s: When each dimension is multiplied by 5, the new volume is \((5l)(5w)(5h) = 125lwh\). Therefore, the volume is multiplied by a factor of 125.

qs.q: Each dimension of a rectangular prism is multiplied by the same scale factor \(k\). If the volume of the prism increases from \(15\text{ cm}^3\) to \(960\text{ cm}^3\), what is the value of \(k\)?
qs.s: Multiplying each dimension by \(k\) scales the volume by \(k^3\), so \(15k^3 = 960\), which gives \(k^3 = 64\) and therefore \(k = 4\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of \(48\text{ cm}^3\). If its length is doubled, its width is tripled, and its height is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{4}\), what is the new volume in cubic centimeters?
qs.s: The volume scales by a factor of \(2 \times 3 \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{2}\). Multiplying the original volume gives \(48 \times \frac{9}{2} = 216\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular prism is multiplied by 4, and its width is multiplied by 6. By what factor must its height be multiplied so that the total volume of the prism is multiplied by 8?
qs.s: Let \(k\) be the scale factor for the height; then \(4 \times 6 \times k = 8\), which simplifies to \(24k = 8\), so \(k = \frac{8}{24} = \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). If the length is multiplied by 3, the width is multiplied by 4, and the height is multiplied by \(\frac{1}{2}\), by what factor is the volume multiplied?
qs.s: The new volume is \((3l)(4w)(\frac{1}{2}h) = (3 \times 4 \times \frac{1}{2})lwh = 6lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by a factor of 6.

qs.q: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(l\), \(w\), and \(h\). If the length is multiplied by \(2x\), the width is multiplied by \(3x^2\), and the height is multiplied by \(\frac{4}{x}\), by what factor is the volume multiplied?
qs.s: The new volume is \((2x)(3x^2)(\frac{4}{x})lwh = (2 \times 3 \times 4)(x \cdot x^2 \cdot x^{-1})lwh = 24x^2lwh\), so the volume is multiplied by \(24x^2\).

exercises.name: Surface Area of a Cylinder from Dimensions

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 8\text{ cm}, h = 7\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: First find the radius: \(r = \frac{d}{2} = \frac{8}{2} = 4\text{ cm}\). Then \(SA = 2\pi(4)(7) + 2\pi(4)^2 = 56\pi + 32\pi = 88\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 2\text{ cm}, h = 6\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The surface area is given by \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 2\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 6\text{ cm}\) gives \(SA = 2\pi(2)(6) + 2\pi(2)^2 = 24\pi + 8\pi = 32\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 5\text{ cm}, h = 6\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The surface area is given by \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 5\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 6\text{ cm}\) yields \(SA = 2\pi(5)(6) + 2\pi(5)^2 = 60\pi + 50\pi = 110\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions, rounded to two decimal places: \(r = 4\text{ cm}, h = 5\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(4)(5) + 2\pi(4)^2 = 40\pi + 32\pi = 72\pi\text{ cm}^2\). Using a calculator, \(72\pi \approx 226.19\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions, rounded to two decimal places: \(d = 14\text{ cm}, h = 3\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{14}{2} = 7\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(7)(3) + 2\pi(7)^2 = 42\pi + 98\pi = 140\pi \approx 439.82\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 16\text{ cm}, h = 25\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{16}{2} = 8\text{ cm}\). The exact surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(8)(25) + 2\pi(8)^2 = 400\pi + 128\pi = 528\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area in square centimeters of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 6\text{ cm}, h = 1.5\text{ m}\).
qs.s: First convert the height to centimeters: \(h = 1.5\text{ m} = 150\text{ cm}\). Then \(SA = 2\pi(6)(150) + 2\pi(6)^2 = 1800\pi + 72\pi = 1872\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions, rounded to two decimal places: \(d = 15\text{ cm}, h = 18\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{15}{2} = 7.5\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(7.5)(18) + 2\pi(7.5)^2 = 270\pi + 112.5\pi = 382.5\pi \approx 1201.66\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions, rounded to two decimal places: \(r = 3.5\text{ cm}, h = 8.5\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(3.5)(8.5) + 2\pi(3.5)^2 = 59.5\pi + 24.5\pi = 84\pi\text{ cm}^2\). Evaluating to two decimal places gives \(84\pi \approx 263.89\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area in square centimeters of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 20\text{ cm}, h = 1.2\text{ m}\).
qs.s: Convert the height to centimeters (\(h = 1.2\text{ m} = 120\text{ cm}\)) and find the radius (\(r = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ cm}\)). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(10)(120) + 2\pi(10)^2 = 2400\pi + 200\pi = 2600\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 5\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 9\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The total surface area is \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(5)(9) + 2\pi(5)^2 = 90\pi + 50\pi = 140\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 4\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 6\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Using the formula \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\), substitute \(r = 4\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 6\text{ cm}\) to get \(SA = 2\pi(4)(6) + 2\pi(4)^2 = 48\pi + 32\pi = 80\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 6\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 4\text{ cm}\). Round the answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: Using \(SA = 2\pi(6)(4) + 2\pi(6)^2 = 48\pi + 72\pi = 120\pi\text{ cm}^2\), rounding to two decimal places gives \(120\pi \approx 376.99\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 2\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 10\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(r = 2\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 10\text{ cm}\) into \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\) to find \(SA = 2\pi(2)(10) + 2\pi(2)^2 = 40\pi + 8\pi = 48\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 3\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 8\text{ cm}\). Round the answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: Substitute \(r = 3\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 8\text{ cm}\) into \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\) to get \(SA = 2\pi(3)(8) + 2\pi(3)^2 = 66\pi\text{ cm}^2\). Evaluating gives \(66\pi \approx 207.35\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area, in square centimetres, of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 40\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 1.5\text{ m}\). Round the answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: Convert the dimensions to \(r = 40 / 2 = 20\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 1.5\text{ m} = 150\text{ cm}\), giving \(SA = 2\pi(20)(150) + 2\pi(20^2) = 6800\pi\text{ cm}^2 \approx 21362.83\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area, in square centimetres, of a cylinder with radius \(r = 25\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 1.2\text{ m}\).
qs.s: Convert the height to centimetres: \(h = 1.2\text{ m} = 120\text{ cm}\). Then \(SA = 2\pi(25)(120) + 2\pi(25^2) = 6000\pi + 1250\pi = 7250\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 3.5\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 11.5\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Using the formula \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\), calculate \(SA = 2\pi(3.5)(11.5) + 2\pi(3.5^2) = 80.5\pi + 24.5\pi = 105\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 16\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 15\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: First find the radius \(r = 16 / 2 = 8\text{ cm}\). Then calculate \(SA = 2\pi(8)(15) + 2\pi(8^2) = 240\pi + 128\pi = 368\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 9\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 14.5\text{ cm}\). Round the answer to two decimal places.
Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions. Give the exact answer in terms of \(\pi\). \(d = 6.4\text{ cm}, h = 3.5\text{ cm}\)
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{6.4}{2} = 3.2\text{ cm}\), so the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(3.2)(3.5) + 2\pi(3.2)^2 = 22.4\pi + 20.48\pi = 42.88\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions. Give the exact answer in terms of \(\pi\). \(d = 3.6\text{ cm}, h = 6.5\text{ cm}\)
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{3.6}{2} = 1.8\text{ cm}\), so the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(1.8)(6.5) + 2\pi(1.8)^2 = 23.4\pi + 6.48\pi = 29.88\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions. Give the exact answer in terms of \(\pi\). \(d = 8.6\text{ cm}, h = 4.2\text{ cm}\)
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{8.6}{2} = 4.3\text{ cm}\), so the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(4.3)(4.2) + 2\pi(4.3)^2 = 36.12\pi + 36.98\pi = 73.1\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions. Give the exact answer in terms of \(\pi\). \(d = 7.2\text{ cm}, h = 5.8\text{ cm}\)
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{7.2}{2} = 3.6\text{ cm}\), so the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(3.6)(5.8) + 2\pi(3.6)^2 = 41.76\pi + 25.92\pi = 67.68\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder with the given dimensions. Give the exact answer in terms of \(\pi\). \(d = 4.8\text{ cm}, h = 7.1\text{ cm}\)
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{4.8}{2} = 2.4\text{ cm}\), so the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(2.4)(7.1) + 2\pi(2.4)^2 = 34.08\pi + 11.52\pi = 45.6\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A closed cylinder has a base diameter of \(d = 12\text{ cm}\), and its height is \(2.5\) times its radius. Find the exact surface area of the cylinder in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 6\text{ cm}\) and the height is \(h = 2.5 \times 6 = 15\text{ cm}\), giving \(SA = 2\pi(6)(15) + 2\pi(6)^2 = 180\pi + 72\pi = 252\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: An open-topped cylindrical container (closed at the bottom, open at the top) has a diameter of \(d = 14\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(h = 20\text{ cm}\). Find its exact surface area in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: With \(r = 7\text{ cm}\), the surface area consists of one base plus the side: \(SA = 2\pi(7)(20) + \pi(7)^2 = 280\pi + 49\pi = 329\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A hollow cylindrical metal pipe is \(2\text{ m}\) long, with an inside radius of \(8\text{ cm}\) and an outside radius of \(10\text{ cm}\). Find the exact total surface area of the pipe (inside, outside, and both circular ring ends) in square centimeters in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: With \(h = 200\text{ cm}\), the two ends contribute \(2(\pi \cdot 10^2 - \pi \cdot 8^2) = 72\pi\text{ cm}^2\) and the curved sides contribute \(2\pi(10)(200) + 2\pi(8)(200) = 7200\pi\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total of \(7272\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A closed cylinder has a diameter of \(d = 60\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(h = 1.8\text{ m}\). Find its exact surface area in square centimeters in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Converting the height gives \(h = 180\text{ cm}\) and the radius is \(r = 30\text{ cm}\), so \(SA = 2\pi(30)(180) + 2\pi(30)^2 = 10800\pi + 1800\pi = 12600\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a closed cylinder with diameter \(d = 15.6\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 24.2\text{ cm}\). Give the exact answer in terms of \(\pi\).
Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 1\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 2\frac{1}{4}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Using \(r = \frac{3}{2}\text{ cm}\) and \(h = \frac{9}{4}\text{ cm}\), the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) + 2\pi\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{27}{4}\pi + \frac{9}{2}\pi = \frac{45}{4}\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with radius \(r = 2\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 3\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Using \(r = \frac{7}{3}\text{ cm}\) and \(h = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}\), the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi\left(\frac{7}{3}\right)\left(\frac{7}{2}\right) + 2\pi\left(\frac{7}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{3}\pi + \frac{98}{9}\pi = \frac{245}{9}\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 5\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 2\frac{1}{4}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{8}{3}\text{ cm}\) and \(h = \frac{9}{4}\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) + 2\pi\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)^2 = 12\pi + \frac{128}{9}\pi = \frac{236}{9}\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 2\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 3\frac{1}{5}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{d}{2} = \frac{5}{4}\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)\left(\frac{16}{5}\right) + 2\pi\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2 = 8\pi + \frac{25}{8}\pi = \frac{89}{8}\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 3\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 2\frac{2}{5}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{5}{3}\text{ cm}\) and \(h = \frac{12}{5}\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)\left(\frac{12}{5}\right) + 2\pi\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2 = 8\pi + \frac{50}{9}\pi = \frac{122}{9}\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 8\frac{2}{3}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 4\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{13}{3}\text{ cm}\) and \(h = \frac{9}{2}\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi\left(\frac{13}{3}\right)\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) + 2\pi\left(\frac{13}{3}\right)^2 = 39\pi + \frac{338}{9}\pi = \frac{689}{9}\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 40\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 1.5\text{ m}\). Express your answer in square centimeters.
qs.s: Convert the height to centimeters (\(h = 150\text{ cm}\)) and find \(r = 20\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(20)(150) + 2\pi(20)^2 = 6000\pi + 800\pi = 6800\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the exact surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 36\text{ mm}\) and height \(h = 7.5\text{ cm}\). Express your answer in square centimeters.
qs.s: Convert diameter to centimeters: \(d = 3.6\text{ cm}\), so \(r = 1.8\text{ cm}\). The surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(1.8)(7.5) + 2\pi(1.8)^2 = 27\pi + 6.48\pi = 33.48\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A cylindrical pipe is \(2\text{ m}\) long with an inside radius of \(4\text{ cm}\) and an outside radius of \(5\text{ cm}\). What is the exact total surface area of the pipe in square centimeters?
qs.s: The length is \(h = 200\text{ cm}\). The two annular ends have area \(2(\pi\cdot 5^2 - \pi\cdot 4^2) = 18\pi\text{ cm}^2\) and the lateral surfaces have area \(2\pi(5)(200) + 2\pi(4)(200) = 3600\pi\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total of \(3618\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A metal pipe is \(50\text{ cm}\) long with an outside diameter of \(14\text{ cm}\) and an inside diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\). What is the exact total surface area of the pipe in square centimeters?
qs.s: The radii are \(R = 7\text{ cm}\) and \(r = 5\text{ cm}\). The total surface area is \(2(\pi\cdot 7^2 - \pi\cdot 5^2) + 2\pi(7)(50) + 2\pi(5)(50) = 48\pi + 700\pi + 500\pi = 1248\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

exercises.name: Surface Area of a Cylinder from Diagram

qs.q: Find the surface area of the cylinder shown in the diagram. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Using the surface area formula \(SA = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\) with radius \(r = 3\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 7\text{ cm}\), we have \(SA = 2\pi(3^2) + 2\pi(3)(7) = 18\pi + 42\pi = 60\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The solid shown is formed by stacking a smaller cylinder centered on top of a larger cylinder. Find the total surface area of the solid. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The sum of all horizontal surface areas equals twice the base area of the larger cylinder: \(2(\pi \cdot 4^2) = 32\pi\text{ in}^2\). Adding both lateral areas gives \(2\pi(4)(6) + 2\pi(2)(3) = 48\pi + 12\pi = 60\pi\text{ in}^2\), for a total of \(32\pi + 60\pi = 92\pi\text{ in}^2\).

qs.q: The cylindrical container shown has an open top (no top lid). Find its total exterior surface area. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Because the top is open, the surface area consists of one circular base and the curved lateral surface: \(SA = \pi r^2 + 2\pi rh = \pi(5^2) + 2\pi(5)(12) = 25\pi + 120\pi = 145\pi\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Use the diagram to calculate the total surface area of the cylinder. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The diameter is \(8\text{ m}\), so the radius is \(r = 4\text{ m}\). Using \(SA = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\), we find \(SA = 2\pi(4^2) + 2\pi(4)(5) = 32\pi + 40\pi = 72\pi\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Use the diagram to find the total surface area of the cylinder. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The total surface area is given by \(SA = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh\). Substituting \(r = 3\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 7\text{ cm}\), we have \(SA = 2\pi(3^2) + 2\pi(3)(7) = 18\pi + 42\pi = 60\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the total surface area of the cylinder shown in the diagram. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: With a radius \(r = 5\text{ in}\) and height \(h = 9\text{ in}\), the surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(5^2) + 2\pi(5)(9) = 50\pi + 90\pi = 140\pi\text{ in}^2\).

qs.q: Based on the labeled dimensions in the diagram, find the total surface area of the cylinder. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(4\text{ yd}\) and the height is \(4\text{ yd}\). The total surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(4^2) + 2\pi(4)(4) = 32\pi + 32\pi = 64\pi\text{ yd}^2\).

qs.q: Find the total surface area of the solid figure formed by stacking two cylinders as shown in the diagram. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The sum of all exposed horizontal surfaces equals twice the bottom base area: \(2 \times \pi(5^2) = 50\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The combined lateral area is \(2\pi(2)(3) + 2\pi(5)(4) = 12\pi + 40\pi = 52\pi\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total surface area of \(50\pi + 52\pi = 102\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The diagram shows a cylindrical pipe with a hole drilled straight through its center. Find the total surface area of the pipe. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The total surface area includes the outer lateral area, inner lateral area, and two ring bases: \(SA = 2\pi(5)(8) + 2\pi(3)(8) + 2\pi(5^2 - 3^2) = 80\pi + 48\pi + 32\pi = 160\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Use the diagram to determine the total surface area of the cylindrical storage tank. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 28 / 2 = 14\text{ ft}\). The total surface area is \(SA = 2\pi(14^2) + 2\pi(14)(35) = 392\pi + 980\pi = 1372\pi\text{ sq ft}\).

exercises.name: Surface Area of a Compound Cylinder

qs.q: A pedestal is formed by placing a wider cylinder on top of a narrower cylinder, as shown in the figure. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), find the total surface area of the pedestal.
qs.s: All top and bottom horizontal faces combine to equal \(2\pi R^2 = 2(3.14)(5^2) = 157\text{ cm}^2\). The lateral surface areas are \(2\pi(3)(4) = 75.36\text{ cm}^2\) and \(2\pi(5)(2) = 62.8\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total of \(157 + 75.36 + 62.8 = 295.16\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A compound cylinder is formed by stacking two cylinders, as shown in the figure. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), calculate the total surface area of the solid.
qs.s: The total horizontal area equals the bottom and top projected circular faces, \(2\pi r_1^2 = 2(3.14)(4^2) = 100.48\text{ cm}^2\). Adding the lateral areas \(2\pi(4)(6) = 150.72\text{ cm}^2\) and \(2\pi(2)(3) = 37.68\text{ cm}^2\) gives a total surface area of \(288.88\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The composite solid shown in the figure consists of two stacked cylinders. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), find its total surface area.
qs.s: The radii are \(r_1 = 5\text{ m}\) and \(r_2 = 3\text{ m}\). The total horizontal surface area is \(2\pi(5^2) = 157\text{ m}^2\), and the curved areas are \(2\pi(5)(4) = 125.6\text{ m}^2\) and \(2\pi(3)(5) = 94.2\text{ m}^2\), yielding \(157 + 125.6 + 94.2 = 376.8\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Refer to the figure showing a compound cylinder made of two stacked cylinders. What is the total surface area of the solid? (Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\)).
qs.s: The combined horizontal base areas are \(2\pi(5^2) = 157\text{ cm}^2\). Adding the lateral areas of the lower cylinder, \(2\pi(5)(3) = 94.2\text{ cm}^2\), and the upper cylinder, \(2\pi(2)(6) = 75.36\text{ cm}^2\), gives \(157 + 94.2 + 75.36 = 326.56\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the total surface area of the compound cylinder shown in the figure. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\).
qs.s: The radii are \(r_1 = 4\text{ cm}\) and \(r_2 = 2\text{ cm}\). The base area total is \(2\pi(4^2) = 100.48\text{ cm}^2\), and the curved areas are \(2\pi(4)(5) = 125.6\text{ cm}^2\) and \(2\pi(2)(7) = 87.92\text{ cm}^2\), so the total area is \(100.48 + 125.6 + 87.92 = 314.00\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A metal pipe is shaped like a cylinder with a cylindrical hole drilled completely through its center, as shown in the figure. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), find the total surface area of the pipe (including the inner curved surface).
qs.s: The two annular bases have area \(2\pi(5^2 - 2^2) = 42\pi = 131.88\text{ cm}^2\). The outer curved area is \(2\pi(5)(10) = 100\pi\) and the inner curved area is \(2\pi(2)(10) = 40\pi\), giving a total of \(182\pi \approx 571.48\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A three-tiered display stand is composed of three coaxial cylinders stacked as shown in the figure. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), find the total surface area of the entire stand.
qs.s: The total horizontal area equals twice the bottom base area: \(2\pi(6^2) = 226.08\text{ cm}^2\). The sum of the lateral areas is \(2\pi(3)(6 + 4 + 2) = 226.08\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total surface area of \(226.08 + 226.08 = 452.16\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A cylindrical block of wood has a cylindrical recess drilled into the center of its top surface, as shown in the figure. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), find the total surface area of the resulting solid.
qs.s: The horizontal surfaces (bottom base, top rim, and bottom of recess) project to \(2\pi R^2 = 72\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The outer lateral area is \(2\pi(6)(8) = 96\pi\text{ cm}^2\) and the inner recess lateral area is \(2\pi(2)(3) = 12\pi\text{ cm}^2\), for a total of \(180\pi = 565.2\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The spool shown in the figure is formed by joining a narrow cylinder to two identical wider cylindrical caps at its ends. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), calculate the total surface area of the spool.
qs.s: The two outer bases have area \(2\pi(5^2) = 50\pi\) and the two inner exposed shelves have area \(2\pi(5^2 - 2^2) = 42\pi\). Adding the core lateral area \(2\pi(2)(6) = 24\pi\) and the two cap lateral areas \(2[2\pi(5)(2)] = 40\pi\) gives \(156\pi = 489.84\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A compound cylinder is composed of two stacked cylinders with dimensions shown in the figure. Using \(\pi \approx 3.14\), calculate the total surface area of the compound solid.
qs.s: The radii are \(r_1 = 6\text{ cm}\) and \(r_2 = 2.5\text{ cm}\). The horizontal base area total is \(2\pi(6^2) = 226.08\text{ cm}^2\), and the lateral areas are \(2\pi(6)(4.5) = 169.56\text{ cm}^2\) and \(2\pi(2.5)(6.4) = 100.48\text{ cm}^2\), resulting in a sum of \(496.12\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A composite cylinder consists of two stacked cylinders with base diameters of 8 cm and 4 cm, respectively. What is the total surface area of the solid? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The radii are \(R = 4\text{ cm}\) and \(r = 2\text{ cm}\). Total surface area is \(2\pi R^2 + 2\pi R H + 2\pi r h = 2(3.14)(16) + 2(3.14)(4)(5) + 2(3.14)(2)(5) = 100.48 + 125.6 + 62.8 \approx 288.9\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the total surface area of the compound cylinder shown, where the diameters of the bases are given. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The radii are \(R = 5\text{ m}\) and \(r = 3\text{ m}\). The combined flat area is \(2\pi R^2 = 2(3.14)(25) = 157.0\text{ m}^2\), and the curved areas are \(2\pi(5)(4) = 125.6\text{ m}^2\) and \(2\pi(3)(5) = 94.2\text{ m}^2\), yielding a total of \(376.8\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Use the dimensions in the figure to calculate the total surface area of the compound cylinder. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The total area of flat surfaces is \(2\pi R^2 = 2(3.14)(25) = 157.0\text{ cm}^2\). The curved surface areas are \(2\pi(5)(3) = 94.2\text{ cm}^2\) and \(2\pi(3)(7) = 131.88\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total of \(157.0 + 94.2 + 131.88 \approx 383.1\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The pedestal shown is made of two coaxial cylinders. What is its total surface area? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The bottom cylinder has radius \(R = 6\text{ cm}\) and height \(2\text{ cm}\); the top cylinder has radius \(r = 2\text{ cm}\) and height \(8\text{ cm}\). Total surface area is \(2\pi R^2 + 2\pi R H + 2\pi r h = 2(3.14)(36) + 2(3.14)(6)(2) + 2(3.14)(2)(8) = 226.08 + 75.36 + 100.48 \approx 401.9\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The compound cylinder shown is formed by joining two cylinders. What is the total surface area of the solid? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round your answer to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The flat surfaces sum to \(2\pi R^2 = 2(3.14)(4^2) = 100.48\text{ cm}^2\), and the curved areas are \(2\pi(4)(5) = 125.6\text{ cm}^2\) and \(2\pi(2)(3) = 37.68\text{ cm}^2\). Adding these gives a total surface area of \(100.48 + 125.6 + 37.68 \approx 263.8\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The pedestal shown stands on a display floor. All exposed surfaces (excluding the bottom base on the floor) are to be painted. What is the total area that needs to be painted? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The exposed flat top surfaces (ring + top face) equal \(\pi R^2 = 3.14(49) = 153.86\text{ cm}^2\). The lateral areas are \(2\pi(7)(4) = 175.84\text{ cm}^2\) and \(2\pi(3)(8) = 150.72\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total painted area of \(153.86 + 175.84 + 150.72 \approx 480.4\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The spool-shaped solid shown consists of a central cylindrical shaft joined to two identical cylindrical end discs. What is the total surface area of the spool? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The flat surfaces include 2 outer circles and 2 inner rings: \(2\pi(5^2) + 2\pi(5^2 - 2^2) = 50\pi + 42\pi = 92\pi = 288.88\text{ cm}^2\). The lateral areas are \(2(2\pi \times 5 \times 2) + 2\pi(2)(6) = 40\pi + 24\pi = 64\pi = 200.96\text{ cm}^2\). Total surface area is \(288.88 + 200.96 \approx 489.8\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A cylindrical socket has an outer diameter of 12 cm and a height of 10 cm. A cylindrical hole of diameter 8 cm and depth 6 cm is drilled into the center of the top face. What is the total surface area of the socket? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The horizontal surfaces (bottom base, top ring, hole floor) equal \(2\pi R^2 = 2(3.14)(36) = 226.08\text{ cm}^2\). The outer lateral area is \(2\pi(6)(10) = 376.8\text{ cm}^2\) and inner lateral area is \(2\pi(4)(6) = 150.72\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total of \(226.08 + 376.8 + 150.72 = 753.6\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A cylindrical pipe has an outer radius of 5 cm, a cylindrical hole of radius 2 cm drilled through its center, and a height of 8 cm. What is the total surface area of the hollow cylinder? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The surface area includes the outer lateral area \(2\pi(5)(8) = 251.2\text{ cm}^2\), the inner lateral area \(2\pi(2)(8) = 100.48\text{ cm}^2\), and two ring bases \(2\pi(5^2 - 2^2) = 2(3.14)(21) = 131.88\text{ cm}^2\). Summing these gives \(251.2 + 100.48 + 131.88 \approx 483.6\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A three-tier cake stand is made of three coaxial stacked cylinders, each with a height of 3 cm. The radii of the tiers are 6 cm, 4 cm, and 2 cm. Find the total surface area of the structure. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: All top flat surfaces plus the bottom base equal \(2\pi R_1^2 = 2(3.14)(36) = 226.08\text{ cm}^2\). The three lateral areas are \(2\pi(3)[6 + 4 + 2] = 2(3.14)(3)(12) = 226.08\text{ cm}^2\), giving a total of \(226.08 + 226.08 \approx 452.2\text{ cm}^2\).

exercises.name: Surface Area of an Inscribed Cylinder

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with side length \(4\text{ cm}\). Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = \frac{4}{2} = 2\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 4\text{ cm}\). Its surface area is \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(2)(4) + 2\pi(2^2) = 16\pi + 8\pi = 24\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with side length \(12\text{ mm}\). Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 6\text{ mm}\) and height \(h = 12\text{ mm}\). Its surface area is \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(6)(12) + 2\pi(6^2) = 144\pi + 72\pi = 216\pi\text{ mm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with side length \(10\text{ cm}\). Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 5\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 10\text{ cm}\). Its surface area is \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(5)(10) + 2\pi(5^2) = 100\pi + 50\pi = 150\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with side length \(6\text{ m}\). Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 3\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 6\text{ m}\). Its surface area is \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(3)(6) + 2\pi(3^2) = 36\pi + 18\pi = 54\pi\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Find the surface area of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with side length \(16\text{ cm}\). Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
