qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(1)(1) + 2\pi(1^2) = 4\pi\text{ m}^2\). With height \(3\text{ m}\) and radius \(1\text{ m}\), the new surface area is \(2\pi(1)(3) + 2\pi(1^2) = 8\pi\text{ m}^2\), which is \(8\pi \div 4\pi = 2\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does doubling only the height have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(1\text{ m}\) and height \(1\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(1)(1) + 2\pi(1^2) = 4\pi\text{ m}^2\). With height \(2\text{ m}\) and radius \(1\text{ m}\), the new surface area is \(2\pi(1)(2) + 2\pi(1^2) = 6\pi\text{ m}^2\), which is \(6\pi \div 4\pi = 1.5\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does quadrupling both the radius and the height have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(1\text{ m}\) and height \(1\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(1)(1) + 2\pi(1^2) = 4\pi\text{ m}^2\). With radius \(4\text{ m}\) and height \(4\text{ m}\), the new surface area is \(2\pi(4)(4) + 2\pi(4^2) = 64\pi\text{ m}^2\), which is \(64\pi \div 4\pi = 16\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does doubling only the radius have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(1\text{ m}\) and height \(1\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(1)(1) + 2\pi(1^2) = 4\pi\text{ m}^2\). With radius \(2\text{ m}\) and height \(1\text{ m}\), the new surface area is \(2\pi(2)(1) + 2\pi(2^2) = 12\pi\text{ m}^2\), which is \(12\pi \div 4\pi = 3\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does doubling both the radius and the height have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(1\text{ m}\) and height \(1\text{ m}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(1)(1) + 2\pi(1^2) = 4\pi\text{ m}^2\). With a radius of \(2\text{ m}\) and height of \(2\text{ m}\), the new surface area is \(2\pi(2)(2) + 2\pi(2^2) = 16\pi\text{ m}^2\), which is \(16\pi \div 4\pi = 4\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does multiplying both the radius and the height by \(\frac{2}{3}\) have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and height \(6\text{ cm}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(3)(6) + 2\pi(3^2) = 54\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The new radius is \(2\text{ cm}\) and new height is \(4\text{ cm}\), giving a surface area of \(2\pi(2)(4) + 2\pi(2^2) = 24\pi\text{ cm}^2\), so the surface area is multiplied by \(\frac{24\pi}{54\pi} = \frac{4}{9}\).

qs.q: What effect does doubling the radius and halving the height have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and height \(6\text{ cm}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(3)(6) + 2\pi(3^2) = 54\pi\text{ cm}^2\). With new radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and new height \(3\text{ cm}\), the surface area becomes \(2\pi(6)(3) + 2\pi(6^2) = 108\pi\text{ cm}^2\), which is \(108\pi \div 54\pi = 2\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does halving the radius and multiplying the height by \(5\) have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and height \(6\text{ cm}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(4)(6) + 2\pi(4^2) = 80\pi\text{ cm}^2\). With new radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and new height \(30\text{ cm}\), the surface area becomes \(2\pi(2)(30) + 2\pi(2^2) = 128\pi\text{ cm}^2\), which is \(128\pi \div 80\pi = 1.6\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does doubling the diameter have on the surface area of a cylinder with diameter \(4\text{ cm}\) and height \(6\text{ cm}\), if the height remains unchanged?
qs.s: The original radius is \(2\text{ cm}\), so the surface area is \(2\pi(2)(6) + 2\pi(2^2) = 32\pi\text{ cm}^2\). Doubling the diameter gives a radius of \(4\text{ cm}\), producing a surface area of \(2\pi(4)(6) + 2\pi(4^2) = 80\pi\text{ cm}^2\), which is \(80\pi \div 32\pi = 2.5\) times the original.

qs.q: What effect does tripling the radius and doubling the height have on the surface area of a cylinder with radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and height \(4\text{ cm}\)?
qs.s: The original surface area is \(2\pi(2)(4) + 2\pi(2^2) = 24\pi\text{ cm}^2\). With radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and height \(8\text{ cm}\), the new surface area is \(2\pi(6)(8) + 2\pi(6^2) = 168\pi\text{ cm}^2\), which is \(168\pi \div 24\pi = 7\) times the original.

exercises.name: Volume from radius or diameter and height

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 6\text{ m}\), \(h = 8\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is half of the diameter, so \(r = 3\text{ m}\). Thus, \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (3^2)(8) = 72\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 2\text{ m}\), \(h = 9\text{ m}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(r = 2\text{ m}\) and \(h = 9\text{ m}\) into \(V = \pi r^2 h\) to get \(V = \pi (2^2)(9) = 36\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 5\text{ mm}\), \(h = 7\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: Using the volume formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\), substitute \(r = 5\text{ mm}\) and \(h = 7\text{ mm}\) to find \(V = \pi (5^2)(7) = 175\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 10\text{ cm}\), \(h = 4\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 10 / 2 = 5\text{ cm}\). Therefore, the volume is \(V = \pi (5^2)(4) = 100\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 4\text{ cm}\), \(h = 6\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The volume of a cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\). Substituting \(r = 4\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 6\text{ cm}\) gives \(V = \pi (4^2)(6) = 96\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: diameter \(d = 9\text{ cm}\), height \(h = 10\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{9}{2}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi \left(\frac{9}{2}\right)^2(10) = \pi \left(\frac{81}{4}\right)(10) = \frac{405}{2}\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A cylinder has a diameter of \(14\text{ cm}\), and its height is \(3\) times its radius. Find the exact volume of the cylinder.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 14 / 2 = 7\text{ cm}\), so the height is \(h = 3 \times 7 = 21\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi (7^2)(21) = 1029\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder of radius \(r = 6\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 10\text{ m}\) with a \(90^\circ\) section removed along its entire height.
qs.s: With a \(90^\circ\) section removed, \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the cylinder remains. The volume is \(V = \frac{3}{4}\pi r^2 h = \frac{3}{4}\pi (6^2)(10) = 270\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder in cubic centimeters (\(\text{cm}^3\)) if its diameter is \(8\text{ cm}\) and its height is \(0.75\text{ m}\).
qs.s: Convert height to centimeters: \(h = 0.75\text{ m} = 75\text{ cm}\), and find radius \(r = 8 / 2 = 4\text{ cm}\). Then \(V = \pi (4^2)(75) = 1200\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: diameter \(d = 24\text{ cm}\), height \(h = 35\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 24 / 2 = 12\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi (12^2)(35) = \pi (144)(35) = 5040\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 10\text{ cm}\), \(h = 11\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ cm}\). Then calculate \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (5^2)(11) = 275\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 6\text{ mm}\), \(h = 7\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(r = 6\text{ mm}\) and \(h = 7\text{ mm}\) into \(V = \pi r^2 h\) to obtain \(V = \pi (6^2)(7) = 252\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 4\text{ in.}\), \(h = 9\text{ in.}\).
qs.s: Using \(V = \pi r^2 h\), substitute \(r = 4\text{ in.}\) and \(h = 9\text{ in.}\) to get \(V = \pi (4^2)(9) = 144\pi\text{ in.}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 8\text{ m}\), \(h = 6\text{ m}\).
qs.s: First find the radius \(r = \frac{8}{2} = 4\text{ m}\), then use \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (4^2)(6) = 96\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = 3\text{ cm}\), \(h = 8\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(r = 3\text{ cm}\) and \(h = 8\text{ cm}\) into the formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\) to get \(V = \pi (3^2)(8) = 72\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 24\text{ m}\), \(h = 25\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{24}{2} = 12\text{ m}\). Using \(V = \pi r^2 h\), we have \(V = \pi (12^2)(25) = \pi (144)(25) = 3600\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: A cylinder has a diameter of \(16\text{ cm}\). Its height is \(5\text{ cm}\) greater than its radius. Find the exact volume of the cylinder.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{16}{2} = 8\text{ cm}\) and the height is \(h = 8 + 5 = 13\text{ cm}\). Then \(V = \pi (8^2)(13) = 832\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(r = \frac{3}{4}\text{ m}\), \(h = \frac{8}{3}\text{ m}\).
qs.s: Substitute the fractions into \(V = \pi r^2 h\) to get \(V = \pi \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) = \pi \left(\frac{9}{16}\right)\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) = \frac{3}{2}\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with radius \(r = 6\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 10\text{ cm}\) that has a \(90^\circ\) section removed.
qs.s: The remaining cylinder is \(\frac{360^\circ - 90^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{3}{4}\) of the full cylinder, so \(V = \frac{3}{4}\pi (6^2)(10) = \frac{3}{4}\pi (360) = 270\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of the cylinder with the given dimensions: \(d = 7\text{ cm}\), \(h = 12\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}\). Then \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2(12) = \pi \left(\frac{49}{4}\right)(12) = 147\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 7.4\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 6.3\text{ cm}\). Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 7.4 / 2 = 3.7\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi (3.7)^2 (6.3) = 86.247\pi \approx 270.95\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 6.4\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 5.5\text{ cm}\). Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 6.4 / 2 = 3.2\text{ cm}\). Using \(V = \pi r^2 h\), the volume is \(V = \pi (3.2)^2 (5.5) = 56.32\pi \approx 176.94\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius \(r = 2.5\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 9.1\text{ cm}\). Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: Using \(V = \pi r^2 h\), the volume is \(V = \pi (2.5)^2 (9.1) = 56.875\pi \approx 178.68\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 8.6\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 3.4\text{ cm}\). Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 8.6 / 2 = 4.3\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi (4.3)^2 (3.4) = 62.866\pi \approx 197.50\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius \(r = 3.8\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 7.2\text{ cm}\). Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: Using \(V = \pi r^2 h\), we calculate \(V = \pi (3.8)^2 (7.2) = 103.968\pi \approx 326.62\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 16\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 18\text{ cm}\) that has a \(90^\circ\) section removed. Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 8\text{ cm}\), and removing \(90^\circ\) leaves \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the cylinder. Thus, \(V = \frac{3}{4}\pi (8)^2 (18) = 864\pi \approx 2714.34\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a solid half-cylinder with a diameter of \(15.6\text{ cm}\) and a length of \(24.0\text{ cm}\). Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 15.6 / 2 = 7.8\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{1}{2}\pi (7.8)^2 (24.0) = 730.08\pi \approx 2293.62\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A solid cylinder has a diameter of \(18.4\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(32.5\text{ cm}\). A cylindrical hole with a diameter of \(6.2\text{ cm}\) is drilled through its center from top to bottom. Find the remaining volume of the cylinder. Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The outer radius is \(R = 9.2\text{ cm}\) and the inner radius is \(r = 3.1\text{ cm}\). The remaining volume is \(V = \pi (9.2^2 - 3.1^2)(32.5) = 2438.475\pi \approx 7660.70\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A hollow steel pipe has an outer diameter of \(14\text{ cm}\), an inner diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\), and a height of \(25\text{ cm}\). What is the volume of steel in the pipe? Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The outer radius is \(R = 7\text{ cm}\) and the inner radius is \(r = 5\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi(R^2 - r^2)h = \pi(7^2 - 5^2)(25) = 600\pi \approx 1884.96\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A solid sculpture is formed by stacking two cylinders. The bottom cylinder has a diameter of \(24\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(15\text{ cm}\), and the top cylinder has a diameter of \(14\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(20\text{ cm}\). What is the total volume of the sculpture? Round your answer to two decimal places.
qs.s: The bottom cylinder has radius \(12\text{ cm}\) giving volume \(\pi(12)^2(15) = 2160\pi\), and the top has radius \(7\text{ cm}\) giving \(\pi(7)^2(20) = 980\pi\). The total volume is \(3140\pi \approx 9864.60\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 5\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 2\frac{1}{4}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{16}{3}\right) = \frac{8}{3}\text{ cm}\) and the height is \(h = \frac{9}{4}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)^2\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 3\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 2\frac{2}{3}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{7}{2}\right) = \frac{7}{4}\text{ cm}\) and height is \(h = \frac{8}{3}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) = \frac{49}{6}\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with radius \(r = 1\frac{1}{4}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 3\frac{1}{5}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{5}{4}\text{ cm}\) and the height is \(h = \frac{16}{5}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^2\left(\frac{16}{5}\right) = 5\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 1\frac{1}{3}\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 4\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) = \frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\) and the height is \(h = \frac{9}{2}\text{ m}\). Thus, \(V = \pi\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) = 2\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with radius \(r = 2\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 1\frac{1}{5}\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{5}{2}\text{ cm}\) and the height is \(h = \frac{6}{5}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2\left(\frac{6}{5}\right) = \frac{15}{2}\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has diameter \(4\text{ cm}\) and height \(4\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\), while Cylinder B has diameter \(6\text{ cm}\) and height \(3\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\). Find the positive difference between their exact volumes.
qs.s: The volume of Cylinder A is \(\pi(2^2)\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) = 18\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and Cylinder B is \(\pi(3^2)\left(\frac{10}{3}\right) = 30\pi\text{ cm}^3\). The positive difference is \(30\pi - 18\pi = 12\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 6\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 4\frac{2}{3}\text{ cm}\) that has a \(90^\circ\) section removed.
qs.s: Removing a \(90^\circ\) section leaves \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the cylinder. With \(r = 3\text{ cm}\) and \(h = \frac{14}{3}\text{ cm}\), \(V = \frac{3}{4}\pi(3^2)\left(\frac{14}{3}\right) = \frac{63}{2}\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with diameter \(d = 6x\) and height \(h = \frac{4}{3}x^2\) in terms of \(\pi\) and \(x\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{6x}{2} = 3x\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(3x)^2\left(\frac{4}{3}x^2\right) = \pi(9x^2)\left(\frac{4}{3}x^2\right) = 12\pi x^4\).

qs.q: A solid pedestal consists of two stacked cylinders. The lower cylinder has diameter \(8\text{ cm}\) and height \(3\text{ cm}\), and the upper cylinder has diameter \(4\text{ cm}\) and height \(2\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\). Find the total exact volume of the pedestal.
qs.s: The lower cylinder has volume \(\pi(4^2)(3) = 48\pi\text{ cm}^3\) and the upper cylinder has volume \(\pi(2^2)\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) = 10\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Summing them gives \(48\pi + 10\pi = 58\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A hollow metal pipe has an outer diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\), an inner diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\), and a height of \(12\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\). Find the exact volume of metal in the pipe.
qs.s: The outer radius is \(R = 5\text{ cm}\) and the inner radius is \(r = 3\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi(R^2 - r^2)h = \pi(25 - 9)\left(\frac{25}{2}\right) = 200\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

exercises.name: Volume of partial cylinder from figure

qs.q: Find the volume of the figure shown, which is a cylinder with a \(180^\circ\) sector removed. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: A half-cylinder has \(\frac{180^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\) the volume of the full cylinder. Therefore, \(V = \frac{1}{2} \pi (5)^2 (6) = 75\pi\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the figure, which is a cylinder with a sector removed. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The cylinder has a radius of \(4\text{ cm}\) and height of \(10\text{ cm}\) with a \(90^\circ\) sector removed, leaving \(\frac{270^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{3}{4}\) of the cylinder. The volume is \(V = \frac{3}{4} \pi (4)^2 (10) = 120\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the figure, which is a cylinder of base diameter \(10\text{ m}\) with a sector removed. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ m}\). With a \(72^\circ\) sector removed, the fraction remaining is \(\frac{360^\circ - 72^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{288^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{4}{5}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{4}{5} \pi (5)^2 (14) = 280\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: The figure shows a partial cylinder of base diameter \(18\text{ in.}\) with the remaining central angle labeled. Find the volume of the figure. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ in.}\) and the remaining sector angle is \(240^\circ\). The fraction of the cylinder is \(\frac{240^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{2}{3}\), so \(V = \frac{2}{3} \pi (9)^2 (14) = 756\pi\text{ in.}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the figure, which is a cylinder of base diameter \(6\text{ ft}\) with a \(40^\circ\) sector removed. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ ft}\). The fraction remaining after removing a \(40^\circ\) sector is \(\frac{360^\circ - 40^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{320^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{8}{9}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{8}{9} \pi (3)^2 (15) = 120\pi\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the figure, which is a cylinder of base diameter \(12\text{ cm}\) with a sector removed. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ cm}\). With a \(135^\circ\) sector removed, the fraction remaining is \(\frac{360^\circ - 135^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{225^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{5}{8}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{5}{8} \pi (6)^2 (16) = 360\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the figure, which is a cylinder of radius \(12\text{ cm}\) with a \(150^\circ\) sector removed. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The remaining angle is \(360^\circ - 150^\circ = 210^\circ\), which is a fraction of \(\frac{210^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{7}{12}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{7}{12} \pi (12)^2 (7) = 588\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the half-cylinder shown in the figure. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The volume of a half-cylinder is half the volume of a complete cylinder: \(V = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{2}\pi (5^2)(8) = 100\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the partial cylinder shown in the figure. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: A \(90^\circ\) sector is removed from the cylinder, leaving \(\frac{360^\circ - 90^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{3}{4}\) of the full volume. The volume is \(V = \frac{3}{4}\pi r^2 h = \frac{3}{4}\pi (4^2)(6) = 72\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the partial cylinder shown in the figure, which has a diameter of 8 cm. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{8}{2} = 4\text{ cm}\). Removing a \(45^\circ\) sector leaves \(\frac{360^\circ - 45^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{7}{8}\) of the cylinder. The volume is \(V = \frac{7}{8}\pi (4^2)(14) = 196\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the partial cylinder shown in the figure, which has a diameter of 12 in. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ in.}\), and the central angle of the remaining base is \(240^\circ\), giving a fraction of \(\frac{240^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{2}{3}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{2}{3}\pi (6^2)(15) = 360\pi\text{ in.}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of the partial cylinder shown in the figure, which has a diameter of 10 cm. Leave the answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ cm}\). The fraction of the cylinder remaining is \(\frac{360^\circ - 144^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{216^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{3}{5}\). The volume is \(V = \frac{3}{5}\pi (5^2)(16) = 240\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Use the dimensions labeled in the figure to calculate the total volume of the two stacked cylinders. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The bottom cylinder has radius 4 cm and volume 3.14 * 4^2 * 6 = 301.44 cm^3, while the top cylinder has radius 2 cm and volume 3.14 * 2^2 * 4 = 50.24 cm^3. The total volume is 301.44 + 50.24 = 351.68 cm^3, which rounds to 351.7 cm^3.

qs.q: Use the figure to find the volume of material in the cylindrical metal tube. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The outer volume is 3.14 * 5^2 * 12 = 942.0 cm^3 and the inner hollow volume is 3.14 * 3^2 * 12 = 339.12 cm^3. Subtracting gives 942.0 - 339.12 = 602.88 cm^3, which rounds to 602.9 cm^3.

qs.q: Use the figure to find the total volume of the compound cylinder. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The volume of the bottom cylinder is 3.14 * 4^2 * 5 = 251.2 cm^3 and the top cylinder is 3.14 * 2^2 * 3 = 37.68 cm^3. Adding them gives a total volume of 251.2 + 37.68 = 288.88 cm^3, which rounds to 288.9 cm^3.

qs.q: Use the figure to find the volume of the hollow cylindrical pipe. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The outer cylinder volume is 3.14 * 5^2 * 8 = 628 m^3 and the inner hole volume is 3.14 * 2^2 * 8 = 100.48 m^3. Subtracting the inner volume from the outer volume gives 628 - 100.48 = 527.52 m^3, which rounds to 527.5 m^3.

qs.q: A pedestal is made of a narrow cylinder supporting a wider cylinder on top, as shown. Use the figure to determine its total volume. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The volume of the bottom cylinder is 3.14 * 2^2 * 7 = 87.92 cm^3 and the top cylinder is 3.14 * 5^2 * 3 = 235.5 cm^3. The sum of the volumes is 87.92 + 235.5 = 323.42 cm^3, which rounds to 323.4 cm^3.

qs.q: A stepped metal bushing consists of two stacked cylinders with a central hole of radius 2 cm running all the way through both tiers. Using the measurements in the figure, calculate the total volume of the bushing. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The solid volume of the lower tier is 3.14 * (6^2 - 2^2) * 4 = 3.14 * 32 * 4 = 401.92 cm^3. The solid volume of the upper tier is 3.14 * (4^2 - 2^2) * 6 = 3.14 * 12 * 6 = 226.08 cm^3. Summing these gives 401.92 + 226.08 = 628.0 cm^3.

qs.q: A cylindrical container has an outer height of 10 cm and outer radius of 6 cm. A cylindrical hole of radius 4 cm is drilled into the top to a depth of 7 cm (it does not go all the way through). Use the figure to find the volume of the remaining solid. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The outer cylinder has volume 3.14 * 6^2 * 10 = 1130.4 cm^3. The excavated cylindrical cavity has volume 3.14 * 4^2 * 7 = 351.68 cm^3. Subtracting the cavity gives 1130.4 - 351.68 = 778.72 cm^3, which rounds to 778.7 cm^3.

qs.q: A three-tier trophy stand is formed by stacking three cylinders, as shown. Use the dimensions in the figure to calculate the total volume of the stand. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The volume of each cylinder is 3.14 * r^2 * 3. Adding the three tiers gives 3.14 * 3 * (6^2 + 4^2 + 2^2) = 9.42 * (36 + 16 + 4) = 9.42 * 56 = 527.52 cm^3, which rounds to 527.5 cm^3.

qs.q: A hollow concrete cylinder has an outer diameter of 20 cm, a uniform wall thickness of 3 cm, and a length of 30 cm. Use the figure to determine the volume of concrete in the pipe. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The outer radius is 20 / 2 = 10 cm and the inner radius is 10 - 3 = 7 cm. The volume of concrete is 3.14 * (10^2 - 7^2) * 30 = 3.14 * 51 * 30 = 4804.2 cm^3.

qs.q: A cylindrical metal block has a radius of 7 cm and a height of 12 cm. Two identical cylindrical holes, each of radius 2 cm, are bored straight through from top to bottom. Find the volume of the remaining metal. Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The full cylinder volume is 3.14 * 7^2 * 12 = 1846.32 cm^3. The combined volume of the two holes is 2 * (3.14 * 2^2 * 12) = 301.44 cm^3. Subtracting the holes gives 1846.32 - 301.44 = 1544.88 cm^3, which rounds to 1544.9 cm^3.

qs.q: Find the total volume of the tiered cylindrical pedestal shown in the figure. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The lower cylinder has volume \(V_1 = 3.14 \times 5^2 \times 2 = 157.0\text{ cm}^3\) and the upper cylinder has volume \(V_2 = 3.14 \times 3^2 \times 4 = 113.04\text{ cm}^3\). The combined volume is \(157.0 + 113.04 = 270.04 \approx 270.0\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Use the given dimensions in the figure to calculate the volume of the compound cylinder. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The bottom cylinder has radius \(r_1 = 8 / 2 = 4\text{ m}\), so \(V_1 = 3.14 \times 4^2 \times 3 = 150.72\text{ m}^3\). The top cylinder has radius \(r_2 = 4 / 2 = 2\text{ m}\), so \(V_2 = 3.14 \times 2^2 \times 6 = 75.36\text{ m}^3\). The total volume is \(150.72 + 75.36 = 226.08 \approx 226.1\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Use the figure to find the total volume of the compound cylinder. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The bottom cylinder has volume \(V_1 = 3.14 \times 4^2 \times 5 = 251.2\text{ cm}^3\) and the top cylinder has volume \(V_2 = 3.14 \times 1^2 \times 5 = 15.7\text{ cm}^3\). Total volume \(= 251.2 + 15.7 = 266.9\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: The figure shows a solid composed of two stacked cylinders. What is its total volume? Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The base cylinder has volume \(V_1 = 3.14 \times 6^2 \times 2 = 226.08\text{ in}^3\). The top cylinder has volume \(V_2 = 3.14 \times 2^2 \times 7 = 87.92\text{ in}^3\). Total volume \(= 226.08 + 87.92 = 314.0\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: Use the figure to find the total volume of the compound cylinder. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round your answer to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The volume of the bottom cylinder is \(\pi r_1^2 h_1 \approx 3.14 \times 3^2 \times 4 = 113.04\text{ cm}^3\), and the top cylinder is \(\pi r_2^2 h_2 \approx 3.14 \times 2^2 \times 5 = 62.8\text{ cm}^3\). Adding them gives \(113.04 + 62.8 = 175.84 \approx 175.8\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A cylindrical pipe has a height of \(20\text{ cm}\), an outer diameter of \(14\text{ cm}\), and a uniform wall thickness of \(2\text{ cm}\). Find the volume of material used in the pipe. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The outer radius is \(R = 14 / 2 = 7\text{ cm}\) and the inner radius is \(r = 7 - 2 = 5\text{ cm}\). The volume of the pipe wall is \(V = \pi (R^2 - r^2) h \approx 3.14 \times (7^2 - 5^2) \times 20 = 3.14 \times 24 \times 20 = 1507.2\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylindrical block has a diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(12\text{ cm}\). A centered cylindrical hole with a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a depth of \(8\text{ cm}\) is drilled into the top face. Find the remaining volume of the block. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The outer cylinder has radius \(5\text{ cm}\) and volume \(3.14 \times 5^2 \times 12 = 942.0\text{ cm}^3\). The hole has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and volume \(3.14 \times 3^2 \times 8 = 226.08\text{ cm}^3\). Remaining volume \(= 942.0 - 226.08 = 715.92 \approx 715.9\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: The trophy base shown in the figure consists of three stacked cylinders, each having a height of \(3\text{ cm}\). The radii of the tiers from bottom to top are \(6\text{ cm}\), \(4\text{ cm}\), and \(2\text{ cm}\). Find the total volume of the base. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The volume of the bottom tier is \(3.14 \times 6^2 \times 3 = 339.12\text{ cm}^3\), the middle tier is \(3.14 \times 4^2 \times 3 = 150.72\text{ cm}^3\), and the top tier is \(3.14 \times 2^2 \times 3 = 37.68\text{ cm}^3\). Total volume \(= 339.12 + 150.72 + 37.68 = 527.52 \approx 527.5\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: The symmetrical machine shaft shown in the figure consists of a large middle cylinder and two identical smaller cylindrical ends. Calculate the total volume of the shaft. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The middle cylinder has radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and volume \(3.14 \times 4^2 \times 10 = 502.4\text{ cm}^3\). Each end cylinder has radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and volume \(3.14 \times 2^2 \times 5 = 62.8\text{ cm}^3\). Total volume \(= 502.4 + 2 \times 62.8 = 628.0\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: The figure shows a cylindrical hollow metal pipe with outer radius \(R = 5\text{ cm}\), inner radius \(r = 3\text{ cm}\), and height \(10\text{ cm}\). Find the volume of metal in the pipe. Use \(\pi \approx 3.14\) and round to the nearest tenth.
qs.s: The volume of the hollow cylinder is \(V = \pi(R^2 - r^2)h \approx 3.14 \times (5^2 - 3^2) \times 10 = 3.14 \times (25 - 9) \times 10 = 3.14 \times 16 \times 10 = 502.4\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(4\text{ in}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = 4 / 2 = 2\text{ in}\) and height \(h = 4\text{ in}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (2^2)(4) = 16\pi\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(14\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = 14 / 2 = 7\text{ mm}\) and height \(h = 14\text{ mm}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (7^2)(14) = 686\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(10\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = 10 / 2 = 5\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 10\text{ m}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (5^2)(10) = 250\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(6\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = 6 / 2 = 3\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 6\text{ cm}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (3^2)(6) = 54\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(12\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = 12 / 2 = 6\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 12\text{ cm}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (6^2)(12) = 432\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ m}\) and height \(h = \frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{27}\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(4x\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = \frac{4x}{2} = 2x\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 4x\text{ cm}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (2x)^2(4x) = 16\pi x^3\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: The perimeter of one face of a cube is \(64\text{ cm}\). Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in the cube.
qs.s: The side length of the cube is \(s = 64 / 4 = 16\text{ cm}\). The cylinder has radius \(r = 8\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 16\text{ cm}\), so its volume is \(V = \pi (8^2)(16) = 1024\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A cube has a volume of \(8000\text{ cm}^3\). Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in this cube.
qs.s: The edge length of the cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{8000} = 20\text{ cm}\). The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 10\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 20\text{ cm}\), giving a volume of \(V = \pi (10^2)(20) = 2000\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with a side length of \(5\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = \frac{5}{2}\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 5\text{ cm}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2(5) = \frac{125\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(6\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 3\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 6\text{ m}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(3^2)(6) = 54\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(4\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 2\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 4\text{ cm}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(2^2)(4) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(3\text{ in.}\)
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = \frac{3}{2}\text{ in.}\) and height \(h = 3\text{ in.}\) Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2(3) = \frac{27\pi}{4}\text{ in.}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(2\text{ ft}\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 1\text{ ft}\) and height \(h = 2\text{ ft}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(1^2)(2) = 2\pi\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(8\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 4\text{ mm}\) and height \(h = 8\text{ mm}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(4^2)(8) = 128\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(1.2\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 0.6\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 1.2\text{ m}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(0.6)^2(1.2) = 0.432\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(15\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = \frac{15}{2}\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 15\text{ m}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^2(15) = \frac{3375\pi}{4}\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(\frac{4}{3}\text{ ft}\).
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = \frac{2}{3}\text{ ft}\) and height \(h = \frac{4}{3}\text{ ft}\). Its volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) = \frac{16\pi}{27}\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: A cylinder is inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(6\text{ m}\). If a \(90^\circ\) section is removed from the cylinder along its entire height, find the volume of the remaining portion of the cylinder.
qs.s: The inscribed cylinder has radius \(r = 3\text{ m}\) and height \(h = 6\text{ m}\). With a \(90^\circ\) section removed, the remaining volume is \(\frac{3}{4}\pi r^2 h = \frac{3}{4}\pi(3^2)(6) = \frac{81\pi}{2}\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: A cylinder is inscribed in a cube with sides of length \(10\text{ cm}\). Find the volume of the space inside the cube that is outside the cylinder.
qs.s: The cube's volume is \(10^3 = 1000\text{ cm}^3\), and the inscribed cylinder has volume \(\pi(5^2)(10) = 250\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Subtracting the cylinder's volume from the cube's volume gives \((1000 - 250\pi)\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 11\text{ mm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 12\pi\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: From the circumference \(C = 2\pi r = 12\pi\text{ mm}\), the radius is \(r = 6\text{ mm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (6^2)(11) = 396\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 4\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 10\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: From the circumference \(C = 2\pi r = 10\pi\text{ m}\), the radius is \(r = 5\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (5^2)(4) = 100\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 2\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 18\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: From the circumference \(C = 2\pi r = 18\pi\text{ m}\), the radius is \(r = 9\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (9^2)(2) = 162\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 5\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 16\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: From the circumference \(C = 2\pi r = 16\pi\text{ cm}\), the radius is \(r = 8\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (8^2)(5) = 320\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 7\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 6\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: From the circumference \(C = 2\pi r = 6\pi\text{ cm}\), the radius is \(r = 3\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (3^2)(7) = 63\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 5x\), \(\text{circumference} = 6\pi x\).
qs.s: From \(C = 2\pi r = 6\pi x\), the radius is \(r = 3x\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (3x)^2(5x) = \pi (9x^2)(5x) = 45\pi x^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 4.5\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 1.2\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: From \(C = 2\pi r = 1.2\pi\text{ cm}\), the radius is \(r = 0.6\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (0.6^2)(4.5) = 1.62\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 24\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 22\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: From the circumference \(C = 2\pi r = 22\pi\text{ cm}\), the radius is \(r = 11\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (11^2)(24) = 2904\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 3\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: From \(C = 2\pi r = 3\pi\text{ m}\), the radius is \(r = \frac{3}{2}\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) = \frac{15}{4}\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 9\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 7\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: From \(C = 2\pi r = 7\pi\text{ m}\), the radius is \(r = \frac{7}{2}\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2(9) = \frac{441}{4}\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 9\text{ mm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 16\pi\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{16\pi}{2\pi} = 8\text{ mm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(8^2)(9) = 576\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 4\text{ ft}\), \(\text{circumference} = 10\pi\text{ ft}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{10\pi}{2\pi} = 5\text{ ft}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(5^2)(4) = 100\pi\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 10\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 6\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{6\pi}{2\pi} = 3\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(3^2)(10) = 90\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 3\text{ in}\), \(\text{circumference} = 14\pi\text{ in}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{14\pi}{2\pi} = 7\text{ in}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(7^2)(3) = 147\pi\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 5\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 8\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{8\pi}{2\pi} = 4\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(4^2)(5) = 80\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 45\text{ mm}\), \(\text{circumference} = \frac{4\pi}{3}\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{4\pi/3}{2\pi} = \frac{2}{3}\text{ mm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2(45) = \pi\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)(45) = 20\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 18\text{ in}\), \(\text{circumference} = 11\pi\text{ in}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{11}{2}\text{ in}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{11}{2}\right)^2(18) = \pi\left(\frac{121}{4}\right)(18) = \frac{1089}{2}\pi\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 8\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 7\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2(8) = \pi\left(\frac{49}{4}\right)(8) = 98\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 25\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 32\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{32\pi}{2\pi} = 16\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(16^2)(25) = \pi(256)(25) = 6400\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 5\text{ yd}\), \(\text{circumference} = 9\pi\text{ yd}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{9}{2}\text{ yd}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi\left(\frac{9}{2}\right)^2(5) = \frac{405}{4}\pi\text{ yd}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 6.4\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 5.6\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{5.6\pi}{2\pi} = 2.8\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (2.8)^2 (6.4) = 50.176\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 8.5\text{ mm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 9.4\pi\text{ mm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{9.4\pi}{2\pi} = 4.7\text{ mm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (4.7)^2 (8.5) = 187.765\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 3.5\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 8.2\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{8.2\pi}{2\pi} = 4.1\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (4.1)^2 (3.5) = 58.835\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 7.2\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 4.6\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{4.6\pi}{2\pi} = 2.3\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (2.3)^2 (7.2) = 38.088\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 4.5\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 6.8\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{6.8\pi}{2\pi} = 3.4\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (3.4)^2 (4.5) = 52.02\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements in cubic centimeters: \(\text{height} = 0.75\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 14.8\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Convert the height to centimeters: \(h = 0.75\text{ m} = 75\text{ cm}\). With \(r = \frac{14.8\pi}{2\pi} = 7.4\text{ cm}\), the volume is \(V = \pi (7.4)^2 (75) = 4107\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 35\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 48\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{48\pi}{2\pi} = 24\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (24)^2 (35) = 20160\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements in cubic centimeters: \(\text{height} = 1.2\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 26\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: Convert the height to centimeters: \(h = 1.2\text{ m} = 120\text{ cm}\). With \(r = \frac{26\pi}{2\pi} = 13\text{ cm}\), the volume is \(V = \pi (13)^2 (120) = 20280\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = \frac{5}{4}\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = \frac{6}{5}\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{6}{5}\pi \div (2\pi) = \frac{3}{5}\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2 \left(\frac{5}{4}\right) = \frac{9}{20}\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = \frac{9}{2}\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = \frac{8}{3}\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{8}{3}\pi \div (2\pi) = \frac{4}{3}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi \left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 \left(\frac{9}{2}\right) = 8\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 2\frac{1}{4}\text{ ft}\), \(\text{circumference} = 3\frac{1}{2}\pi\text{ ft}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{\frac{7}{2}\pi}{2\pi} = \frac{7}{4}\text{ ft}\), and the height is \(h = \frac{9}{4}\text{ ft}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 \left(\frac{9}{4}\right) = \frac{441}{64}\pi\text{ ft}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 3\frac{1}{3}\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 6\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{6\pi}{2\pi} = 3\text{ cm}\), and the height is \(h = \frac{10}{3}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (3^2)\left(\frac{10}{3}\right) = 30\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 4\frac{1}{2}\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 5\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{5\pi}{2\pi} = \frac{5}{2}\text{ m}\), and the height is \(h = \frac{9}{2}\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^2 \left(\frac{9}{2}\right) = \frac{225}{8}\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 1\frac{3}{4}\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 4\frac{1}{2}\pi\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{\frac{9}{2}\pi}{2\pi} = \frac{9}{4}\text{ m}\), and the height is \(h = \frac{7}{4}\text{ m}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^2 \left(\frac{7}{4}\right) = \frac{567}{64}\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 2\frac{1}{2}\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 3\frac{1}{3}\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{C}{2\pi} = \frac{\frac{10}{3}\pi}{2\pi} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ cm}\), and the height is \(h = \frac{5}{2}\text{ cm}\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2 \left(\frac{5}{2}\right) = \frac{125}{18}\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with a \(90^\circ\) section removed, given the measurements of the original full cylinder: \(\text{height} = 8\text{ cm}\), \(\text{circumference} = 12\pi\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The radius of the base is \(r = \frac{12\pi}{2\pi} = 6\text{ cm}\), giving a full volume of \(V_{\text{full}} = \pi (6^2)(8) = 288\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Removing a \(90^\circ\) section leaves \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the cylinder, so \(V = \frac{3}{4}(288\pi) = 216\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 1.2\text{ m}\), \(\text{circumference} = 30\pi\text{ cm}\). Express your answer in cubic centimeters.
qs.s: Convert the height to centimeters to get \(h = 120\text{ cm}\), and find the radius \(r = \frac{30\pi}{2\pi} = 15\text{ cm}\). Then, calculate the volume: \(V = \pi (15^2)(120) = 27{,}000\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Two cylinders each have a height of \(10\text{ cm}\). Cylinder A has a base circumference of \(12\pi\text{ cm}\), and Cylinder B has a base circumference of \(16\pi\text{ cm}\). How much greater is the volume of Cylinder B than Cylinder A?
qs.s: The radius of Cylinder A is \(r_A = 6\text{ cm}\) and that of Cylinder B is \(r_B = 8\text{ cm}\). The difference in volume is \(V_B - V_A = \pi(8^2)(10) - \pi(6^2)(10) = 640\pi - 360\pi = 280\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylinder in terms of \(x\) with the given measurements: \(\text{height} = 5x\), \(\text{circumference} = 8\pi x\).
qs.s: The radius is \(r = \frac{8\pi x}{2\pi} = 4x\). The volume is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (4x)^2 (5x) = \pi (16x^2)(5x) = 80\pi x^3\).

qs.q: A hollow cylindrical pipe has \(\text{height} = 14\text{ cm}\), \(\text{outer circumference} = 16\pi\text{ cm}\), and \(\text{inner circumference} = 10\pi\text{ cm}\). Find the volume of the material used to make the pipe.
qs.s: The outer and inner radii are \(r_{\text{outer}} = 8\text{ cm}\) and \(r_{\text{inner}} = 5\text{ cm}\). The volume of material is \(V = \pi(r_{\text{outer}}^2 - r_{\text{inner}}^2)h = \pi(8^2 - 5^2)(14) = \pi(39)(14) = 546\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Rod 1 has a diameter of \(10\text{ mm}\) and a height of \(8\text{ mm}\). Rod 2 has a diameter of \(8\text{ mm}\) and a height of \(10\text{ mm}\). By how much does the volume of Rod 1 exceed the volume of Rod 2? Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Rod 1 has radius \(5\text{ mm}\) and volume \(V_1 = \pi(5^2)(8) = 200\pi\text{ mm}^3\), while Rod 2 has radius \(4\text{ mm}\) and volume \(V_2 = \pi(4^2)(10) = 160\pi\text{ mm}^3\). The volume of Rod 1 exceeds that of Rod 2 by \(200\pi - 160\pi = 40\pi\text{ mm}^3\).

qs.q: Can A has a diameter of \(14\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(6\text{ cm}\). Can B has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(14\text{ cm}\). How much greater is the volume of Can A than the volume of Can B? Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Can A has radius \(7\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_A = \pi(7^2)(6) = 294\pi\text{ cm}^3\), and Can B has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_B = \pi(3^2)(14) = 126\pi\text{ cm}^3\). The difference in volume is \(294\pi - 126\pi = 168\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Cylinder X has a diameter of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(8\text{ cm}\). Cylinder Y has a diameter of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(12\text{ cm}\). How much greater is the volume of Cylinder X than the volume of Cylinder Y? Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Cylinder X has radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_X = \pi(6^2)(8) = 288\pi\text{ cm}^3\), and Cylinder Y has radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_Y = \pi(4^2)(12) = 192\pi\text{ cm}^3\). The volume of Cylinder X exceeds that of Cylinder Y by \(288\pi - 192\pi = 96\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Container A has a diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(4\text{ cm}\). Container B has a diameter of \(4\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(10\text{ cm}\). How much greater is the volume of Container A than the volume of Container B? Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Container A has radius \(5\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_A = \pi(5^2)(4) = 100\pi\text{ cm}^3\), while Container B has radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_B = \pi(2^2)(10) = 40\pi\text{ cm}^3\). The volume of Container A is greater by \(100\pi - 40\pi = 60\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(6\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(8\text{ cm}\). How much greater is the volume of Cylinder A than the volume of Cylinder B? Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Cylinder A has radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_A = \pi(4^2)(6) = 96\pi\text{ cm}^3\), while Cylinder B has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_B = \pi(3^2)(8) = 72\pi\text{ cm}^3\). The difference in volume is \(96\pi - 72\pi = 24\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a radius of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(12\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a height of \(3\text{ cm}\). What must the diameter of Cylinder B be so that both cylinders have the same volume?
qs.s: The volume of Cylinder A is \(V_A = \pi(6^2)(12) = 432\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Equating this to Cylinder B's volume gives \(\pi r_B^2(3) = 432\pi\), so \(r_B^2 = 144\) and \(r_B = 12\text{ cm}\), making the diameter \(2 \times 12 = 24\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Silo A has a diameter of \(14\text{ m}\) and a height of \(15\text{ m}\). Silo B has a diameter of \(12\text{ m}\) and a height of \(20\text{ m}\). How much greater is the volume of Silo A than the volume of Silo B? Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
qs.s: Silo A has radius \(7\text{ m}\) with volume \(V_A = \pi(7^2)(15) = 735\pi\text{ m}^3\), and Silo B has radius \(6\text{ m}\) with volume \(V_B = \pi(6^2)(20) = 720\pi\text{ m}^3\). The difference is \(735\pi - 720\pi = 15\pi\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(5\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(8\text{ cm}\). By how much must the height of Cylinder B be increased so that both cylinders have the same volume?
qs.s: Cylinder A has volume \(V_A = \pi(6^2)(5) = 180\pi\text{ cm}^3\). For Cylinder B to reach \(180\pi\text{ cm}^3\), its height must satisfy \(\pi(3^2)h = 180\pi\), giving \(h = 20\text{ cm}\), which is an increase of \(20 - 8 = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(20\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(5\text{ cm}\). By how much must the radius of Cylinder B be increased so that its volume equals the volume of Cylinder A?
qs.s: Cylinder A has volume \(V_A = \pi(4^2)(20) = 320\pi\text{ cm}^3\). For Cylinder B with new radius \(r'\), \(\pi (r')^2(5) = 320\pi\) implies \((r')^2 = 64\) and \(r' = 8\text{ cm}\), which is an increase of \(8 - 5 = 3\text{ cm}\) over its original radius.

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(24\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has its radius equal to its height (\(r = h\)) and has the same volume as Cylinder A. What is the radius of Cylinder B?
qs.s: Cylinder A has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V_A = \pi(3^2)(24) = 216\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Setting \(V_B = \pi r^3 = 216\pi\) yields \(r^3 = 216\), which gives \(r = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If cylinder A has a diameter of \(4\text{ cm}\), with a height of \(9\text{ cm}\), and cylinder B has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) with a height of $2\text{ cm}: What new height of cylinder B would make its volume the same as cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(V_A = \pi (2)^2(9) = 36\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Equating this to cylinder B gives \(\pi (3)^2 h = 36\pi\), which solves to \(9h = 36\) or \(h = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If cylinder A has a diameter of \(8\text{ cm}\), with a height of \(3\text{ cm}\), and cylinder B has a diameter of \(4\text{ cm}\) with a height of \(8\text{ cm}\): What new height of cylinder B would make its volume the same as cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(V_A = \pi (4)^2(3) = 48\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Setting \(V_B = \pi (2)^2 h = 48\pi\) yields \(4h = 48\), so the new height is \(h = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If cylinder A has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\), with a height of \(12\text{ cm}\), and cylinder B has a diameter of \(12\text{ cm}\) with a height of $2\text{ cm}: What new height of cylinder B would make its volume the same as cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(V_A = \pi (3)^2(12) = 108\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Setting \(\pi (6)^2 h = 108\pi\) gives \(36h = 108\), which solves to \(h = 3\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If cylinder A has a diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\), with a height of \(8\text{ cm}\), and cylinder B has a diameter of \(8\text{ cm}\) with a height of $7\text{ cm}: What new height of cylinder B would make its volume the same as cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(V_A = \pi (5)^2(8) = 200\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Setting \(\pi (4)^2 h = 200\pi\) results in \(16h = 200\), so \(h = 12.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If cylinder A has a diameter of \(12\text{ cm}\), with a height of \(5\text{ cm}\), and cylinder B has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) with a height of $10\text{ cm}: What new height of cylinder B would make its volume the same as cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(V_A = \pi (6)^2(5) = 180\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Equating this to the volume of cylinder B gives \(\pi (3)^2 h = 180\pi\), which simplifies to \(9h = 180\) and gives \(h = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If cylinder A has a diameter of \(15\text{ cm}\), with a height of \(8\text{ cm}\), and cylinder B has a diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\) with a height of $12\text{ cm}: What new height of cylinder B would make its volume the same as cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(\pi (7.5)^2(8) = 450\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Equating this to cylinder B gives \(\pi (5)^2 h = 450\pi\), so \(25h = 450\) and \(h = 18\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(9\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a diameter of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(10\text{ cm}\). By how many centimeters must the height of cylinder B be decreased so that its volume equals the volume of cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(\pi (4)^2(9) = 144\pi\text{ cm}^3\). For cylinder B to match this volume, its height must be \(h = 144\pi / (\pi \cdot 6^2) = 4\text{ cm}\), meaning it must decrease by \(10 - 4 = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(16\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(9\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a height of \(4\text{ cm}\). What diameter must cylinder B have to make its volume equal to the volume of cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(\pi (8)^2(9) = 576\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Setting \(\pi r^2(4) = 576\pi\) yields \(r^2 = 144\), so \(r = 12\text{ cm}\) and the diameter is \(2 \times 12 = 24\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(18\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a height of \(8\text{ cm}\). What new diameter must cylinder B have to make its volume equal to the volume of cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(\pi (4)^2(18) = 288\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Equating to cylinder B gives \(\pi r^2(8) = 288\pi \implies r^2 = 36 \implies r = 6\text{ cm}\), giving a diameter of \(2 \times 6 = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter of \(10\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(9\text{ cm}\). Cylinder B has a diameter of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(15\text{ cm}\). By how many centimeters must the height of cylinder B be increased so that its volume equals the volume of cylinder A?
qs.s: The volume of cylinder A is \(\pi (5)^2(9) = 225\pi\text{ cm}^3\), so cylinder B needs a total height of \(h = 225\pi / (\pi \cdot 3^2) = 25\text{ cm}\). The required increase is \(25 - 15 = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Can A has half the diameter of Can B, but 3 times the height. What is the ratio of the volume of Can A to the volume of Can B?
qs.s: Halving the diameter scales the radius by \(\frac{1}{2}\) and the base area by \((\frac{1}{2})^2 = \frac{1}{4}\). Multiplying by \(3\) for the height gives \(\frac{1}{4} \times 3 = \frac{3}{4}\), so the ratio is \(3 : 4\).

qs.q: Cylinder M is twice as wide as Cylinder N and 3 times as tall. What is the ratio of the volume of Cylinder M to the volume of Cylinder N?
qs.s: Doubling the width scales the radius by \(2\) and the base area by \(2^2 = 4\). Multiplying by \(3\) for the height gives \(4 \times 3 = 12\), producing a ratio of \(12 : 1\).

qs.q: Cylinder X has 3 times the radius of cylinder Y, but only one-third the height. What is the ratio of the volume of cylinder X to the volume of cylinder Y?
qs.s: Using \(V = \pi r^2 h\), tripling the radius multiplies the volume by \(3^2 = 9\), and taking one-third the height multiplies it by \(\frac{1}{3}\), giving \(9 \times \frac{1}{3} = 3\), or a ratio of \(3 : 1\).

qs.q: Cylinder P has half the radius of cylinder Q, but twice the height. What is the ratio of the volume of cylinder P to the volume of cylinder Q?
qs.s: Halving the radius scales the base area by \((\frac{1}{2})^2 = \frac{1}{4}\), and doubling the height multiplies the volume by \(2\), yielding \(\frac{1}{4} \times 2 = \frac{1}{2}\), or a ratio of \(1 : 2\).

qs.q: Cylinder 1 is 4 times as tall as Cylinder 2, but has half the width. What is the ratio of the volume of Cylinder 1 to the volume of Cylinder 2?
qs.s: Halving the width scales the radius by \(\frac{1}{2}\), reducing the base area by \((\frac{1}{2})^2 = \frac{1}{4}\), while multiplying the height by \(4\) gives \(\frac{1}{4} \times 4 = 1\), resulting in a ratio of \(1 : 1\).

qs.q: Cylinder X has 18 times the volume of Cylinder Y, but only twice the height of Cylinder Y. How many times the radius of Cylinder Y is the radius of Cylinder X?
qs.s: From \(\frac{V_X}{V_Y} = (\frac{r_X}{r_Y})^2 \times \frac{h_X}{h_Y}\), we have \(18 = (\frac{r_X}{r_Y})^2 \times 2\), which gives \((\frac{r_X}{r_Y})^2 = 9\), so the radius ratio is \(\sqrt{9} = 3\).

qs.q: Cylinder B has 3 times the radius and \(\frac{1}{2}\) the height of Cylinder A. Cylinder C has \(\frac{2}{3}\) the radius and 4 times the height of Cylinder B. What is the ratio of the volume of Cylinder C to the volume of Cylinder A?
qs.s: Cylinder C has a radius of \(\frac{2}{3} \times 3 = 2\) times Cylinder A and a height of \(4 \times \frac{1}{2} = 2\) times Cylinder A, so its volume is \(2^2 \times 2 = 8\) times that of A, or \(8 : 1\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has a diameter that is \(\frac{3}{4}\) the diameter of Cylinder B, and a height that is \(\frac{8}{3}\) the height of Cylinder B. What is the ratio of the volume of Cylinder A to the volume of Cylinder B?
qs.s: The volume scales by the square of the diameter ratio times the height ratio, giving \((\frac{3}{4})^2 \times \frac{8}{3} = \frac{9}{16} \times \frac{8}{3} = \frac{3}{2}\), or a ratio of \(3 : 2\).

qs.q: A cylindrical tank has a volume of \(72\text{ m}^3\). A second tank has \(\frac{2}{3}\) the radius and \(\frac{5}{2}\) the height of the first tank. What is the volume of the second tank?
qs.s: Scaling the radius by \(\frac{2}{3}\) and height by \(\frac{5}{2}\) multiplies the volume by \((\frac{2}{3})^2 \times \frac{5}{2} = \frac{10}{9}\). The new volume is \(72 \times \frac{10}{9} = 80\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: Cylinder A has twice the radius and 3 times the height of Cylinder B. If the volume of Cylinder B is \(14\text{ cm}^3\), what is the difference between the volume of Cylinder A and the volume of Cylinder B?
qs.s: Cylinder A has a volume of \(2^2 \times 3 = 12\) times Cylinder B, which is \(12 \times 14 = 168\text{ cm}^3\). The difference between their volumes is \(168 - 14 = 154\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder with radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and height \(20\text{ cm}\) is melted down to form a solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The cylinder's volume is \(V = \pi (3^2)(20) = 180\pi \approx 565.49\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of the cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{180\pi} \approx 8.27\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder with diameter \(8\text{ cm}\) and height \(12\text{ cm}\) is melted down to form a solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 8 / 2 = 4\text{ cm}\), so the cylinder's volume is \(V = \pi (4^2)(12) = 192\pi \approx 603.19\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of the cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{192\pi} \approx 8.45\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder with diameter \(10\text{ cm}\) and height \(15\text{ cm}\) is melted down to form a solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 5\text{ cm}\), giving a cylinder volume of \(V = \pi (5^2)(15) = 375\pi \approx 1178.10\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of the cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{375\pi} \approx 10.56\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder with radius \(5\text{ cm}\) and height \(10\text{ cm}\) is melted down to form a solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The volume of the cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h = \pi (5^2)(10) = 250\pi \approx 785.40\text{ cm}^3\). Setting this equal to the volume of the cube \(s^3\), the side length is \(s = \sqrt[3]{250\pi} \approx 9.23\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid bronze cylinder with radius \(7\text{ cm}\) and height \(14\text{ cm}\) is melted down to form a solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The volume of the cylinder is \(V = \pi (7^2)(14) = 686\pi \approx 2155.13\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of the cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{686\pi} \approx 12.92\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two identical solid metal cylinders, each with radius \(5\text{ cm}\) and height \(18\text{ cm}\), are melted down and recast into a single solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The total volume of the two cylinders is \(2 \times \pi (5^2)(18) = 900\pi \approx 2827.43\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of the recast cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{900\pi} \approx 14.14\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder with radius \(8\text{ cm}\) and height \(18\text{ cm}\) has a \(90^\circ\) sector removed along its entire height. The remaining portion is melted down to form a solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The volume remaining is \(\frac{3}{4}\pi (8^2)(18) = 864\pi \approx 2714.34\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of the cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{864\pi} \approx 13.95\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A hollow metal cylinder has an outer radius of \(8\text{ cm}\), an inner radius of \(4\text{ cm}\), and a height of \(15\text{ cm}\). It is melted down and recast into a solid cube. Find the side length of the cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The volume of metal is \(V = \pi (8^2 - 4^2)(15) = \pi(48)(15) = 720\pi \approx 2261.95\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of the cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{720\pi} \approx 13.13\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder with radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and height \(12\text{ cm}\) is melted down and recast into \(4\) identical solid cubes. Find the side length of each cube to two decimal places.
qs.s: The volume of the cylinder is \(\pi (6^2)(12) = 432\pi\text{ cm}^3\), so each cube has a volume of \(\frac{432\pi}{4} = 108\pi\text{ cm}^3\). The side length of each cube is \(s = \sqrt[3]{108\pi} \approx 6.97\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder with radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and height \(25\text{ cm}\) is melted down and recast into a solid rectangular prism with a base measuring \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(15\text{ cm}\). Find the height of the prism to two decimal places.
qs.s: The volume of the cylinder is \(V = \pi (6^2)(25) = 900\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Dividing by the prism's base area of \(10 \times 15 = 150\text{ cm}^2\) gives a height of \(h = \frac{900\pi}{150} = 6\pi \approx 18.85\text{ cm}\).

exercises.name: Volume of cylinder with missing slice

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical watermelon carving with a diameter of \(30\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(8\text{ cm}\), if a wedge with a central angle of \(30^\circ\) is cut out.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 15\text{ cm}\). The remaining fraction of the cylinder is \(\frac{360^\circ - 30^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{11}{12}\), so the volume is \(\frac{11}{12} \cdot \pi \cdot 15^2 \cdot 8 = 1650\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical fruit pie with a diameter of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(5\text{ cm}\), if a slice with a central angle of \(120^\circ\) has been eaten.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 6\text{ cm}\). The remaining fraction of the pie is \(\frac{360^\circ - 120^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{2}{3}\), giving a volume of \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot \pi \cdot 6^2 \cdot 5 = 120\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a wheel of Gouda cheese with a diameter of \(24\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(10\text{ cm}\), if a slice with a central angle of \(90^\circ\) has been removed.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 12\text{ cm}\). The remaining portion represents \(\frac{360^\circ - 90^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{3}{4}\) of the full cylinder, so the remaining volume is \(\frac{3}{4} \cdot \pi \cdot 12^2 \cdot 10 = 1080\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical ice cream cake with a diameter of \(16\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(9\text{ cm}\), if a slice with a central angle of \(45^\circ\) is missing.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 8\text{ cm}\). The fraction of the cake remaining is \(\frac{360^\circ - 45^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{7}{8}\), which gives a volume of \(\frac{7}{8} \cdot \pi \cdot 8^2 \cdot 9 = 504\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical foam cushion with a diameter of \(40\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(12\text{ cm}\), if a sector with a central angle of \(45^\circ\) is missing.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 20\text{ cm}\). The remaining fraction is \(\frac{360^\circ - 45^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{7}{8}\), so the volume is \(\frac{7}{8} \cdot \pi \cdot 20^2 \cdot 12 = 4200\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical block of ice with a diameter of \(30\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(20\text{ cm}\), if two separate slices, each with a central angle of \(54^\circ\), are removed.
qs.s: The total angle removed is \(2 \times 54^\circ = 108^\circ\), leaving a fraction of \(\frac{360^\circ - 108^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{252}{360} = \frac{7}{10}\). With radius \(r = 15\text{ cm}\), the remaining volume is \(\frac{7}{10} \cdot \pi \cdot 15^2 \cdot 20 = 3150\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A two-tier cylindrical cake has a bottom tier with a radius of \(16\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(10\text{ cm}\), and a top tier with a radius of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(10\text{ cm}\). If a single slice with a central angle of \(45^\circ\) is cut out from both tiers, what is the total volume of the remaining cake?
qs.s: The total volume before cutting is \(\pi(16^2)(10) + \pi(8^2)(10) = 2560\pi + 640\pi = 3200\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Since a \(45^\circ\) slice is cut through both tiers, \(\frac{360^\circ - 45^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{7}{8}\) remains, giving \(\frac{7}{8} \cdot 3200\pi = 2800\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical display cake with a diameter of \(36\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(15\text{ cm}\), if three slices with central angles of \(35^\circ\), \(40^\circ\), and \(45^\circ\) have been removed.
qs.s: The total angle removed is \(35^\circ + 40^\circ + 45^\circ = 120^\circ\), leaving \(\frac{360^\circ - 120^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{2}{3}\) of the cake. With radius \(r = 18\text{ cm}\), the volume is \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot \pi \cdot 18^2 \cdot 15 = 3240\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: Find the exact volume of a cylindrical block of granite with a diameter of \(20\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(15\text{ cm}\), if a wedge with a central angle of \(75^\circ\) is cut out.
qs.s: The radius is \(r = 10\text{ cm}\) and the fraction remaining is \(\frac{360^\circ - 75^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{285}{360} = \frac{19}{24}\). The remaining volume is \(\frac{19}{24} \cdot \pi \cdot 10^2 \cdot 15 = \frac{2375}{2}\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A cake is shaped like a cylinder of outer diameter \(20\text{ cm}\) with a cylindrical hole of diameter \(4\text{ cm}\) through its centre, and has a height of \(9\text{ cm}\). If a slice with a central angle of \(60^\circ\) is removed, what is the volume of the remaining cake?
qs.s: The full volume before cutting is \((\pi \cdot 10^2 - \pi \cdot 2^2) \cdot 9 = 96\pi \cdot 9 = 864\pi\text{ cm}^3\). With a \(60^\circ\) slice removed, the remaining volume is \(\frac{360^\circ - 60^\circ}{360^\circ} \cdot 864\pi = \frac{5}{6} \cdot 864\pi = 720\pi\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume. The rectangular prism has a length of \(2\pi\text{ cm}\), and its height is the same as the cylinder's height. If the cylinder has a radius of \(8\text{ cm}\), what is the width of the prism?
qs.s: Since both shapes have the same height \(h\), their volumes satisfy \(l \cdot w \cdot h = \pi r^2 h\), which simplifies to \(2\pi \cdot w = \pi (8)^2 = 64\pi\). Dividing both sides by \(2\pi\) gives \(w = 32\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume and equal heights. The rectangular prism has a width of \(4\pi\text{ cm}\). If the cylinder has a radius of \(10\text{ cm}\), what is the length of the rectangular prism?
qs.s: Equating the volumes with equal heights gives \(l \cdot w \cdot h = \pi r^2 h\), which reduces to \(l \cdot 4\pi = \pi (10)^2 = 100\pi\). Dividing by \(4\pi\) yields \(l = 25\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume. The rectangular prism has a width of \(3\pi\text{ in.}\), and a height equal to that of the cylinder. If the cylinder has a radius of \(9\text{ in.}\), what is the length of the rectangular prism?
qs.s: Since the heights are equal, the base areas must be equal, so \(l \cdot 3\pi = \pi (9)^2 = 81\pi\). Dividing both sides by \(3\pi\) results in \(l = 27\text{ in.}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume and the same height. If the cylinder has a radius of \(4\text{ cm}\) and the rectangular prism has a length of \(\pi\text{ cm}\), what is the width of the rectangular prism?
qs.s: Equating the volume formulas and canceling the common height gives \(l \cdot w = \pi r^2\), so \(\pi \cdot w = \pi (4)^2 = 16\pi\). Dividing both sides by \(\pi\) gives \(w = 16\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume. The rectangular prism has a length of \(6\pi\text{ mm}\), and its height is equal to the cylinder's height. If the cylinder has a radius of \(12\text{ mm}\), what is the width of the rectangular prism?
qs.s: Setting the volumes equal with equal heights gives \(l \cdot w = \pi r^2\), meaning \(6\pi \cdot w = \pi (12)^2 = 144\pi\). Dividing both sides by \(6\pi\) gives \(w = 24\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder has a radius of \(6\text{ m}\) and a height of \(10\text{ m}\). A rectangular prism with the same volume has a length of \(9\pi\text{ m}\) and a width of \(8\text{ m}\). What is the height of the prism?
qs.s: The cylinder's volume is \(\pi (6^2)(10) = 360\pi\text{ m}^3\). Equating this to the prism's volume \((9\pi)(8)(h) = 72\pi h\) gives \(h = \frac{360\pi}{72\pi} = 5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume. The cylinder has a diameter of \(16\text{ cm}\). The height of the rectangular prism is twice the height of the cylinder, and the length of the prism is \(8\pi\text{ cm}\). What is the width of the prism?
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(r = 8\text{ cm}\) and volume \(V = \pi (8^2) h = 64\pi h\). Setting this equal to the prism's volume \(V = (8\pi)(w)(2h) = 16\pi h \cdot w\), we find \(w = \frac{64\pi h}{16\pi h} = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume. The cylinder has a radius of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(20\text{ cm}\). The rectangular prism has a square base and a height of \(5\pi\text{ cm}\). What is the side length of the prism's base?
qs.s: The cylinder's volume is \(\pi (12^2)(20) = 2880\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Setting this equal to the prism's volume \(s^2 \cdot (5\pi)\) yields \(s^2 = \frac{2880\pi}{5\pi} = 576\), so \(s = \sqrt{576} = 24\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume. The cylinder has a radius of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(h\). The rectangular prism has a height of \(\frac{2}{3}h\) and a width of \(8\pi\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the rectangular prism?
qs.s: The cylinder's volume is \(\pi (12^2) h = 144\pi h\). Equating this to the prism's volume \(l \cdot (8\pi) \cdot \left(\frac{2}{3}h\right) = \frac{16}{3}\pi h \cdot l\), we solve for \(l = 144 \div \frac{16}{3} = 27\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder and a rectangular prism have the same volume. The cylinder has a diameter of \(20\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(14\text{ cm}\). The rectangular prism has a width of \(7\pi\text{ cm}\) and a height of \(8\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the rectangular prism?
qs.s: The cylinder has radius \(10\text{ cm}\), giving volume \(\pi (10^2)(14) = 1400\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Setting this equal to the prism's volume \(l \times 7\pi \times 8 = 56\pi l\), we get \(l = \frac{1400\pi}{56\pi} = 25\text{ cm}\).

exercises.name: Find radius from volume and dimension ratio

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(128\pi\). If the diameter is equal to the height, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since the diameter equals the height, \(h = 2r\). Substituting into the volume formula gives \(V = \pi r^2(2r) = 2\pi r^3 = 128\pi\), so \(r^3 = 64\) and \(r = 4\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(48\pi\). If the height is three times the diameter, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since \(h = 3d = 6r\), the volume is \(V = \pi r^2(6r) = 6\pi r^3 = 48\pi\). Dividing by \(6\pi\) gives \(r^3 = 8\), so \(r = 2\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(125\pi\). If the diameter is twice the height, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since \(d = 2h\) and \(d = 2r\), we have \(2r = 2h\), so \(h = r\). Substituting into the volume formula gives \(V = \pi r^3 = 125\pi\), which yields \(r^3 = 125\) and \(r = 5\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(216\pi\). If the diameter is one-fourth the height, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since \(d = \frac{1}{4}h\), we have \(h = 4d = 8r\). Substituting into the volume formula gives \(V = \pi r^2(8r) = 8\pi r^3 = 216\pi\), so \(r^3 = 27\) and \(r = 3\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(80\pi\). If the height is five times the diameter, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since the height is five times the diameter, \(h = 5(2r) = 10r\). Then \(V = \pi r^2(10r) = 10\pi r^3 = 80\pi\), which gives \(r^3 = 8\) and \(r = 2\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(\frac{27}{2}\pi\). If the height is twice the diameter, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since \(h = 2d = 4r\), the volume is \(V = \pi r^2(4r) = 4\pi r^3 = \frac{27}{2}\pi\). Dividing by \(4\pi\) gives \(r^3 = \frac{27}{8}\), which yields \(r = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(1715\pi\). If the diameter is two-fifths of the height, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since \(2r = \frac{2}{5}h\), we have \(h = 5r\). Substituting this into \(V = \pi r^2 h\) yields \(5\pi r^3 = 1715\pi\), which gives \(r^3 = 343\) and \(r = 7\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(972\pi\). If the height is two-thirds of the diameter, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Writing the height in terms of the radius gives \(h = \frac{2}{3}(2r) = \frac{4}{3}r\). Then \(V = \pi r^2\left(\frac{4}{3}r\right) = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 972\pi\), so \(r^3 = 729\) and \(r = 9\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(160\pi\). If the diameter is four-fifths of the height, find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: Since \(2r = \frac{4}{5}h\), we have \(h = \frac{5}{2}r\). Substituting into the volume formula gives \(V = \pi r^2\left(\frac{5}{2}r\right) = \frac{5}{2}\pi r^3 = 160\pi\), which gives \(r^3 = 64\) and \(r = 4\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is \(324\pi\). If the height is three-fourths of the diameter, find the radius of the cylinder.
