qs.s: Because \(AB \parallel CD\), the alternate interior angles make \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE\). Using the proportion \(\frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{BE}{CE}\), we have \(\frac{8}{12} = \frac{6}{x}\), which gives \(2x = 18\) and \(x = 9\).

qs.q: The two triangles shown are similar: \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Use the figure to find the length of side \(DF\), labeled \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\), corresponding sides are proportional: \(\frac{AB}{DE} = \frac{AC}{DF}\). Substituting the given values gives \(\frac{4}{10} = \frac{6}{x}\), which cross-multiplies to \(4x = 60\), so \(x = 15\).

qs.q: In the figure, both \(DE\) and \(AB\) are perpendicular to the ground segment \(CB\). Find the height \(AB\), labeled \(x\).
qs.s: Since both segments are perpendicular to \(CB\), \(\triangle CDE \sim \triangle CAB\). With \(CB = 4 + 8 = 12\), set up \(\frac{CE}{CB} = \frac{DE}{AB}\), which gives \(\frac{4}{12} = \frac{3}{x}\), so \(x = 9\).

qs.q: The two right triangles shown are similar: \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Find the length of side \(EF\), labeled \(x\).
qs.s: Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional: \(\frac{AB}{DE} = \frac{BC}{EF}\). Substituting the given dimensions yields \(\frac{6}{9} = \frac{8}{x}\), which simplifies to \(6x = 72\), so \(x = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, line segment \(BC\) is parallel to \(DE\). Find the length of \(DE\), labeled \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(BC \parallel DE\), \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADE\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{AB}{AD} = \frac{BC}{DE}\) with \(AD = 3 + 6 = 9\) gives \(\frac{3}{9} = \frac{4}{x}\), so \(x = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, segments \(AD\) and \(BC\) intersect at point \(E\), and \(AB \parallel CD\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(AB \parallel CD\), \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE\). Setting up \(\frac{AE}{ED} = \frac{BE}{EC}\) gives \(\frac{3x-2}{14} = \frac{8}{16} = \frac{1}{2}\), which gives \(2(3x - 2) = 14\), so \(6x = 18\) and \(x = 3\).

qs.q: In the figure, line segment \(BC\) is parallel to \(DE\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(BC \parallel DE\), \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADE\), so \(\frac{AB}{AD} = \frac{BC}{DE}\). With \(AD = (x + 1) + 6 = x + 7\), we get \(\frac{x+1}{x+7} = \frac{8}{20} = \frac{2}{5}\), which simplifies to \(5x + 5 = 2x + 14\), yielding \(x = 3\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\angle ADE\) and \(\angle C\) are equal angles of \(45^\circ\). Find the length of side \(AC\), labeled \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(\triangle ADE\) and \(\triangle ACB\) share \(\angle A\) and have \(\angle ADE = \angle C = 45^\circ\), they are similar by AA (\(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ACB\)). Setting up \(\frac{AD}{AC} = \frac{AE}{AB}\) with \(AB = 8 + 1 = 9\) gives \(\frac{8}{x} = \frac{6}{9}\), which solves to \(x = 12\).

qs.q: The two triangles shown are similar: \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Use the given dimensions to find the value of \(x + y\).
qs.s: The scale factor from \(\triangle ABC\) to \(\triangle DEF\) is \(\frac{DE}{AB} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5\). Therefore, \(x = 12 \times 1.5 = 18\) and \(y = 14 \times 1.5 = 21\), so \(x + y = 18 + 21 = 39\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(DE \parallel BC\) and \(\angle B = 90^\circ\). Find the length of segment \(DB\), labeled \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(DE \parallel BC\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). Using the proportion \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC}\) with \(AB = 6 + x\) gives \(\frac{6}{6+x} = \frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}\), which solves to \(6 + x = 18\), so \(x = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, segment \(DE\) is parallel to segment \(BC\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). The total length of side \(AB\) is \(AD + DB = 3 + 3 = 6\). Using the proportion \(\frac{BC}{DE} = \frac{AB}{AD}\), we get \(\frac{x}{5} = \frac{6}{3} = 2\), which gives \(x = 10\).

qs.q: A vertical post of height \(2\text{ m}\) casts a shadow of \(3\text{ m}\). At the same time, a nearby flagpole casts a shadow of \(9\text{ m}\). Using the similar triangles shown in the figure, find the height \(h\) of the flagpole.
qs.s: The triangles formed by the objects and their shadows are similar, so corresponding sides are proportional: \(\frac{h}{2} = \frac{9}{3}\). Solving gives \(h = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\), corresponding sides are proportional: \(\frac{EF}{BC} = \frac{DE}{AB}\). Substituting the given lengths gives \(\frac{x}{8} = \frac{9}{6}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{9 \times 8}{6} = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, line segment \(AB\) is parallel to line segment \(CD\), intersecting at \(E\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(AB \parallel CD\), alternate interior angles give \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{ED}{BE} = \frac{CD}{AB}\) yields \(\frac{x}{6} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5\), so \(x = 9\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DFE\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: From the similarity statement \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DFE\), side \(AB\) corresponds to side \(DF\), and side \(AC\) corresponds to side \(DE\). Thus, \(\frac{DE}{AC} = \frac{DF}{AB}\), which gives \(\frac{x}{4} = \frac{15}{5} = 3\), so \(x = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, both \(DE\) and \(BC\) are perpendicular to \(AB\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Since both segments are perpendicular to \(AB\), \(DE \parallel BC\) and \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{AB}{AD} = \frac{BC}{DE}\) gives \(\frac{5 + x}{5} = \frac{10.5}{3.5} = 3\), so \(5 + x = 15\), yielding \(x = 10\).

qs.q: In the figure, line segment \(DE\) is parallel to \(BC\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(DE \parallel BC\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\), meaning \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC}\). Substituting side lengths gives \(\frac{4}{4 + x} = \frac{6}{15} = \frac{2}{5}\). Cross-multiplying yields \(2(4 + x) = 20\), so \(8 + 2x = 20\) and \(x = 6\).

qs.q: In the figure, line segment \(AB\) is parallel to line segment \(CD\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(AB \parallel CD\), \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE\). Corresponding sides are proportional: \(\frac{AE}{ED} = \frac{AB}{CD}\), which gives \(\frac{3x - 2}{15} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3}\). Cross-multiplying yields \(3(3x - 2) = 30\), so \(3x - 2 = 10\), giving \(3x = 12\) and \(x = 4\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\angle B = 90^\circ\) and segment \(DE\) is perpendicular to segment \(AC\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Both \(\triangle ADE\) and \(\triangle ABC\) share \(\angle A\) and have a right angle, so \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\) by AA similarity. Corresponding sides give \(\frac{AB}{AD} = \frac{BC}{DE}\), so \(\frac{x}{5} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\), which results in \(x = 15\).

qs.q: A vertical post of height \(3\text{ m}\) casts a shadow of \(4\text{ m}\) on level ground. At the same time, a nearby tree casts a shadow of \(16\text{ m}\). Using the similar triangles formed by the sun's rays, find the height \(h\) of the tree.
qs.s: The ratio of the tree's height to its shadow equals the ratio of the post's height to its shadow: \(\frac{h}{3} = \frac{16}{4} = 4\). Solving for \(h\) gives \(h = 3 \times 4 = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Find the length of side \(DF\) (labeled \(x\)).
qs.s: Because the triangles are similar, corresponding sides are in proportion: \(\frac{DF}{AC} = \frac{DE}{AB}\). Setting up the ratio gives \(\frac{x}{6} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5\), so \(x = 6 \times 1.5 = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: In the figure, segment \(DE\) is parallel to side \(BC\), which forms similar triangles \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). Find the length of \(BC\) (labeled \(x\)).
qs.s: The length of side \(AB\) is \(4 + 6 = 10\). Using the proportion of similar triangles, \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC} \implies \frac{4}{10} = \frac{6}{x}\), which gives \(4x = 60\), so \(x = 15\).

qs.q: The two right triangles shown are similar, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Find the length of the hypotenuse \(x\).
qs.s: Set up a proportion between corresponding sides: \(\frac{DF}{AC} = \frac{DE}{AB}\). Substituting gives \(\frac{x}{10} = \frac{9}{6} = 1.5\), so \(x = 10 \times 1.5 = 15\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: In the figure, segment \(AB\) is parallel to segment \(CD\) (\(AB \parallel CD\)), so \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Since the triangles are similar, corresponding sides are in proportion: \(\frac{ED}{AE} = \frac{CD}{AB}\). Substituting the given lengths yields \(\frac{x}{6} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5\), giving \(x = 9\).

qs.q: In \(\triangle ABC\), segment \(DE\) is parallel to \(BC\), which forms similar triangles \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). Solve for \(x\).
qs.s: The full side length is \(AB = 6 + 9 = 15\). By similarity, \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC} \implies \frac{6}{15} = \frac{x+1}{3x-1}\). Simplifying to \(\frac{2}{5} = \frac{x+1}{3x-1}\) and cross-multiplying yields \(2(3x - 1) = 5(x + 1) \implies 6x - 2 = 5x + 5\), so \(x = 7\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(DE \parallel BC\), forming similar triangles \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). Given the lengths shown, find the length of segment \(EC\) (labeled \(x\)).
qs.s: The full length \(AB\) is \(12 + 16 = 28\text{ m}\). Using similar triangles, \(\frac{AE}{AC} = \frac{AD}{AB} \implies \frac{15}{AC} = \frac{12}{28} = \frac{3}{7}\), which yields \(AC = 35\text{ m}\). Therefore, \(x = AC - AE = 35 - 15 = 20\text{ m}\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Based on the given side lengths, find the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\).
qs.s: The ratio of corresponding sides is \(\frac{DE}{AB} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5\). The perimeter of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(8 + 10 + 14 = 32\text{ cm}\), so multiplying by the scale factor gives the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\) as \(32 \times 1.5 = 48\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(AB \parallel CD\), which makes \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE\). Find the total length of segment \(AD\).
qs.s: By similarity, \(\frac{ED}{AE} = \frac{CD}{AB} \implies \frac{2x - 1}{x + 2} = \frac{18}{12} = \frac{3}{2}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(2(2x - 1) = 3(x + 2) \implies 4x - 2 = 3x + 6\), so \(x = 8\). Then \(AE = 8 + 2 = 10\) and \(ED = 2(8) - 1 = 15\), giving a total length \(AD = 10 + 15 = 25\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Find the value of \(x + y\).
qs.s: The scale factor from \(\triangle ABC\) to \(\triangle DEF\) is \(\frac{15}{6} = 2.5\). Thus, \(x = 8 \times 2.5 = 20\) and \(y = 7 \times 2.5 = 17.5\), giving \(x + y = 20 + 17.5 = 37.5\).

qs.q: In the figure, segment \(\overline{ST}\) is parallel to segment \(\overline{QR}\). Use the given lengths to find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(\overline{ST} \parallel \overline{QR}\), \(\triangle PST \sim \triangle PQR\). Side \(PQ = 4 + 8 = 12\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{PS}{PQ} = \frac{ST}{QR}\) gives \(\frac{4}{12} = \frac{5}{x}\), so \(x = 15\).

qs.q: In the figure, a \(4\text{ m}\) vertical pole \(\overline{BD}\) casts a shadow \(\overline{AB}\) of length \(6\text{ m}\). A vertical tree \(\overline{CE}\) casts a shadow along the same line. Find the height of the tree, \(h\).
qs.s: Triangles \(\triangle ABD\) and \(\triangle ACE\) are similar by AA similarity. The total shadow length is \(AC = 6 + 12 = 18\text{ m}\). Using the proportion \(\frac{CE}{BD} = \frac{AC}{AB}\), we get \(\frac{h}{4} = \frac{18}{6} = 3\), so \(h = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) intersect at point \(E\), and \(\angle A = \angle B = 90^\circ\). Find the length of \(\overline{BD}\), labeled as \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(\angle A = \angle B = 90^\circ\) and vertical angles at \(E\) are equal, \(\triangle ACE \sim \triangle BDE\). Using the proportion \(\frac{BD}{AC} = \frac{EB}{AE}\), we have \(\frac{x}{6} = \frac{12}{8}\), which yields \(x = 9\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Find the length of side \(\overline{EF}\), labeled as \(x\).
qs.s: Since the triangles are similar, corresponding sides are proportional: \(\frac{DE}{AB} = \frac{EF}{BC}\), which gives \(\frac{9}{6} = \frac{x}{8}\). Cross-multiplying yields \(6x = 72\), so \(x = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because the triangles are similar, corresponding sides are proportional: \(\frac{EF}{BC} = \frac{DE}{AB}\). Substituting the given lengths yields \(\frac{x}{10} = \frac{12}{8}\), so \(x = \frac{12 \times 10}{8} = 15\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\), and both are right triangles. Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: First calculate the hypotenuse of \(\triangle ABC\) using the Pythagorean theorem: \(AC = \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = 15\). Since \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\), the ratio of corresponding sides gives \(\frac{DE}{AB} = \frac{DF}{AC}\), so \(\frac{x}{9} = \frac{25}{15} = \frac{5}{3}\), which gives \(x = 15\).

qs.q: Based on the angle measures and side lengths given in the figure, find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Both triangles share angle measures of \(60^\circ\) and \(50^\circ\), so \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle EDF\). Side \(\overline{DE}\) corresponds to \(\overline{AB}\) between the \(60^\circ\) and \(50^\circ\) angles, giving a scale factor of \(\frac{12}{15} = \frac{4}{5}\). Side \(x\) lies between the \(60^\circ\) and unmarked angles, corresponding to side length 20, so \(x = 20 \times \frac{4}{5} = 16\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}\). Find the values of the missing sides \(x\) and \(y\).
qs.s: Since \(\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{CD}\), \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE\). Using the ratio \(\frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{12}{18} = \frac{2}{3}\), we set up \(\frac{AE}{ED} = \frac{8}{x} = \frac{2}{3}\) to find \(x = 12\), and \(\frac{BE}{EC} = \frac{y}{15} = \frac{2}{3}\) to find \(y = 10\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\). Solve for \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). The total length of \(\overline{AB}\) is \(5 + 10 = 15\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC}\) gives \(\frac{5}{15} = \frac{x}{x + 8}\), or \(\frac{1}{3} = \frac{x}{x + 8}\). Cross-multiplying yields \(3x = x + 8\), so \(2x = 8\) and \(x = 4\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\overline{AB} \perp \overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{DE} \perp \overline{BC}\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Both segments are perpendicular to \(\overline{BC}\), so \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{AB}\) and \(\triangle CDE \sim \triangle CBA\). The total length \(BC = 8.4 + 5.6 = 14.0\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{DE}{AB} = \frac{CE}{CB}\) gives \(\frac{7.2}{x} = \frac{8.4}{14.0} = 0.6\), so \(x = \frac{7.2}{0.6} = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, the two right triangles are similar (\(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\)). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because the triangles are similar, corresponding sides are proportional: \(\frac{x}{8} = \frac{9}{6}\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{9 \times 8}{6} = 12\).

qs.q: In the figure, line segment \(DE\) is parallel to \(BC\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). The total side length \(AB = 4 + 6 = 10\), so \(\frac{4}{10} = \frac{6}{x}\), which gives \(x = 15\).

qs.q: The two triangles shown are similar (\(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR\)). Find the length of side \(QR\), denoted by \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR\), the corresponding sides are in proportion: \(\frac{QR}{BC} = \frac{PQ}{AB}\). Substituting the values yields \(\frac{x}{6} = \frac{20}{8}\), giving \(x = 15\).

qs.q: In the figure, both \(DE\) and \(BC\) are perpendicular to \(AB\). Find the height \(x\).
qs.s: The triangles share \(\angle A\) and both contain a right angle, so \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). The entire base length is \(AB = 6 + 9 = 15\), so \(\frac{x}{4} = \frac{15}{6}\), which results in \(x = 10\).

qs.q: In the figure, segments \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at point \(E\), and line segment \(AB\) is parallel to \(CD\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Because \(AB \parallel CD\), \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE\). Setting up the proportion of corresponding sides gives \(\frac{x}{8} = \frac{9}{6}\), which simplifies to \(x = 12\).

qs.q: In the triangle shown, line segment \(DE\) is parallel to \(BC\). Find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), by the side splitter theorem \(\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{AE}{EC}\). Thus, \(\frac{x}{9} = \frac{x+2}{15}\). Cross-multiplying yields \(15x = 9x + 18\), so \(6x = 18\) and \(x = 3\).

qs.q: In the figure, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\). Calculate the value of \(x + y\).
qs.s: The scale factor from \(\triangle ABC\) to \(\triangle DEF\) is \(\frac{9}{6} = 1.5\). Thus, \(x = 8 \times 1.5 = 12\) and \(y = 10 \times 1.5 = 15\). Their sum is \(x + y = 12 + 15 = 27\).

qs.q: In right triangle \(\triangle ABC\), \(CD\) is the altitude to the hypotenuse \(AB\). Using the similar triangles \(\triangle ACD \sim \triangle CBD\), find the length of \(h\).
qs.s: From \(\triangle ACD \sim \triangle CBD\), the ratio of the corresponding legs gives \(\frac{h}{AD} = \frac{BD}{h}\), so \(\frac{h}{4} = \frac{9}{h}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(h^2 = 36\), which yields \(h = 6\).

qs.q: In the figure, segments \(AD\) and \(BC\) intersect at \(E\), and \(AB \parallel CD\). Find the total length of line segment \(AD\).
qs.s: Because \(AB \parallel CD\), \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE\). Then \(\frac{x - 1}{x + 3} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}\). Solving gives \(3(x - 1) = 2(x + 3) \implies 3x - 3 = 2x + 6 \implies x = 9\). Thus, the total length is \(AD = (9 - 1) + (9 + 3) = 8 + 12 = 20\).

qs.q: In \(\triangle ABC\), point \(D\) lies on \(AB\) and point \(E\) lies on \(AC\) such that \(\angle ADE = \angle ACB\). Find the length of side \(AC\).
qs.s: Because \(\angle A\) is shared and \(\angle ADE = \angle ACB\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ACB\) by AA similarity. Therefore, \(\frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{AD}{AE}\). Since \(AB = 4 + 6 = 10\), we have \(\frac{AC}{10} = \frac{4}{5}\), giving \(AC = 8\).

qs.q: A vertical signpost that is 2.5 metres tall casts a shadow of 1.5 metres. At the same time, an office building casts a shadow of 21 metres. What is the height of the office building?
qs.s: Setting up the proportion \(\frac{h}{21} = \frac{2.5}{1.5}\), we solve for the building's height: \(h = \frac{2.5 \times 21}{1.5} = 35\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A surveyor who is 1.6 metres tall casts a shadow that is 1.2 metres long. At the same moment, a cell phone tower casts a shadow that is 45 metres long. What is the height of the cell phone tower?
qs.s: Setting up the proportion \(\frac{h}{45} = \frac{1.6}{1.2}\), we find \(h = \frac{1.6 \times 45}{1.2} = 60\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A statue that is 3.6 metres tall casts a shadow that is 2.4 metres long. At the same time, how long is the shadow cast by a 9-metre-tall telephone pole?
qs.s: Setting up the proportion \(\frac{s}{9} = \frac{2.4}{3.6}\), we find the shadow length \(s = \frac{2.4 \times 9}{3.6} = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A 1.8-metre-tall person casts a shadow that is 2.4 metres long. At the same time, a nearby streetlamp casts a shadow that is 6 metres long. What is the height of the streetlamp?
qs.s: Setting up the proportion \(\frac{h}{6} = \frac{1.8}{2.4}\), we cross-multiply to find \(h = \frac{1.8 \times 6}{2.4} = 4.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A fence post 2 metres tall casts a shadow that is 3.2 metres long. At the same time, a water tower casts a shadow that is 24 metres long. What is the height of the water tower?
qs.s: Setting up the proportion \(\frac{h}{24} = \frac{2}{3.2}\), we find \(h = \frac{2 \times 24}{3.2} = 15\text{ m}\).

qs.q: In the morning, a 12-metre flagpole casts an 8-metre shadow. In the afternoon, the sun's position changes so that a 1.5-metre vertical stick casts a 0.6-metre shadow. How much did the flagpole's shadow decrease in length between the two times?
qs.s: In the afternoon, the flagpole's shadow length \(s\) satisfies \(\frac{s}{12} = \frac{0.6}{1.5}\), which gives \(s = 4.8\text{ m}\). The shadow decreased by \(8 - 4.8 = 3.2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A fence post of height 180 cm casts a shadow of 2.4 m. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow of 16 m and a flagpole casts a shadow of 10 m. How many metres taller is the tree than the flagpole?
qs.s: Converting \(180\text{ cm} = 1.8\text{ m}\), the height-to-shadow ratio is \(\frac{1.8}{2.4} = 0.75\). The difference between their shadow lengths is \(16 - 10 = 6\text{ m}\), so the tree is \(6 \times 0.75 = 4.5\text{ m}\) taller than the flagpole.

qs.q: A straight ramp rises to a platform that is 4.5 metres high. A vertical support brace is installed under the ramp at a horizontal distance of 14 metres from the bottom of the ramp, where the ramp reaches a height of 1.5 metres. What is the remaining horizontal distance from the brace to the platform?
qs.s: Let the remaining horizontal distance be \(x\), making the total run \(14 + x\). By similar triangles, \(\frac{1.5}{4.5} = \frac{14}{14 + x}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{1}{3} = \frac{14}{14 + x}\), so \(14 + x = 42\) and \(x = 28\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two vertical poles stand on level ground. The shorter pole is 3 metres tall and casts a shadow of \(x\) metres. The taller pole is 5 metres tall, and its shadow is 4 metres longer than the shorter pole's shadow. What is the length of the shorter pole's shadow?
qs.s: Equating the height-to-shadow ratios gives \(\frac{3}{x} = \frac{5}{x + 4}\). Cross-multiplying yields \(3(x + 4) = 5x\), which simplifies to \(2x = 12\), giving \(x = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A 1.8-metre-tall person stands 6 metres away from the base of a streetlamp. The person casts a 3-metre shadow along the ground pointing directly away from the streetlamp. What is the height of the streetlamp?
qs.s: The streetlamp and the person form similar right triangles with the tip of the shadow, so the total base is \(6 + 3 = 9\text{ m}\). Using the proportion \(\frac{h}{9} = \frac{1.8}{3}\), we get \(h = 9 \times 0.6 = 5.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An art museum produces a miniature postcard replica of a rectangular painting. The original painting is 24 cm wide by 36 cm long. The replica is similar and has a length of 27 cm. What is the width of the replica?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{w}{27} = \frac{24}{36}\). Solving for \(w\) gives \(w = 27 \times \frac{2}{3} = 18\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular postcard measures 10 cm wide by 16 cm long. A similar greeting card is made with a length of 24 cm. What is the width of the greeting card?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{w}{24} = \frac{10}{16}\). Solving for \(w\) gives \(w = 24 \times \frac{5}{8} = 15\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two photographic prints of a landscape are made. The smaller print is 12 cm wide by 18 cm long. The larger print is similar and has a length of 45 cm. What is the width of the larger print?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{w}{45} = \frac{12}{18}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(18w = 540\), so \(w = 30\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A photograph measuring 6 cm wide by 9 cm long is enlarged to make a poster. The enlarged poster has a width of 15 cm. What is the length of the enlarged poster?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{L}{15} = \frac{9}{6}\). Solving for \(L\) gives \(L = 15 \times 1.5 = 22.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two similar rectangular computer monitors are designed with the same aspect ratio. The smaller monitor has a height of 16 cm and a width of 28 cm. If the larger monitor has a width of 35 cm, what is its height?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{h}{35} = \frac{16}{28}\). Solving for \(h\) gives \(h = 35 \times \frac{4}{7} = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A graphic designer is scaling a rectangular banner so that the new banner is similar to the original. The original banner is 15 cm wide and 24 cm long. In the new banner, the width is \(x\text{ cm}\) and the length is \((x + 18)\text{ cm}\). What is the width of the new banner?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{x}{x + 18} = \frac{15}{24} = \frac{5}{8}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(8x = 5(x + 18) = 5x + 90\), so \(3x = 90\) and \(x = 30\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two similar rectangular fields have perimeters proportional to their corresponding sides. The smaller field has a width of 45 m and a length of 60 m. If the larger field has a perimeter of 350 m, what is the length of the larger field?
qs.s: The perimeter of the smaller field is \(2(45 + 60) = 210\text{ m}\). Using the ratio of perimeters, \(\frac{L}{60} = \frac{350}{210} = \frac{5}{3}\), which gives \(L = 60 \times \frac{5}{3} = 100\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A photographic print measuring 8 cm wide by 12 cm long is enlarged so that its length becomes 30 cm. What is the perimeter of the enlarged print?
qs.s: First find the enlarged width using \(\frac{w}{30} = \frac{8}{12}\), giving \(w = 20\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of the enlarged print is \(2(30 + 20) = 100\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular print has a width of \(x\text{ cm}\) and a length that is 5 cm longer than its width. An enlargement of the print is similar and measures 36 cm wide by 51 cm long. What is the width of the original print?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{x}{x + 5} = \frac{36}{51} = \frac{12}{17}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(17x = 12(x + 5) = 12x + 60\), which simplifies to \(5x = 60\), so \(x = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A regular photo is 12 cm wide and 16 cm long. A similar enlarged copy has a width of 18 cm. By how many square centimeters does the area of the enlarged copy exceed the area of the regular photo?
qs.s: The enlarged length is \(L = 16 \times \frac{18}{12} = 24\text{ cm}\). The difference in area is \((18 \times 24) - (12 \times 16) = 432 - 192 = 240\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: If it costs $400 to carpet a rectangular room measuring 4 m by 5 m, what would it cost to carpet a room that is 6 m by 6 m at the same rate?
qs.s: The first room has an area of \(4\text{ m} \times 5\text{ m} = 20\text{ m}^2\), so the rate is \(\$400 / 20\text{ m}^2 = \$20/\text{m}^2\). The second room has an area of \(6\text{ m} \times 6\text{ m} = 36\text{ m}^2\), so the cost is \(36 \times \$20 = \$720\).

qs.q: If it costs $150 to paint a rectangular wall measuring 3 m by 5 m, what would it cost to paint a wall that is 4 m by 6 m at the same rate?
qs.s: The area of the first wall is \(3\text{ m} \times 5\text{ m} = 15\text{ m}^2\), giving a rate of \(\$150 / 15\text{ m}^2 = \$10/\text{m}^2\). Painting the second wall with an area of \(4\text{ m} \times 6\text{ m} = 24\text{ m}^2\) costs \(24 \times \$10 = \$240\).

qs.q: If it costs $180 to seal a rectangular driveway measuring 2 m by 6 m, what would it cost to seal a driveway that is 3 m by 8 m at the same rate?
qs.s: The first driveway has an area of \(2\text{ m} \times 6\text{ m} = 12\text{ m}^2\), giving a rate of \(\$180 / 12\text{ m}^2 = \$15/\text{m}^2\). The second driveway has an area of \(3\text{ m} \times 8\text{ m} = 24\text{ m}^2\), which costs \(24 \times \$15 = \$360\).

qs.q: If it costs $240 to lay sod on a rectangular lawn measuring 6 m by 8 m, what would it cost to lay sod on a lawn that is 8 m by 9 m at the same rate?
qs.s: The area of the first lawn is \(6\text{ m} \times 8\text{ m} = 48\text{ m}^2\), giving a rate of \(\$240 / 48\text{ m}^2 = \$5/\text{m}^2\). For the second lawn with an area of \(8\text{ m} \times 9\text{ m} = 72\text{ m}^2\), the cost is \(72 \times \$5 = \$360\).

qs.q: If it costs $360 to tile a rectangular patio measuring 3 m by 4 m, what would it cost to tile a patio that is 4 m by 5 m at the same rate?
qs.s: The first patio has an area of \(3\text{ m} \times 4\text{ m} = 12\text{ m}^2\), so the cost per square meter is \(\$360 / 12\text{ m}^2 = \$30/\text{m}^2\). The second patio has an area of \(4\text{ m} \times 5\text{ m} = 20\text{ m}^2\), which costs \(20 \times \$30 = \$600\).

qs.q: It costs $216 to stain a solid rectangular deck measuring 4 m by 6 m. How much would it cost, at the same rate per square meter, to stain a deck measuring 6 m by 8 m that has an unstained 2 m by 3 m hot tub in the center?
qs.s: The staining rate is \(\$216 / (4\text{ m} \times 6\text{ m}) = \$9/\text{m}^2\). The area to stain on the second deck is \((6\text{ m} \times 8\text{ m}) - (2\text{ m} \times 3\text{ m}) = 42\text{ m}^2\), costing \(42 \times \$9 = \$378\).

qs.q: A contractor charges $180 to stain a rectangular deck measuring 3 m by 5 m. If a customer builds a similar deck with each dimension enlarged by a scale factor of 2.5, how much MORE will it cost to stain the larger deck than the original deck?
qs.s: Since the dimensions scale by a factor of \(2.5\), the area scales by \(2.5^2 = 6.25\), making the total cost of the larger deck \(\$180 \times 6.25 = \$1,125\). The extra cost is \(\$1,125 - \$180 = \$945\).

qs.q: It costs $180 to seal a rectangular wooden deck measuring 3 m by 5 m. What would it cost to seal an L-shaped deck composed of two adjacent rectangular sections measuring 4 m by 5 m and 3 m by 6 m at the same rate per square meter?
qs.s: The rate is \(\$180 / (3\text{ m} \times 5\text{ m}) = \$12/\text{m}^2\). The total area of the L-shaped deck is \((4\text{ m} \times 5\text{ m}) + (3\text{ m} \times 6\text{ m}) = 38\text{ m}^2\), so the cost is \(38 \times \$12 = \$456\).

qs.q: It costs $280 to stain a rectangular deck measuring 4 m by 7 m. At the same rate per square meter, staining a second rectangular deck with a width of 6 m costs $450. What is the length of the second deck?
qs.s: The first deck's unit cost is \(\$280 / (4\text{ m} \times 7\text{ m}) = \$10/\text{m}^2\). The area of the second deck is \(\$450 / (\$10/\text{m}^2) = 45\text{ m}^2\), so its length is \(45\text{ m}^2 / 6\text{ m} = 7.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A landscaper charges $120 to fertilize a triangular lawn with a base of 6 m and a height of 8 m. At the same rate per square meter, how much would it cost to fertilize a triangular lawn with a base of 9 m and a height of 14 m?
qs.s: The area of the first lawn is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6\text{ m} \times 8\text{ m} = 24\text{ m}^2\), giving a rate of \(\$120 / 24\text{ m}^2 = \$5/\text{m}^2\). The second lawn's area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 9\text{ m} \times 14\text{ m} = 63\text{ m}^2\), costing \(63 \times \$5 = \$315\).

qs.q: A certificate measuring 30 cm wide by 20 cm tall is mounted on a wooden plaque. It leaves a margin of 3 cm wide at the bottom and each side of the certificate. If the certificate is similar to the plaque, what must be the width of the margin at the top of the certificate?
qs.s: The plaque's width is \(30 + 2(3) = 36\text{ cm}\), so by similarity its height is \(36 \times \frac{20}{30} = 24\text{ cm}\). The top margin is therefore \(24 - 20 - 3 = 1\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A mirror measuring 50 cm wide by 70 cm tall is mounted on a decorative backing board. It leaves a margin of 5 cm wide at the top and each side of the mirror. If the mirror is similar to the backing board, what must be the width of the margin at the bottom of the mirror?
qs.s: The width of the backing board is \(50 + 2(5) = 60\text{ cm}\). By similarity, the height of the board is \(60 \times \frac{70}{50} = 84\text{ cm}\), so the bottom margin is \(84 - 70 - 5 = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A poster measuring 80 cm wide by 60 cm tall is mounted on a display board. It leaves a margin of 8 cm wide at the top and each side of the poster. If the poster is similar to the display board, what must be the width of the margin at the bottom of the poster?
qs.s: The display board has a width of \(80 + 2(8) = 96\text{ cm}\). Since the board is similar to the poster, its height is \(96 \times \frac{60}{80} = 72\text{ cm}\), making the bottom margin \(72 - 60 - 8 = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A photograph measuring 40 cm wide by 50 cm tall is mounted on a mat board. It leaves a margin of 4 cm wide at the top and each side of the photograph. If the photograph is similar to the mat board, what must be the width of the margin at the bottom of the photograph?
qs.s: The mat board has a width of \(40 + 2(4) = 48\text{ cm}\). By similarity, the height of the board is \(48 \times \frac{50}{40} = 60\text{ cm}\), so the bottom margin is \(60 - 50 - 4 = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An art print measuring 100 cm wide by 75 cm tall is mounted on a backing frame. It leaves a margin of 6 cm wide at the top and each side of the print. If the print is similar to the frame, what must be the width of the margin at the bottom of the print?
qs.s: The frame width is \(100 + 2(6) = 112\text{ cm}\). Since the frame is similar to the print, the frame height is \(112 \times \frac{75}{100} = 84\text{ cm}\), which gives a bottom margin of \(84 - 75 - 6 = 3\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular print measuring 45 cm wide by 30 cm tall is mounted in a frame such that the frame is similar to the print. The border between the print and the frame is 3 cm wide at the top and on both the left and right sides. What is the total area of the border surrounding the print?
qs.s: The frame's width is \(45 + 2(3) = 51\text{ cm}\), so its height by similarity is \(51 \times \frac{30}{45} = 34\text{ cm}\). The area of the border is the frame's area minus the print's area: \((51 \times 34) - (45 \times 30) = 1734 - 1350 = 384\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: An art canvas measuring 160 cm wide by 100 cm tall is set within a display frame that is similar to the canvas. The frame leaves a side margin of 8 cm on both the left and right sides, and a top margin of 6.5 cm. What is the width of the bottom margin?
qs.s: The frame's width is \(160 + 2(8) = 176\text{ cm}\), so by similarity its height is \(176 \times \frac{100}{160} = 110\text{ cm}\). The bottom margin is \(110 - 100 - 6.5 = 3.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A poster measuring 40 cm wide by 60 cm tall is mounted on a backing board such that the board is similar to the poster. The margins on the left, right, and top are all equal to \(x\) cm, while the bottom margin is 6 cm wider than the top margin. What is the value of \(x\)?
qs.s: The board has width \(40 + 2x\) and height \(60 + x + (x + 6) = 66 + 2x\). Solving the similarity ratio \(\frac{40+2x}{66+2x} = \frac{40}{60} = \frac{2}{3}\) gives \(3(40 + 2x) = 2(66 + 2x)\), which simplifies to \(2x = 12\), so \(x = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A monitor screen measuring 64 cm wide by 36 cm tall is surrounded by an outer casing that is similar in shape to the screen. The casing leaves a border of 2 cm on both the left and right sides, and a border of 1.5 cm at the top. What is the width of the border at the bottom of the screen?
qs.s: The outer casing has width \(64 + 2(2) = 68\text{ cm}\), so by similarity its height is \(68 \times \frac{36}{64} = 38.25\text{ cm}\). The bottom border is \(38.25 - 36 - 1.5 = 0.75\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A tapestry measuring 120 cm wide by 180 cm tall is mounted on a wall panel that is similar in shape to the tapestry. The panel extends 14 cm above the tapestry and 16 cm below it. If the side margins on the left and right are of equal width, what is the width of each side margin?
qs.s: The total height of the panel is \(180 + 14 + 16 = 210\text{ cm}\), so by similarity its width is \(210 \times \frac{120}{180} = 140\text{ cm}\). Each side margin is \(\frac{140 - 120}{2} = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A commercial airplane is 50 m long with a wingspan of 60 m and a tail height of 15 m. A scale model is built with a wingspan of 48 cm. What is the length of the scale model in centimeters?
qs.s: The scale ratio is \(\frac{48\text{ cm}}{60\text{ m}} = 0.8\text{ cm/m}\). Multiplying the actual length by this ratio gives \(50 \times 0.8 = 40\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A fire truck is 12 m long, 2.5 m wide, and 3 m tall. A toy manufacturer produces a scale model of the fire truck with a length of 30 cm. What is the height of the toy fire truck in centimeters?
qs.s: The scale ratio is \(\frac{30\text{ cm}}{12\text{ m}} = 2.5\text{ cm/m}\). Multiplying the actual height by this scale gives \(3 \times 2.5 = 7.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A historic windmill is 18 m tall and 8 m wide at its base, with sails that are 12 m long. A souvenir replica is made with a base width of 6 cm. What is the height of the replica in centimeters?
qs.s: The scale ratio is \(\frac{6\text{ cm}}{8\text{ m}} = 0.75\text{ cm/m}\). Multiplying the actual height by this scale gives \(18 \times 0.75 = 13.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A sailboat is 24 m long and 6 m wide, with a mast that is 16 m high. A scale model of the sailboat is constructed with a length of 36 cm. What is the height of the mast on the scale model in centimeters?
qs.s: The scale ratio is \(\frac{36\text{ cm}}{24\text{ m}} = 1.5\text{ cm/m}\). Multiplying the mast's actual height by this scale gives \(16 \times 1.5 = 24\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cargo ship is 120 m long and 20 m wide, with a bridge tower 30 m high. A museum builds a scale model of the ship that is 48 cm long. What is the width of the scale model in centimeters?
qs.s: The scale ratio is \(\frac{48\text{ cm}}{120\text{ m}} = 0.4\text{ cm/m}\). Multiplying the ship's actual width by this ratio gives \(20 \times 0.4 = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A warehouse is 48 m long, 36 m wide, and 15 m tall. An architect builds a scale model such that the sum of the model's length and width is 70 cm. What is the height of the scale model in centimeters?
qs.s: The sum of the actual length and width is \(48 + 36 = 84\text{ m}\), giving a scale of \(\frac{70\text{ cm}}{84\text{ m}} = \frac{5}{6}\text{ cm/m}\). Multiplying the actual height by this scale gives \(15 \times \frac{5}{6} = 12.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cruise ship is 320 m long, 40 m wide, and 64 m tall. A scale model of the ship is built with a length of 80 cm. How many centimeters greater is the height of the model than its width?
qs.s: The scale factor is \(\frac{80\text{ cm}}{320\text{ m}} = 0.25\text{ cm/m}\). The model's height is \(64 \times 0.25 = 16\text{ cm}\) and its width is \(40 \times 0.25 = 10\text{ cm}\), giving a difference of \(16 - 10 = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A scale model of a cargo airplane has a fuselage length of 48 cm, a wingspan of 60 cm, and a tail height of 16 cm. On the actual airplane, the wingspan is 9 m longer than the fuselage. What is the actual tail height of the airplane in meters?
qs.s: Setting \(\frac{L}{L+9} = \frac{48}{60} = \frac{4}{5}\) yields an actual fuselage length of \(L = 36\text{ m}\). Using the scale ratio of \(\frac{36\text{ m}}{48\text{ cm}} = 0.75\text{ m/cm}\), the actual tail height is \(16 \times 0.75 = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An architect creates two different scale models of the same rectangular courtyard. Model A has a length of 45 cm and a width of 30 cm. Model B is enlarged so that its perimeter is 350 cm. What is the length of Model B in centimeters?
qs.s: The perimeter of Model A is \(2(45 + 30) = 150\text{ cm}\), so the scale factor to Model B is \(\frac{350}{150} = \frac{7}{3}\). The length of Model B is \(45 \times \frac{7}{3} = 105\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular billboard is designed to be similar in shape to a printed flyer. The flyer is 12 cm wide and 18 cm long. If the length of the billboard is 5 m longer than its width, what is the width of the billboard in meters?
qs.s: Setting up the proportion \(\frac{w}{w+5} = \frac{12}{18} = \frac{2}{3}\) gives \(3w = 2(w + 5)\), which simplifies to \(3w = 2w + 10\), so \(w = 10\text{ m}\).
