qs.s: Convert 2.75 liters to 2750 milliliters to write the ratio as 2750 to 825. Dividing both terms by their greatest common factor, 275, simplifies the ratio to 10 : 3.

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: \(2\frac{1}{4}\) pounds to 20 ounces
qs.s: Convert \(2\frac{1}{4}\) pounds to ounces by calculating \(\frac{9}{4} \times 16 = 36\) ounces. The ratio becomes 36 ounces to 20 ounces, which reduces by dividing both terms by 4 to 9 : 5.

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 1.5 hours to 45 minutes to 30 minutes
qs.s: Convert 1.5 hours to 90 minutes to write the three quantities in the same unit: 90 : 45 : 30. Dividing each term by their greatest common factor, 15, gives 6 : 3 : 2.

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 3 square meters to 4500 square centimeters
qs.s: Since 1 m = 100 cm, 1 square meter is 10,000 square centimeters, making 3 square meters equal to 30,000 square centimeters. The ratio is 30,000 to 4500, which reduces by dividing both terms by 1500 to 20 : 3.

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 800 mL to 3 L.
qs.s: Convert 3 L to millilitres: \(3\text{ L} = 3000\text{ mL}\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{800}{3000} = \frac{4}{15}\), which is \(4 : 15\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 35 cm to 2 m.
qs.s: Convert 2 m to centimetres: \(2\text{ m} = 200\text{ cm}\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{35}{200} = \frac{7}{40}\), which is \(7 : 40\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 20 ounces to 2 pounds. (Note: \(1\text{ lb} = 16\text{ oz}\))
qs.s: Convert 2 pounds to ounces: \(2\text{ lb} = 32\text{ oz}\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{20}{32} = \frac{5}{8}\), which is \(5 : 8\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 16 hours to 3 days.
qs.s: Convert 3 days to hours: \(3\text{ days} = 72\text{ hours}\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{16}{72} = \frac{2}{9}\), which is \(2 : 9\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: \(1\frac{1}{4}\text{ kg}\) to 750 g.
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{1}{4}\text{ kg}\) to grams: \(1.25 \times 1000\text{ g} = 1250\text{ g}\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{1250}{750} = \frac{5}{3}\), which is \(5 : 3\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 45 cm to 1.2 m to 75 cm.
qs.s: Convert 1.2 m to centimetres: \(1.2\text{ m} = 120\text{ cm}\). Divide each term in \(45 : 120 : 75\) by their greatest common factor, 15, to obtain \(3 : 8 : 5\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 3.6 m to 96 cm.
qs.s: Convert 3.6 m to centimetres: \(3.6\text{ m} = 360\text{ cm}\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{360}{96} = \frac{15}{4}\), which is \(15 : 4\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 54 square feet to 4 square yards. (Note: \(1\text{ yd} = 3\text{ ft}\))
qs.s: Since \(1\text{ yd} = 3\text{ ft}\), \(1\text{ yd}^2 = 9\text{ ft}^2\), giving \(4\text{ yd}^2 = 36\text{ ft}^2\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{54}{36} = \frac{3}{2}\), which is \(3 : 2\).

qs.q: Write the ratio in simplest form: 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes.
qs.s: Convert both quantities to minutes: \(1\text{ h } 45\text{ min} = 105\text{ min}\) and \(2\text{ h } 30\text{ min} = 150\text{ min}\). Simplify the ratio \(\frac{105}{150} = \frac{7}{10}\), which is \(7 : 10\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 12 kilometres in 40 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{12\text{ kilometres}}{40\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both terms by 4 to get \(\frac{3\text{ kilometres}}{10\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 14 baskets in 35 attempts
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{14\text{ baskets}}{35\text{ attempts}}\) and divide both terms by their common factor of 7 to obtain \(\frac{2\text{ baskets}}{5\text{ attempts}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 6 wins in 30 games
qs.s: Express the rate as a fraction \(\frac{6\text{ wins}}{30\text{ games}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 6 to get \(\frac{1\text{ win}}{5\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 15 beats in 20 seconds
qs.s: Form the rate \(\frac{15\text{ beats}}{20\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 5 to find \(\frac{3\text{ beats}}{4\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 9 pages in 36 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{9\text{ pages}}{36\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 9, to simplify to \(\frac{1\text{ page}}{4\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 3.6 metres in 45 seconds
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal to get \(\frac{36\text{ metres}}{450\text{ seconds}}\), then divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 18, to simplify to \(\frac{2\text{ metres}}{25\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 2.4 kilograms in 32 days
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by 10 to eliminate the decimal, yielding \(\frac{24\text{ kilograms}}{320\text{ days}}\), then divide both terms by 8 to get \(\frac{3\text{ kilograms}}{40\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 140 revolutions in 84 seconds
qs.s: Form the rate fraction \(\frac{140\text{ revolutions}}{84\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 28, to obtain \(\frac{5\text{ revolutions}}{3\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 315 kilometres in 42 hours
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{315\text{ kilometres}}{42\text{ hours}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 21, to get \(\frac{15\text{ kilometres}}{2\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 108 kilometres on 24 litres
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{108\text{ kilometres}}{24\text{ litres}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 12, to obtain \(\frac{9\text{ kilometres}}{2\text{ litres}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 45 pages in 10 days
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{45\text{ pages}}{10\text{ days}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(5\). This gives \(\frac{9\text{ pages}}{2\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 50 words in 15 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{50\text{ words}}{15\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both numbers by their greatest common factor, \(5\). The resulting rate is \(\frac{10\text{ words}}{3\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 36 goals in 16 games
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{36\text{ goals}}{16\text{ games}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by \(4\). The simplified rate is \(\frac{9\text{ goals}}{4\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 75 kilometers in 18 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{75\text{ km}}{18\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both numerator and denominator by \(\gcd(75, 18) = 3\). This gives \(\frac{25\text{ km}}{6\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 84 heartbeats in 8 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{84\text{ heartbeats}}{8\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both terms by \(\gcd(84, 8) = 4\). This simplifies to \(\frac{21\text{ heartbeats}}{2\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 84 meters in 3.2 seconds
qs.s: Multiply both terms by \(10\) to eliminate the decimal, giving \(\frac{840\text{ m}}{32\text{ s}}\). Then divide the numerator and denominator by \(\gcd(840, 32) = 8\) to obtain \(\frac{105\text{ m}}{4\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: (140 + 280) bolts in 48 minutes
qs.s: Add the quantities to get \(140 + 280 = 420\text{ bolts}\). Then simplify the rate \(\frac{420\text{ bolts}}{48\text{ minutes}}\) by dividing the numerator and denominator by \(\gcd(420, 48) = 12\) to get \(\frac{35\text{ bolts}}{4\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 540 students in 24 buses
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{540\text{ students}}{24\text{ buses}}\) and divide both numerator and denominator by \(\gcd(540, 24) = 12\). This yields the simplified rate \(\frac{45\text{ students}}{2\text{ buses}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 630 kilometers in 108 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{630\text{ km}}{108\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by \(\gcd(630, 108) = 18\). This gives the simplified rate \(\frac{35\text{ km}}{6\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 7.2 kilograms in 15 days
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(10\) to clear the decimal, resulting in \(\frac{72\text{ kg}}{150\text{ days}}\). Then divide both by their greatest common factor, \(6\), to get \(\frac{12\text{ kg}}{25\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 250 kilometers on 35 liters
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{250\text{ km}}{35\text{ L}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 5, giving \(\frac{50\text{ kilometers}}{7\text{ liters}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 180 words in 40 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as the fraction \(\frac{180\text{ words}}{40\text{ seconds}}\). Divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 20, to get \(\frac{9\text{ words}}{2\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: $75 for 20 hours
qs.s: Set up the rate as \(\frac{\$75}{20\text{ hours}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 5, to obtain \(\frac{\$15}{4\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 210 pages in 60 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{210\text{ pages}}{60\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 30, to obtain \(\frac{7\text{ pages}}{2\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 140 grams in 24 servings
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{140\text{ grams}}{24\text{ servings}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 4 to get \(\frac{35\text{ grams}}{6\text{ servings}}\).

qs.q: Write the overall rate in simplest form: a runner burns 380 calories in 45 minutes and then 220 calories in 35 minutes
qs.s: Add the quantities to find totals of \(380 + 220 = 600\text{ calories}\) and \(45 + 35 = 80\text{ minutes}\). Simplifying \(\frac{600\text{ calories}}{80\text{ minutes}}\) by dividing both by 40 yields \(\frac{15\text{ calories}}{2\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 8.4 kilograms in 35 minutes
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{84\text{ kg}}{350\text{ min}}\). Then divide both by their greatest common factor, 14, to obtain \(\frac{6\text{ kilograms}}{25\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 1,470 kilometers on 126 liters
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{1470\text{ km}}{126\text{ L}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 42, to get \(\frac{35\text{ kilometers}}{3\text{ liters}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 1,170 megabytes in 520 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{1170\text{ megabytes}}{520\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 130, to get \(\frac{9\text{ megabytes}}{4\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 54 meters in 4.8 seconds
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal, yielding \(\frac{540\text{ meters}}{48\text{ seconds}}\). Then divide both by their greatest common factor, 12, to obtain \(\frac{45\text{ meters}}{4\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 20 km in 8 hours.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 4: \(\frac{20\text{ km}}{8\text{ hr}} = \frac{20 \div 4\text{ km}}{8 \div 4\text{ hr}} = \frac{5\text{ km}}{2\text{ hr}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 16 tickets for $36.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 4: \(\frac{16\text{ tickets}}{\$36} = \frac{16 \div 4\text{ tickets}}{\$36 \div 4} = \frac{4\text{ tickets}}{\$9}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 28 points in 8 games.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide both quantities by their greatest common factor, 4: \(\frac{28\text{ points}}{8\text{ games}} = \frac{28 \div 4\text{ points}}{8 \div 4\text{ games}} = \frac{7\text{ points}}{2\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: $45 for 6 hours.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 3: \(\frac{\$45}{6\text{ hr}} = \frac{\$45 \div 3}{6 \div 3\text{ hr}} = \frac{\$15}{2\text{ hr}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 15 pens for $20.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 5: \(\frac{15\text{ pens}}{\$20} = \frac{15 \div 5\text{ pens}}{\$20 \div 5} = \frac{3\text{ pens}}{\$4}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 525 words in 14 minutes.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 7: \(\frac{525\text{ words}}{14\text{ min}} = \frac{525 \div 7\text{ words}}{14 \div 7\text{ min}} = \frac{75\text{ words}}{2\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 6.4 m in 12 seconds.
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to obtain whole numbers, \(\frac{64\text{ m}}{120\text{ s}}\), then divide both by their greatest common factor, 8: \(\frac{64 \div 8\text{ m}}{120 \div 8\text{ s}} = \frac{8\text{ m}}{15\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: $270 for 36 hours.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 18: \(\frac{\$270}{36\text{ hr}} = \frac{\$270 \div 18}{36 \div 18\text{ hr}} = \frac{\$15}{2\text{ hr}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 280 km on 24 L.
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 8: \(\frac{280\text{ km}}{24\text{ L}} = \frac{280 \div 8\text{ km}}{24 \div 8\text{ L}} = \frac{35\text{ km}}{3\text{ L}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4.5 kg for $15.
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to eliminate the decimal to get \(\frac{45\text{ kg}}{\$150}\), then divide by their greatest common factor, 15: \(\frac{45 \div 15\text{ kg}}{\$150 \div 15} = \frac{3\text{ kg}}{\$10}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 20 kilometers in 36 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{20\text{ kilometers}}{36\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both numbers by their greatest common factor, 4, resulting in \(\frac{5\text{ kilometers}}{9\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 28 questions in 35 minutes
qs.s: Form the rate \(\frac{28\text{ questions}}{35\text{ minutes}}\) and simplify by dividing both terms by 7, which gives \(\frac{4\text{ questions}}{5\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 14 strikes in 49 pitches
qs.s: Express the comparison as \(\frac{14\text{ strikes}}{49\text{ pitches}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by 7 to simplify to \(\frac{2\text{ strikes}}{7\text{ pitches}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 15 goals in 25 games
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{15\text{ goals}}{25\text{ games}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 5, to get \(\frac{3\text{ goals}}{5\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 18 laps in 42 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{18\text{ laps}}{42\text{ minutes}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by 6 to obtain \(\frac{3\text{ laps}}{7\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 315 kilometers in 140 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{315\text{ kilometers}}{140\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 35, to obtain \(\frac{9\text{ kilometers}}{4\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4.8 kilograms in 30 days
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to eliminate the decimal, giving \(\frac{48\text{ kilograms}}{300\text{ days}}\), then divide both numerator and denominator by 12 to get \(\frac{4\text{ kilograms}}{25\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 432 words in 180 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{432\text{ words}}{180\text{ seconds}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 36, to simplify to \(\frac{12\text{ words}}{5\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 3.5 litres in 8.4 hours
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by 10 to clear the decimals, yielding \(\frac{35\text{ litres}}{84\text{ hours}}\), and then divide both by 7 to simplify to \(\frac{5\text{ litres}}{12\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 2.25 metres in 30 seconds
qs.s: Multiply both quantities by 100 to clear the two decimal places to get \(\frac{225\text{ metres}}{3000\text{ seconds}}\), then divide numerator and denominator by 75 to obtain \(\frac{3\text{ metres}}{40\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 45 liters in 600 kilometers
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{45\text{ liters}}{600\text{ kilometers}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor, 15. This simplifies to \(\frac{3\text{ liters}}{40\text{ kilometers}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 42 laps in 280 minutes
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{42\text{ laps}}{280\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common divisor, 14. This gives the simplified rate of \(\frac{3\text{ laps}}{20\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 35 wins in 140 matches
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{35\text{ wins}}{140\text{ matches}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 35. The simplified rate is \(\frac{1\text{ win}}{4\text{ matches}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 32 revolutions in 480 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{32\text{ revolutions}}{480\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 32. This simplifies to \(\frac{1\text{ revolution}}{15\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 24 goals in 360 games
qs.s: Write the rate as a fraction \(\frac{24\text{ goals}}{360\text{ games}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor, 24. This simplifies to \(\frac{1\text{ goal}}{15\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 588 heartbeats in 1,029 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{588\text{ heartbeats}}{1029\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common divisor, 147. This results in the simplified rate \(\frac{4\text{ heartbeats}}{7\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 7.25 kilometers in 116 minutes
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by 100 to remove the decimal, resulting in \(\frac{725\text{ kilometers}}{11600\text{ minutes}}\). Dividing both terms by 25 and then by 29 simplifies the rate to \(\frac{1\text{ kilometer}}{16\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 8.4 kilograms in 140 liters
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by 10 to eliminate the decimal, giving \(\frac{84\text{ kilograms}}{1400\text{ liters}}\). Then, divide both terms by their greatest common divisor, 28, to obtain \(\frac{3\text{ kilograms}}{50\text{ liters}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4.5 meters in 1.25 seconds
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 100 to clear the decimals, yielding \(\frac{450\text{ meters}}{125\text{ seconds}}\). Dividing both the numerator and denominator by 25 gives the simplified rate \(\frac{18\text{ meters}}{5\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 1,008 revolutions in 2,520 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{1008\text{ revolutions}}{2520\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 504. This simplifies to \(\frac{2\text{ revolutions}}{5\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 920 words in 6 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{920\text{ words}}{6\text{ min}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 2 to get \(\frac{460\text{ words}}{3\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: $14 700 in 9 months
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{\$14\,700}{9\text{ months}}\) and divide both terms by their common factor of 3 to obtain \(\frac{\$4900}{3\text{ months}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 620 points in 15 games
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{620\text{ points}}{15\text{ games}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 5, to get \(\frac{124\text{ points}}{3\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 380 km on 14 L
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{380\text{ km}}{14\text{ L}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 2, to get \(\frac{190\text{ km}}{7\text{ L}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 550 revolutions in 8 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{550\text{ revolutions}}{8\text{ s}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by 2 to get \(\frac{275\text{ revolutions}}{4\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 750 km in 4.5 hours
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by 10 to obtain whole numbers, \(\frac{7500\text{ km}}{45\text{ h}}\), then divide both by 15 to get \(\frac{500\text{ km}}{3\text{ h}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 37 500 copies in 140 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{37\,500\text{ copies}}{140\text{ min}}\) and simplify by dividing both terms by their greatest common factor, 20, to obtain \(\frac{1875\text{ copies}}{7\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: $58 800 in 36 months
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{\$58\,800}{36\text{ months}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 12, to obtain \(\frac{\$4900}{3\text{ months}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 7.5 kg in 18 minutes
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal to get \(\frac{75\text{ kg}}{180\text{ min}}\), then divide numerator and denominator by 15 to get \(\frac{5\text{ kg}}{12\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 16.8 L for 260 km
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to write whole numbers, \(\frac{168\text{ L}}{2600\text{ km}}\), then divide both terms by 8 to reach lowest terms, \(\frac{21\text{ L}}{325\text{ km}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 980 revolutions in 15 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{980\text{ revolutions}}{15\text{ s}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 5. The simplified rate is \(\frac{196\text{ revolutions}}{3\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 1600 metres in 6 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{1600\text{ m}}{6\text{ min}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 2. This gives the rate in simplest form as \(\frac{800\text{ m}}{3\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 1350 words in 4 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{1350\text{ words}}{4\text{ min}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 2. This results in the simplified rate \(\frac{675\text{ words}}{2\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 450 pages in 12 days
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{450\text{ pages}}{12\text{ days}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 6. This simplifies the rate to \(\frac{75\text{ pages}}{2\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 520 kilometres in 15 hours
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{520\text{ km}}{15\text{ h}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 5. This gives the simplified rate \(\frac{104\text{ km}}{3\text{ h}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 22,500 copies in 48 hours
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{22,500\text{ copies}}{48\text{ h}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 12. This gives the simplified rate \(\frac{1875\text{ copies}}{4\text{ h}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 14,400 bricks in 84 crates
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{14,400\text{ bricks}}{84\text{ crates}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 12. This simplifies the rate to \(\frac{1200\text{ bricks}}{7\text{ crates}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 17.5 kilograms in 40 days
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{175\text{ kg}}{400\text{ days}}\). Dividing the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 25, yields \(\frac{7\text{ kg}}{16\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4.25 litres in 30 minutes
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 100 to eliminate the decimal, giving \(\frac{425\text{ L}}{3000\text{ min}}\). Dividing the numerator and denominator by 25 results in \(\frac{17\text{ L}}{120\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 7.2 metres in 1.6 seconds
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to eliminate the decimals, yielding \(\frac{72\text{ m}}{16\text{ s}}\). Dividing both the numerator and denominator by 8 gives \(\frac{9\text{ m}}{2\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(\$1374\) for \(12\text{ m}^2\) of flooring
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{\$1374}{12\text{ m}^2}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(6\), to get \(\frac{\$229}{2\text{ m}^2}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(\$1575\) for \(28\text{ m}^2\) of tile
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{\$1575}{28\text{ m}^2}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(7\), to get \(\frac{\$225}{4\text{ m}^2}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(1485\text{ km}\) in \(18\text{ h}\)
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{1485\text{ km}}{18\text{ h}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(9\), to get \(\frac{165\text{ km}}{2\text{ h}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(\$1422\) for \(21\text{ kg}\) of coffee beans
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{\$1422}{21\text{ kg}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(3\), to get \(\frac{\$474}{7\text{ kg}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(1128\text{ km}\) on \(15\text{ L}\) of gasoline
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{1128\text{ km}}{15\text{ L}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(3\), to get \(\frac{376\text{ km}}{5\text{ L}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(\$58.50\) for \(18\text{ m}^2\) of laminate
qs.s: Multiply both terms by \(10\) to eliminate the decimal, giving \(\frac{\$585}{180\text{ m}^2}\), then divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(45\), to get \(\frac{\$13}{4\text{ m}^2}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \((\$1480 + \$1670)\) for \(28\text{ m}^2\) of hardwood flooring
qs.s: Calculate the total cost as \(\$1480 + \$1670 = \$3150\), then divide both terms of \(\frac{\$3150}{28\text{ m}^2}\) by their greatest common factor, \(14\), to get \(\frac{\$225}{2\text{ m}^2}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(\$2550\) for \((16\text{ m}^2 + 20\text{ m}^2)\) of carpet
qs.s: First calculate the total area as \(16\text{ m}^2 + 20\text{ m}^2 = 36\text{ m}^2\), then simplify \(\frac{\$2550}{36\text{ m}^2}\) by dividing both terms by their greatest common factor, \(6\), to get \(\frac{\$425}{6\text{ m}^2}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(\$11600\) for \(48\text{ m}^2\) of office space
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{\$11600}{48\text{ m}^2}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(16\), to get \(\frac{\$725}{3\text{ m}^2}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(346.5\text{ km}\) on \(22\text{ L}\) of fuel
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(10\) to clear the decimal to obtain \(\frac{3465\text{ km}}{220\text{ L}}\), then divide both terms by their greatest common factor, \(55\), to get \(\frac{63\text{ km}}{4\text{ L}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 50 miles driven in 15 minutes
qs.s: Set up the rate as \(\frac{50\text{ miles}}{15\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both terms by 5 to simplify to \(\frac{10\text{ miles}}{3\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 45 dollars for 12 tickets
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{45\text{ dollars}}{12\text{ tickets}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 3, giving \(\frac{15\text{ dollars}}{4\text{ tickets}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 20 points scored in 8 games
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{20\text{ points}}{8\text{ games}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 4, to get \(\frac{5\text{ points}}{2\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 28 kilograms in 16 boxes
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{28\text{ kilograms}}{16\text{ boxes}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by 4 to obtain \(\frac{7\text{ kilograms}}{4\text{ boxes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 42 pages read in 18 minutes
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{42\text{ pages}}{18\text{ minutes}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by 6 to get \(\frac{7\text{ pages}}{3\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: A cyclist rode 75 kilometres on Saturday and 45 kilometres on Sunday over a total riding time of 32 hours. Write the rate of total distance to total time in simplest form.
qs.s: Add the distances to find a total of \(75 + 45 = 120\text{ kilometres}\), then simplify the rate \(\frac{120\text{ kilometres}}{32\text{ hours}}\) by dividing both terms by 8 to get \(\frac{15\text{ kilometres}}{4\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: A storage reservoir held 350 megalitres of water. After 45 days of use, 110 megalitres remained. Write the rate of water used to time elapsed in simplest form.
qs.s: The amount of water used is \(350 - 110 = 240\text{ megalitres}\). Simplify \(\frac{240\text{ megalitres}}{45\text{ days}}\) by dividing numerator and denominator by 15 to get \(\frac{16\text{ megalitres}}{3\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: In a workshop, machine A produced 140 parts in 18 hours and machine B produced 220 parts in 30 hours. Write the rate of total parts to total time in simplest form.
qs.s: Find total parts, \(140 + 220 = 360\text{ parts}\), and total time, \(18 + 30 = 48\text{ hours}\). Divide both by 24 to simplify \(\frac{360\text{ parts}}{48\text{ hours}}\) to \(\frac{15\text{ parts}}{2\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 504 kilometres on 48 litres of fuel
qs.s: Set up the rate as \(\frac{504\text{ kilometres}}{48\text{ litres}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 24, to arrive at \(\frac{21\text{ kilometres}}{2\text{ litres}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4.5 kilograms of flour in 12 bags
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{45\text{ kilograms}}{120\text{ bags}}\), then divide the numerator and denominator by 15 to get \(\frac{3\text{ kilograms}}{8\text{ bags}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 36 apples for every 16 baskets
qs.s: Divide both quantities by their greatest common factor, 4, to obtain 9 apples for every 4 baskets.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 30 computers for every 20 students
qs.s: Divide both numbers by their greatest common factor, 10, to get 3 computers for every 2 students.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 60 tickets for every 45 attendees
qs.s: Divide both numbers by their greatest common factor, 15, yielding 4 tickets for every 3 attendees.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 24 nurses for every 18 patients
qs.s: Divide both quantities by their greatest common factor, 6, which simplifies the rate to 4 nurses for every 3 patients.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 70 passengers for every 28 cars
qs.s: Divide both values by their greatest common factor, 14, giving 5 passengers for every 2 cars.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 2.8 litres for every 35 kilometres
qs.s: Multiply both values by 10 to clear the decimal, yielding 28 litres for every 350 kilometres, then divide both by 14 to get 2 litres for every 25 kilometres.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 7.2 metres for every 4.8 seconds
qs.s: Multiply both quantities by 10 to eliminate the decimals, giving 72 metres for every 48 seconds, then divide both by 24 to get 3 metres for every 2 seconds.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4.5 kilograms for every 12 batches
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal, giving 45 kilograms for every 120 batches, then divide both by 15 to get 3 kilograms for every 8 batches.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 540 visitors for every 225 tours
qs.s: Divide both quantities by their greatest common factor, 45, which simplifies the rate to 12 visitors for every 5 tours.

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 420 megabytes for every 112 seconds
qs.s: Divide both quantities by their greatest common factor, 28, to simplify the rate to 15 megabytes for every 4 seconds.

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 8 chaperones for every 100 students.
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{8\text{ chaperones}}{100\text{ students}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 4, to get \(\frac{2\text{ chaperones}}{25\text{ students}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 3 coaches for every 45 athletes.
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{3\text{ coaches}}{45\text{ athletes}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by 3 to get \(\frac{1\text{ coach}}{15\text{ athletes}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 4 flight attendants for every 120 passengers.
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{4\text{ flight attendants}}{120\text{ passengers}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 4 to get \(\frac{1\text{ flight attendant}}{30\text{ passengers}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 5 lifeguards for every 60 swimmers.
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{5\text{ lifeguards}}{60\text{ swimmers}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 5, to get \(\frac{1\text{ lifeguard}}{12\text{ swimmers}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 6 technicians for every 48 machines.
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{6\text{ technicians}}{48\text{ machines}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 6, to get \(\frac{1\text{ technician}}{8\text{ machines}}\).

qs.q: A community center has 14 morning volunteers and 16 afternoon volunteers to serve 720 meals. Write the rate of total volunteers to meals in simplest form.
qs.s: Find the total number of volunteers by calculating \(14 + 16 = 30\), then simplify the rate \(\frac{30\text{ volunteers}}{720\text{ meals}}\) by dividing numerator and denominator by 30 to get \(\frac{1\text{ volunteer}}{24\text{ meals}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 420 kilometers for every 32 liters of fuel.
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{420\text{ kilometers}}{32\text{ liters}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by \(\gcd(420, 32) = 4\) to obtain \(\frac{105\text{ kilometers}}{8\text{ liters}}\).

qs.q: A vehicle used 32 liters of fuel while traveling 165 kilometers on the highway and 75 kilometers in the city. Write the rate of total distance to fuel in simplest form.
qs.s: Add the distances to find the total distance, \(165 + 75 = 240\text{ kilometers}\), and simplify the rate \(\frac{240\text{ kilometers}}{32\text{ liters}}\) by dividing both terms by 16 to get \(\frac{15\text{ kilometers}}{2\text{ liters}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 4.5 kilograms of fertilizer for every 75 square meters of lawn.
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{45\text{ kilograms}}{750\text{ square meters}}\), then divide by \(\gcd(45, 750) = 15\) to get \(\frac{3\text{ kilograms}}{50\text{ square meters}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 315 revolutions for every 140 seconds.
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{315\text{ revolutions}}{140\text{ seconds}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 35, to obtain \(\frac{9\text{ revolutions}}{4\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(18\text{ L}\) of water for 4 trees
qs.s: Write the comparison as \(\frac{18\text{ L}}{4\text{ trees}}\) and simplify by dividing both numbers by 2 to get \(\frac{9\text{ L}}{2\text{ trees}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(15\text{ kg}\) of fertilizer for 6 garden beds
qs.s: Express the rate as a fraction, \(\frac{15\text{ kg}}{6\text{ garden beds}}\), and reduce by dividing numerator and denominator by 3 to obtain \(\frac{5\text{ kg}}{2\text{ garden beds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(14\text{ g}\) of spice for 4 batches of soup
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{14\text{ g}}{4\text{ batches}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by 2 to get \(\frac{7\text{ g}}{2\text{ batches}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(12\text{ m}^2\) of fabric for 8 costumes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{12\text{ m}^2}{8\text{ costumes}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 4, to get \(\frac{3\text{ m}^2}{2\text{ costumes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(20\text{ km}\) of trail for 6 checkpoints
qs.s: Form the rate \(\frac{20\text{ km}}{6\text{ checkpoints}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 2 to obtain \(\frac{10\text{ km}}{3\text{ checkpoints}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(280\text{ m}^2\) of wall space for 24 classrooms
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{280\text{ m}^2}{24\text{ classrooms}}\) and simplify by dividing numerator and denominator by 8 to reach \(\frac{35\text{ m}^2}{3\text{ classrooms}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(8.4\text{ kg}\) of grass seed for 15 lawn sections
qs.s: Clear the decimal by multiplying both terms by 10 to get \(\frac{84\text{ kg}}{150\text{ lawn sections}}\), then divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 6, to get \(\frac{14\text{ kg}}{25\text{ lawn sections}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(4.5\text{ m}^2\) of fabric for 12 pillows
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by 10 to clear the decimal: \(\frac{4.5\text{ m}^2}{12\text{ pillows}} = \frac{45\text{ m}^2}{120\text{ pillows}}\). Then divide both terms by 15 to get \(\frac{3\text{ m}^2}{8\text{ pillows}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(375\text{ L}\) of water for 45 garden plots
qs.s: Form the rate fraction \(\frac{375\text{ L}}{45\text{ garden plots}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 15, to obtain \(\frac{25\text{ L}}{3\text{ garden plots}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: \(144\text{ km}\) on \(42\text{ L}\) of fuel
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{144\text{ km}}{42\text{ L}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 6, to get \(\frac{24\text{ km}}{7\text{ L}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 24 words in 36 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{24\text{ words}}{36\text{ s}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 12, to obtain \(\frac{2\text{ words}}{3\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 32 L in 40 minutes
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{32\text{ L}}{40\text{ min}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by 8 to get \(\frac{4\text{ L}}{5\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 15 km in 25 minutes
qs.s: Express the rate as the fraction \(\frac{15\text{ km}}{25\text{ min}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 5 to get \(\frac{3\text{ km}}{5\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 18 dollars for 42 kg
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{18\text{ dollars}}{42\text{ kg}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 6 to simplify to \(\frac{3\text{ dollars}}{7\text{ kg}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 28 metres in 16 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{28\text{ m}}{16\text{ s}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by 4 to obtain \(\frac{7\text{ m}}{4\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 6.4 km in 28 minutes
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to eliminate the decimal, yielding \(\frac{64\text{ km}}{280\text{ min}}\), and then divide by 8 to get \(\frac{8\text{ km}}{35\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4.5 L in 75 minutes
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{45\text{ L}}{750\text{ min}}\), then divide both by 15 to get \(\frac{3\text{ L}}{50\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 540 words in 144 seconds
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{540\text{ words}}{144\text{ s}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 36, to simplify to \(\frac{15\text{ words}}{4\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 280 metres in 105 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{280\text{ m}}{105\text{ s}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by 35 to obtain \(\frac{8\text{ m}}{3\text{ s}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 168 km in 72 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{168\text{ km}}{72\text{ min}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 24, to simplify to \(\frac{7\text{ km}}{3\text{ min}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 6 boxes of tiles to cover 15 square meters
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{6\text{ boxes}}{15\text{ square meters}}\) and divide both numbers by their greatest common factor, 3. The simplified rate is \(\frac{2\text{ boxes}}{5\text{ square meters}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 9 rolls of tape to seal 24 boxes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{9\text{ rolls}}{24\text{ boxes}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 3. This gives \(\frac{3\text{ rolls}}{8\text{ boxes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 4 gallons of paint to cover 14 walls
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{4\text{ gallons}}{14\text{ walls}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 2. This simplifies to \(\frac{2\text{ gallons}}{7\text{ walls}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 5 bags of fertilizer to treat 35 trees
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{5\text{ bags}}{35\text{ trees}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 5. The resulting rate in simplest form is \(\frac{1\text{ bag}}{7\text{ trees}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 8 hours of labor to assemble 18 bicycles
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{8\text{ hours}}{18\text{ bicycles}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 2. This simplifies to \(\frac{4\text{ hours}}{9\text{ bicycles}}\).

qs.q: A volunteer worked 18 hours in the first week and 27 hours in the second week to complete 12 community projects. Write the rate of total hours worked to projects completed in simplest form.
qs.s: The total time worked is \(18 + 27 = 45\) hours, giving the rate \(\frac{45\text{ hours}}{12\text{ projects}}\). Dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 3, yields \(\frac{15\text{ hours}}{4\text{ projects}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 5.6 meters of fabric to make 16 shirts
qs.s: Multiply both quantities by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{56\text{ meters}}{160\text{ shirts}}\). Dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 8, results in \(\frac{7\text{ meters}}{20\text{ shirts}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 3.5 kilograms of fertilizer for 14 garden plots
qs.s: Multiply both quantities by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{35\text{ kilograms}}{140\text{ garden plots}}\). Dividing both terms by their greatest common factor, 35, yields \(\frac{1\text{ kilogram}}{4\text{ garden plots}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: $4.20 for 24 kilograms of apples, expressed as a rate of cents to kilograms
qs.s: Convert $4.20 to 420 cents to write the rate as \(\frac{420\text{ cents}}{24\text{ kilograms}}\). Dividing both terms by their greatest common factor, 12, gives \(\frac{35\text{ cents}}{2\text{ kilograms}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 144 miles driven on 32 gallons of fuel
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{144\text{ miles}}{32\text{ gallons}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 16. This simplifies to \(\frac{9\text{ miles}}{2\text{ gallons}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 85 words typed in 10 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{85\text{ words}}{10\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 5 to obtain \(\frac{17\text{ words}}{2\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 90 miles driven on 4 gallons
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{90\text{ miles}}{4\text{ gallons}}\) and simplify by dividing both the numerator and denominator by 2 to obtain \(\frac{45\text{ miles}}{2\text{ gallons}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 75 points scored in 6 games
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{75\text{ points}}{6\text{ games}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 3, to get \(\frac{25\text{ points}}{2\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 42 laps swum in 8 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{42\text{ laps}}{8\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 2, to get \(\frac{21\text{ laps}}{4\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 68 dollars earned in 6 hours
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{68\text{ dollars}}{6\text{ hours}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 2 to get \(\frac{34\text{ dollars}}{3\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: A delivery truck traveled 115 kilometers in the morning and 95 kilometers in the afternoon, taking a total of 24 hours. Write the rate of kilometers to hours in simplest form.
qs.s: First find the total distance: \(115 + 95 = 210\text{ km}\). Then write the rate \(\frac{210\text{ km}}{24\text{ hours}}\) and divide both terms by 6 to get \(\frac{35\text{ km}}{4\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 378 miles driven on 28 gallons of fuel
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{378\text{ miles}}{28\text{ gallons}}\) and simplify by dividing both terms by their greatest common factor, 14, yielding \(\frac{27\text{ miles}}{2\text{ gallons}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 720 meters sprinted in 54 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{720\text{ meters}}{54\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 18, to get \(\frac{40\text{ meters}}{3\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write in simplest form: 7.5 kilograms of flour packed into 12 bags
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator of \(\frac{7.5\text{ kg}}{12\text{ bags}}\) by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{75\text{ kg}}{120\text{ bags}}\), then divide both by 15 to get \(\frac{5\text{ kg}}{8\text{ bags}}\).

qs.q: A printer printed 260 pages of a report and 190 pages of a manual during a run of 15 minutes before lunch and 25 minutes after lunch. Write the rate of total pages printed to total minutes in simplest form.
qs.s: First calculate total pages, \(260 + 190 = 450\), and total time, \(15 + 25 = 40\text{ minutes}\). Then simplify the rate \(\frac{450\text{ pages}}{40\text{ minutes}}\) by dividing both terms by 10 to obtain \(\frac{45\text{ pages}}{4\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: $278 for 4 concert tickets
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{\$278}{4\text{ tickets}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by 2 to obtain \(\frac{\$139}{2\text{ tickets}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 345 words in 6 minutes
qs.s: Divide both 345 words and 6 minutes by their common factor of 3 to simplify the rate to \(\frac{115\text{ words}}{2\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 425 meters in 10 seconds
qs.s: Express as a fraction \(\frac{425\text{ meters}}{10\text{ seconds}}\) and divide both terms by 5 to obtain \(\frac{85\text{ meters}}{2\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 290 km on 12 L of fuel
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{290\text{ km}}{12\text{ L}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 2, to get \(\frac{145\text{ km}}{6\text{ L}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: $218 for 6 days of equipment rental
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{\$218}{6\text{ days}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by 2 to get \(\frac{\$109}{3\text{ days}}\).

qs.q: A delivery driver earned $270 for a 16-hour shift on Friday and $186 for a 12-hour shift on Saturday. Write the overall rate of earnings to hours worked in simplest form.
qs.s: Find the totals: \(\$270 + \$186 = \$456\) and \(16 + 12 = 28\text{ hours}\), then divide both terms of \(\frac{\$456}{28\text{ hours}}\) by 4 to get \(\frac{\$114}{7\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 14.4 kg of seed for 32 bird feeders
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to eliminate the decimal, yielding \(\frac{144\text{ kg}}{320\text{ feeders}}\), then divide numerator and denominator by 16 to get \(\frac{9\text{ kg}}{20\text{ feeders}}\).

qs.q: A factory produced 1,480 bolts in a 24-hour shift and 1,160 bolts in an 18-hour shift. Write the overall rate of total bolts produced to total hours in simplest form.
qs.s: Calculate total bolts as \(1,480 + 1,160 = 2,640\) and total time as \(24 + 18 = 42\text{ hours}\), then divide both terms of \(\frac{2,640\text{ bolts}}{42\text{ hours}}\) by 6 to obtain \(\frac{440\text{ bolts}}{7\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 1,224 km on 45 L of fuel
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{1,224\text{ km}}{45\text{ L}}\) and divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 9, to get \(\frac{136\text{ km}}{5\text{ L}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: $52.50 for 14 hours of equipment rental
qs.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{\$525}{140\text{ hours}}\), then divide both by 35 to get \(\frac{\$15}{4\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 450 dollars earned for 12 hours of work
qs.s: Set up the rate as \(\frac{450\text{ dollars}}{12\text{ hours}}\) and divide both terms by their greatest common factor, 6, resulting in \(\frac{75\text{ dollars}}{2\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 180 meters run in 24 seconds
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{180\text{ meters}}{24\text{ seconds}}\) and divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 12, to obtain \(\frac{15\text{ meters}}{2\text{ seconds}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 140 points scored in 8 games
qs.s: Express the rate as \(\frac{140\text{ points}}{8\text{ games}}\) and reduce by dividing both numerator and denominator by 4 to get \(\frac{35\text{ points}}{2\text{ games}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 260 words typed in 8 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{260\text{ words}}{8\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 4, to get \(\frac{65\text{ words}}{2\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 350 miles driven on 15 gallons of gasoline
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{350\text{ miles}}{15\text{ gallons}}\) and simplify by dividing both numbers by their greatest common factor, 5, to get \(\frac{70\text{ miles}}{3\text{ gallons}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 8.4 gigabytes downloaded in 2.24 minutes
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 100 to eliminate the decimals to get \(\frac{840\text{ gigabytes}}{224\text{ minutes}}\), then divide both by their greatest common factor, 56, to reach \(\frac{15\text{ gigabytes}}{4\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 6.75 pounds of seed planted across 18 garden beds
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 100 to clear decimals, resulting in \(\frac{675\text{ pounds}}{1800\text{ garden beds}}\), then divide both by their greatest common factor, 225, to get \(\frac{3\text{ pounds}}{8\text{ garden beds}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 1,330 liters of water pumped in 315 minutes
qs.s: Write the rate as \(\frac{1330\text{ liters}}{315\text{ minutes}}\) and divide both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 35, to obtain \(\frac{38\text{ liters}}{9\text{ minutes}}\).

qs.q: Write the rate in simplest form: 17.5 kilograms of fertilizer spread over 28 square meters
qs.s: Multiply both terms by 10 to clear the decimal, giving \(\frac{175\text{ kilograms}}{280\text{ square meters}}\), then divide numerator and denominator by 35 to get \(\frac{5\text{ kilograms}}{8\text{ square meters}}\).

qs.q: A factory produces 380 small toys and 340 large toys over a period of 56 hours. Write the rate of total toys produced to hours in simplest form.
qs.s: Find the total quantity of toys, \(380 + 340 = 720\text{ toys}\), and write the rate \(\frac{720\text{ toys}}{56\text{ hours}}\), then divide both terms by 8 to get \(\frac{90\text{ toys}}{7\text{ hours}}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
15 baskets in 60 attempts
qs.s: Divide the number of baskets by the number of attempts: \(\frac{15\text{ baskets}}{60\text{ attempts}} = 0.25\text{ baskets/attempt}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
6 runs in 30 innings
qs.s: Divide the number of runs by the number of innings: \(\frac{6\text{ runs}}{30\text{ innings}} = 0.2\text{ runs/inning}\).

qs.q:

21 questions in 35 minutes
