qs.q: Determine the unit rate: \(18\text{ m}\) of rope for 5 tents
qs.s: Divide \(18\text{ m}\) by 5 tents: \(18 \div 5 = 3.6\text{ m/tent}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: \(558\text{ km}\) on \(45\text{ L}\) of gasoline
qs.s: Divide \(558\text{ km}\) by \(45\text{ L}\): \(558 \div 45 = 12.4\text{ km/L}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in meters per costume: \(0.18\text{ km}\) of fabric for 75 costumes
qs.s: Convert \(0.18\text{ km}\) to \(180\text{ m}\), then divide by 75 costumes: \(180 \div 75 = 2.4\text{ m/costume}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in dollars per kilogram: \(\$7.80\) for \(650\text{ g}\) of cheese
qs.s: Convert \(650\text{ g}\) to \(0.65\text{ kg}\), then divide: \(\$7.80 \div 0.65\text{ kg} = \$12/\text{kg}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in calories per kilogram: \(224\text{ calories}\) in \(350\text{ g}\) of yogurt
qs.s: Convert \(350\text{ g}\) to \(0.35\text{ kg}\), then divide \(224\text{ calories}\) by \(0.35\text{ kg}\): \(224 \div 0.35 = 640\text{ calories/kg}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in cents per ounce: \(\$4.56\) for \(16\text{ ounces}\) of juice
qs.s: Convert \(\$4.56\) to \(456\text{ cents}\), then divide by \(16\text{ ounces}\): \(456 \div 16 = 28.5\text{ cents/ounce}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 14 litres in 56 minutes.
qs.s: Divide the volume by the time: 14 L / 56 min = 0.25 L/min.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 18 km in 45 minutes.
qs.s: Divide the distance by the time: 18 km / 45 min = 0.4 km/min.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: $9 for 12 pens.
qs.s: Divide the total cost by the number of pens: $9 / 12 = $0.75/pen.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 24 questions in 30 minutes.
qs.s: Divide the number of questions by the time: 24 questions / 30 min = 0.8 questions/min.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 15 metres in 25 seconds.
qs.s: Divide the distance by the time: 15 m / 25 s = 0.6 m/s.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in cents per millilitre: $3.85 for 250 millilitres.
qs.s: Convert $3.85 to 385 cents, then divide by the volume: 385 cents / 250 mL = 1.54 cents/mL.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in kilometres per hour: 28 km in 35 minutes.
qs.s: Convert 35 minutes to hours (35/60 h = 7/12 h), then divide: 28 km / (7/12 h) = 48 km/h.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in calories per kilogram: a 400-gram serving contains 350 calories.
qs.s: Convert 400 grams to 0.4 kilograms, then divide the calories: 350 calories / 0.4 kg = 875 calories/kg.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in cents per gram: $6.48 for 360 grams.
qs.s: Convert $6.48 to 648 cents, then divide by the mass: 648 cents / 360 g = 1.8 cents/g.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in metres per second: 1.62 km in 45 seconds.
qs.s: Convert 1.62 kilometres to 1620 metres, then divide by the time: 1620 m / 45 s = 36 m/s.

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 4 bags of mulch to cover 20 garden beds.
qs.s: Divide the number of garden beds by the number of bags: \(\frac{20\text{ garden beds}}{4\text{ bags}} = 5\text{ garden beds/bag}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 6 packs of shingles to repair 24 square metres of roof.
qs.s: Divide the area repaired by the number of packs: \(\frac{24\text{ square metres}}{6\text{ packs}} = 4\text{ square metres/pack}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 3 hours to assemble 12 bicycles.
qs.s: Divide the number of bicycles by the number of hours: \(\frac{12\text{ bicycles}}{3\text{ hours}} = 4\text{ bicycles/hour}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 6 rolls of ribbon to wrap 48 gift boxes.
qs.s: Divide the number of gift boxes by the number of rolls: \(\frac{48\text{ gift boxes}}{6\text{ rolls}} = 8\text{ gift boxes/roll}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 8 packets of seeds to plant 40 rows of carrots.
qs.s: Divide the number of rows by the number of packets: \(\frac{40\text{ rows}}{8\text{ packets}} = 5\text{ rows/packet}\).

qs.q: A forestry crew cleared 210 hectares of land. The team began with 20 drums of fuel and had 5 drums remaining when the work was completed. Determine the unit rate in hectares per drum of fuel consumed.
qs.s: Find the fuel consumed: \(20 - 5 = 15\text{ drums}\). Then divide the area cleared by the drums consumed: \(\frac{210\text{ hectares}}{15\text{ drums}} = 14\text{ hectares/drum}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in cents per can: $13.20 for a case of 24 cans of sparkling water.
qs.s: Convert the total cost to cents: \(\$13.20 = 1320\text{ cents}\). Then divide by the number of cans: \(\frac{1320\text{ cents}}{24\text{ cans}} = 55\text{ cents/can}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in kilometres per hour: 45 minutes to travel 54 kilometres.
qs.s: Convert 45 minutes to hours: \(\frac{45}{60}\text{ hours} = 0.75\text{ hours}\). Then divide the distance by time: \(\frac{54\text{ km}}{0.75\text{ hours}} = 72\text{ km/h}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 8 tanks of fuel to cultivate 372 acres of farmland.
qs.s: Divide the total acreage by the number of tanks: \(\frac{372\text{ acres}}{8\text{ tanks}} = 46.5\text{ acres/tank}\).

qs.q: A mowing crew used 2.5 tanks of fuel in the morning and 3.5 tanks in the afternoon to cut 105 acres of grass. Determine the unit rate in acres per tank.
qs.s: First, find the total fuel used: \(2.5 + 3.5 = 6\text{ tanks}\). Then divide the total acreage by the total fuel: \(\frac{105\text{ acres}}{6\text{ tanks}} = 17.5\text{ acres/tank}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 84 laps swum in 8 practices.
qs.s: Divide the number of laps by the number of practices: \(\frac{84\text{ laps}}{8\text{ practices}} = 10.5\text{ laps/practice}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 195 words typed in 4 minutes.
qs.s: Divide the number of words by the minutes: \(\frac{195\text{ words}}{4\text{ min}} = 48.75\text{ words/min}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 75 meters sprinted in 6 seconds.
qs.s: Divide the distance by the time: \(\frac{75\text{ m}}{6\text{ s}} = 12.5\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 105 kilometers traveled on 6 litres of fuel.
qs.s: Divide the distance by the volume of fuel: \(\frac{105\text{ km}}{6\text{ L}} = 17.5\text{ km/L}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate: 54 points scored in 4 games.
qs.s: Divide the total points by the number of games: \(\frac{54\text{ points}}{4\text{ games}} = 13.5\text{ points/game}\).

qs.q: Determine the unit rate in kilometers per hour: a cyclist travels 18 kilometers in 45 minutes.
qs.s: Convert 45 minutes to hours (\(45\text{ min} = 0.75\text{ h}\)), then divide: \(\frac{18\text{ km}}{0.75\text{ h}} = 24\text{ km/h}\).

qs.q: A 400-gram container of yogurt contains 350 calories. Determine the caloric unit rate in calories per kilogram.
qs.s: Convert 400 grams to kilograms (\(400\text{ g} = 0.4\text{ kg}\)), then divide: \(\frac{350\text{ calories}}{0.4\text{ kg}} = 875\text{ calories/kg}\).

qs.q: A delivery van travels 145 kilometers in the morning and 215 kilometers in the afternoon, taking a total of 8 hours. Determine the overall unit rate in kilometers per hour.
qs.s: Add the distances to find the total (\(145\text{ km} + 215\text{ km} = 360\text{ km}\)), then divide by total time: \(\frac{360\text{ km}}{8\text{ h}} = 45\text{ km/h}\).

qs.q: A butcher sells a 6-pound turkey breast for $20.91. Determine the unit rate in cents per pound.
qs.s: Convert $20.91 to 2091 cents, then divide by the weight: \(\frac{2091\text{ cents}}{6\text{ lbs}} = 348.5\text{ cents/lb}\).

qs.q: A factory machine produces 585 parts in 4.5 hours of continuous operation. Determine the unit rate in parts per hour.
qs.s: Divide the total parts by the decimal number of hours: \(\frac{585\text{ parts}}{4.5\text{ h}} = 130\text{ parts/h}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
$375 for 6 nights at a campsite
qs.s: Divide the total cost by the number of nights: \(\frac{\$375}{6} = \$62.50\) per night.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
$474 for 5 days of car rental
qs.s: Divide the total cost by the number of days: \(\frac{\$474}{5} = \$94.80\) per day.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
$258 for 4 concert tickets
qs.s: Divide the total cost by the number of tickets: \(\frac{\$258}{4} = \$64.50\) per ticket.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
186 km driven in 4 hours
qs.s: Divide the total distance by the time: \(\frac{186\text{ km}}{4\text{ h}} = 46.5\text{ km/h}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
315 pages read in 6 days
qs.s: Divide the total number of pages by the number of days: \(\frac{315\text{ pages}}{6\text{ days}} = 52.5\text{ pages per day}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in meters per minute.
5.4 km traveled in 15 minutes
qs.s: Convert 5.4 km to 5,400 meters, then divide by the time: \(\frac{5,400\text{ m}}{15\text{ min}} = 360\text{ m/min}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in calories per kilogram.
310 calories in a 400-gram serving of yogurt
qs.s: Convert 400 grams to 0.4 kilograms, then divide calories by kilograms: \(\frac{310\text{ calories}}{0.4\text{ kg}} = 775\text{ calories per kilogram}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in dollars per hour.
$1,092 earned for 32.5 hours of work
qs.s: Divide the total earnings by the number of hours worked: \(\frac{\$1,092}{32.5\text{ h}} = \$33.60\) per hour.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in cents per ounce.
$7.56 for a 24-ounce jar of honey
qs.s: Convert $7.56 to 756 cents, then divide by the number of ounces: \(\frac{756\text{ cents}}{24\text{ oz}} = 31.5\text{ cents per ounce}\).

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate per night.
A 4-night hotel stay costing $588 plus a one-time $48 service fee
qs.s: Add the service fee to get the total cost, \(\$588 + \$48 = \$636\), and divide by 4 nights: \(\frac{\$636}{4} = \$159\) per night.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
378 words typed in 4 minutes
qs.s: Divide 378 words by 4 minutes to get the unit rate of 94.5 words/minute.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
348 grams of sugar in an 8-serving cake
qs.s: Divide 348 grams by 8 servings to determine the unit rate: 348 / 8 = 43.5 grams/serving.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
182 miles traveled on 5 gallons of fuel
qs.s: Divide 182 miles by 5 gallons to find the unit rate: 182 / 5 = 36.4 miles/gallon.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
$45 paid for 6 movie tickets
qs.s: Divide $45 by 6 tickets to calculate the unit price: 45 / 6 = $7.50 per ticket.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
234 kilometers in a 4-hour drive
qs.s: Divide 234 kilometers by 4 hours to find the unit rate: 234 / 4 = 58.5 kilometers/hour.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in kilometers per hour.
10.5 kilometers traveled in 1.25 hours
qs.s: Divide 10.5 kilometers by 1.25 hours to obtain the unit rate of 8.4 km/hour.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in calories per kilogram.
A 400-gram container of yogurt contains 290 calories
qs.s: Convert 400 grams to 0.4 kilograms, then divide 290 calories by 0.4 kilograms to obtain 725 calories/kg.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in meters per second.
1.8 kilometers traveled in 4 minutes
qs.s: Convert 1.8 kilometers to 1,800 meters and 4 minutes to 240 seconds, then divide 1,800 by 240 to get 7.5 meters/second.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate.
1,458 kilometers traveled on 72 liters of fuel
qs.s: Divide 1,458 kilometers by 72 liters to calculate the unit rate of 20.25 km/L.

qs.q:
Determine the unit rate in cents per ounce.
$3.80 for a 16-ounce bottle of shampoo
qs.s: Convert $3.80 to 380 cents, then divide by 16 ounces to get 23.75 cents/ounce.

exercises.name: Word Problems Involving Rates and Unit Rates

qs.q: Liam works at a community center. He earns $1271 for working 41 hours over two weeks. What was his hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Divide the total earnings by the total hours worked: \(\frac{\$1271}{41\text{ h}} = \$31/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Elena works at a bookstore. She earns $1140 for working 76 hours over two weeks. What was her hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Divide the total earnings by the total hours worked: \(\frac{\$1140}{76\text{ h}} = \$15/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Marcus works at an electronics store. He earns $1128 for working 48 hours over two weeks. What was his hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Divide the total earnings by the total number of hours: \(\frac{\$1128}{48\text{ h}} = \$23.50/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Brenda works at a bakery. She earns $988 for working 52 hours over two weeks. What was her hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Divide the total earnings by the total hours worked: \(\frac{\$988}{52\text{ h}} = \$19/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Kendra works at a veterinary clinic. She earns $1564 for working 68 hours over two weeks. What was her hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Divide the total earnings by the total hours worked: \(\frac{\$1564}{68\text{ h}} = \$23/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Mateo worked 38 hours during his first week on the job and 42 hours during his second week. If he earned a total of $1960 over the two weeks, what was his hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Find the total hours worked: \(38\text{ h} + 42\text{ h} = 80\text{ h}\). Then divide total earnings by total hours: \(\frac{\$1960}{80\text{ h}} = \$24.50/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Devontae worked 5 shifts that were each 7 hours and 30 minutes long. If he earned a total of $975 for these shifts, what was his hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Convert the shift length to hours: \(7\text{ h } 30\text{ min} = 7.5\text{ h}\), so the total time worked is \(5 \times 7.5\text{ h} = 37.5\text{ h}\). Divide total earnings by total hours: \(\frac{\$975}{37.5\text{ h}} = \$26/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Talia and two of her coworkers were paid a total of $2970 to split equally for working 45 hours each on a community project. What was Talia's hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Divide the total pay equally among the 3 workers to find Talia's earnings: \(\frac{\$2970}{3} = \$990\). Then divide her earnings by her hours worked: \(\frac{\$990}{45\text{ h}} = \$22/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Aaron earned $936 for working 52 hours at a warehouse, while Beatrice earned $1344 for working 56 hours at a retail store. How much more did Beatrice earn per hour than Aaron?
qs.s: Aaron's hourly rate is \(\frac{\$936}{52\text{ h}} = \$18/\text{h}\), and Beatrice's hourly rate is \(\frac{\$1344}{56\text{ h}} = \$24/\text{h}\). The difference between their rates is \(\$24/\text{h} - \$18/\text{h} = \$6/\text{h}\).

qs.q: Chloe worked 38 hours last week. Her paycheck included a $75 attendance bonus, bringing her total earnings for the week to $1044. What was her hourly rate of pay?
qs.s: Subtract the bonus from the total paycheck to find earnings from hourly work: \(\$1044 - \$75 = \$969\). Then divide by the hours worked: \(\frac{\$969}{38\text{ h}} = \$25.50/\text{h}\).

qs.q: A student earns $108.00 for 9 hours of work. How much would the student earn for 14 hours of work at the same hourly rate?
qs.s: The hourly rate is $108.00 ÷ 9 = $12.00 per hour. For 14 hours of work, the student earns 14 × $12.00 = $168.00.

qs.q: Six kilograms of apples cost $15.00. What would be the cost of nine kilograms of the same apples?
qs.s: The unit price is $15.00 ÷ 6 = $2.50 per kilogram. Therefore, nine kilograms cost 9 × $2.50 = $22.50.

qs.q: Eight notebooks cost $28.00. What would be the cost of five of the same notebooks?
qs.s: The unit rate is $28.00 ÷ 8 = $3.50 per notebook. For five notebooks, the cost is 5 × $3.50 = $17.50.

qs.q: Fifteen pens cost $18.00. What would be the cost of eight of the same pens?
qs.s: The unit price is $18.00 ÷ 15 = $1.20 per pen. Eight pens will cost 8 × $1.20 = $9.60.

qs.q: A car travels 210 kilometres in 3 hours at a constant speed. At the same rate, how far would the car travel in 5 hours?
qs.s: The unit rate is 210 km ÷ 3 h = 70 km/h. In 5 hours, the car travels 5 h × 70 km/h = 350 km.

qs.q: A store sells a 400-gram block of cheese for $5.20. At the same rate, how much more does a 1.5-kilogram block of the same cheese cost than the 400-gram block?
qs.s: Since 400 g = 0.4 kg, the unit rate is $5.20 ÷ 0.4 = $13.00 per kg. A 1.5 kg block costs 1.5 × $13.00 = $19.50, which is $19.50 - $5.20 = $14.30 more.

qs.q: A cyclist travels 14 kilometres in 40 minutes at a constant speed. At this rate, how many kilometres will the cyclist travel in 2.5 hours?
qs.s: The cyclist's speed is 14 km ÷ 40 min = 0.35 km/min, which is 0.35 × 60 = 21 km/h. In 2.5 hours, the distance traveled is 2.5 h × 21 km/h = 52.5 km.

qs.q: A printing press prints 840 posters in 35 minutes. At this rate, how many posters can it print in 2 hours and 15 minutes?
qs.s: The printing rate is 840 ÷ 35 = 24 posters per minute. Since 2 hours and 15 minutes equals 135 minutes, the press can print 135 × 24 = 3240 posters.

qs.q: At a market, 6 baskets of strawberries cost $33.00 and 4 baskets of blueberries cost $26.00. What is the total cost for 5 baskets of strawberries and 3 baskets of blueberries?
qs.s: Strawberries cost $33.00 ÷ 6 = $5.50 per basket, and blueberries cost $26.00 ÷ 4 = $6.50 per basket. The total cost is (5 × $5.50) + (3 × $6.50) = $27.50 + $19.50 = $47.00.

qs.q: A car uses 18 litres of petrol to travel 225 kilometres. Petrol costs $1.65 per litre. At this consumption rate, what is the cost of the petrol needed to travel 350 kilometres?
qs.s: The rate of fuel consumption is 18 L ÷ 225 km = 0.08 L/km, so traveling 350 km requires 350 × 0.08 = 28 litres. At $1.65 per litre, the total cost is 28 × $1.65 = $46.20.

qs.q: A factory machine packages 319.2 kg of dog food in 6 hours. At this constant rate, how many kilograms of dog food will it package in 8 hours?
qs.s: The unit rate is \(319.2\text{ kg} \div 6\text{ h} = 53.2\text{ kg/h}\). In 8 hours, it packages \(53.2\text{ kg/h} \times 8\text{ h} = 425.6\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: Maya earned $187.50 for working 5 hours at a bookstore. If she is paid at the same hourly rate, how much will she earn for working 12 hours?
qs.s: Maya's hourly rate is \(\$187.50 \div 5\text{ h} = \$37.50/\text{h}\). Working 12 hours earns her \(\$37.50/\text{h} \times 12\text{ h} = \$450.00\).

qs.q: A printing press prints 437.5 pages in 5 minutes. At this constant rate, how many pages can it print in 14 minutes?
qs.s: The unit rate is \(437.5\text{ pages} \div 5\text{ min} = 87.5\text{ pages/min}\). In 14 minutes, it prints \(87.5\text{ pages/min} \times 14\text{ min} = 1225\text{ pages}\).

qs.q: A cyclist travels at a constant speed and covers 85.5 km in 3 hours. If the cyclist travels at the same rate, how far would they travel in 7 hours?
qs.s: The cyclist's unit rate is \(85.5\text{ km} \div 3\text{ h} = 28.5\text{ km/h}\). Traveling at this rate for 7 hours yields \(28.5\text{ km/h} \times 7\text{ h} = 199.5\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A water pump discharges 162.4 liters of water in 4 minutes. At this constant rate, how many liters of water can it pump in 9 minutes?
qs.s: The unit rate is \(162.4\text{ L} \div 4\text{ min} = 40.6\text{ L/min}\). In 9 minutes, the pump discharges \(40.6\text{ L/min} \times 9\text{ min} = 365.4\text{ L}\).

qs.q: Marcus drives 184 km in 2 hours, and Elena drives 217.5 km in 2.5 hours. If both continue driving at their constant speeds, how much farther will Marcus travel than Elena in 6 hours?
qs.s: Marcus drives at \(184\text{ km} \div 2\text{ h} = 92\text{ km/h}\) and Elena at \(217.5\text{ km} \div 2.5\text{ h} = 87\text{ km/h}\). The difference in distance over 6 hours is \((92\text{ km/h} - 87\text{ km/h}) \times 6\text{ h} = 30\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A bulk food store sells 350 grams of almonds for $4.90. At the same rate per kilogram, how much more does a customer pay for a 1.2 kg bag of almonds than for an 800 g bag?
qs.s: Since \(350\text{ g} = 0.35\text{ kg}\), the unit rate is \(\$4.90 \div 0.35\text{ kg} = \$14.00/\text{kg}\). The weight difference is \(1.2\text{ kg} - 0.8\text{ kg} = 0.4\text{ kg}\), so the customer pays \(0.4\text{ kg} \times \$14.00/\text{kg} = \$5.60\) more.

qs.q: A water purification system filters 50.4 liters of water in 45 minutes. At this constant rate, how many hours will it take to filter 235.2 liters of water?
qs.s: The filtration rate is \(50.4\text{ L} \div 45\text{ min} = 1.12\text{ L/min}\), which equals \(1.12 \times 60 = 67.2\text{ L/h}\). Filtering \(235.2\text{ L}\) will take \(235.2\text{ L} \div 67.2\text{ L/h} = 3.5\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A high-speed train travels 148.5 km in 45 minutes at a constant speed. At this rate, how many kilometers does the train travel in 2.5 hours?
qs.s: The speed is \(148.5\text{ km} \div 45\text{ min} = 3.3\text{ km/min}\). Since \(2.5\text{ hours} = 150\text{ minutes}\), the distance traveled is \(3.3\text{ km/min} \times 150\text{ min} = 495\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A runner burned 540 calories during a 45-minute workout. If the runner continues running at the exact same rate, how many calories will they burn in 1 hour and 35 minutes?
qs.s: The runner burns \(540\text{ calories} \div 45\text{ min} = 12\text{ calories/min}\). Converting 1 hour 35 minutes to 95 minutes, the total burned is \(12\text{ calories/min} \times 95\text{ min} = 1140\text{ calories}\).

qs.q: An arcade charges a fixed rate per game token. If 8 tokens cost $6.80, how much would 11 tokens cost?
qs.s: Each token costs $6.80 / 8 = $0.85. For 11 tokens, the total cost is 11 * $0.85 = $9.35.

qs.q: A bakery charges the same price for every bagel. If 5 bagels cost $6.25, how much would 7 bagels cost?
qs.s: The cost per bagel is $6.25 / 5 = $1.25. For 7 bagels, the cost is 7 * $1.25 = $8.75.

qs.q: A convenience store charges the same price for each bottle of juice. If 3 bottles cost $5.85, how much do 5 bottles cost?
qs.s: The unit price is $5.85 / 3 = $1.95 per bottle. Thus, 5 bottles cost 5 * $1.95 = $9.75.

qs.q: A stationery store sells notebooks at a constant price per notebook. If 6 notebooks cost $8.70, how much would 8 notebooks cost?
qs.s: The unit price is $8.70 / 6 = $1.45 per notebook. Multiplying by 8 gives 8 * $1.45 = $11.60.

qs.q: An orchard charges the same price per kilogram of apples. If 4 kilograms of apples cost $9.80, how much do 6 kilograms cost?
qs.s: The unit rate is $9.80 / 4 = $2.45 per kilogram. Therefore, 6 kilograms cost 6 * $2.45 = $14.70.

qs.q: A hybrid car travels 372 km on 24 L of fuel. At this same rate of fuel consumption, how many litres of fuel are needed to travel 589 km?
qs.s: The car's fuel efficiency is 372 / 24 = 15.5 km/L. To travel 589 km, the fuel needed is 589 / 15.5 = 38 L.

qs.q: A fabric store sells ribbon at a constant rate per meter. If a 60-centimeter strip of ribbon costs $1.50, how much would a 2.5-meter strip of the same ribbon cost?
qs.s: Converting 60 cm to 0.6 m, the rate is $1.50 / 0.6 = $2.50 per meter. For 2.5 meters, the cost is 2.5 * $2.50 = $6.25.

qs.q: An office supply store charges the same price for each box of printer paper. A company pays $74.25 for 9 boxes. How much more would it cost to purchase 16 boxes instead of 9 boxes?
qs.s: The unit rate is $74.25 / 9 = $8.25 per box. Purchasing 16 boxes instead of 9 requires 7 more boxes, which costs 7 * $8.25 = $57.75.

qs.q: A bulk food store sells roasted almonds at a constant price. A 400-gram bag of almonds costs $5.40. How much would a 1.4-kilogram bag of almonds cost?
qs.s: Since 400 g is 0.4 kg, the price per kilogram is $5.40 / 0.4 = $13.50. A 1.4-kilogram bag costs 1.4 * $13.50 = $18.90.

qs.q: A farm stand sells peaches at a constant price per basket. If 6 baskets of peaches cost $34.50, how much change would a customer receive from a $50 bill after buying 8 baskets of peaches?
qs.s: The price per basket is $34.50 / 6 = $5.75, so 8 baskets cost 8 * $5.75 = $46.00. The change from a $50 bill is $50.00 - $46.00 = $4.00.

qs.q: An employee earns an annual salary of $75 000 and contributes $6000 each year to a retirement fund. Find the ratio of the retirement contribution to the annual salary in simplest form.
qs.s: Set up the ratio as \(\frac{6000}{75\,000}\). Divide both numbers by \(3000\) to get \(\frac{2}{25}\), or \(2 : 25\).

qs.q: A charity organization raised $250 000 during an annual fundraiser and spent $15 000 on event expenses. Find the ratio of event expenses to the total amount raised in simplest form.
qs.s: Set up the ratio as \(\frac{15\,000}{250\,000}\). Divide both numerator and denominator by \(5000\) to simplify to \(\frac{3}{50}\), or \(3 : 50\).

qs.q: A company earned $480 000 in revenue and paid $16 000 in local licensing fees. Find the ratio of local fees to total revenue in simplest form.
qs.s: Set up the ratio as \(\frac{16\,000}{480\,000}\). Divide both the numerator and denominator by \(16\,000\) to get \(\frac{1}{30}\), or \(1 : 30\).

qs.q: A buyer purchased a vehicle for $36 000 and made a down payment of $4500. Find the ratio of the down payment to the total vehicle price in simplest form.
qs.s: Set up the ratio as \(\frac{4500}{36\,000}\). Divide both terms by their greatest common factor, \(4500\), to obtain \(\frac{1}{8}\), or \(1 : 8\).

qs.q: A homeowner budgeted $84 000 for a home renovation, of which $14 000 was spent on permits and architectural plans. Find the ratio of the cost of permits and plans to the total renovation budget in simplest form.
qs.s: Form the ratio \(\frac{14\,000}{84\,000}\). Dividing both terms by \(14\,000\) simplifies the ratio to \(\frac{1}{6}\), or \(1 : 6\).

qs.q: An athlete completed a 5 km race. During the final sprint, the athlete covered 400 m. Find the ratio of the sprint distance to the distance covered before the sprint in simplest form.
qs.s: Convert \(5\text{ km}\) to \(5000\text{ m}\). The distance before the sprint is \(5000\text{ m} - 400\text{ m} = 4600\text{ m}\), giving a ratio of \(\frac{400}{4600} = \frac{2}{23}\), or \(2 : 23\).

qs.q: A commercial building is valued at $850 000. The owner pays $5100 in city property tax and $1700 in regional transit tax. Find the ratio of total taxes paid to the building's value in simplest form.
qs.s: The total taxes are $5100 + 1700 = $6800. The ratio of total taxes to value is \(\frac{6800}{850\,000} = \frac{68}{8500} = \frac{4}{500} = \frac{1}{125}\), or \(1 : 125\).

qs.q: A student spent 1 hour and 15 minutes on math homework and 45 minutes reading a novel. Find the ratio of reading time to total study time in simplest form.
qs.s: Convert the math time to minutes: \(1\text{ h } 15\text{ min} = 75\text{ min}\). The total study time is \(75 + 45 = 120\text{ min}\), giving a ratio of \(\frac{45}{120} = \frac{3}{8}\), or \(3 : 8\).

qs.q: A small business earned a total revenue of $720 000 last year. Its operating costs were $480 000 and taxes were $90 000, with the remaining amount being net profit. Find the ratio of net profit to total revenue in simplest form.
qs.s: Subtract the expenses to find the net profit: \(720\,000 - (480\,000 + 90\,000) = 150\,000\). The ratio of profit to revenue is \(\frac{150\,000}{720\,000} = \frac{5}{24}\), or \(5 : 24\).

qs.q: A bakery uses 750 g of flour from a 6 kg bag to bake bread. Find the ratio of the flour used to the flour remaining in the bag in simplest form.
qs.s: Convert \(6\text{ kg}\) to \(6000\text{ g}\). The remaining flour is \(6000\text{ g} - 750\text{ g} = 5250\text{ g}\), so the ratio of used to remaining flour is \(\frac{750}{5250} = \frac{1}{7}\), or \(1 : 7\).

qs.q: A bakery made 720 pastries in one morning. If 450 of the pastries were croissants and the rest were muffins, what is the ratio of muffins to croissants?
qs.s: The number of muffins is 720 - 450 = 270. The ratio of muffins to croissants is 270 : 450 = 3 : 5.

qs.q: At a conference with 1170 attendees, 650 attendees are from out of state, and the remaining attendees are local. What is the ratio of local attendees to out-of-state attendees?
qs.s: The number of local attendees is 1170 - 650 = 520. The ratio of local to out-of-state attendees is 520 : 650 = 4 : 5.

qs.q: An animal shelter cares for 1080 animals. If 720 of the animals are dogs and the rest are cats, what is the ratio of cats to dogs?
qs.s: The number of cats is 1080 - 720 = 360. The ratio of cats to dogs is 360 : 720 = 1 : 2.

qs.q: A company has 850 employees. If 510 of the employees work full-time and the rest work part-time, what is the ratio of part-time to full-time employees?
qs.s: The number of part-time employees is 850 - 510 = 340. The ratio of part-time to full-time employees is 340 : 510 = 2 : 3.

qs.q: In a youth sports league, 420 of the 980 registered players play soccer, while the rest play basketball. What is the ratio of basketball players to soccer players?
qs.s: The number of basketball players is 980 - 420 = 560. The ratio of basketball players to soccer players is 560 : 420 = 4 : 3.

qs.q: A carpenter has a 7.2-meter wooden plank. He cuts off a piece that is 320 centimeters long. What is the ratio of the length of the remaining piece to the length of the cut piece?
qs.s: Convert 7.2 m to 720 cm. The remaining piece is 720 cm - 320 cm = 400 cm, so the ratio of the remaining piece to the cut piece is 400 : 320 = 5 : 4.

qs.q: A bakery received a 25-kilogram bag of flour. The baker used 6000 grams in the morning and 9000 grams in the afternoon. What is the ratio of the mass of flour used in the afternoon to the mass of the remaining flour in the bag?
qs.s: Convert 25 kg to 25 000 g. The remaining flour is 25 000 - (6000 + 9000) = 10 000 g, so the ratio of afternoon flour to remaining flour is 9000 : 10 000 = 9 : 10.

qs.q: In an election with 5400 total votes cast among three candidates, Candidate A received 2400 votes, Candidate B received 1600 votes, and Candidate C received the remaining votes. What is the ratio of votes received by Candidate C to votes received by Candidate A?
qs.s: Candidate C received 5400 - (2400 + 1600) = 1400 votes. The ratio of Candidate C's votes to Candidate A's votes is 1400 : 2400 = 7 : 12.

qs.q: During a 4-hour flight, a passenger spent 1 hour and 15 minutes watching a movie, and the rest of the flight reading. What is the ratio of the time spent reading to the time spent watching the movie?
qs.s: Convert the times to minutes: 4 hours is 240 minutes and 1 hour 15 minutes is 75 minutes. The time spent reading is 240 - 75 = 165 minutes, so the ratio is 165 : 75 = 11 : 5.

qs.q: A school club had 180 members, of which 105 were girls and the rest were boys. Then, 15 new girls and 25 new boys joined the club. What is the ratio of boys to girls in the club now?
qs.s: Initially, there were 180 - 105 = 75 boys. After new members joined, there were 75 + 25 = 100 boys and 105 + 15 = 120 girls, giving a ratio of 100 : 120 = 5 : 6.

exercises.name: Word Problems Involving Rates and Unit Rates

qs.q: What rate of increase did Elena receive if her biweekly salary rose from $1500 to $1650?
qs.s: The biweekly increase is $1650 - $1500 = $150. The rate of increase is 150 / 1500 = 0.10 = 10%.

qs.q: What rate of increase did Jordan receive if his hourly wage rose from $16 to $24?
qs.s: The hourly increase is $24 - $16 = $8. The rate of increase is 8 / 16 = 0.50 = 50%.

qs.q: What rate of increase did Marcus receive if his weekly pay rose from $400 to $520?
qs.s: The increase in pay is $520 - $400 = $120. The rate of increase is 120 / 400 = 0.30 = 30%.

qs.q: What rate of increase did Liam receive if his weekly salary rose from $500 to $600?
qs.s: The weekly increase is $600 - $500 = $100. The rate of increase is 100 / 500 = 0.20 = 20%.

qs.q: What rate of increase did Priya receive if her monthly salary rose from $2400 to $3000?
qs.s: The monthly increase is $3000 - $2400 = $600. The rate of increase is 600 / 2400 = 0.25 = 25%.

qs.q: What rate of increase did an engineer receive if his annual salary rose from $75,000 to $93,000?
qs.s: The salary increase is $93,000 - $75,000 = $18,000. The rate of increase is 18,000 / 75,000 = 0.24 = 24%.

qs.q: Nathan previously worked 40 hours per week at $15 per hour. He recently switched to a position where he works 36 hours per week at $20 per hour. What rate of increase did he receive in his weekly earnings?
qs.s: Nathan's original weekly pay was 40 × $15 = $600, and his new pay is 36 × $20 = $720. The increase is $720 - $600 = $120, so the rate of increase is 120 / 600 = 0.20 = 20%.

qs.q: Before receiving a promotion, Jackson worked 35 hours per week at an hourly rate of $20. After the promotion, his weekly salary was set at $875. What rate of increase did Jackson receive in his weekly salary?
qs.s: Jackson's original weekly salary was 35 × $20 = $700. The increase is $875 - $700 = $175, so the rate of increase is 175 / 700 = 0.25 = 25%.

qs.q: A store manager's biweekly pay was originally $1600. After taking on additional duties, she received a $150 increase to her base pay plus an extra $90 biweekly stipend. What was the rate of increase in her total biweekly pay?
qs.s: The total biweekly increase is $150 + $90 = $240. The rate of increase is 240 / 1600 = 0.15 = 15%.

qs.q: When hired, Rachel earned a weekly salary of $500. After one year, she received a raise to $550, and after her second year, her weekly salary rose to $660. What was the overall rate of increase from her starting salary to her salary after two years?
qs.s: The total increase from her starting salary to her final salary is $660 - $500 = $160. The overall rate of increase is 160 / 500 = 0.32 = 32%.

qs.q: A quality control inspector tests 50 light bulbs and finds that 6 are defective. What is the ratio of non-defective bulbs to defective bulbs in simplest form?
qs.s: The number of non-defective bulbs is 50 - 6 = 44. The ratio of non-defective to defective bulbs is 44 : 6, which simplifies to 22 : 3.

qs.q: A gardener plants 48 seeds, and 30 of them sprout into seedlings. What is the ratio of seeds that sprouted to seeds that did not sprout in simplest form?
qs.s: The number of seeds that did not sprout is 48 - 30 = 18. The ratio of sprouted seeds to non-sprouted seeds is 30 : 18, which simplifies to 5 : 3.

qs.q: A train makes a 40 km trip, traveling 28 km above ground and the rest underground through tunnels. What is the ratio of the distance traveled above ground to the distance traveled underground in simplest form?
qs.s: The underground distance is 40 - 28 = 12 km. The ratio of above-ground to underground distance is 28 : 12, which simplifies to 7 : 3.

qs.q: A baseball team plays 45 games in a season and wins 25 of them. Assuming there are no ties, what is the ratio of wins to losses in simplest form?
qs.s: The team lost 45 - 25 = 20 games. The ratio of wins to losses is 25 : 20, which simplifies to 5 : 4.

qs.q: In an art class of 36 students, 24 are girls and the rest are boys. What is the ratio of girls to boys in simplest form?
qs.s: The number of boys is 36 - 24 = 12. The ratio of girls to boys is 24 : 12, which simplifies to 2 : 1.

qs.q: During a 2-hour television broadcast, 35 minutes are commercials, 25 minutes are studio interviews, and the rest is live sports coverage. What is the ratio of commercial time to live sports coverage in simplest form?
qs.s: Since 2 hours equals 120 minutes, the live sports coverage is 120 - (35 + 25) = 60 minutes. The ratio of commercials to live sports coverage is 35 : 60, which simplifies to 7 : 12.

qs.q: A soccer team plays 84 games over two seasons. The team wins 45 games, ties 15 games, and loses the rest. What is the ratio of wins to losses in simplest form?
qs.s: The team lost 84 - (45 + 15) = 24 games. The ratio of wins to losses is 45 : 24, which simplifies to 15 : 8.

qs.q: A high school has an enrollment of 1260 students consisting of freshmen, sophomores, juniors, and seniors. There are 350 freshmen, 310 sophomores, and 320 juniors. What is the ratio of seniors to freshmen in simplest form?
qs.s: The number of seniors is 1260 - (350 + 310 + 320) = 280. The ratio of seniors to freshmen is 280 : 350, which simplifies to 4 : 5.

qs.q: In an election, 2400 total votes were cast among Candidate A, Candidate B, and Candidate C. Candidate A received 1050 votes, Candidate B received 750 votes, and Candidate C received the remaining votes. What is the ratio of Candidate C's votes to Candidate A's votes in simplest form?
qs.s: Candidate C received 2400 - (1050 + 750) = 600 votes. The ratio of Candidate C's votes to Candidate A's votes is 600 : 1050, which simplifies to 4 : 7.

qs.q: A hiking trail is 2.4 km long. A hiker walks 900 m before stopping to rest, and then walks the rest of the trail. What is the ratio of the distance walked before resting to the remaining distance in simplest form?
qs.s: Convert 2.4 km to 2400 m, so the remaining distance is 2400 - 900 = 1500 m. The ratio of distance walked to remaining distance is 900 : 1500, which simplifies to 3 : 5.

exercises.name: Word Problems Involving Rates and Unit Rates

qs.q: In 2020, Australia had a population of approximately 26 million people and a land area of 7.7 million square kilometers. The ratio of the number of people to the area is called the population density. What was the population density of Australia to one decimal place?
qs.s: Divide the population by the land area: \(26 \div 7.7 \approx 3.38\). Rounded to one decimal place, the population density is 3.4 people per square kilometer.

qs.q: A marine sanctuary has an area of 8.5 square kilometers and is home to 112 sea otters. The ratio of the number of otters to the area is called the otter density. What is the otter density of the sanctuary to one decimal place?
qs.s: Divide the otter population by the area: \(112 \div 8.5 \approx 13.18\). Rounded to one decimal place, the otter density is 13.2 otters per square kilometer.

qs.q: A nature reserve has an area of 7.2 square kilometers and is home to 89 moose. The ratio of the number of moose to the area is called the moose population density. What is the moose population density of the reserve to one decimal place?
qs.s: Divide the number of moose by the reserve's area: \(89 \div 7.2 \approx 12.36\). Rounded to one decimal place, the moose density is 12.4 moose per square kilometer.

qs.q: In 2021, Iceland had a population of approximately 370 thousand people and a land area of 103 thousand square kilometers. The ratio of the number of people to the area is called the population density. What was the population density of Iceland to one decimal place?
qs.s: Divide the population by the land area: \(370 \div 103 \approx 3.59\). Rounded to one decimal place, the population density is 3.6 people per square kilometer.

qs.q: A country has a population of approximately 48 million people and a land area of 5.8 million square kilometers. The ratio of the number of people to the area is called the population density. What is the population density of this country to one decimal place?
qs.s: Divide the population by the land area: \(48 \div 5.8 \approx 8.28\). Rounded to one decimal place, the population density is 8.3 people per square kilometer.

qs.q: District A has a population of 14 million people and an area of 2.0 million square kilometers. District B has a population of 25 million people and an area of 6.0 million square kilometers. If the two districts merge, what will be the population density of the combined region to one decimal place?
qs.s: The total population is \(14 + 25 = 39\) million people and the total land area is \(2.0 + 6.0 = 8.0\) million square kilometers. Dividing gives \(39 \div 8.0 = 4.875\), which rounds to 4.9 people per square kilometer.

qs.q: A conservation area covers 650 hectares and has an estimated population of 148 wild boar. There are 100 hectares in 1 square kilometer. What is the population density of wild boar in boar per square kilometer, to one decimal place?
qs.s: Convert the area to square kilometers: \(650 \div 100 = 6.5\text{ km}^2\). Dividing the number of wild boar by the area gives \(148 \div 6.5 \approx 22.77\), which rounds to 22.8 boar per square kilometer.

qs.q: A rectangular national forest measures 64 kilometers in length and 25 kilometers in width. Biologists count an estimated 3,700 white-tailed deer living in the forest. What is the deer population density in deer per square kilometer, to one decimal place?
qs.s: The forest area is \(64 \times 25 = 1,600\text{ km}^2\). Dividing the population by the area gives \(3,700 \div 1,600 = 2.3125\), which rounds to 2.3 deer per square kilometer.

qs.q: In 2010, an island had a population of 84 thousand people and a land area of 3.5 thousand square kilometers. Over the next decade, the island's population increased by 15 thousand people while the land area remained unchanged. What was the island's population density in 2020, to one decimal place?
qs.s: The population in 2020 was \(84 + 15 = 99\) thousand people. Dividing by the land area gives \(99 \div 3.5 \approx 28.29\), which rounds to 28.3 people per square kilometer.

qs.q: Country A has a population of 45 million people and an area of 5.0 million square kilometers. Country B has a population of 38 million people and an area of 6.0 million square kilometers. How much greater is the population density of Country A than Country B, in people per square kilometer, to one decimal place?
qs.s: The population density of Country A is \(45 \div 5.0 = 9.0\text{ people/km}^2\) and that of Country B is \(38 \div 6.0 \approx 6.33\text{ people/km}^2\). The difference is \(9.0 - 6.33 \approx 2.67\), which rounds to 2.7 people per square kilometer.

exercises.name: Word Problems Involving Rates and Unit Rates

qs.q: On October 3, 2023, an import business paid $3150 US dollars to acquire €2500 (Euros). What was the exchange rate in US dollars per Euro?
qs.s: Divide the amount in US dollars by the amount in Euros: $3150 / 2500 = $1.26 USD per Euro.

qs.q: On June 12, 2023, it cost $5220 Australian dollars to buy $3600 US dollars. What was the exchange rate in Australian dollars per US dollar?
qs.s: Divide the Australian dollar amount by the US dollar amount: $5220 / 3600 = $1.45 AUD per US dollar.

qs.q: A bakery purchased a 150-kilogram shipment of specialty flour for $246. What was the unit cost of the flour in dollars per kilogram?
qs.s: Divide the total cost by the mass: $246 / 150 kg = $1.64 per kilogram.

qs.q: A delivery van consumed 120 litres of fuel to travel a distance of 450 kilometres. What was the vehicle's fuel efficiency in kilometres per litre?
qs.s: Divide the distance traveled by the amount of fuel used: 450 km / 120 L = 3.75 km/L.

qs.q: On March 15, 2022, a traveler paid $4125 Canadian dollars to purchase £2500 (British pounds). What was the exchange rate in Canadian dollars per British pound?
qs.s: Divide the total Canadian dollars by the number of British pounds: $4125 / 2500 = $1.65 CAD per British pound.

qs.q: A travel agency conducted two foreign currency exchanges on the same day. First, it converted $2640 USD to receive €2000. Later, it converted another $4110 USD to receive €3000. What was the overall exchange rate in US dollars per Euro for the total currency exchanged?
qs.s: The total amount spent was $2640 + $4110 = $6750 USD to receive €2000 + €3000 = €5000. The overall exchange rate was $6750 / 5000 = $1.35 USD per Euro.

qs.q: A bank offers an exchange rate of $1.36 CAD per Euro, but charges a flat service fee of $20 CAD on every currency transaction. If a customer exchanges Canadian dollars to receive €500, what is the customer's effective exchange rate in Canadian dollars per Euro, including the fee?
qs.s: The base cost is 500 × $1.36 = $680 CAD, and adding the fee gives $680 + $20 = $700 CAD. The effective exchange rate is $700 / 500 = $1.40 CAD per Euro.

qs.q: On Monday, an import company paid $4200 CAD to purchase €3000. On Friday, the company paid $3875 CAD to purchase €2500. By how much did the exchange rate in Canadian dollars per Euro increase from Monday to Friday?
qs.s: On Monday, the rate was $4200 / 3000 = $1.40 CAD per Euro, and on Friday it was $3875 / 2500 = $1.55 CAD per Euro. The rate increased by $1.55 - $1.40 = $0.15 CAD per Euro.

qs.q: A grocery store sells a 350-gram bag of coffee beans for $8.40, and a 1.2-kilogram bag of the same coffee beans for $25.20. What is the difference in their unit prices, in dollars per kilogram?
qs.s: The unit price of the small bag is $8.40 / 0.35 kg = $24.00 per kg, and for the large bag it is $25.20 / 1.2 kg = $21.00 per kg. The difference is $24.00 - $21.00 = $3.00 per kilogram.

qs.q: A motorist drove 180 km in 2 hours on the highway, and then drove 30 km in 30 minutes through city traffic. What was the motorist's average speed for the entire trip, in kilometres per hour?
qs.s: The total distance is 180 km + 30 km = 210 km, and the total time is 2 h + 0.5 h = 2.5 h. The average speed is 210 km / 2.5 h = 84 km/h.

exercises.name: Comparing Two Options for Best Buy

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 4 notebooks for $5.40
Option 2: 6 notebooks for $7.50
qs.s: Option 1 costs $5.40 / 4 = $1.35 per notebook, while Option 2 costs $7.50 / 6 = $1.25 per notebook. Option 2 is the best buy with a unit rate of $1.25 per notebook.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 5 juice boxes for $3.25
Option 2: 8 juice boxes for $5.76
qs.s: Option 1 costs $3.25 / 5 = $0.65 per juice box, and Option 2 costs $5.76 / 8 = $0.72 per juice box. Option 1 is the best buy with a unit rate of $0.65 per juice box.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 6 granola bars for $4.68
Option 2: 10 granola bars for $7.20
qs.s: Option 1 costs $4.68 / 6 = $0.78 per granola bar, and Option 2 costs $7.20 / 10 = $0.72 per granola bar. Option 2 is the best buy with a unit rate of $0.72 per granola bar.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 4 pens for $3.36
Option 2: 9 pens for $8.01
qs.s: Option 1 costs $3.36 / 4 = $0.84 per pen, while Option 2 costs $8.01 / 9 = $0.89 per pen. Option 1 is the best buy with a unit rate of $0.84 per pen.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 4 folders for $3.12
Option 2: 9 folders for $7.38
qs.s: Option 1 costs $3.12 / 4 = $0.78 per folder, and Option 2 costs $7.38 / 9 = $0.82 per folder. Option 1 is the best buy with a unit rate of $0.78 per folder.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate in dollars per kilogram for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 8 kg for $25.20
Option 2: 12.5 kg for $40.50
qs.s: Option 1 costs $25.20 / 8 = $3.15 per kg, while Option 2 costs $40.50 / 12.5 = $3.24 per kg. Option 1 is the best buy with a unit rate of $3.15 per kg.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 25 packs of paper for $105.00
Option 2: 50 packs of paper regularly priced at $260.00, with a 15% discount applied
qs.s: Option 1 costs $105.00 / 25 = $4.20 per pack. With the 15% discount, Option 2 costs $260.00 * 0.85 = $221.00, which is $221.00 / 50 = $4.42 per pack. Option 1 is the best buy with a unit rate of $4.20 per pack.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate in dollars per litre for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 500 mL for $4.25
Option 2: 1.5 L for $12.00
qs.s: Convert 500 mL to 0.5 L: Option 1 costs $4.25 / 0.5 = $8.50 per litre. Option 2 costs $12.00 / 1.5 = $8.00 per litre, making Option 2 the best buy with a unit rate of $8.00 per litre.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate in dollars per kilogram for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 750 g of coffee beans for $12.75
Option 2: 2 kg of coffee beans for $33.00
qs.s: Convert 750 g to 0.75 kg: Option 1 costs $12.75 / 0.75 = $17.00 per kg. Option 2 costs $33.00 / 2 = $16.50 per kg, so Option 2 is the best buy with a unit rate of $16.50 per kg.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 12 energy bars for $18.60
Option 2: 20 energy bars for $32.00 with a $3.00 coupon applied
qs.s: Option 1 costs $18.60 / 12 = $1.55 per bar. With the coupon, Option 2 costs ($32.00 - $3.00) / 20 = $29.00 / 20 = $1.45 per bar. Option 2 is the best buy with a unit rate of $1.45 per bar.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 5 notebooks for $6.45
Option 2: 12 notebooks for $14.76
qs.s: Option 1 costs $6.45 ÷ 5 = $1.29 per notebook, while Option 2 costs $14.76 ÷ 12 = $1.23 per notebook. Option 2 is the best buy at $1.23 per notebook.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 4 glue sticks for $5.40
Option 2: 15 glue sticks for $20.70
qs.s: Option 1 costs $5.40 ÷ 4 = $1.35 per glue stick, while Option 2 costs $20.70 ÷ 15 = $1.38 per glue stick. Option 1 is the best buy at $1.35 per glue stick.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 10 juice boxes for $6.80
Option 2: 25 juice boxes for $17.50
qs.s: Option 1 costs $6.80 ÷ 10 = $0.68 per juice box, while Option 2 costs $17.50 ÷ 25 = $0.70 per juice box. Option 1 is the best buy at $0.68 per juice box.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 8 granola bars for $5.44
Option 2: 20 granola bars for $13.00
qs.s: Option 1 costs $5.44 ÷ 8 = $0.68 per bar, while Option 2 costs $13.00 ÷ 20 = $0.65 per bar. Option 2 is the best buy at $0.65 per bar.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy?
Option 1: 8 pens for $5.20
Option 2: 24 pens for $14.88
qs.s: Option 1 costs $5.20 ÷ 8 = $0.65 per pen, while Option 2 costs $14.88 ÷ 24 = $0.62 per pen. Option 2 has the lower unit price and is the best buy at $0.62 per pen.

qs.q:
A shopper has a coupon for $3.00 off any size bag of dog food. Calculate the unit rate for each option after applying the coupon to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy in dollars per kilogram?
Option 1: 4 kg bag with a regular price of $17.00
Option 2: 10 kg bag with a regular price of $39.00
qs.s: With the coupon, Option 1 costs ($17.00 - $3.00) ÷ 4 = $3.50 per kg, and Option 2 costs ($39.00 - $3.00) ÷ 10 = $3.60 per kg. Option 1 is the best buy at $3.50 per kg.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy in dollars per litre? (1000 mL = 1 L)
Option 1: 750 mL of laundry detergent for $6.30
Option 2: 2 L of laundry detergent for $15.60
qs.s: Convert 750 mL to 0.75 L, giving $6.30 ÷ 0.75 = $8.40 per litre for Option 1, while Option 2 is $15.60 ÷ 2 = $7.80 per litre. Option 2 is the best buy at $7.80 per litre.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy in dollars per litre?
Option 1: 1.8 L of cooking oil for $15.12
Option 2: 2.4 L of cooking oil for $19.68
qs.s: Option 1 costs $15.12 ÷ 1.8 = $8.40 per litre, while Option 2 costs $19.68 ÷ 2.4 = $8.20 per litre. Option 2 is the best buy at $8.20 per litre.

qs.q:
