Option 2: 3 lbs for $7.80
Using the conversion \(1\text{ kg} = 2.2\text{ lbs}\), determine which option is the better buy. What is the unit price of the better buy in dollars per pound?
qs.s: Option 1 costs \(\$5.50 \div 2.2 = \$2.50\) per pound, while Option 2 costs \(\$7.80 \div 3 = \$2.60\) per pound. Option 1 is the better buy at \(\$2.50\) per pound.

qs.q:
A market offers two options for fresh strawberries:
Option 1: 1 kg for $7.70
Option 2: 2 lbs for $7.40
Using the conversion \(1\text{ kg} = 2.2\text{ lbs}\), determine which option is the better buy. What is the unit price of the better buy in dollars per pound?
qs.s: Option 1 costs \(\$7.70 \div 2.2 = \$3.50\) per pound, while Option 2 costs \(\$7.40 \div 2 = \$3.70\) per pound. Option 1 is the better buy at \(\$3.50\) per pound.

qs.q:
A shopper is comparing two options for buying chicken broth:
Option 1: A 1-quart carton for $2.40
Option 2: Two 500 mL cans for $2.70 total
Using \(1\text{ qt} = 32\text{ fl oz}\) and the approximation \(1\text{ fl oz} \approx 30\text{ mL}\), determine which option is the better buy. What is the unit price of the better buy in dollars per litre?
qs.s: One quart is approximately \(32 \times 30\text{ mL} = 960\text{ mL} = 0.96\text{ L}\), giving a unit price of \(\$2.40 \div 0.96 = \$2.50\) per litre for Option 1, while Option 2 provides \(1000\text{ mL} = 1\text{ L}\) for \(\$2.70\) per litre. Option 1 is the better buy at \(\$2.50\) per litre.

qs.q:
A bulk food store offers two options for purchasing walnuts:
Option 1: A 2 kg bag with a regular price of $22.00, on sale for 20% off
Option 2: A 5 lb bag for $21.50 with no discount
Using the conversion \(1\text{ kg} = 2.2\text{ lbs}\), determine which option is the better buy. What is the unit price of the better buy in dollars per pound?
qs.s: Option 1's sale price is \(\$22.00 \times 0.80 = \$17.60\) for \(2 \times 2.2 = 4.4\text{ lbs}\), giving \(\$17.60 \div 4.4 = \$4.00\) per pound, while Option 2 costs \(\$21.50 \div 5 = \$4.30\) per pound. Option 1 is the better buy at \(\$4.00\) per pound.

qs.q:
A bulk store offers two sizes of pet food:
Option 1: A 5 kg bag for $26.40
Option 2: A 12 lb bag for $27.00
Using the conversion \(1\text{ kg} = 2.2\text{ lbs}\), determine which option is the better buy. What is the unit price of the better buy in dollars per pound?
qs.s: A 5 kg bag weighs \(5 \times 2.2 = 11\text{ lbs}\), costing \(\$26.40 \div 11 = \$2.40\) per pound, whereas Option 2 costs \(\$27.00 \div 12 = \$2.25\) per pound. Option 2 is the better buy at \(\$2.25\) per pound.

qs.q:
A customer is choosing between two sizes of honey:
Option 1: A 1.5 kg jar for $16.50, with a coupon for $1.65 off
Option 2: A 4 lb jar for $19.00 (no coupon)
Using the conversion \(1\text{ kg} = 2.2\text{ lbs}\), determine which option is the better buy after applying the coupon. What is the unit price of the better buy in dollars per pound?
qs.s: With the coupon, Option 1 costs \(\$16.50 - \$1.65 = \$14.85\) for \(1.5 \times 2.2 = 3.3\text{ lbs}\), giving \(\$14.85 \div 3.3 = \$4.50\) per pound, while Option 2 costs \(\$19.00 \div 4 = \$4.75\) per pound. Option 1 is the better buy at \(\$4.50\) per pound.

qs.q:
A store sells iced tea in two packaging options:
Option 1: A pack of eight 250 mL bottles for $5.60
Option 2: A 3 L jug for $7.80
Using the conversion \(1000\text{ mL} = 1\text{ L}\), determine which option is the better buy. What is the unit price of the better buy in dollars per litre?
qs.s: Option 1 provides \(8 \times 250\text{ mL} = 2000\text{ mL} = 2\text{ L}\) for \(\$5.60\), which is \(\$5.60 \div 2 = \$2.80\) per litre, while Option 2 costs \(\$7.80 \div 3 = \$2.60\) per litre. Option 2 is the better buy at \(\$2.60\) per litre.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 100 mL for $3.70
Option 2: 4 fl oz for $4.20
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL)
qs.s: Option 1 costs $3.70 per 100 mL, while Option 2 contains 4 × 30 = 120 mL and costs ($4.20 / 120) × 100 = $3.50 per 100 mL. Option 2 is the best buy at $3.50 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 200 mL for $4.80
Option 2: 5 fl oz for $3.90
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL)
qs.s: Option 1 costs $4.80 / 2 = $2.40 per 100 mL, while Option 2 contains 5 × 30 = 150 mL and costs ($3.90 / 150) × 100 = $2.60 per 100 mL. Since Option 1 has a lower unit price, it is the best buy at $2.40 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 150 mL for $4.95
Option 2: 8 fl oz for $7.20
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL)
qs.s: Option 1 costs $4.95 / 1.5 = $3.30 per 100 mL, and Option 2 contains 8 × 30 = 240 mL costing ($7.20 / 240) × 100 = $3.00 per 100 mL. Option 2 is the best buy at $3.00 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 300 mL for $5.40
Option 2: 6 fl oz for $3.60
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL)
qs.s: Option 1 costs $5.40 / 3 = $1.80 per 100 mL, whereas Option 2 contains 6 × 30 = 180 mL and costs ($3.60 / 180) × 100 = $2.00 per 100 mL. Option 1 is the best buy at $1.80 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 250 mL for $7.00
Option 2: 10 fl oz for $7.80
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL)
qs.s: Option 1 costs $7.00 / 2.5 = $2.80 per 100 mL, while Option 2 contains 10 × 30 = 300 mL and costs ($7.80 / 300) × 100 = $2.60 per 100 mL. Option 2 is the best buy at $2.60 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 20 fl oz for $6.60 with a 20% discount
Option 2: 800 mL for $6.80 with no discount
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL)
qs.s: With the 20% discount, Option 1 costs $6.60 × 0.80 = $5.28 for 20 × 30 = 600 mL, which is ($5.28 / 600) × 100 = $0.88 per 100 mL. Option 2 costs $6.80 / 8 = $0.85 per 100 mL, making Option 2 the best buy at $0.85 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
A customer wants to buy maple syrup and has a coupon for $2.50 off Option 1. Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 500 mL for $14.50 (before coupon)
Option 2: 16 fl oz for $11.76 (no coupon)
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL)
qs.s: With the coupon, Option 1 costs $14.50 - $2.50 = $12.00 for 500 mL, which is $2.40 per 100 mL. Option 2 contains 16 × 30 = 480 mL, costing ($11.76 / 480) × 100 = $2.45 per 100 mL, so Option 1 is the best buy at $2.40 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per litre?
Option 1: 1 qt for $3.84
Option 2: 750 mL for $3.15
(Use 1 qt = 32 fl oz, 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL, and 1000 mL = 1 L)
qs.s: Option 1 contains 32 × 30 = 960 mL = 0.96 L, giving a unit rate of $3.84 / 0.96 = $4.00 per litre. Option 2 contains 0.75 L and costs $3.15 / 0.75 = $4.20 per litre, making Option 1 the best buy at $4.00 per litre.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy among the three choices. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per 100 mL?
Option 1: 250 mL for $3.25
Option 2: 10 fl oz for $3.75
Option 3: 0.5 L for $6.75
(Use 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL and 1 L = 1000 mL)
qs.s: The unit rates are $3.25 / 2.5 = $1.30 per 100 mL for Option 1, ($3.75 / 300) × 100 = $1.25 per 100 mL for Option 2, and $6.75 / 5 = $1.35 per 100 mL for Option 3. Therefore, Option 2 is the best buy at $1.25 per 100 mL.

qs.q:
Calculate the unit rate for each option to determine the best buy. What is the unit rate of the best buy, in dollars per pound?
Option 1: 2 kg for $18.48
Option 2: 3 lb for $13.20
(Use 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb)
qs.s: Option 1 weighs 2 × 2.2 = 4.4 lb, giving a unit rate of $18.48 / 4.4 = $4.20 per lb. Since Option 2 costs $13.20 / 3 = $4.40 per lb, Option 1 is the best buy at $4.20 per lb.

qs.q:
A pet store sells dry dog food in two bag sizes:
Option 1: 4 kg for $26.40
Option 2: 10 lb for $31.00
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the unit price per kilogram of the best buy?
qs.s: Option 1 costs $26.40 / 4 kg = $6.60 per kg. Option 2 costs $31.00 / 10 lb = $3.10 per lb, which is $3.10 * 2.2 = $6.82 per kg. Option 1 is the best buy at $6.60 per kg.

qs.q:
A market sells blocks of cheddar cheese in two sizes:
Option 1: 2.5 kg for $22.00
Option 2: 5 lb for $21.00
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the unit price per kilogram of the best buy?
qs.s: Option 1 costs $22.00 / 2.5 kg = $8.80 per kg. Option 2 costs $21.00 / 5 lb = $4.20 per lb, which is $4.20 * 2.2 = $9.24 per kg. Option 1 is the best buy at $8.80 per kg.

qs.q:
A grocery store sells basmati rice in two different bags:
Option 1: 1.5 kg for $19.80
Option 2: 4 lb for $23.00
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the unit price per pound of the best buy?
qs.s: Option 1 costs $19.80 / 1.5 kg = $13.20 per kg, which is $13.20 / 2.2 = $6.00 per lb. Option 2 costs $23.00 / 4 lb = $5.75 per lb. Option 2 is the best buy at $5.75 per lb.

qs.q:
A store sells premium coffee beans under two options:
Option 1: 1 kg for $15.40
Option 2: 2 lb for $14.50
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the unit price per pound of the best buy?
qs.s: Option 1 costs $15.40 / 1 kg = $15.40 per kg, which is $15.40 / 2.2 = $7.00 per lb. Option 2 costs $14.50 / 2 lb = $7.25 per lb. Option 1 is the best buy at $7.00 per lb.

qs.q:
A butcher shop offers ground turkey in two package sizes:
Option 1: 0.5 kg for $5.50
Option 2: 1.5 lb for $7.80
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the unit price per kilogram of the best buy?
qs.s: Option 1 costs $5.50 / 0.5 kg = $11.00 per kg. Option 2 costs $7.80 / 1.5 lb = $5.20 per lb, which is $5.20 * 2.2 = $11.44 per kg. Option 1 is the best buy at $11.00 per kg.

qs.q:
A bulk food store offers three purchase sizes for roasted almonds:
Option 1: 0.5 kg for $7.15
Option 2: 1.5 lb for $9.90
Option 3: 2 kg for $27.00
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the unit price per kilogram of the best buy?
qs.s: Option 1 is $7.15 / 0.5 = $14.30/kg. Option 2 is ($9.90 / 1.5) * 2.2 = $14.52/kg. Option 3 is $27.00 / 2 = $13.50/kg. Option 3 has the lowest unit price at $13.50 per kg.

qs.q:
Two brands of bulk flour are available:
Brand A: 4 kg for $9.80
Brand B: 10 lb for $12.50
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, how much cheaper per kilogram is the best buy compared to the other brand?
qs.s: Brand A costs $9.80 / 4 kg = $2.45 per kg. Brand B costs ($12.50 / 10 lb) * 2.2 = $2.75 per kg. Brand A is the best buy, saving $2.75 - $2.45 = $0.30 per kg.

qs.q:
A shopper compares two brands of olive oil:
Brand A: 1.5 L for $16.80, with a store coupon for $2.25 off
Brand B: 500 mL for $5.20, with no coupon
Using the conversion 1 L = 1000 mL, what is the unit price per litre of the best buy after applying the coupon?
qs.s: With the coupon, Brand A costs ($16.80 - $2.25) / 1.5 L = $14.55 / 1.5 = $9.70 per L. Brand B costs $5.20 / 0.5 L = $10.40 per L. Brand A is the best buy at $9.70 per L.

qs.q:
A supermarket offers two options for purchasing apple juice:
Option 1: A pack of eight 250 mL juice boxes for $4.40
Option 2: A 2.5 L jug for $5.75
Using the conversion 1 L = 1000 mL, what is the unit price per litre of the best buy?
qs.s: Option 1 contains 8 * 250 mL = 2000 mL = 2 L, costing $4.40 / 2 L = $2.20 per L. Option 2 costs $5.75 / 2.5 L = $2.30 per L. Option 1 is the best buy at $2.20 per L.

qs.q:
A store sells two brands of dry dog food:
Brand 1: 5 kg for $32.00, but it is on sale for 25% off
Brand 2: 12 lb for $24.00 at regular price
Using the conversion 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the unit price per kilogram of the best buy?
qs.s: Brand 1's sale price is $32.00 * 0.75 = $24.00, so its unit price is $24.00 / 5 kg = $4.80 per kg. Brand 2 costs ($24.00 / 12 lb) * 2.2 = $4.40 per kg. Brand 2 is the best buy at $4.40 per kg.

qs.q: Marcus visits the local public pool and currently pays $6 per visit. A monthly pass costs $24 and reduces the price to $2 per visit. What is the minimum number of visits Marcus must make in a month in order to save money with the pass?
qs.s: Let \(n\) be the number of visits. The pass saves money when \(6n > 24 + 2n\), which simplifies to \(4n > 24\), or \(n > 6\), meaning Marcus must make at least 7 visits in a month.

qs.q: Liam skates at a community ice rink and pays $8 per session. A seasonal discount card costs $45 and reduces the admission to $3 per session. What is the minimum number of sessions Liam must attend during the season in order to save money with the card?
qs.s: The inequality to save money is \(8n > 45 + 3n\), which simplifies to \(5n > 45\), or \(n > 9\). Thus, Liam must attend at least 10 sessions to save money.

qs.q: Chloe washes her car at a car wash where a single wash costs $10. A monthly subscription costs $28 and lowers the price of each wash to $3. What is the minimum number of car washes Chloe must get in a month in order to save money with the subscription?
qs.s: The subscription is cheaper when \(10n > 28 + 3n\), which simplifies to \(7n > 28\), or \(n > 4\). Chloe must get at least 5 washes in a month.

qs.q: Maya attends a rock climbing gym where she currently pays $12 per visit. The gym offers a monthly membership for $35 that reduces the cost per visit to $5. What is the minimum number of visits Maya must make in a month in order to save money with the membership?
qs.s: The membership saves money when \(12n > 35 + 5n\), which simplifies to \(7n > 35\), or \(n > 5\). Therefore, Maya must make a minimum of 6 visits in a month.

qs.q: Devonte takes classes at a yoga studio that charges $15 for a single drop-in class. The studio offers a monthly membership for $48 that reduces the drop-in rate to $7 per class. What is the minimum number of classes Devonte must take in a month in order to save money with the membership?
qs.s: The membership saves money when \(15n > 48 + 7n\), which simplifies to \(8n > 48\), or \(n > 6\). Therefore, Devonte must take at least 7 classes in a month.

qs.q: A commuter pays a regular fare of $3.50 per transit ride. A monthly transit pass costs $45, and it gives the rider a 60% discount off the regular fare for each ride. What is the minimum number of rides the commuter must take in a month in order to save money with the pass?
qs.s: A 60% discount saves $3.50 \times 0.60 = $2.10 per ride, making each ride cost $1.40. The pass saves money when \(2.10n > 45\), giving \(n > 21.43\), so the commuter must take at least 22 rides.

qs.q: Leo pays $18 per class for drop-in martial arts sessions. The studio offers a monthly membership with a regular price of $80, but Leo has a coupon for 25% off the membership fee. With a membership, each class costs $6. What is the minimum number of classes Leo must attend in a month in order to save money with the discounted membership?
qs.s: With the 25% coupon, the membership fee is $80 \times 0.75 = $60. The membership saves money when \(18n > 60 + 6n\), which gives \(12n > 60\), or \(n > 5\), meaning Leo must attend at least 6 classes.

qs.q: A golfer currently pays $8.50 per large bucket of balls at a driving range. The range offers a seasonal discount card for $50 that reduces the price per bucket to $4.75. What is the minimum number of buckets the golfer must purchase during the season in order to save money with the discount card?
qs.s: The inequality to save money is \(8.50n > 50 + 4.75n\), which simplifies to \(3.75n > 50\), or \(n > 13.\overline{3}\). Rounding up to the next whole number, the golfer must purchase at least 14 buckets.

qs.q: A dancer currently pays a flat fee of $16 per dance class. The studio offers a 3-month membership that requires a one-time registration fee of $25 plus a monthly fee of $35, and reduces each class to $6. Over the entire 3-month period, what is the minimum number of classes the dancer must take in order to save money with the membership?
qs.s: The total fixed cost for 3 months is \(25 + 3(\)35) = $130. Setting up the inequality \(16n > 130 + 6n\) yields \(10n > 130\), so \(n > 13\), requiring a minimum of 14 classes.

qs.q: Movie tickets at a local cinema cost $15 each. The cinema offers an annual loyalty pass for $50 plus 12% sales tax, which reduces the price of each movie ticket to $8 (tax included). What is the minimum number of movies a person must see in a year in order to save money with the loyalty pass?
qs.s: Including 12% tax, the pass costs $50 \times 1.12 = $56. The pass saves money when \(15n > 56 + 8n\), which simplifies to \(7n > 56\), or \(n > 8\), meaning at least 9 movies must be seen.

qs.q: A bike rental shop offers two pricing plans for an afternoon: Plan A charges 40¢ per minute. Plan B charges a $12 base fee plus 15¢ per minute. How many minutes must a customer ride to save money with Plan B?
qs.s: Plan B saves $0.40 - $0.15 = $0.25 per minute. Setting 12 + 0.15m < 0.40m gives 0.25m > 12, so m > 48 minutes.

qs.q: A gaming lounge offers two payment methods: Pay-as-you-go costs 35¢ per minute. A day pass costs $14 plus 15¢ per minute. How many minutes must a gamer play to save money with the day pass?
qs.s: The day pass saves $0.35 - $0.15 = $0.20 per minute. Setting 14 + 0.15m < 0.35m gives 0.20m > 14, so m > 70 minutes.

qs.q: A moving company offers two rental options for a cargo van: Option 1 charges 60¢ per kilometre. Option 2 charges a $45 flat fee plus 15¢ per kilometre. How many kilometres must a driver travel to save money with Option 2?
qs.s: Option 2 saves $0.60 - $0.15 = $0.45 per kilometre. Setting 45 + 0.15k < 0.60k gives 0.45k > 45, so k > 100 km.

qs.q: Carlos wants to rent a lawn aerator for the weekend. Plan X charges 75¢ per hour. Plan Y charges an $18 flat fee plus 15¢ per hour. How many hours must Carlos use the aerator to save money with Plan Y?
qs.s: Plan Y saves $0.75 - $0.15 = $0.60 per hour. Setting 18 + 0.15h < 0.75h gives 0.60h > 18, so h > 30 hours.

qs.q: A local print shop offers two options for printing high-resolution photos: Option A charges 50¢ per photo. Option B charges a $24 membership fee plus 20¢ per photo. How many photos must a customer print to save money with Option B?
qs.s: Option B saves $0.50 - $0.20 = $0.30 per photo. Setting 24 + 0.20p < 0.50p gives 0.30p > 24, so p > 80 photos.

qs.q: A contractor needs to rent a generator for 4 days. Option A charges a flat rate of $9.00 per hour of operation. Option B charges $35 per day, a one-time insurance fee of $20, plus $4.00 per hour of operation. How many hours must the generator run over the 4 days to save money with Option B?
qs.s: Option B has a total fixed cost of 4 × $35 + $20 = $160. Setting 160 + 4h < 9h gives 5h > 160, so h > 32 hours.

qs.q: A logistics company is choosing between two freight services to transport cargo: Service A charges a flat rate of $1.75 per kilometre. Service B charges a base dispatch fee of $390, a fuel surcharge of $60, plus $0.25 per kilometre. How many kilometres must the cargo be transported to save money with Service B?
qs.s: Service B has a total fixed charge of $390 + $60 = $450. Setting 450 + 0.25k < 1.75k gives 1.50k > 450, so k > 300 km.

qs.q: A tool rental shop offers two payment plans for a commercial floor sander: Plan A charges a flat rate of $30 per day. Plan B charges an annual membership fee of $450, currently discounted by 20%, plus $12 per day. How many days must a contractor rent the sander in a year to save money with Plan B?
qs.s: The discounted membership fee is $450 × 0.80 = $360. Setting 360 + 12d < 30d gives 18d > 360, so d > 20 days.

qs.q: Elena is renting a moving van for 3 days. Plan A charges a flat rate of 70¢ per kilometre with no daily fee. Plan B charges $45 per day plus 25¢ per kilometre. How many kilometres must Elena drive over the 3 days to save money with Plan B?
qs.s: Plan B has a fixed cost of 3 × $45 = $135. Setting 135 + 0.25k < 0.70k gives 0.45k > 135, so k > 300 km.

qs.q: A community art studio offers two pottery wheel plans: Pay-as-you-go charges a flat rate of $20 per visit. Studio Membership charges an annual fee of $180, but Maya has a coupon for $30 off the fee, plus members pay $5 per visit. How many visits must Maya make in a year to save money with the Studio Membership?
qs.s: After the coupon discount, the membership fee is $180 - $30 = $150. Setting 150 + 5v < 20v gives 15v > 150, so v > 10 visits.

exercises.name: Calculating Final Price with Discounts and Coupons

qs.q: Determine the final price of a blender if the original price was $42.50, and it was on sale for 10% off, plus there was a store coupon worth $5.00.
qs.s: The sale price after the 10% discount is $42.50 \times 0.90 = $38.25. Subtracting the $5.00 coupon gives a final price of $38.25 - $5.00 = $33.25.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a coffee maker if the original price was $74.50, and it was on sale for 20% off, plus there was a store coupon worth $12.00.
qs.s: The sale price after the 20% discount is $74.50 \times 0.80 = $59.60. Subtracting the $12.00 coupon gives a final price of $59.60 - $12.00 = $47.60.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a jacket if the original price was $58.50, and it was on sale for 20% off, plus there was a store coupon worth $10.00.
qs.s: The sale price after the 20% discount is $58.50 \times 0.80 = $46.80. Subtracting the $10.00 store coupon gives a final price of $46.80 - $10.00 = $36.80.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a pair of running shoes if the original price was $65.00, and it was on sale for 30% off, plus there was a store coupon worth $7.50.
qs.s: The sale price after the 30% discount is $65.00 \times 0.70 = $45.50. Subtracting the $7.50 coupon gives a final price of $45.50 - $7.50 = $38.00.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a backpack if the original price was $48.00, and it was on sale for 25% off, plus there was a store coupon worth $6.00.
qs.s: The sale price after the 25% discount is $48.00 \times 0.75 = $36.00. Subtracting the $6.00 coupon gives a final price of $36.00 - $6.00 = $30.00.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a mountain bike if the original price was $450.00, it was on sale for 20% off, the buyer used a loyalty coupon for an additional 10% off the sale price, and applied a store credit coupon worth $25.00.
qs.s: The sale price after 20% off is $450.00 \times 0.80 = $360.00, and applying the 10% coupon yields $360.00 \times 0.90 = $324.00. Subtracting the $25.00 coupon gives a final price of $324.00 - $25.00 = $299.00.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a laptop if the original price was $840.00, it was marked down by 15%, and the customer applied both a $50.00 manufacturer coupon and a $30.00 store rewards voucher.
qs.s: The discounted price after 15% off is $840.00 \times 0.85 = $714.00. Subtracting both stacked coupons ($50.00 + $30.00 = $80.00) gives a final price of $714.00 - $80.00 = $634.00.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a television if the original price was $650.00, it was on sale for 30% off, plus there was an additional coupon for 10% off the sale price and a register coupon worth $40.00.
qs.s: The price after the 30% sale is $650.00 \times 0.70 = $455.00, and taking an additional 10% off gives $455.00 \times 0.90 = $409.50. Subtracting the $40.00 register coupon gives $409.50 - $40.00 = $369.50.

qs.q: Determine the total final price for two identical winter coats if each coat was originally priced at $120.00, both were on sale for 25% off, and the customer used a single $35.00 store coupon off the total purchase.
qs.s: The original total for both coats is 2 \times $120.00 = $240.00, which is discounted by 25% to $240.00 \times 0.75 = $180.00. Subtracting the $35.00 coupon gives a final price of $180.00 - $35.00 = $145.00.

qs.q: Determine the final price of a patio set if the original price was $850.00, it was on sale for 20% off, plus there was an extra coupon for 15% off the sale price and a manufacturer coupon worth $50.00.
qs.s: The price after 20% off is $850.00 \times 0.80 = $680.00, and applying the extra 15% off gives $680.00 \times 0.85 = $578.00. Subtracting the $50.00 coupon results in a final price of $578.00 - $50.00 = $528.00.

qs.q: What percent total discount is there on a $25.00 gaming headset that has a 12% off sale, plus a coupon worth $4.50?
qs.s: A 12% discount on $25.00 saves $3.00, making the total savings with the $4.50 coupon equal to $7.50. Dividing $7.50 by $25.00 results in a 30% total discount.

qs.q: What percent total discount is there on an $80.00 pair of running shoes that has a 25% off sale, plus a coupon worth $12.00?
qs.s: The 25% discount saves $20.00, so adding the $12.00 coupon gives total savings of $32.00. The total percent discount is $32.00 / $80.00 = 40%.

qs.q: What percent total discount is there on a $64.00 winter jacket that has a 25% off sale, plus a coupon worth $8.00?
qs.s: A 25% discount on $64.00 is $16.00, which combined with the $8.00 coupon results in $24.00 in total savings. Dividing $24.00 by $64.00 gives a total discount of 37.5%.

qs.q: What percent total discount is there on a $50.00 backpack that has a 20% off sale, plus a coupon worth $7.50?
qs.s: A 20% discount on $50.00 saves $10.00, and adding the $7.50 coupon gives a total discount of $17.50. Dividing $17.50 by the original price of $50.00 yields a 35% total discount.

qs.q: What percent total discount is there on a $40.00 blender that has a 30% off sale, plus a coupon worth $5.00?
qs.s: The 30% discount saves $12.00, and adding the $5.00 coupon gives a total discount of $17.00. Dividing $17.00 by $40.00 gives a 42.5% total discount.

qs.q: A store offers a 'Buy one pair of boots, get the second pair at 50% off' promotion. Elena buys two pairs of boots regularly priced at $70.00 each, and also applies a coupon worth $14.00 off her total purchase. What percent total discount does Elena receive on the two pairs of boots?
qs.s: The regular cost for both pairs is 2 * $70.00 = $140.00, and the promotion saves 50% on one pair, which is $35.00. Adding the $14.00 coupon gives total savings of $49.00, which is $49.00 / $140.00 = 35%.

qs.q: A teacher purchases 5 identical calculators regularly priced at $30.00 each. The store offers a 12% discount on the purchase, and the teacher uses a $6.00 manufacturer coupon plus a $9.00 store coupon. What percent total discount did the teacher receive?
qs.s: The total regular price is 5 * $30.00 = $150.00, and the 12% discount saves $18.00. Adding the two coupons worth $15.00 gives a total discount of $18.00 + $15.00 = $33.00, which equals $33.00 / $150.00 = 22%.

qs.q: A dishwasher regularly priced at $400.00 is on sale for 15% off. In addition, the buyer uses a $30.00 instant store coupon and receives a $20.00 mail-in rebate. What percent total discount did the buyer receive on the dishwasher?
qs.s: The 15% discount saves 0.15($400.00) = $60.00, and the coupon plus rebate save an additional $30.00 + $20.00 = $50.00. The total discount is $60.00 + $50.00 = $110.00, which is $110.00 / $400.00 = 27.5%.

qs.q: A desktop computer regularly costs $550.00 and a monitor regularly costs $250.00. A store offers a 25% discount when they are purchased together as a bundle, and the buyer also uses a $35.00 store coupon and a $25.00 manufacturer coupon. What percent total discount is applied to the bundle?
qs.s: The original total price is $550.00 + $250.00 = $800.00, and the 25% discount saves $200.00. Adding the two coupons saves an additional $60.00 for a total discount of $260.00, which gives $260.00 / $800.00 = 32.5%.

qs.q: A customer buys a suit consisting of a jacket regularly priced at $180.00 and trousers regularly priced at $70.00. The store offers 25% off the jacket and 20% off the trousers, and the customer also uses a coupon worth $15.00 off the total purchase. What percent total discount did the customer receive?
qs.s: The regular total is $180.00 + $70.00 = $250.00, and the discounts are 0.25($180.00) = $45.00 for the jacket and 0.20($70.00) = $14.00 for the trousers. Adding the $15.00 coupon gives total savings of $45.00 + $14.00 + $15.00 = $74.00, so $74.00 / $250.00 = 29.6%.

exercises.name: Calculating Final Price with Discounts and Coupons

qs.q: Coupon stacking is using both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon on a single item. Tubes of toothpaste are priced at two for $7.50. A manufacturer's coupon is $0.75 off when buying two tubes, and an in-store coupon is $1.25 off when buying two tubes. What is the final price for one tube of toothpaste using both coupons?
qs.s: The total discount for both tubes is $0.75 + $1.25 = $2.00, reducing the price to $7.50 - $2.00 = $5.50. The price for one tube is $5.50 / 2 = $2.75.

qs.q: Coupon stacking is using both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon on a single item. Bottles of shampoo are priced at two for $11.50. A manufacturer's coupon is $1.20 off when buying two bottles, and an in-store coupon is $1.50 off when buying two bottles. What is the final price for one bottle of shampoo using both coupons?
qs.s: The combined coupon savings is $1.20 + $1.50 = $2.70, so the price for both bottles is $11.50 - $2.70 = $8.80. The price for one bottle is $8.80 / 2 = $4.40.

qs.q: Coupon stacking is using both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon on a single item. Jars of pasta sauce are priced at three for $9.90. A manufacturer's discount is $1.25 off when buying three jars, and an in-store coupon is $1.45 off when buying three jars. What is the final price for one jar of pasta sauce using both coupons?
qs.s: The total savings from both coupons is $1.25 + $1.45 = $2.70, which reduces the total price for three jars to $9.90 - $2.70 = $7.20. Dividing by 3 gives $2.40 per jar.

qs.q: Coupon stacking is using both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon on a single item. Packs of batteries are priced at two for $14.80. A manufacturer's coupon gives $2.00 off when buying two packs, and an in-store coupon gives $1.60 off when buying two packs. What is the final price for one pack of batteries using both coupons?
qs.s: Subtracting both coupons gives a combined price of $14.80 - $2.00 - $1.60 = $11.20 for two packs. Dividing by 2 gives a final unit price of $5.60.

qs.q: Coupon stacking is using both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon on a single item. Boxes of cereal are priced at two for $8.60. A manufacturer's coupon gives $1.10 off when buying two boxes, and an in-store coupon gives $0.70 off when buying two boxes. What is the final price for one box of cereal using both coupons?
qs.s: The total discount is $1.10 + $0.70 = $1.80, making the price for two boxes $8.60 - $1.80 = $6.80. Dividing by 2 gives a final price of $3.40 for one box.

qs.q: Boxes of protein bars are priced at $16.00 each under a promotion of 'Buy 2 boxes, get 25% off a third box.' A customer buys 3 boxes and stacks a manufacturer's coupon for $1.50 off each box with a store coupon for $3.00 off the total purchase. What is the final total price for all 3 boxes?
qs.s: The store promotion price before coupons is $16.00 + \(16.00 + (\)16.00 × 0.75) = $44.00. Subtracting the manufacturer coupons (3 × $1.50 = $4.50) and the $3.00 store coupon gives $44.00 - $4.50 - $3.00 = $36.50.

qs.q: An electronic tablet is on sale for 15% off its regular price. A customer stacks a manufacturer's coupon for $30.00 off with a store coupon for $20.00 off. If the final price before taxes is $256.00, what was the tablet's original regular price?
qs.s: Adding the $50.00 in total coupons back to the final price gives $256.00 + $50.00 = $306.00, which represents 85% of the regular price. Dividing by 0.85 gives an original price of $306.00 / 0.85 = $360.00.

qs.q: A store offers a 20% discount on headphones normally priced at $45.00 each. A customer buys two pairs of headphones and stacks a manufacturer's coupon for $5.00 off the purchase of two with a store coupon for $7.00 off the purchase of two. What is the final price for one pair of headphones?
qs.s: Two pairs regularly cost $90.00, which becomes $90.00 × 0.80 = $72.00 after the 20% store discount. Applying the stacked coupons gives $72.00 - $5.00 - $7.00 = $60.00 for both, so one pair costs $60.00 / 2 = $30.00.

qs.q: Brand A detergent costs $18.00 for a 3 L bottle and has a 10% store discount stacked with a $1.80 manufacturer coupon. Brand B detergent costs $22.50 for a 4.5 L bottle and has an in-store coupon for $4.50 off. What is the difference in the final price per litre between the two brands?
qs.s: Brand A costs ($18.00 × 0.90 - $1.80) / 3 = $14.40 / 3 = $4.80 per litre, while Brand B costs ($22.50 - $4.50) / 4.5 = $18.00 / 4.5 = $4.00 per litre. The difference is $4.80 - $4.00 = $0.80 per litre.

qs.q: Energy drinks are priced at two for $5.50. A customer buys 4 energy drinks and stacks a manufacturer's coupon of $0.80 off every two drinks with an in-store coupon of $0.70 off every two drinks. A sales tax of 5% is then added to the discounted subtotal. What is the total final cost for all 4 drinks?
qs.s: The base price for 4 drinks is 2 × $5.50 = $11.00, and the two pairs receive a total discount of 2 × ($0.80 + $0.70) = $3.00, giving a subtotal of $8.00. Adding 5% tax gives a final cost of $8.00 × 1.05 = $8.40.

exercises.name: Calculating Final Price with Discounts and Coupons

qs.q: Danielle has both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon for a laptop. If the laptop is selling for $650, with a store coupon worth 15% off, and a manufacturer's coupon worth $80, what does Danielle pay for the laptop?
qs.s: Applying the 15% store coupon gives $650 \times (1 - 0.15) = $552.50. Subtracting the $80 manufacturer's coupon gives a final price of $552.50 - $80 = $472.50.

qs.q: Priya has both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon for a tablet. If the tablet is selling for $449, with a store coupon worth 20% off, and a manufacturer's coupon worth $50, what does Priya pay for the tablet?
qs.s: The 20% store coupon reduces the price to $449 \times 0.80 = $359.20. Subtracting the $50 manufacturer's coupon gives $359.20 - $50 = $309.20.

qs.q: Brenda has both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon for a sound system. If the sound system is selling for $350, with a store coupon worth 15% off, and a manufacturer's coupon worth $40, what does Brenda pay for the sound system?
qs.s: Applying the 15% store coupon gives $350 \times 0.85 = $297.50. Then, applying the $40 manufacturer's coupon gives $297.50 - $40 = $257.50.

qs.q: Kevin has both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon for a washing machine. If the washing machine is selling for $720, with a store coupon worth 25% off, and a manufacturer's coupon worth $95, what does Kevin pay for the washing machine?
qs.s: Applying the 25% store coupon gives $720 \times 0.75 = $540.00. Subtracting the $95 manufacturer's coupon yields $540.00 - $95 = $445.00.

qs.q: Marcus has both a store coupon and a manufacturer's coupon for a refrigerator. If the refrigerator is selling for $899, with a store coupon worth 20% off, and a manufacturer's coupon worth $110, what does Marcus pay for the refrigerator?
qs.s: Applying the 20% store coupon gives $899 \times 0.80 = $719.20. Deducting the $110 manufacturer's coupon results in $719.20 - $110 = $609.20.

qs.q: Maya has a store coupon, a loyalty member coupon, and a manufacturer's coupon for a laptop priced at $1,200. The store coupon gives 20% off the regular price, the loyalty coupon gives an additional 10% off the discounted price, and the manufacturer's coupon is worth $75 off. What does Maya pay for the laptop?
qs.s: Applying the 20% store coupon gives $1,200 \times 0.80 = $960.00. The 10% loyalty discount reduces this to $960.00 \times 0.90 = $864.00, and subtracting the $75 manufacturer's coupon leaves $864.00 - $75 = $789.00.

qs.q: Elena is shopping for an elliptical trainer listed at $1,200. Store A offers a 15% discount plus a $100 manufacturer's coupon. Store B offers the same model at 25% off plus a $30 store coupon. If Elena buys the elliptical from the store that gives the lowest final price, what will she pay?
qs.s: Store A's final price is ($1,200 \times 0.85) - $100 = $920.00, while Store B's final price is ($1,200 \times 0.75) - $30 = $870.00. The lowest final price is $870.00 at Store B.

qs.q: Carlos is buying a riding lawnmower selling for $1,600. He uses a store coupon for 25% off and a manufacturer's coupon for $150. If a sales tax of 8% is applied to the final discounted price after all coupons, what is the total amount Carlos pays?
qs.s: Applying the 25% coupon gives $1,600 \times 0.75 = $1,200.00, and subtracting the $150 coupon leaves $1,050.00. Adding 8% sales tax gives a final total of $1,050.00 \times 1.08 = $1,134.00.

qs.q: Nadia wants to buy a refrigerator priced at $1,450. She has a store coupon for 20% off, a manufacturer's coupon for $120, and a $50 store rewards certificate. If sales tax of 6% is applied to the discounted price after all coupons and certificates are deducted, what does Nadia pay in total?
qs.s: The 20% coupon lowers the price to $1,450 \times 0.80 = $1,160.00, and deducting the $120 coupon and $50 certificate leaves $1,160.00 - $170 = $990.00. Adding 6% sales tax yields $990.00 \times 1.06 = $1,049.40.

qs.q: Liam purchases a television for $850 and a soundbar for $250. The store offers a bundle coupon of 15% off the total purchase price, and Liam also has a manufacturer's coupon for $100 off the television and another manufacturer's coupon for $30 off the soundbar. What does Liam pay in total for both items?
qs.s: The total regular price is $850 + $250 = $1,100. Applying the 15% bundle coupon gives $1,100 \times 0.85 = $935.00, and subtracting both manufacturer coupons ($100 + $30 = $130) results in $935.00 - $130 = $805.00.

Solve.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2\frac{1}{4}}{p} = \frac{1\frac{7}{8}}{3\frac{1}{8}}\)
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions to get \(\frac{9/4}{p} = \frac{15/8}{25/8}\), then cross-multiply to obtain \(\frac{15}{8}p = \frac{9}{4} \cdot \frac{25}{8} = \frac{225}{32}\), which simplifies to \(p = \frac{225}{32} \cdot \frac{8}{15} = 3\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 1\frac{1}{2}}{2\frac{1}{4}} = \frac{5\frac{1}{3}}{1\frac{1}{5}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the right side to \(\frac{16/3}{6/5} = \frac{40}{9}\), then cross-multiply with the left side to get \(x + 1\frac{1}{2} = \frac{40}{9} \cdot \frac{9}{4} = 10\), giving \(x = 10 - 1\frac{1}{2} = 8\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\displaystyle \frac{3m}{1\frac{3}{4}} = \frac{5\frac{1}{7}}{2\frac{1}{2}}\)
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions to get \(\frac{3m}{7/4} = \frac{36/7}{5/2}\), then cross-multiply to find \(\frac{5}{2}(3m) = \frac{7}{4} \cdot \frac{36}{7} = 9\), which gives \(3m = \frac{18}{5}\) and \(m = 1\frac{1}{5}\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\displaystyle \frac{6\frac{2}{3}}{4\frac{4}{9}} = \frac{7\frac{1}{2}}{x - 2\frac{1}{3}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the left side to \(\frac{20/3}{40/9} = \frac{3}{2}\), then cross-multiply in \(\frac{3}{2} = \frac{15/2}{x - 2\frac{1}{3}}\) to get \(x - 2\frac{1}{3} = \frac{15}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = 5\), giving \(x = 5 + 2\frac{1}{3} = 7\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\displaystyle \frac{4\frac{1}{2}}{2w - 1\frac{1}{4}} = \frac{3\frac{3}{8}}{1\frac{7}{8}}\)
qs.s: Simplify the right side to \(\frac{27/8}{15/8} = \frac{9}{5}\), then cross-multiply to get \(\frac{9}{5}(2w - 1\frac{1}{4}) = \frac{9}{2}\), giving \(2w - \frac{5}{4} = \frac{5}{2}\), which leads to \(2w = \frac{15}{4}\) and \(w = 1\frac{7}{8}\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\displaystyle \frac{2\frac{1}{3} + 1\frac{1}{6}}{y} = \frac{4\frac{2}{3}}{3\frac{1}{5}}\)
qs.s: Add the numerator terms on the left to obtain \(2\frac{1}{3} + 1\frac{1}{6} = \frac{7}{2}\), then cross-multiply in \(\frac{7/2}{y} = \frac{14/3}{16/5}\) to get \(\frac{14}{3}y = \frac{7}{2} \cdot \frac{16}{5} = \frac{56}{5}\), so \(y = \frac{56}{5} \cdot \frac{3}{14} = 2\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{x}{2} = \frac{32}{x}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(x^2 = 2 \cdot 32 = 64\). Taking the square root of both sides yields \(x = \pm 8\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{m}{8} = \frac{2}{m}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(m^2 = 8 \cdot 2 = 16\). Taking the square root of both sides yields \(m = \pm 4\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{3}{a} = \frac{a}{27}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(a^2 = 3 \cdot 27 = 81\). Taking the square root of both sides yields \(a = \pm 9\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{y}{5} = \frac{20}{y}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(y^2 = 5 \cdot 20 = 100\). Taking the square root of both sides yields \(y = \pm 10\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{c}{6} = \frac{24}{c}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(c^2 = 6 \cdot 24 = 144\). Taking the square root of both sides yields \(c = \pm 12\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{w}{2.5} = \frac{10}{w}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(w^2 = 2.5 \cdot 10 = 25\). Taking the square root of both sides yields \(w = \pm 5\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{2p}{5} = \frac{5}{2p}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(4p^2 = 5 \cdot 5 = 25\). Dividing both sides by \(4\) gives \(p^2 = \frac{25}{4}\), so \(p = \pm \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{3m}{10} = \frac{120}{m}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(3m^2 = 10 \cdot 120 = 1200\). Dividing both sides by \(3\) gives \(m^2 = 400\), so \(m = \pm 20\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{3y}{7} = \frac{21}{y}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(3y^2 = 7 \cdot 21 = 147\). Dividing both sides by \(3\) gives \(y^2 = 49\), so \(y = \pm 7\).

qs.q:
Solve.
\(\frac{2x}{5} = \frac{90}{x}\)
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(2x^2 = 5 \cdot 90 = 450\). Dividing both sides by \(2\) gives \(x^2 = 225\), so \(x = \pm 15\).

qs.q: A survey found that 3 out of every 8 students in a school district participate in after-school sports. If there are 5,600 students in the district, how many students participate in after-school sports?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{3}{8} = \frac{x}{5,600}\). Cross multiply and solve for \(x\) to get \(x = \frac{3 \cdot 5,600}{8} = 2,100\) students.

qs.q: Thirty-two out of every 100 commuters in a metropolitan area take public transit to work. If there are 650,000 commuters in the area, how many of them take public transit?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{32}{100} = \frac{x}{650,000}\). Cross multiplying gives \(x = \frac{32 \cdot 650,000}{100} = 208,000\) commuters.

qs.q: Twelve out of every 50 households in a town own an electric vehicle. If the town has 24,000 households, how many households own an electric vehicle?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{12}{50} = \frac{x}{24,000}\). Cross multiply and divide to find \(x = \frac{12 \cdot 24,000}{50} = 5,760\) households.

qs.q: In a manufacturing plant, 7 out of every 200 light bulbs inspected are defective. If the plant produces 90,000 light bulbs in a week, how many of them are expected to be defective?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{7}{200} = \frac{x}{90,000}\). Cross multiply to find \(x = \frac{7 \cdot 90,000}{200} = 3,150\) defective light bulbs.

qs.q: A wildlife biologist estimates that 9 out of every 40 fish in a lake are trout. If the lake contains an estimated population of 18,000 fish, how many trout are in the lake?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{9}{40} = \frac{x}{18,000}\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{9 \cdot 18,000}{40} = 4,050\) trout.

qs.q: At an electronics factory, quality control tests show that 3 out of every 125 microchips produced are defective. During one shift, exactly 72 defective microchips were identified. How many non-defective microchips were produced during that shift?
qs.s: First find the total microchips produced by solving \(\frac{3}{125} = \frac{72}{\text{total}}\), giving \(\text{total} = \frac{72 \cdot 125}{3} = 3,000\). Subtract the 72 defective chips to find \(3,000 - 72 = 2,928\) non-defective microchips.

qs.q: A city with 850,000 residents reported that five years ago, 38 out of every 100 residents recycled regularly. Today, that rate has risen to 54 out of every 100 residents. Assuming the population remained at 850,000, how many more residents recycle regularly today than five years ago?
qs.s: The recycling rate increased by \(54 - 38 = 16\) per 100 residents. Solve the proportion \(\frac{16}{100} = \frac{x}{850,000}\) to get \(x = \frac{16 \cdot 850,000}{100} = 136,000\) more residents.

qs.q: In a province with 5,500,000 residents, 4 out of every 5 people have a family doctor. Among those with a family doctor, 3 out of every 20 had a virtual appointment last year. How many residents had a virtual appointment with their family doctor last year?
qs.s: First solve \(\frac{4}{5} = \frac{x}{5,500,000}\) to find that \(4,400,000\) people have a family doctor. Then solve \(\frac{3}{20} = \frac{y}{4,400,000}\) to find \(y = \frac{3 \cdot 4,400,000}{20} = 660,000\) virtual appointments.

qs.q: A public health survey found that 17 out of every 25 teenagers sleep less than the recommended 8 hours per night. In a region with 450,000 teenagers, how many teenagers get at least the recommended 8 hours of sleep per night?
qs.s: Since 17 of 25 sleep less than 8 hours, \(25 - 17 = 8\) out of every 25 get at least 8 hours. Solve the proportion \(\frac{8}{25} = \frac{x}{450,000}\) to get \(x = \frac{8 \cdot 450,000}{25} = 144,000\) teenagers.

qs.q: In County A, 16 out of every 50 workers work remotely out of a workforce of 75,000. In County B, 9 out of every 25 workers work remotely out of a workforce of 60,000. What is the total number of remote workers in both counties combined?
qs.s: County A has \(\frac{16 \cdot 75,000}{50} = 24,000\) remote workers, and County B has \(\frac{9 \cdot 60,000}{25} = 21,600\) remote workers. Adding them together gives \(24,000 + 21,600 = 45,600\) remote workers.

qs.q: An office printer takes 4 minutes to print 140 pages. At this rate, how many minutes are needed to print 455 pages?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{4}{140} = \frac{x}{455}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(140x = 1820\), so \(x = 13\) minutes.

qs.q: A groundskeeper uses 6 kg of grass seed to cover 160 square metres of lawn. At this rate, how many kilograms of grass seed are needed to cover 400 square metres?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{6}{160} = \frac{x}{400}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(160x = 2400\), so \(x = 15\) kg.

qs.q: A veterinarian prescribes 18 mL of medication for a 24 kg dog. At this rate, how many millilitres of medication are needed for a 36 kg dog?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{18}{24} = \frac{x}{36}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(24x = 648\), so \(x = 27\) mL.

qs.q: A bakery uses 15 kg of flour to make 40 loaves of bread. At this rate, how many kilograms of flour are needed to make 64 loaves of bread?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{15}{40} = \frac{x}{64}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(40x = 960\), so \(x = 24\) kg.

qs.q: A hybrid car traveled 216 km on 9 litres of fuel. At this rate, how many litres of fuel are needed to travel 384 km?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{216}{9} = \frac{384}{x}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(216x = 3456\), so \(x = 16\) litres.

qs.q: A print shop charges $48 for printing 120 brochures. A business orders 350 brochures and pays with a $200 bill. At this rate, how much change should the business receive?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{48}{120} = \frac{C}{350}\) to find the total cost $C = $140. The change from a $200 bill is $200 - $140 = $60.

qs.q: A delivery truck traveled 270 km on 18 litres of diesel. The driver currently has 12 litres of diesel in the tank and needs to travel a total of 495 km. At this rate, how many additional litres of diesel must be added to the tank to complete the trip?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{270}{18} = \frac{495}{x}\) to find that \(x = 33\) litres are needed in total. Subtracting the 12 litres already in the tank gives \(33 - 12 = 21\) additional litres needed.

qs.q: On a map, 2.5 cm represents 75 km. The distance between two towns on the map is 14 cm. A driver travels between these two towns at an average speed of 70 km/h. How many hours does the trip take?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{2.5}{75} = \frac{14}{d}\) to find the actual distance \(d = 420\) km. Traveling 420 km at 70 km/h takes \(420 \div 70 = 6\) hours.

qs.q: A bottling machine fills 840 bottles in 35 minutes. At this rate, how many bottles can the machine fill in 2.5 hours?
qs.s: Convert 2.5 hours to \(2.5 \times 60 = 150\) minutes, then set up the proportion \(\frac{840}{35} = \frac{x}{150}\). Solving gives \(35x = 126000\), so \(x = 3600\) bottles.

qs.q: Machine A produces 180 bolts in 20 minutes, while Machine B produces 264 bolts in 22 minutes. Working at their respective rates, how many more bolts will Machine B produce than Machine A in 1.5 hours?
qs.s: In 90 minutes (1.5 hours), Machine A produces \(\frac{180}{20} \times 90 = 810\) bolts and Machine B produces \(\frac{264}{22} \times 90 = 1080\) bolts. The difference is \(1080 - 810 = 270\) bolts.

qs.q: If a car uses \(8\text{ L}\) of fuel to travel \(120\text{ km}\), how many liters of fuel are needed to travel \(450\text{ km}\)?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{8}{120} = \frac{x}{450}\), which gives \(120x = 3600\). Dividing by \(120\) yields \(x = 30\text{ L}\).

qs.q: If \(6\text{ cups}\) of flour are needed to bake \(45\text{ muffins}\), how many cups of flour are needed to bake \(150\text{ muffins}\)?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{6}{45} = \frac{x}{150}\), giving \(45x = 900\). Dividing both sides by \(45\) yields \(x = 20\text{ cups}\).

qs.q: If an office printer takes \(3\text{ minutes}\) to print \(105\text{ pages}\), how many minutes will it take to print \(840\text{ pages}\)?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{3}{105} = \frac{x}{840}\), giving \(105x = 2520\). Dividing both sides by \(105\) yields \(x = 24\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: If a \(4\text{ kg}\) bag of fertilizer covers \(2400\text{ ft}^2\), how many kilograms of fertilizer are needed to cover \(18\,000\text{ ft}^2\)?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{4}{2400} = \frac{x}{18000}\), which gives \(2400x = 72\,000\). Dividing both sides by \(2400\) gives \(x = 30\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: If \(8\text{ bundles}\) of roofing shingles cover \(260\text{ ft}^2\), how many bundles of shingles are needed to cover \(1430\text{ ft}^2\)?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{8}{260} = \frac{x}{1430}\), which gives \(260x = 11\,440\). Dividing both sides by \(260\) gives \(x = 44\text{ bundles}\).

qs.q: A commercial greenhouse requires \(15\text{ pounds}\) of plant food for every \(4500\text{ ft}^2\) of growing area. If plant food is sold only in \(25\text{-pound}\) bags, how many full bags must be purchased to treat \(67\,500\text{ ft}^2\) of growing area?
qs.s: Solve the proportion \(\frac{15}{4500} = \frac{x}{67500}\) to find that \(x = 225\text{ pounds}\) of plant food are needed. Dividing by \(25\text{ pounds per bag}\) gives \(225 \div 25 = 9\text{ bags}\).

qs.q: A printing press uses \(16\text{ liters}\) of ink to print \(3600\text{ posters}\). The shop already has \(9\text{ liters}\) of ink on hand. How many more liters of ink must be purchased to fulfill an order of \(8100\text{ posters}\)?
qs.s: Solve the proportion \(\frac{16}{3600} = \frac{x}{8100}\) to find that \(x = 36\text{ liters}\) are needed in total. Subtracting the \(9\text{ liters}\) on hand leaves \(36 - 9 = 27\text{ liters}\) to purchase.

qs.q: An industrial pump drains \(420\text{ gallons}\) of water in \(14\text{ minutes}\). How many gallons of water can the pump drain in \(2.5\text{ hours}\)?
qs.s: First convert \(2.5\text{ hours}\) to \(150\text{ minutes}\). Using the proportion \(\frac{420}{14} = \frac{x}{150}\), cross-multiplying yields \(14x = 63\,000\), which gives \(x = 4500\text{ gallons}\).

qs.q: A recipe requires \(2\frac{1}{2}\text{ pounds}\) of ground beef to serve \(6\text{ people}\). How many pounds of ground beef are needed to serve \(28\text{ people}\)?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{2.5}{6} = \frac{x}{28}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{5}{12} = \frac{x}{28}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(12x = 140\), so \(x = \frac{140}{12} = 11\frac{2}{3}\text{ pounds}\).

qs.q: A \(2\text{ gallon}\) can of wood sealant covers \(450\text{ ft}^2\). How many gallons of sealant are needed to apply \(2\) coats to a rectangular deck measuring \(45\text{ ft}\) by \(25\text{ ft}\)?
qs.s: The total area for 2 coats is \(2 \times (45\text{ ft} \times 25\text{ ft}) = 2250\text{ ft}^2\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{2}{450} = \frac{x}{2250}\) gives \(450x = 4500\), so \(x = 10\text{ gallons}\).

qs.q: A baker uses 7.5 g of yeast for every 250 g of flour. How many grams of yeast are needed for 4 kg of flour?
qs.s: Convert 4 kg to 4000 g. Set up the proportion 7.5 / 250 = x / 4000 to find x = (7.5 * 4000) / 250 = 120 g.

qs.q: A specialized copper cable weighs 4.5 g for every 30 cm of length. How many grams does a 12 m coil of this cable weigh?
qs.s: Convert 12 m to 1200 cm. Solve the proportion 4.5 / 30 = x / 1200 to obtain x = (4.5 * 1200) / 30 = 180 g.

qs.q: A certain brand of ribbon shrinks 1.2 cm for every 40 cm of length when ironed. How many centimeters will a 5 m spool of ribbon shrink when ironed?
qs.s: Convert 5 m to 500 cm. Solve the proportion 1.2 / 40 = x / 500 by cross-multiplying to get x = (1.2 * 500) / 40 = 15 cm.

qs.q: A metal pipe expands 0.8 mm for every 25 cm increase in length when heated. By how many millimeters will a 4 m pipe expand under the same heat?
qs.s: Convert 4 m to 400 cm. Solve the proportion 0.8 / 25 = x / 400 to find x = (0.8 * 400) / 25 = 12.8 mm.

qs.q: A dripping faucet leaks 3.5 mL of water every 20 seconds. How many milliliters of water will it leak in 6 minutes?
qs.s: Convert 6 minutes to 360 seconds. Solve the proportion 3.5 / 20 = x / 360 to get x = (3.5 * 360) / 20 = 63 mL.

qs.q: An industrial printing press uses 85 mL of ink to print 125 posters. A print shop has a 2-liter container of ink. After printing 2,500 posters, how many milliliters of ink remain in the container?
qs.s: Solve 85 / 125 = x / 2500 to find that 1700 mL of ink is used. Subtract this from the full container of 2000 mL (2 L) to find 2000 - 1700 = 300 mL remaining.

qs.q: A water filtration system extracts 35 mg of minerals from every 250 mL of well water. A family consumes 1.4 L of well water on Monday and 2.1 L on Tuesday. In total, how many grams of minerals were extracted from the water consumed over these two days?
qs.s: The total volume consumed is 1.4 L + 2.1 L = 3.5 L = 3500 mL. Solve the proportion 35 / 250 = x / 3500 to find x = 490 mg, which converts to 0.49 g.

qs.q: A farmer uses a drip irrigation line that delivers 4.2 L of water every 35 m of line. The farmer currently has a 150 m line, but plans to extend it to a total length of 400 m. How many more liters of water will the extended line deliver than the current line?
qs.s: The additional length is 400 - 150 = 250 m. Solve the proportion 4.2 / 35 = x / 250 to find the additional water delivered: x = (4.2 * 250) / 35 = 30 L.

qs.q: On average, 45 cm of loose snow compresses down to 36 mm of compacted ice. How many meters of loose snow would be required to produce 1.2 m of compacted ice?
qs.s: Convert 36 mm to 3.6 cm and 1.2 m to 120 cm. Solve the proportion 45 / 3.6 = x / 120 to find x = 1500 cm, which equals 15 m.

qs.q: A drainage pipe discharges water at a constant rate of 48 L every 15 minutes. How many cubic meters of water will the pipe discharge in 10 hours? (1 m^3 = 1000 L)
qs.s: Convert 10 hours to 600 minutes and solve 48 / 15 = x / 600 to find x = 1920 L. Convert liters to cubic meters: 1920 / 1000 = 1.92 m^3.

qs.q: A high-speed printer prints 1176 pages in 28 minutes. At this rate, how long will it take to print 1596 pages?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1176}{28} = \frac{1596}{x}\), which gives \(1176x = 28 \times 1596\). Solving for \(x\) yields \(x = \frac{44688}{1176} = 38\) minutes.

qs.q: A car travels 1564 kilometers on 68 liters of fuel. At this rate, how many liters of fuel are needed to travel 2116 kilometers?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1564}{68} = \frac{2116}{x}\), which gives \(1564x = 68 \times 2116\). Solving for \(x\) yields \(x = \frac{143888}{1564} = 92\) liters.

qs.q: A contractor pays $2304 for 48 meters of industrial wire. At this rate, how much will 65 meters of the same wire cost?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{2304}{48} = \frac{x}{65}\), which gives \(48x = 2304 \times 65\). Solving for \(x\) yields \(x = \frac{149760}{48} = 3120\) dollars.

qs.q: A water pump empties 2145 liters of water in 39 minutes. At this rate, how long will it take to empty 2970 liters of water?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{2145}{39} = \frac{2970}{x}\), which gives \(2145x = 39 \times 2970\). Solving for \(x\) yields \(x = \frac{115830}{2145} = 54\) minutes.

qs.q: A factory machine produces 1872 bolts in 36 minutes. At this rate, how many bolts will the machine produce in 45 minutes?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1872}{36} = \frac{x}{45}\), which gives \(36x = 1872 \times 45\). Solving for \(x\) yields \(x = \frac{84240}{36} = 2340\) bolts.

qs.q: A commercial printing press prints 3450 flyers in 46 minutes. A second print job requires 5625 flyers printed at the exact same rate. How many more minutes will the second print job take than the first?
qs.s: The printing rate is \(\frac{3450}{46} = 75\) flyers per minute, so the second job takes \(\frac{5625}{75} = 75\) minutes. The difference in time is \(75 - 46 = 29\) minutes.

qs.q: A server is backing up a 8160-gigabyte database at a constant rate. In the first 48 minutes, it backs up 2304 gigabytes. At this rate, how many more minutes will it take to finish the backup?
qs.s: The backup rate is \(\frac{2304}{48} = 48\) gigabytes per minute, so the total backup takes \(\frac{8160}{48} = 170\) minutes. Subtracting the 48 minutes already elapsed gives \(170 - 48 = 122\) more minutes.

qs.q: A packaging machine packs boxes at a constant rate. It packs 432 boxes in \((t + 4)\) minutes and 648 boxes in \((2t - 1)\) minutes. How many boxes does the machine pack per minute?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{432}{t + 4} = \frac{648}{2t - 1}\), which simplifies to \(2(2t - 1) = 3(t + 4)\) and gives \(t = 14\). The first batch takes \(14 + 4 = 18\) minutes, so the rate is \(\frac{432}{18} = 24\) boxes per minute.

qs.q: A freight train travels at a constant speed, covering 378 miles in 4.5 hours. At this same speed, what is the total distance the train will cover during a two-part trip consisting of a 3.5-hour morning run and a 4-hour afternoon run?
qs.s: The train's speed is \(\frac{378}{4.5} = 84\) miles per hour, and the total travel time is \(3.5 + 4 = 7.5\) hours. Multiplying the speed by the total time gives \(84 \times 7.5 = 630\) miles.

qs.q: Two files download at the same constant speed. The first file has a size of \((x + 40)\) megabytes and takes 30 seconds to download, while the second file has a size of \((2x - 10)\) megabytes and takes 45 seconds to download. What is the size of the first file?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{x + 40}{30} = \frac{2x - 10}{45}\), which simplifies to \(3(x + 40) = 2(2x - 10)\) and solves to \(x = 140\). Substituting into the first file's expression gives \(140 + 40 = 180\) megabytes.

qs.q: During a vacation in Mexico, 1 US dollar was equivalent to 17.5 Mexican pesos. If a guided tour costs 48 US dollars, what is its cost in Mexican pesos?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1}{17.5} = \frac{48}{x}\) and solve for \(x\) by multiplying \(48 \cdot 17.5 = 840\) Mexican pesos.

qs.q: On a financial market, 1 British pound was worth 1.32 US dollars. If an online purchase from a UK retailer costs 75 British pounds, what is the cost in US dollars?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1}{1.32} = \frac{75}{x}\) and cross-multiply to find \(x = 75 \cdot 1.32 = 99\) US dollars.

qs.q: On a certain day, 1 euro was worth 1.25 US dollars. If a train pass in Germany costs 120 euros, what is its cost in US dollars?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1}{1.25} = \frac{120}{x}\) and cross-multiply to get \(x = 120 \cdot 1.25 = 150\) US dollars.

qs.q: On October 12, 1 New Zealand dollar was worth 0.88 Canadian dollars. If a handmade woolen sweater in Auckland costs 150 New Zealand dollars, what is its equivalent price in Canadian dollars?
qs.s: Using the proportion \(\frac{1}{0.88} = \frac{150}{x}\), cross-multiply to obtain \(x = 150 \cdot 0.88 = 132\) Canadian dollars.

qs.q: An exchange service converts 1 Australian dollar to 96 Japanese yen. If a dining bill totals 65 Australian dollars, what is the cost in Japanese yen?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1}{96} = \frac{65}{x}\), which gives \(x = 65 \cdot 96 = 6240\) Japanese yen.

qs.q: At an exchange bureau, 85 Australian dollars can be exchanged for 55 euros. At this same rate, how many Australian dollars are needed to obtain 231 euros?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{85}{55} = \frac{x}{231}\), cross-multiply to get \(55x = 85 \cdot 231\), and divide by 55 to find \(x = 357\) Australian dollars.

qs.q: A traveler exchanges money across multiple currencies. If 1 US dollar is worth 1.30 Canadian dollars and 1 Canadian dollar is worth 110 Japanese yen, how many Japanese yen will the traveler receive for 250 US dollars?
qs.s: First, convert to Canadian dollars using \(\frac{1}{1.30} = \frac{250}{y}\), giving \(y = 325\) CAD; then convert to Japanese yen using \(\frac{1}{110} = \frac{325}{x}\), giving \(x = 325 \cdot 110 = 35{,}750\) Japanese yen.

qs.q: At a border exchange kiosk, 75 Canadian dollars can be exchanged for 54 euros. A traveler exchanges 350 Canadian dollars and then spends 180 euros on lodging. How many euros does the traveler have remaining?
qs.s: Solve \(\frac{75}{54} = \frac{350}{x}\) to find the total euros received: \(x = \frac{54 \cdot 350}{75} = 252\) euros. Subtracting the lodging expense gives \(252 - 180 = 72\) euros remaining.

qs.q: A tourist in Vancouver stays 3 nights at a hotel for 160 Canadian dollars per night, plus a one-time cleaning fee of 40 Canadian dollars. If 1 euro is worth 1.30 Canadian dollars, what is the total cost of the stay in euros?
qs.s: The total cost in Canadian dollars is \(3(160) + 40 = 520\) CAD. Solving the proportion \(\frac{1}{1.30} = \frac{x}{520}\) gives \(1.30x = 520\), so \(x = \frac{520}{1.30} = 400\) euros.

qs.q: A bookstore sells a collector's edition novel in two countries. In the United Kingdom, it costs 45 British pounds, while in the United States, it costs 68 US dollars. If 1 British pound is worth 1.40 US dollars, how much less does the book cost in the United Kingdom, expressed in US dollars?
qs.s: Convert the UK price to US dollars using \(\frac{1}{1.40} = \frac{45}{x}\), which gives \(x = 45 \cdot 1.40 = 63\) USD, then subtract from the US price: \(68 - 63 = 5\) US dollars.

qs.q: In 5 minutes, a typist types 260 words. At this rate, how long will it take the typist to type 728 words?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{5}{260} = \frac{t}{728}\). Cross multiply to get \(260t = 5 \cdot 728 = 3640\), so \(t = \frac{3640}{260} = 14\) minutes.

qs.q: In 3 hours, a gardener mows 225 square metres of lawn. At this rate, how long will it take to mow 600 square metres of lawn?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{3}{225} = \frac{t}{600}\). Cross multiply to get \(225t = 3 \cdot 600 = 1800\), so \(t = \frac{1800}{225} = 8\) hours.

qs.q: In 5 minutes, 140 pages are printed by a press. At this rate, how long will it take to print 532 pages?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{5}{140} = \frac{t}{532}\). Cross multiply to get \(140t = 5 \cdot 532 = 2660\), so \(t = \frac{2660}{140} = 19\) minutes.

qs.q: In 6 minutes, a pump drains 84 litres of water from a tank. At this rate, how long will it take to drain 294 litres of water?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{6}{84} = \frac{t}{294}\). Cross multiply to get \(84t = 6 \cdot 294 = 1764\), so \(t = \frac{1764}{84} = 21\) minutes.

qs.q: In 4 hours, 180 bolts are produced by a factory machine. At this rate, how long will it take to produce 315 bolts?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{4}{180} = \frac{t}{315}\). Cross multiply to get \(180t = 4 \cdot 315 = 1260\), so \(t = \frac{1260}{180} = 7\) hours.

qs.q: A laboratory filtration system filters 850 millilitres of solution in 12 minutes. At this rate, how many hours will it take to filter 21.25 litres of the solution?
qs.s: Convert 21.25 L to 21,250 mL and solve the proportion \(\frac{12}{850} = \frac{t}{21250}\), which yields \(t = \frac{12 \cdot 21250}{850} = 300\) minutes. Convert to hours: \(\frac{300}{60} = 5\) hours.

qs.q: A drainage pipe discharges 168 litres of water in 4 hours. If a total of 714 litres of water must be discharged, how many more hours must the pipe run?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{4}{168} = \frac{t}{714}\) to find the total time \(t = \frac{4 \cdot 714}{168} = 17\) hours. The pipe must run for \(17 - 4 = 13\) more hours.

qs.q: A fuel pump delivers \(3\frac{1}{3}\) litres of gasoline every 2 minutes. At this rate, how many litres of gasoline will it deliver in \(1\frac{1}{4}\) hours?
qs.s: Convert \(1\frac{1}{4}\) hours to 75 minutes, then set up the proportion \(\frac{10/3}{2} = \frac{V}{75}\). Cross multiplying gives \(2V = \frac{10}{3} \cdot 75 = 250\), so \(V = 125\) litres.

qs.q: An industrial pump empties an oil reservoir at a constant rate. It pumps out 280 litres in \(t\) hours, and it pumps out 700 litres in \(t + 6\) hours. What is the value of \(t\)?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{t}{280} = \frac{t + 6}{700}\) and cross multiply to get \(700t = 280(t + 6)\). Expanding gives \(700t = 280t + 1680\), so \(420t = 1680\), which solves to \(t = 4\).

qs.q: In \(3\frac{1}{2}\) hours, 420 litres of oil flow through a pipe. At this rate, how long will it take 1520 litres to flow through the same pipe?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{7/2}{420} = \frac{t}{1520}\). Cross multiply to get \(420t = \frac{7}{2} \cdot 1520 = 5320\), so \(t = \frac{5320}{420} = \frac{38}{3} = 12\frac{2}{3}\) hours.

qs.q: A hiking trail map has a scale of 4.5 cm to 18 km. Find the actual distance between two campsites that are 27 cm apart on the map.
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{4.5}{18} = \frac{27}{x}\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{18 \cdot 27}{4.5} = 108\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A state map has a scale of 3.5 cm to 175 km. Find the actual distance between two towns that are 14 cm apart on the map.
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{3.5}{175} = \frac{14}{x}\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{175 \cdot 14}{3.5} = 700\text{ km}\).

qs.q: An architectural blueprint has a scale of 1.5 cm to 40 m. Find the actual length of a building wall that measures 13.5 cm on the blueprint.
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1.5}{40} = \frac{13.5}{x}\). Cross-multiply and solve to get \(x = \frac{40 \cdot 13.5}{1.5} = 360\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A scale model of a bridge uses a scale of 2.4 cm to 75 m. Find the actual length of a bridge section that measures 16.8 cm on the model.
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{2.4}{75} = \frac{16.8}{x}\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{75 \cdot 16.8}{2.4} = 525\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A park map has a scale of 1.8 cm to 25 km. Find the actual distance between two ranger stations that are 12.6 cm apart on the map.
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{1.8}{25} = \frac{12.6}{x}\). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{25 \cdot 12.6}{1.8} = 175\text{ km}\).

qs.q: On a state map with a scale of 2.4 cm to 36 km, Route 1 measures 17.6 cm and Route 2 measures 23.2 cm. How many kilometers longer is Route 2 than Route 1 in actual distance?
qs.s: The difference on the map is \(23.2 - 17.6 = 5.6\text{ cm}\). Set up the proportion \(\frac{2.4}{36} = \frac{5.6}{x}\) to find the actual difference: \(x = \frac{36 \cdot 5.6}{2.4} = 84\text{ km}\).

qs.q: On a regional map with a scale of 1.6 cm to 40 km, the total driving distance between two cities measures 18.4 cm. A driver has already traveled 235 km along this route. How many actual kilometers remain to be driven?
qs.s: Find the total actual distance using \(\frac{1.6}{40} = \frac{18.4}{x}\), which gives \(x = \frac{40 \cdot 18.4}{1.6} = 460\text{ km}\). Subtract the completed distance to find the remaining distance: \(460 - 235 = 225\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A triangular nature reserve is represented on a map with a scale of 3.5 cm to 14 km. The three boundary sides on the map measure 8.5 cm, 11.0 cm, and 14.5 cm. What is the actual perimeter of the reserve, in kilometers?
qs.s: Add the map side lengths to get a total map perimeter of \(8.5 + 11.0 + 14.5 = 34\text{ cm}\). Using the proportion \(\frac{3.5}{14} = \frac{34}{P}\), the actual perimeter is \(P = \frac{14 \cdot 34}{3.5} = 136\text{ km}\).

qs.q: On a map with a scale of 1.5 cm to 45 km, the distance between two towns is 8.5 cm. If a vehicle uses 1 L of fuel for every 15 km traveled, how many liters of fuel are needed to drive between the two towns?
qs.s: First find the actual distance using \(\frac{1.5}{45} = \frac{8.5}{d}\), which gives \(d = \frac{45 \cdot 8.5}{1.5} = 255\text{ km}\). Then use the proportion \(\frac{1}{15} = \frac{f}{255}\) to find the fuel needed: \(f = \frac{255}{15} = 17\text{ L}\).

qs.q: Two cities are 15 cm apart on Map A, which has a scale of 2.5 cm to 75 km. What is the distance between these two cities on Map B, which has a scale of 4 cm to 90 km?
qs.s: First find the actual distance using \(\frac{2.5}{75} = \frac{15}{x}\), giving \(x = 450\text{ km}\). Then find the distance on Map B using \(\frac{4}{90} = \frac{d}{450}\), which yields \(d = \frac{4 \cdot 450}{90} = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The ratio of copper to tin in a bronze alloy is 9 to 2. If a statue made from this alloy weighs 143 kg, how many kilograms of copper does it contain?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{9}{11} = \frac{x}{143}\), where 11 is the total number of parts (\(9 + 2\)). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{9 \cdot 143}{11} = 117\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A fruit punch recipe mixes orange juice and cranberry juice in the ratio of 5 to 2. If a punch bowl contains 168 mL of the mixture, how many milliliters of orange juice are in the bowl?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{5}{7} = \frac{x}{168}\), where 7 is the total number of parts (\(5 + 2\)). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{5 \cdot 168}{7} = 120\text{ mL}\).

qs.q: A fertilizer blend contains nitrogen and potassium in the ratio of 4 to 5. If a bag contains 225 g of the blend, how many grams of nitrogen does it contain?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{4}{9} = \frac{x}{225}\), where 9 is the total number of parts (\(4 + 5\)). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{4 \cdot 225}{9} = 100\text{ g}\).

qs.q: A concrete mixture consists of gravel and sand in the ratio of 5 to 3. If a contractor prepares 216 kg of this mixture, how many kilograms of sand are needed?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{3}{8} = \frac{x}{216}\), where 8 is the total number of parts (\(5 + 3\)). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{3 \cdot 216}{8} = 81\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: In a school theater production, the ratio of adult tickets to student tickets sold was 3 to 8. If a total of 209 tickets were sold, how many student tickets were sold?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{8}{11} = \frac{x}{209}\), where 11 is the total number of parts (\(3 + 8\)). Solving for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{8 \cdot 209}{11} = 152\).

qs.q: A chemist prepares 31.2 g of a compound composed of two elements in a ratio of 9 to 7. How many grams of the first element are in the compound?
qs.s: The total number of parts is \(9 + 7 = 16\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{9}{16} = \frac{x}{31.2}\) gives \(x = \frac{9 \cdot 31.2}{16} = 17.55\text{ g}\).

qs.q: A commercial bakery blends whole wheat flour, spelt flour, and white flour in the ratio of 4 to 3 to 7. If a batch of the blend weighs 1,750 kg, how many more kilograms of white flour than spelt flour are in the batch?
qs.s: The total number of parts is \(4 + 3 + 7 = 14\), so each part represents \(\frac{1,750}{14} = 125\text{ kg}\). The difference between white flour and spelt flour is \(7 - 3 = 4\) parts, which equals \(4 \cdot 125 = 500\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: A pharmaceutical tablet contains three active ingredients, A, B, and C, in the ratio of 11 to 9 to 4. If the total mass of the active ingredients in the tablet is 2,016 mg, what is the difference in mass between ingredient A and ingredient C?
qs.s: The total number of parts is \(11 + 9 + 4 = 24\), giving \(\frac{2,016}{24} = 84\text{ mg}\) per part. The difference between ingredient A and ingredient C is \(11 - 4 = 7\) parts, which is \(7 \cdot 84 = 588\text{ mg}\).

qs.q: A multivitamin tablet contains calcium, magnesium, and zinc in the ratio of 5 to 6 to 8. If the total mass of these three minerals in a batch of tablets is 456 mg, how many milligrams of magnesium are in the batch?
qs.s: The total number of parts is \(5 + 6 + 8 = 19\). Setting up the proportion \(\frac{6}{19} = \frac{x}{456}\) gives \(x = \frac{6 \cdot 456}{19} = 144\text{ mg}\).

qs.q: The ratio of two chemicals in an industrial cleaning solution is 13 to 8. A large container holds 567 L of this cleaning solution. How many more liters of the first chemical are there than the second chemical?
qs.s: The total number of parts is \(13 + 8 = 21\), so each part represents \(\frac{567}{21} = 27\text{ L}\). The difference between the two chemicals is \(13 - 8 = 5\) parts, so there are \(5 \cdot 27 = 135\text{ L}\) more of the first chemical.

qs.q: Wildlife researchers tagged and released 120 deer in a national park. In a later sample, 15 of 250 deer had tags. About how many deer are in the park?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{15}{250} = \frac{120}{N}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(15N = 120 \cdot 250 = 30000\), which simplifies to \(N = 2000\) deer.

qs.q: Forest rangers banded and released 85 hawks. Months later, a sample of 120 hawks showed that 5 had bands. About how many hawks are in the forest?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{5}{120} = \frac{85}{N}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(5N = 85 \cdot 120 = 10200\), so \(N = 2040\) hawks.

qs.q: Marine biologists tagged and released 140 sea turtles off an island. Later, a survey of 300 sea turtles found that 12 were tagged. What is the estimated total population of sea turtles around the island?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{12}{300} = \frac{140}{N}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(12N = 140 \cdot 300 = 42000\), which gives \(N = 3500\) sea turtles.

qs.q: Park researchers tagged and released 150 frogs in a wetland. Later, they captured 360 frogs and found that 9 of them had tags. About how many frogs are in the wetland?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{9}{360} = \frac{150}{N}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(9N = 150 \cdot 360 = 54000\), so \(N = 6000\) frogs.

qs.q: Ecologists tagged and released 240 birds in a nature reserve. In a later observation of 520 birds, 16 were found to have tags. About how many birds are in the nature reserve?
qs.s: Set up the proportion \(\frac{16}{520} = \frac{240}{N}\). Cross-multiplying gives \(16N = 240 \cdot 520 = 124800\), so \(N = 7800\) birds.

qs.q: In a conservation project, researchers tagged and released 280 penguins on an island. In a follow-up survey, they observed 14 tagged penguins and 406 untagged penguins. About how many penguins are in the total island population?
qs.s: The total number of penguins in the sample is \(14 + 406 = 420\). Set up the proportion \(\frac{14}{420} = \frac{280}{N}\), which gives \(14N = 117600\), so \(N = 8400\) penguins.

qs.q: Marine researchers tagged and released 540 cod in a fishing zone. A month later, a commercial trawler caught 1500 cod, of which 18 were tagged. If the government allows a maximum seasonal catch of 15% of the total estimated cod population, what is the maximum number of cod that can be caught?
qs.s: First find the total population \(N\) from \(\frac{18}{1500} = \frac{540}{N}\), giving \(18N = 810000\), so \(N = 45000\) cod. The allowable catch is \(15\%\) of this total: \(0.15 \times 45000 = 6750\) cod.

qs.q: Biologists tagged and released 250 salmon in a river system. Later, a sample of 600 salmon was collected, and 15 were found to have tags. Based on this proportion, about how many untagged salmon are in the river system?
qs.s: First, find the total population \(N\) using \(\frac{15}{600} = \frac{250}{N}\), which gives \(15N = 150000\), so \(N = 10000\). Then, subtract the 250 tagged salmon to find that there are \(10000 - 250 = 9750\) untagged salmon.

qs.q: Wildlife officers tagged and released 360 elk in a mountain reserve. Later in the season, two separate groups of elk were surveyed: the first group of 380 elk had 6 tagged, and the second group of 420 elk had 10 tagged. Using the combined data from both surveys, about how many elk are in the reserve?
qs.s: The combined survey has \(6 + 10 = 16\) tagged elk out of \(380 + 420 = 800\) total elk sampled. Set up the proportion \(\frac{16}{800} = \frac{360}{N}\), which cross-multiplies to \(16N = 288000\), giving \(N = 18000\) elk.

qs.q: A wildlife biologist tagged and released 210 foxes in a territory. The following year, the total fox population increased by 400. In a new sample of 360 foxes, 12 were found to have tags from the original tagging. Assuming all original tags remained, how many foxes were in the original population?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the original population, making the new population \(x + 400\). Set up the proportion \(\frac{12}{360} = \frac{210}{x + 400}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{1}{30} = \frac{210}{x + 400}\), so \(x + 400 = 6300\) and \(x = 5900\) foxes.

qs.q: Write as a mixed number. Simplify. 175%

qs.s: \(16\frac{2}{3}\% = \frac{50}{3}\% = \frac{50}{3} \times \frac{1}{100} = \frac{50}{300}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.s: \(12\frac{1}{2}\% = \frac{25}{2}\% = \frac{25}{200}\). Dividing the numerator and denominator by 25 gives \(\frac{1}{8}\).

qs.q: Write as a fraction. Simplify. \(\frac{3}{4}\%\)

qs.q: Write as a fraction. Simplify. \(37\frac{1}{2}\%\)

qs.s: Divide 9 by 100 to get \(\frac{9}{100}\). Since 9 and 100 share no common factors other than 1, the fraction is in simplest form.

qs.q: Write as a fraction in simplest form. \(6\frac{1}{4}\%\)

qs.q: Write as a mixed number in simplest form. 260%

qs.q: Write as a mixed number in simplest form. 175%

qs.q: Write as a fraction in simplest form. \(8\frac{1}{3}\%\)

qs.q: Write as a fraction in simplest form. \(12\frac{1}{2}\%\)

qs.q: Write as a fraction in simplest form: 220%
qs.s: Write 220% as \(\frac{220}{100}\). Divide both the numerator and denominator by 20 to get \(\frac{11}{5}\).
