qs.q: A catering service charges a fixed delivery fee of $35, plus $12 per boxed lunch and $3 per beverage. A school club spends their entire budget of $395 on an order. Let \(L\) be the number of boxed lunches and \(b\) be the number of beverages. Write an equation in the form \(Ax + By = C\) that models this situation.
qs.s: The total cost is modeled by \(12L + 3b + 35 = 395\). Subtracting the $35 delivery fee from both sides results in \(12L + 3b = 360\).

qs.q: An art teacher has a budget of $240 to buy supplies for a project. Canvas boards cost $6 each, paint tubes cost $4 each, and brush sets cost $9 each. Let \(c\) be the number of canvas boards, \(p\) be the number of paint tubes, and \(b\) be the number of brush sets. Write an equation that models the total cost if the teacher spends the entire budget.
qs.s: The cost of the three items combined is \(6c + 4p + 9b\). Setting this equal to the $240 budget yields the linear equation \(6c + 4p + 9b = 240\).

qs.q: A sports team is ordering custom jerseys at $22.50 each and custom shorts at $15.00 each. The printing company gives a flat $50 discount on the total order. The team spends exactly $850 after the discount. Let \(j\) be the number of jerseys and \(s\) be the number of shorts. Write an equation in the form \(Ax + By = C\) that models this situation.
qs.s: The cost before the discount is \(22.5j + 15s\), so with the discount the equation is \(22.5j + 15s - 50 = 850\). Adding 50 to both sides gives \(22.5j + 15s = 900\).

qs.q: A coffee shop orders dark roast coffee beans for $8.50 per pound and green tea leaves for $12.75 per pound. The manager has a total budget of $510 for this order. Let \(c\) be the pounds of coffee beans and \(t\) be the pounds of tea leaves. Write an equation that models this situation if the entire budget is spent.
qs.s: Multiply each quantity by its unit price to get the total cost \(8.50c + 12.75t\), then set it equal to the total budget of $510 to get \(8.50c + 12.75t = 510\).

qs.q: A recreation center is buying bottles of water at $1.00 each and boxes of popcorn at $4.00 each for a movie night. The center has a budget of $100. When graphing this linear model with the number of bottles of water on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and boxes of popcorn on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The linear relation is \(x + 4y = 100\). Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(4y = 100\), so the \(y\)-intercept is \(y = 25\).

qs.q: A community garden is purchasing seed packets at $1.00 each and small pots at $3.00 each. The garden has a budget of $45. When graphing this linear relationship with seed packets on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and small pots on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The linear relation is \(x + 3y = 45\). Setting \(x = 0\) yields \(3y = 45\), which gives \(y = 15\).

qs.q: A volunteer group is ordering snacks: juice boxes cost $1.00 each and fruit cups cost $2.00 each. The group has a total of $80 to spend. When graphing this relationship with juice boxes on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and fruit cups on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The linear equation representing the budget is \(x + 2y = 80\). Setting \(x = 0\) yields \(2y = 80\), so the \(y\)-intercept is \(y = 40\).

qs.q: A school club is buying pens at $1.00 each and notebooks at $3.00 each. The club has a total budget of $60. When graphing this linear model with the number of pens on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and the number of notebooks on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The linear relation is \(x + 3y = 60\). To find the \(y\)-intercept, set \(x = 0\) to get \(3y = 60\), which gives \(y = 20\).

qs.q: A dance team is purchasing wristbands at $1.00 each and t-shirts at $5.00 each with a budget of $120. When graphing this linear model with wristbands on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and t-shirts on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The budget is modeled by \(x + 5y = 120\). Setting \(x = 0\) results in \(5y = 120\), giving a \(y\)-intercept of \(y = 24\).

qs.q: A theater company buys hats at $6 each and capes at $10 each for costumes, plus a flat shipping fee of $30. The company has a budget of $480. When graphing this linear model with the number of hats on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and capes on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The budget is modeled by \(6x + 10y + 30 = 480\), so \(6x + 10y = 450\). Setting \(x = 0\) results in \(10y = 450\), which gives \(y = 45\).

qs.q: A science department orders safety goggles at $5 each and lab coats at $8 each, plus a hazardous materials shipping fee of $40. The department has a budget of $440. When graphing this linear model with safety goggles on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and lab coats on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The linear model is \(5x + 8y + 40 = 440\), which simplifies to \(5x + 8y = 400\). Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(8y = 400\), so \(y = 50\).

qs.q: A school band orders customized hoodies at $15 each and jackets at $25 each, plus a one-time artwork setup fee of $50. The band has a budget of $800. When graphing this linear model with the number of hoodies on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and jackets on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The linear relation is \(15x + 25y + 50 = 800\), which simplifies to \(15x + 25y = 750\). Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(25y = 750\), so \(y = 30\).

qs.q: A community center orders sandwiches at $4.00 each and hot meals at $6.00 each, plus a flat delivery fee of $20.00. The center has a total budget of $260. When graphing this linear model with the number of sandwiches on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and the number of hot meals on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The equation representing the total cost is \(4x + 6y + 20 = 260\), which simplifies to \(4x + 6y = 240\). Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(6y = 240\), so \(y = 40\).

qs.q: A sports league purchases soccer balls at $16 each and warm-up jackets at $20 each, plus an order processing fee of $80. The league has a total budget of $1280. When graphing this linear model with soccer balls on the horizontal axis (\(x\)) and warm-up jackets on the vertical axis (\(y\)), what is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph?
qs.s: The total cost is modeled by \(16x + 20y + 80 = 1280\), which simplifies to \(16x + 20y = 1200\). Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(20y = 1200\), so \(y = 60\).

qs.q: A youth group spends $90 on movie tickets. Child tickets cost $5 each and adult tickets cost $10 each. If they buy 4 adult tickets, how many child tickets do they buy?
qs.s: Let \(c\) be the number of child tickets. The equation is \(5c + 10(4) = 90\), which simplifies to \(5c + 40 = 90\). Subtracting 40 gives \(5c = 50\), so \(c = 10\) child tickets.

qs.q: A community centre spends $80 on sports equipment, purchasing cones for $2 each and balls for $5 each. If they buy 8 balls, how many cones do they buy?
qs.s: Let \(c\) be the number of cones. The equation is \(2c + 5(8) = 80\), which gives \(2c + 40 = 80\). Subtracting 40 gives \(2c = 40\), so \(c = 20\) cones.

qs.q: A snack bar sells juice boxes for $2 each and sandwiches for $4 each. A customer spends $36 in total. If the customer buys 5 sandwiches, how many juice boxes do they buy?
qs.s: Let \(j\) be the number of juice boxes. The equation is \(2j + 4(5) = 36\), which gives \(2j + 20 = 36\). Subtracting 20 gives \(2j = 16\), so \(j = 8\) juice boxes.

qs.q: A teacher buys notebooks at $3 each and pens at $1 each for a classroom, spending exactly $60. If she buys 12 notebooks, how many pens does she buy?
qs.s: Let \(p\) be the number of pens. The equation is \(3(12) + 1p = 60\), which simplifies to \(36 + p = 60\). Subtracting 36 gives \(p = 24\) pens.

qs.q: Marcus spends $45 on fruit. Bags of apples cost $4 each and bags of oranges cost $3 each. If he buys 7 bags of oranges, how many bags of apples does he buy?
qs.s: Let \(a\) be the number of bags of apples. The equation is \(4a + 3(7) = 45\), which gives \(4a + 21 = 45\). Subtracting 21 gives \(4a = 24\), so \(a = 6\) bags of apples.

qs.q: A delivery truck was purchased new for $54 000 and depreciates linearly at a constant rate of $4500 per year. If the current value of the truck is $18 000, how many years old is the truck?
qs.s: The depreciation model is \(18 000 = 54 000 - 4500t\). Rearranging gives \(4500t = 36 000\), so \(t = 8\) years.

qs.q: A boutique clothing store pays $1600 in monthly rent. The store makes a profit of $40 on each jacket sold and $20 on each sweater sold. In November, they sold 50 sweaters and made a net profit of $2600 after paying rent. How many jackets did they sell?
qs.s: The net profit equation is \(2600 = 40j + 20(50) - 1600\), which simplifies to \(2600 = 40j - 600\). Adding 600 gives \(40j = 3200\), so \(j = 80\) jackets.

qs.q: A landscaping company charges a flat equipment rental fee of $120, plus $40 per hour for a lead landscaper and $20 per hour for an assistant. On a job where the lead landscaper worked for 10 hours, the total bill was $820. How many hours did the assistant work?
qs.s: Let \(h\) be the assistant's hours. The equation is \(120 + 40(10) + 20h = 820\), which simplifies to \(520 + 20h = 820\). Subtracting 520 gives \(20h = 300\), so \(h = 15\) hours.

qs.q: A catering order has a $36 delivery fee, plus boxed lunches at $12 each and fruit cups at $3 each. The total bill is $420. If 40 fruit cups are ordered, how many boxed lunches are ordered?
qs.s: Let \(L\) be the number of boxed lunches. The equation is \(36 + 12L + 3(40) = 420\), which simplifies to \(12L + 156 = 420\). Subtracting 156 gives \(12L = 264\), so \(L = 22\) boxed lunches.

qs.q: A community theater sells adult tickets for $7.50 each and student tickets for $4.50 each. For opening night, total ticket sales were $990. If 60 adult tickets were sold, how many student tickets were sold?
qs.s: Let \(s\) be the number of student tickets. The equation is \(7.50(60) + 4.50s = 990\), which simplifies to \(450 + 4.50s = 990\). Subtracting 450 gives \(4.50s = 540\), so \(s = 120\) student tickets.

qs.q: Liam is ordering muffins at $2 each and loaves of banana bread at $4 each for a charity breakfast. He has $60 to spend. If he orders 14 muffins, how many loaves of banana bread does he order?
qs.s: The cost is modeled by \(2(14) + 4b = 60\), which simplifies to \(28 + 4b = 60\). Subtracting 28 gives \(4b = 32\), so \(b = 8\) loaves.

qs.q: Elena is buying granola bars at $1 each and fruit smoothies at $3 each for her track team. She has $45 to spend. If she buys 15 granola bars, how many smoothies does she buy?
qs.s: The total cost is \(1(15) + 3s = 45\), which gives \(15 + 3s = 45\). Subtracting 15 yields \(3s = 30\), so \(s = 10\) smoothies.

qs.q: A teacher is buying student folders at $4 each and calculators at $9 each for a classroom. She has $55 to spend. If she buys 3 calculators, how many folders does she buy?
qs.s: The cost equation is \(4f + 9(3) = 55\), which simplifies to \(4f + 27 = 55\). Subtracting 27 gives \(4f = 28\), so \(f = 7\) folders.

qs.q: A craft club is buying stickers at $2 each and enamel pins at $5 each. The club has $65 to spend. If they buy 7 enamel pins, how many stickers do they buy?
qs.s: The equation is \(2s + 5(7) = 65\), which simplifies to \(2s + 35 = 65\). Subtracting 35 gives \(2s = 30\), so \(s = 15\) stickers.

qs.q: Marcus is buying notebooks at $3 each and pens at $2 each for his study group. He has $30 to spend. If he buys 4 notebooks, how many pens does he buy?
qs.s: The total cost is modeled by \(3(4) + 2p = 30\), which simplifies to \(12 + 2p = 30\). Subtracting 12 gives \(2p = 18\), so \(p = 9\) pens.

qs.q: A landscaping service charges a flat fee of $75 for equipment transport, plus $45 per hour of labor and $15 per cubic yard of mulch. On a recent job, the total charge was $600, and the crew worked for 8 hours. How many cubic yards of mulch were delivered?
qs.s: The equation for total cost is \(75 + 45(8) + 15m = 600\), which simplifies to \(435 + 15m = 600\). Subtracting 435 gives \(15m = 165\), so \(m = 11\) cubic yards.

qs.q: A community center sells adult tickets for $7.50 each and student tickets for $4.50 each for a play. The center collected a total of $915 in ticket sales. If 80 adult tickets were sold, how many student tickets were sold?
qs.s: The total sales equation is \(7.50(80) + 4.50s = 915\), which simplifies to \(600 + 4.50s = 915\). Subtracting 600 gives \(4.50s = 315\), so \(s = 70\) student tickets.

qs.q: An office manager has a budget of $1,260 to purchase ergonomic chairs at $140 each and desk lamps at $35 each. The supplier applies a $70 discount coupon to the entire order. If she purchases 7 chairs, how many desk lamps does she buy?
qs.s: The total cost equation is \(140(7) + 35L - 70 = 1260\), which simplifies to \(910 + 35L = 1260\). Subtracting 910 gives \(35L = 350\), so \(L = 10\) desk lamps.

qs.q: A community theater pays $1,800 in production expenses per show. They sell floor tickets for $25 each and balcony tickets for $15 each. For opening night, their net profit was $2,700. If they sold 120 floor tickets, how many balcony tickets did they sell?
qs.s: Profit is given by \(25(120) + 15b - 1800 = 2700\), which simplifies to \(1200 + 15b = 2700\). Subtracting 1200 gives \(15b = 1500\), so \(b = 100\) balcony tickets.

qs.q: A sports team orders custom shirts and water bottles. The printing company charges a flat design fee of $20, plus $6 per shirt and $4 per water bottle. The team has a budget of $330. If they order 35 shirts, how many water bottles do they order?
qs.s: The linear model is \(20 + 6(35) + 4w = 330\), which simplifies to \(230 + 4w = 330\). Subtracting 230 gives \(4w = 100\), so \(w = 25\) water bottles.

qs.q: An art club pays $180 to rent space for an exhibition. The club sells handmade pottery mugs for $15 each. Write an equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of mugs sold, \(m\).
qs.s: The total revenue for \(m\) mugs is \(15m\), and subtracting the fixed space rental fee of \(180\) gives \(P = 15m - 180\).

qs.q: A sports team pays a $500 entry fee to enter a tournament. To raise funds, they sell raffle tickets for $4 each. Write an equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of raffle tickets sold, \(r\).
qs.s: Revenue from selling \(r\) tickets is \(4r\), and subtracting the \(500\) entry fee gives the profit equation \(P = 4r - 500\).

qs.q: A student council rents a photo booth for a school carnival for a flat fee of $250. They charge $5 per photo session. Write an equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of photo sessions, \(s\).
qs.s: The revenue from \(s\) photo sessions is \(5s\) and the fixed cost is \(250\), so subtracting cost from revenue gives \(P = 5s - 250\).

qs.q: A magician charges a flat fee of $320 to perform at a community center. Up to 80 tickets can be sold for $12 each. Write an equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of tickets sold, \(t\).
qs.s: Selling \(t\) tickets generates \(12t\) in revenue, and subtracting the fixed performance fee of \(320\) yields \(P = 12t - 320\).

qs.q: A drama club rents an auditorium for $450 for an evening. Two hundred tickets are available for $8 each. Write an equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of tickets sold, \(n\).
qs.s: Profit is revenue minus cost. Since revenue is \(8n\) and the fixed cost is \(450\), the equation is \(P = 8n - 450\).

qs.q: A charity organizes a 5K race. Fixed costs are $3200 for permits and timing equipment, and $800 for advertising. Each runner receives a race pack costing $9, and registration is $35 per runner. Write a simplified equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of runners registered, \(r\).
qs.s: Fixed costs total \(3200 + 800 = 4000\), and the net profit per runner is \(35 - 9 = 26\). This results in the equation \(P = 26r - 4000\).

qs.q: A food truck owner pays a daily parking permit fee of $120 and insurance of $30 per day. Each gourmet burger costs $4.50 in ingredients and sells for $12.50. Write a simplified equation relating the daily profit, \(P\), to the number of burgers sold, \(b\).
qs.s: Total fixed expenses are \(120 + 30 = 150\), and the net profit per burger is \(12.50 - 4.50 = 8\). Thus, the profit equation is \(P = 8b - 150\).

qs.q: A community theater group produces a play. The script rights cost $1400 and scenery materials cost $850. Tickets are sold for $25 each, but the group must pay $3 per ticket in processing fees. Write a simplified equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of tickets sold, \(t\).
qs.s: Total fixed costs are \(1400 + 850 = 2250\), and net revenue per ticket is \(25 - 3 = 22\). This gives the simplified profit equation \(P = 22t - 2250\).

qs.q: A committee organizes a graduation banquet. The hall rental fee is $1800 and the DJ costs $600. The caterer charges $28 per meal, and tickets are sold for $50 each. Write a simplified equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of tickets sold, \(n\).
qs.s: Total fixed costs are \(1800 + 600 = 2400\), and the net gain per ticket is \(50 - 28 = 22\). Therefore, the simplified profit equation is \(P = 22n - 2400\).

qs.q: A school club sells custom hoodies for $45 each. It costs a one-time screen setup fee of $280, plus $17 to manufacture each hoodie. Write a simplified equation relating profit, \(P\), to the number of hoodies sold, \(h\).
qs.s: Profit equals total revenue minus total cost: \(P = 45h - (17h + 280)\). Simplifying like terms gives \(P = 28h - 280\).

qs.q: A theater company charges $800 to put on a school play. Up to 150 tickets can be sold for $16 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: The profit equation is \(P = 16n - 800\). Setting \(P = 0\) gives \(16n = 800\), which solves to \(n = 50\) tickets.

qs.q: A DJ charges $450 for a graduation party. Up to 120 tickets can be sold for $15 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: The profit equation is \(P = 15n - 450\). Setting \(P = 0\) gives \(15n = 450\), which solves to \(n = 30\) tickets.

qs.q: A guest speaker charges $560 for a workshop. Up to 120 tickets can be sold for $8 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: The profit equation is \(P = 8n - 560\). Setting \(P = 0\) gives \(8n = 560\), which solves to \(n = 70\) tickets.

qs.q: A comedian charges $700 for a community performance. Up to 90 tickets can be sold for $20 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: The profit equation is \(P = 20n - 700\). Setting \(P = 0\) gives \(20n = 700\), which solves to \(n = 35\) tickets.

qs.q: An entertainer charges $480 for a charity show. Up to 100 tickets can be sold for $12 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: The profit equation is \(P = 12n - 480\). Setting \(P = 0\) gives \(12n = 480\), which solves to \(n = 40\) tickets.

qs.q: A tour organizer charters a bus for a flat fee of $1500, with additional costs of $20 for park admission and $15 for lunch per passenger. Up to 80 tickets can be sold for $60 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: Total cost per passenger is $20 + 15 = $35, giving the profit equation \(P = (60 - 35)n - 1500 = 25n - 1500\). Setting \(P = 0\) yields \(25n = 1500\), so \(n = 60\) tickets.

qs.q: A music festival has fixed expenses of $1800 for stage rental and $600 for the sound crew, plus $8 per attendee for security and cleanup. Up to 200 tickets can be sold for $40 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $1800 + 600 = $2400, giving the profit equation \(P = (40 - 8)n - 2400 = 32n - 2400\). Setting \(P = 0\) yields \(32n = 2400\), so \(n = 75\) tickets.

qs.q: A committee organizes a banquet where the hall rental is a fixed fee of $1350, and each meal costs $18 per attendee. Up to 90 tickets can be sold for $45 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: The profit equation is \(P = 45n - (18n + 1350) = 27n - 1350\). Setting \(P = 0\) yields \(27n = 1350\), so \(n = 50\) tickets.

qs.q: A charity hosts a 5K race where the permit and timing service cost a flat fee of $1600, plus $12 per runner for medals and shirts. Up to 150 runners can register at $32 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of registered runners, \(n\), how many runners are needed to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: The profit equation is \(P = 32n - (12n + 1600) = 20n - 1600\). Setting \(P = 0\) yields \(20n = 1600\), so \(n = 80\) runners.

qs.q: A drama club hosts a dinner theatre with fixed costs of $900 for licensing and $500 for costumes and props, plus $15 per guest for catering. Up to 100 tickets are available for $50 each. When graphing profit, \(P\), against the number of tickets sold, \(n\), how many tickets must be sold to break even (where profit is $0)?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $900 + 500 = $1400, giving the profit equation \(P = (50 - 15)n - 1400 = 35n - 1400\). Setting \(P = 0\) yields \(35n = 1400\), so \(n = 40\) tickets.

qs.q: A DJ charges $480 to play music for a charity banquet. A total of 100 tickets are available for $8 each. How many tickets must be sold to cover the cost of the DJ?
qs.s: Set up the equation 8n = 480, where n is the number of tickets sold. Dividing both sides by 8 gives n = 60 tickets.

qs.q: A guest speaker charges $840 for an evening seminar. There are 120 tickets available for $12 each. How many tickets must be sold to pay the speaker's fee?
qs.s: Set up the equation 12n = 840, where n represents tickets sold. Dividing both sides by 12 gives n = 70 tickets.

qs.q: A magician charges $360 for an elementary school assembly. There are 120 tickets available for $4 each. How many tickets must be sold to pay for the magician?
qs.s: Set up the equation 4n = 360, where n is the number of tickets sold. Dividing both sides by 4 gives n = 90 tickets.

qs.q: A community center hires a comedian for a comedy night for $560. There are 100 tickets available for $7 each. How many tickets must be sold to pay for the comedian?
qs.s: Set up the equation 7n = 560, where n is the number of tickets. Dividing both sides by 7 gives n = 80 tickets.

qs.q: A drama club rents a local theater for $450 to stage a one-act play. A maximum of 80 tickets can be sold at $9 each. How many tickets must be sold to pay for the theater rental?
qs.s: Set up the equation 9n = 450, where n is the number of tickets. Dividing both sides by 9 gives n = 50 tickets.

qs.q: The student council is hosting a banquet. The caterer charges a flat fee of $1250 and the hall rental is $550. Tickets are sold for $25 each. How many tickets must be sold to cover both expenses?
qs.s: The total expense is $1250 + $550 = $1800. Solving the equation 25n = 1800 gives n = 72 tickets.

qs.q: A pottery studio rents a booth at an artisan market for $900 for the weekend. The studio makes a profit of $50 on each vase sold. How many vases must be sold to pay for the booth rental and earn an additional profit of $600?
qs.s: Using the profit model P = 50n - 900 with target profit P = 600, solve 50n - 900 = 600 to get 50n = 1500, so n = 30 vases.

qs.q: A school club is selling customized hoodies to pay for a $600 equipment setup fee. Each hoodie sells for $25 and costs the club $15 to manufacture. How many hoodies must the club sell to cover the setup fee?
qs.s: The profit per hoodie is $25 - $15 = $10. Solving 10n = 600 gives n = 60 hoodies.

qs.q: A catering company charges a flat delivery and setup fee of $100, plus $50 per hour of service. If a client was billed a total of $450, for how many hours of service was the client charged?
qs.s: Set up the linear model 50h + 100 = 450, which simplifies to 50h = 350, giving h = 7 hours.

qs.q: A community theatre production has fixed costs of $1400 for sets and costumes, and $850 for auditorium rental. Tickets are sold for $18 each. If a local sponsor donates $450 toward the costs, how many tickets must be sold to cover the remaining expenses?
qs.s: The remaining expenses are $1400 + $850 - $450 = $1800. Solving 18n = 1800 gives n = 100 tickets.

qs.q: A DJ for a school banquet charges $450 for the evening. Eighty tickets are available and sold for $12 each. What is the profit from ticket sales after paying the DJ?
qs.s: Total revenue from 80 tickets at $12 each is \(80 \times 12 = \$960\). Subtracting the $450 DJ fee gives a profit of \(960 - 450 = \$510\).

qs.q: An art studio hires a guest instructor for a weekend workshop for a flat fee of $400. Twenty-five spots are available at $24 each. What is the studio's profit if the workshop is sold out?
qs.s: The studio collects \(25 \times 24 = \$600\) in registration fees. After paying the $400 instructor fee, the profit is \(600 - 400 = \$200\).

qs.q: A drama club rents an auditorium for $500 to stage a play. One hundred fifty tickets are available for $8 each. What is the profit if the play is sold out?
qs.s: Selling all 150 tickets at $8 each yields \(150 \times 8 = \$1200\). The profit after paying the $500 rental fee is \(1200 - 500 = \$700\).

qs.q: A student council hosts an outdoor movie night. The public screening license costs $350. Ninety tickets are available for $7 each. What is the profit if all tickets are sold?
qs.s: Total ticket revenue is \(90 \times 7 = \$630\). After paying the $350 license fee, the profit is \(630 - 350 = \$280\).

qs.q: A sports league rents a gymnasium for a tournament at a flat rate of $750. Twelve team slots are available for an entry fee of $90 each. What is the league's profit if all slots are filled?
qs.s: Revenue from 12 teams at $90 each is \(12 \times 90 = \$1080\). Subtracting the $750 rental cost gives a profit of \(1080 - 750 = \$330\).

qs.q: A school band records an album. The studio charges a flat setup fee of $1600 plus $3.25 per CD pressed. The band sells each CD for $12.00 and donates $1.75 from every sale to charity. What is the band's net profit if they sell 800 CDs?
qs.s: Total revenue is \(800 \times 12 = \$9600\), while total expenses and donations are \(1600 + 800 \times (3.25 + 1.75) = 1600 + 4000 = \$5600\). The band's net profit is \(9600 - 5600 = \$4000\).

qs.q: A charity organizes a 5K race. The permit and equipment rental cost a flat fee of $1850, and each runner receives a race kit costing $8. If 350 runners register and each pays an entry fee of $25, what is the charity's profit?
qs.s: Total revenue is \(350 \times 25 = \$8750\), and total costs are \(1850 + 350 \times 8 = \$4650\). The profit is \(8750 - 4650 = \$4100\).

qs.q: A committee rents a banquet hall for $1250 and pays a caterer $14 per person for dinner. If 180 guests attend and each buys a ticket for $30, what is the committee's net profit?
qs.s: Total revenue is \(180 \times 30 = \$5400\), and total expenses are \(1250 + 180 \times 14 = \$3770\). The net profit is \(5400 - 3770 = \$1630\).

qs.q: A community theater troupe pays $2200 to rent a venue and $650 for costume rentals. Each attendee buys an $18 ticket and a $4 souvenir program, which costs the troupe $1.50 to print. What is the troupe's profit if 400 people attend?
qs.s: Total revenue is \(400 \times (18 + 4) = \$8800\), and total costs are \(2200 + 650 + 400 \times 1.50 = \$3450\). The net profit is \(8800 - 3450 = \$5350\).

qs.q: A museum hosts an evening gala with a fixed facility cost of $1400. For each attendee, food costs $18.50 and table service costs $6.50. If 240 tickets are sold at $45 each, what is the net profit from the gala?
qs.s: Total expenses are \(1400 + 240 \times (18.50 + 6.50) = 1400 + 6000 = \$7400\). With total revenue of \(240 \times 45 = \$10800\), the net profit is \(10800 - 7400 = \$3400\).

qs.q: A DJ for a community youth dance charges $350 for the night. One hundred tickets are available for $12 each. What is the profit if 75 tickets are sold?
qs.s: The revenue from 75 tickets is 75($12) = $900. Subtracting the $350 DJ fee gives a profit of $900 - $350 = $550.

qs.q: A drama club pays $450 to rent an auditorium for a play. One hundred fifty tickets are available for $8 each. What is the profit if 120 tickets are sold?
qs.s: The revenue from selling 120 tickets is 120($8) = $960. Subtracting the fixed rental cost gives a profit of $960 - $450 = $510.

qs.q: An art club pays $180 to rent a booth at a weekend craft market. Sixty ceramic bowls are available for $14 each. What is the profit if 35 bowls are sold?
qs.s: The revenue from selling 35 bowls is 35($14) = $490. Subtracting the $180 booth rental gives a profit of $490 - $180 = $310.

qs.q: A student council pays a $250 licensing fee to show a movie in the gym. Two hundred tickets are available for $5 each. What is the profit if 160 tickets are sold?
qs.s: The revenue from 160 tickets is 160($5) = $800. Subtracting the $250 fee gives a profit of $800 - $250 = $550.

qs.q: A soccer team pays $80 for supplies to host a charity car wash. Space is available to wash up to 80 cars for $15 each. What is the profit if 45 cars are washed?
qs.s: The revenue from washing 45 cars is 45($15) = $675. Subtracting the $80 supply cost gives a profit of $675 - $80 = $595.

qs.q: A charity gala has a venue rental fee of $2500 and catering that costs $32 per guest. A sponsor donates $1000 towards the venue cost. The ballroom seats up to 200 guests, and tickets are sold for $75 each. What is the net profit for the charity if 140 guests attend?
qs.s: Total revenue is 140($75) + $1000 = $11 500, and total expenses are \(2500 + 140(\)32) = $6980. The net profit is $11 500 - $6980 = $4520.

qs.q: A graduation committee organizes a banquet. The venue charges an $1800 rental fee plus $26 per plate for dinner, and a DJ is hired for $500. Up to 200 tickets can be sold at $45 each. What is the committee's profit if 175 tickets are sold?
qs.s: Total revenue is 175($45) = $7875, and total expenses are $1800 + \(500 + 175(\)26) = $6850. The profit is $7875 - $6850 = $1025.

qs.q: A community sports club organizes a tournament. The club pays $1400 to rent the fields and $650 for referees. A maximum of 50 teams can register. Each team pays a $160 registration fee, and the club earns an estimated $45 in concession profit per team. What is the club's total profit if 36 teams participate?
qs.s: Total income is 36($160 + \(45) = 36(\)205) = $7380, and total fixed costs are $1400 + $650 = $2050. The profit is $7380 - $2050 = $5330.

qs.q: A student robotics club manufactures custom phone stands as a fundraiser. The club buys a 3D printer for $750, and materials cost $3.25 per stand. A maximum of 250 stands can be made. If the stands sell for $12 each, what is the club's profit if 180 stands are sold?
qs.s: Revenue from 180 stands is 180($12) = $2160, and total costs are \(750 + 180(\)3.25) = $1335. The profit is $2160 - $1335 = $825.

qs.q: A school band rents a concert hall for $1200. A total of 300 tickets are available at $15 each, but the band also incurs a refreshment cost of $4.50 per attendee. What is the band's profit if 240 tickets are sold?
qs.s: Total revenue is 240($15) = $3600, while total expenses are \(1200 + 240(\)4.50) = $2280. The profit is $3600 - $2280 = $1320.

qs.q: A charity hosts an outdoor movie night and pays $250 to rent the projector. Tickets cost $5 each. How many tickets were sold if the charity made a profit of $150?
qs.s: Let \(n\) be the number of tickets sold. Solving \(5n - 250 = 150\) gives \(5n = 400\), so \(n = 80\) tickets.

qs.q: A student council hires a DJ for the school formal for $480. Tickets are sold for $12 each. How many tickets were sold if the council made a profit of $120?
qs.s: Let \(n\) be the number of tickets sold. Solving \(12n - 480 = 120\) gives \(12n = 600\), so \(n = 50\) tickets.

qs.q: A comedy club rents a venue for $500 for an evening. Two hundred tickets are available for $10 each. How many tickets were sold if the club made a profit of $200?
qs.s: Let \(n\) be the number of tickets sold. Solving \(10n - 500 = 200\) gives \(10n = 700\), so \(n = 70\) tickets.

qs.q: A local band pays $500 to rent sound equipment for a concert. Tickets are sold for $20 each. How many tickets were sold if the band made a profit of $400?
qs.s: Let \(n\) be the number of tickets sold. Solving \(20n - 500 = 400\) gives \(20n = 900\), so \(n = 45\) tickets.

qs.q: An art club pays $360 to rent a gallery space for a weekend exhibit. One hundred tickets are available for $8 each. How many tickets were sold if the club earned a profit of $120?
qs.s: Let \(n\) be the number of tickets sold. Solving \(8n - 360 = 120\) gives \(8n = 480\), so \(n = 60\) tickets.

qs.q: A company purchases a delivery van for $42 000. Under linear depreciation, its value decreases by $3500 each year. After how many years will the value of the van be $14 000?
qs.s: Set up the linear depreciation model \(42000 - 3500t = 14000\). Subtracting 42000 gives \(-3500t = -28000\), so \(t = 8\) years.

qs.q: A school club organizes a banquet. They pay $600 to rent the hall and $400 for audio equipment. Dinner costs $5 per person to prepare, and tickets are sold for $25 each. How many tickets must be sold to earn a profit of $600?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are \(600 + 400 = \$1000\) and net profit per ticket is \(25 - 5 = \$20\). Solving \(20n - 1000 = 600\) gives \(20n = 1600\), so \(n = 80\) tickets.

qs.q: A reservoir initially contains 4500 L of water. Water is drained at a constant rate of 125 L/min. After how many minutes will the reservoir contain 1750 L of water?
qs.s: Set up the equation \(4500 - 125t = 1750\). Subtracting 4500 gives \(-125t = -2750\), so \(t = 22\) minutes.

qs.q: A plumber charges an $80 service call fee plus $40 per hour of labour. On a job that also required $120 for replacement parts, the total bill came to $480. How many hours of labour did the plumber bill?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are \(80 + 120 = \$200\). Solving \(40t + 200 = 480\) gives \(40t = 280\), so \(t = 7\) hours.

qs.q: A student council sells custom t-shirts. The setup cost for the design is $350. Each t-shirt costs $8 to produce and is sold for $15. How many t-shirts were sold if the council made a net profit of $280?
qs.s: The net profit per shirt is \(15 - 8 = \$7\). Solving \(7n - 350 = 280\) gives \(7n = 630\), so \(n = 90\) shirts.

qs.q: A school rents a charter bus for $750 for a field trip. Students are charged $15 each to ride the bus, and 60 seats are available. How many students paid to ride if the school lost $150 on the trip?
qs.s: The school collected $750 - $150 = $600 from student fares. Dividing by the cost per student gives $600 / 15 = 40 students.

qs.q: A DJ charges $500 to provide music for a charity dance. Entry bracelets are sold for $5 each, with 150 bracelets available. How many bracelets were sold if the organizers lost $150 on the dance?
qs.s: The organizers took in $500 - $150 = $350 from sales. Dividing by the price per bracelet gives $350 / 5 = 70 bracelets sold.

qs.q: A club rents a projection system for a movie night for $300. Tickets are sold for $5 each, and up to 100 people can attend. How many tickets were sold if the club lost $75 on the event?
qs.s: The club generated $300 - $75 = $225 from ticket sales. Dividing by the ticket price gives $225 / 5 = 45 tickets sold.

qs.q: A drama club rents a stage for $400 for an evening performance. Tickets are sold for $8 each, and 80 tickets are available. How many tickets were sold if the club lost $120 on the event?
qs.s: The club brought in $400 - $120 = $280 from ticket sales. Dividing this revenue by the price per ticket gives $280 / 8 = 35 tickets sold.

qs.q: A student council rents an ice-skating rink for $420 for an evening. Admission tickets are sold for $7 each, and up to 100 tickets are available. How many tickets were sold if the council lost $140 on the event?
qs.s: The council collected $420 - $140 = $280 in admission fees. Dividing by the ticket price gives $280 / 7 = 40 tickets sold.

qs.q: A club organizes a charity dinner. The venue charges a flat fee of $900, and the catered meal costs $15 per attendee. Tickets are sold for $30 each. How many tickets were sold if the club lost $300 on the dinner?
qs.s: The net profit is P = (30 - 15)n - 900 = 15n - 900. Since the club lost $300, 15n - 900 = -300 gives 15n = 600, so n = 40 tickets were sold.

qs.q: To produce a school musical, the drama department pays $1250 for performance rights, $750 for set materials, and $400 for costumes. Tickets are sold for $15 each. How many tickets were sold if the department lost $450 on the production?
qs.s: Total expenses were $1250 + $750 + $400 = $2400. With a loss of $450, total revenue was $2400 - $450 = $1950, so $1950 / 15 = 130 tickets were sold.

qs.q: A small business prints custom hoodies. The monthly shop rent is $2100, and each hoodie costs $20 in materials to produce. The hoodies sell for $50 each. How many hoodies were sold in a month where the business earned a net profit of $900?
qs.s: The net profit is modeled by P = (50 - 20)n - 2100 = 30n - 2100. Setting 30n - 2100 = 900 gives 30n = 3000, so n = 100 hoodies sold.

qs.q: A committee organizes a graduation banquet. The hall rental costs $1200, and catering costs $10 per person. Tickets are sold for $30 each. How many tickets were sold if the committee made a profit of $600?
qs.s: The profit model is P = (30 - 10)n - 1200 = 20n - 1200. Setting 20n - 1200 = 600 gives 20n = 1800, so n = 90 tickets sold.

qs.q: A concert promoter pays $3600 for venue rental, $1200 for the sound system, and $600 for security. In addition, each attendee receives a program that costs $5 to print. Tickets are sold for $25 each. How many tickets were sold if the promoter earned a profit of $1600?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $3600 + $1200 + $600 = $5400, and net revenue per ticket is $25 - $5 = $20. Setting 20n - 5400 = 1600 gives 20n = 7000, so n = 350 tickets sold.

qs.q: A theater club pays a $300 rental fee for an auditorium to perform a play. Up to 100 tickets can be sold for $8 each. What does the ordered pair (75, 300) represent?
qs.a: Selling 75 tickets results in a net profit of $300.
d: Selling 300 tickets results in a net profit of $75.
Selling 75 tickets brings in a total revenue of $300.

qs.s: Selling 75 tickets brings in \(75 \times 8 = \$600\) in revenue. Subtracting the $300 rental fee gives a net profit of \(600 - 300 = \$300\), so (75, 300) represents a net profit of $300 when 75 tickets are sold.

qs.q: A student club spends $250 on materials to make handmade tote bags. They sell the bags for $10 each at a craft fair. What does the ordered pair (45, 200) represent?
qs.a: Selling 45 tote bags results in a net profit of $200.

qs.s: Selling 45 bags brings in \(45 \times 10 = \$450\). Subtracting the $250 cost of materials gives a profit of \(450 - 250 = \$200\), so (45, 200) represents earning a $200 profit from selling 45 tote bags.

qs.q: A comedy club pays a performer a $450 flat fee for an evening show. Up to 80 tickets can be sold for $15 each. What does the ordered pair (50, 300) represent?
qs.a: Selling 50 tickets results in a net profit of $300.

qs.s: Selling 50 tickets generates \(50 \times 15 = \$750\) in ticket revenue. Deducting the $450 performer fee gives \(750 - 450 = \$300\), so (50, 300) represents a net profit of $300 when 50 tickets are sold.

qs.q: A community center pays $350 to rent an inflatable obstacle course for a festival. Wristbands are sold for $5 each, with up to 120 available. What does the ordered pair (90, 100) represent?
qs.a: Selling 90 wristbands results in a net profit of $100.

qs.s: Selling 90 wristbands brings in \(90 \times 5 = \$450\). After deducting the $350 rental cost, the profit is \(450 - 350 = \$100\), so (90, 100) represents a profit of $100 when 90 wristbands are sold.

qs.q: A sports team pays $400 to rent a bus for a tournament. The team sells up to 150 raffle tickets for $5 each to help cover the expense. What does the ordered pair (120, 200) represent?
qs.a: Selling 120 raffle tickets results in a net profit of $200.

qs.s: Selling 120 raffle tickets generates \(120 \times 5 = \$600\) in revenue. After paying the $400 bus rental, the profit is \(600 - 400 = \$200\), so (120, 200) represents a profit of $200 from 120 tickets sold.

qs.q: A catering company purchases a food truck for $48,000. Under linear depreciation, the truck loses $4,500 in value each year. What does the ordered pair (6, 21000) represent?
qs.a: After 6 years, the value of the food truck is $21,000.
d: The food truck has lost a total of $21,000 in value over 6 years.
The food truck depreciates by $21,000 each year for 6 years.
The food truck was purchased 6 years ago for $21,000.
