qs.q: If a circular rug has an area of \(64\pi\text{ ft}^2\), what is the diameter of the rug? \((A = \pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: Since \(A = \pi r^2 = 64\pi\), we have \(r^2 = 64\), so \(r = 8\text{ ft}\). The diameter is \(d = 2r = 2(8) = 16\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: If a circle has an area of \(100\pi\text{ mm}^2\), what is the diameter of the circle? \((A = \pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: Since \(A = \pi r^2 = 100\pi\), we have \(r^2 = 100\), so \(r = 10\text{ mm}\). The diameter is \(d = 2r = 2(10) = 20\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: If a circular mirror has an area of \(81\pi\text{ in}^2\), what is the diameter of the mirror? \((A = \pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: Since \(A = \pi r^2 = 81\pi\), we have \(r^2 = 81\), so \(r = 9\text{ in}\). The diameter is \(d = 2r = 2(9) = 18\text{ in}\).

qs.q: If a circular pond has an area of \(49\pi\text{ m}^2\), what is the diameter of the pond? \((A = \pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: Since \(A = \pi r^2 = 49\pi\), we have \(r^2 = 49\), so \(r = 7\text{ m}\). The diameter is \(d = 2r = 2(7) = 14\text{ m}\).

qs.q: If a circle has an area of \(256\pi\text{ in}^2\), what is the circumference of the circle in terms of \(\pi\)? \((A = \pi r^2, C = 2\pi r)\)
qs.s: Since \(A = \pi r^2 = 256\pi\), we have \(r^2 = 256\), so \(r = 16\text{ in}\). The circumference is \(C = 2\pi r = 2\pi(16) = 32\pi\text{ in}\).

qs.q: A circular archery target consists of a central bullseye and an outer ring. The bullseye has an area of \(36\pi\text{ ft}^2\), and the outer ring has an area of \(133\pi\text{ ft}^2\). What is the total diameter of the target? \((A = \pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: The total area is \(36\pi + 133\pi = 169\pi\text{ ft}^2\), so \(r^2 = 169\) and \(r = 13\text{ ft}\). The total diameter is \(d = 2r = 2(13) = 26\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A semicircular window has an area of \(98\pi\text{ cm}^2\). What is the diameter of the window? \((A = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: Since \(\frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 = 98\pi\), multiplying both sides by 2 gives \(r^2 = 196\), so \(r = 14\text{ cm}\). The diameter is \(d = 2r = 2(14) = 28\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If a circular sports field has an area of \(225\pi\text{ m}^2\), what is the diameter of the field? \((A = \pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: Since \(\pi r^2 = 225\pi\), we find \(r^2 = 225\), so \(r = 15\text{ m}\). The diameter is \(d = 2r = 2(15) = 30\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two circles have a combined area of \(180\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The area of the larger circle is four times the area of the smaller circle. What is the diameter of the larger circle? \((A = \pi r^2, d = 2r)\)
qs.s: Letting the smaller circle have area \(\pi r^2\), we get \(\pi r^2 + 4\pi r^2 = 180\pi\), so \(5r^2 = 180\) and \(r^2 = 36\). The larger circle has area \(4(36\pi) = 144\pi\), giving radius \(R = 12\text{ cm}\) and diameter \(D = 2(12) = 24\text{ cm}\).

exercises.name: Real-Life Word Problems Modelled with Square Roots

qs.q: A square dance studio floor is made up of parquet squares that are \(400\text{ cm}^2\) each. If the floor has \(3600\) parquet squares, what is the area of the dance studio floor in metres squared?
qs.s: Each tile has a side length of \(\sqrt{400} = 20\text{ cm}\) and there are \(\sqrt{3600} = 60\) tiles along each edge, giving a side length of \(60 \times 0.2\text{ m} = 12\text{ m}\). The total area of the floor is \(12^2 = 144\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A square cafeteria floor is made up of vinyl tiles that are \(1600\text{ cm}^2\) each. If the floor has \(4900\) vinyl tiles, what is the area of the cafeteria floor in metres squared?
qs.s: Each tile has a side length of \(\sqrt{1600} = 40\text{ cm}\) and there are \(\sqrt{4900} = 70\) tiles along each edge, giving a floor side length of \(70 \times 0.4\text{ m} = 28\text{ m}\). Squaring the side length gives an area of \(28^2 = 784\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A square showroom floor is made up of ceramic tiles that are \(625\text{ cm}^2\) each. If the floor has \(14\,400\) ceramic tiles, what is the area of the showroom floor in metres squared?
qs.s: Each tile has a side length of \(\sqrt{625} = 25\text{ cm}\) and there are \(\sqrt{14\,400} = 120\) tiles along each side, giving a showroom side length of \(120 \times 0.25\text{ m} = 30\text{ m}\). Thus, the area of the showroom is \(30^2 = 900\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A square courtyard is made up of granite pavers that are \(3600\text{ cm}^2\) each. If the courtyard has \(1600\) granite pavers, what is the area of the courtyard in metres squared?
qs.s: Each paver has a side length of \(\sqrt{3600} = 60\text{ cm}\) and there are \(\sqrt{1600} = 40\) pavers along each side, so the courtyard side length is \(40 \times 0.6\text{ m} = 24\text{ m}\). Therefore, the area of the courtyard is \(24^2 = 576\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A square patio is made up of stone tiles that are \(2500\text{ cm}^2\) each. If the patio has \(900\) stone tiles, what is the area of the patio in metres squared?
qs.s: Each stone tile has a side length of \(\sqrt{2500} = 50\text{ cm}\) and there are \(\sqrt{900} = 30\) tiles along each edge, making each side of the patio \(30 \times 0.5\text{ m} = 15\text{ m}\). Therefore, the area of the patio is \(15^2 = 225\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular gym floor is covered with \(5000\) square parquet tiles, each with an area of \(900\text{ cm}^2\). If the length of the gym is twice its width, what is the width of the gym in metres?
qs.s: The total floor area is \((5000 \times 900\text{ cm}^2) / 10\,000 = 450\text{ m}^2\). Setting \((2w)(w) = 450\) gives \(2w^2 = 450\), so \(w^2 = 225\) and the width is \(w = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A community centre has two square activity rooms. Room A has an area of \(196\text{ m}^2\), and the side length of Room B is \(3\text{ m}\) longer than the side length of Room A. If Room B is to be covered with square tiles that are \(625\text{ cm}^2\) each, how many tiles are needed?
qs.s: Room A has a side length of \(\sqrt{196} = 14\text{ m}\), so Room B has a side length of \(14 + 3 = 17\text{ m} = 1700\text{ cm}\). Each tile has a side length of \(\sqrt{625} = 25\text{ cm}\), so there are \(1700 / 25 = 68\) tiles per side, requiring a total of \(68^2 = 4624\) tiles.

qs.q: A square banquet hall has a floor area of \(576\text{ m}^2\). A square dance floor is placed in the centre of the hall, leaving a uniform \(2\text{-metre-wide}\) walkway around all four sides. If the dance floor is paved with square tiles that are \(400\text{ cm}^2\) each, how many tiles make up the dance floor?
qs.s: The side length of the hall is \(\sqrt{576} = 24\text{ m}\), so the side length of the dance floor is \(24 - 2(2) = 20\text{ m} = 2000\text{ cm}\). Since each tile has a side length of \(\sqrt{400} = 20\text{ cm}\), there are \(2000 / 20 = 100\) tiles per side, giving a total of \(100^2 = 10\,000\) tiles.

qs.q: A square exhibition hall floor is covered with \(40\,000\) square tiles, each measuring \(900\text{ cm}^2\). Baseboard molding is to be installed around the entire perimeter of the hall, except for a \(4\text{ m}\) doorway opening. If the molding costs \(\$15\) per metre, what is the total cost of the molding?
qs.s: The hall has \(\sqrt{40\,000} = 200\) tiles of side \(\sqrt{900} = 30\text{ cm}\) along each edge, so its side length is \(200 \times 0.3\text{ m} = 60\text{ m}\) and its perimeter is \(4 \times 60 = 240\text{ m}\). Subtracting the \(4\text{ m}\) doorway leaves \(236\text{ m}\) of molding, costing \(236 \times \$15 = \$3540\).

qs.q: A square ballroom floor is made up of parquet squares that each have an area of \(625\text{ cm}^2\). If the floor contains \(19\,600\) parquet squares, what is the perimeter of the ballroom in metres?
qs.s: Each parquet square has a side length of \(\sqrt{625} = 25\text{ cm}\) and there are \(\sqrt{19\,600} = 140\) squares along each edge, so the side length of the ballroom is \(140 \times 0.25\text{ m} = 35\text{ m}\). The perimeter of the ballroom is \(4 \times 35\text{ m} = 140\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A triangular banner has a base equal to its height. If the area of the banner is \(200\text{ cm}^2\), what is its height?
qs.s: Using \(A = \frac{1}{2}h^2\), we set \(200 = \frac{1}{2}h^2\), so \(h^2 = 400\). Taking the square root gives \(h = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If a triangle with equal base and height has an area of \(242\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of its base?
qs.s: Using \(A = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), we have \(242 = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), giving \(b^2 = 484\). Taking the square root gives \(b = 22\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: If a triangle with equal base and height has an area of \(98\text{ m}^2\), what is the length of its base?
qs.s: From \(A = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), we have \(98 = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), so \(b^2 = 196\). Taking the square root yields \(b = 14\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A triangular metal plate has an area of \(128\text{ mm}^2\). If its base and height are equal, what is the height of the plate?
qs.s: Using \(A = \frac{1}{2}h^2\), we have \(128 = \frac{1}{2}h^2\), which means \(h^2 = 256\). Taking the square root gives \(h = 16\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: If a triangle with equal base and height has an area of \(72\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of its base?
qs.s: Using \(A = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), we have \(72 = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), which gives \(b^2 = 144\). Taking the square root gives \(b = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A triangle has a height that is \(\frac{2}{3}\) of its base. If the area of the triangle is \(108\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of its base?
qs.s: With \(h = \frac{2}{3}b\), \(A = \frac{1}{2}b\left(\frac{2}{3}b\right) = \frac{1}{3}b^2 = 108\), so \(b^2 = 324\) and \(b = 18\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A triangle with a base three times its height has an area of \(216\text{ cm}^2\). What is the length of its base?
qs.s: With \(b = 3h\), \(A = \frac{1}{2}(3h)(h) = \frac{3}{2}h^2 = 216\), giving \(h^2 = 144\) and \(h = 12\text{ cm}\). The base is then \(b = 3(12) = 36\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A triangle has a base that is 4 times its height. If the area of the triangle is \(450\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of its base?
qs.s: Since \(b = 4h\), \(A = \frac{1}{2}(4h)(h) = 2h^2 = 450\), so \(h^2 = 225\) and \(h = 15\text{ cm}\). Therefore, the base is \(b = 4(15) = 60\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A triangle with equal base and height has an area of \(1800\text{ cm}^2\). What is the sum of its base and height?
qs.s: Using \(A = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), we have \(1800 = \frac{1}{2}b^2\), so \(b^2 = 3600\) and \(b = 60\text{ cm}\). Since both base and height are \(60\text{ cm}\), their sum is \(60 + 60 = 120\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A triangle with equal base and height has an area of \(72\text{ cm}^2\). A square has a side length equal to the base of this triangle. What is the perimeter of the square?
qs.s: For the triangle, \(\frac{1}{2}b^2 = 72\), so \(b^2 = 144\) and \(b = 12\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of a square with side length \(12\text{ cm}\) is \(4 \times 12 = 48\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a height of \(5\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(320\text{ cm}^3\). What is the side length of the square base?
qs.s: Using \(V = s^2 h\), we have \(320 = s^2 \times 5\), which gives \(s^2 = 64\). Taking the square root gives \(s = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cardboard box in the shape of a rectangular solid with a square base has a height of \(3\text{ m}\) and a volume of \(432\text{ m}^3\). What is the side length of the base?
qs.s: The base area is \(s^2 = 432 \div 3 = 144\). Taking the square root gives \(s = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A wooden block is shaped like a rectangular solid with a square base. It has a height of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(486\text{ cm}^3\). What is the length of one side of the base?
qs.s: From \(V = s^2 h\), we get \(s^2 = 486 \div 6 = 81\). Therefore, the side length is \(s = \sqrt{81} = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A glass display case is a rectangular solid with a square base. The case has a height of \(2\text{ m}\) and a volume of \(200\text{ m}^3\). What is the side length of the base?
qs.s: The area of the base is \(s^2 = 200 \div 2 = 100\). Taking the square root yields \(s = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism with a square base has a height of \(7\text{ m}\) and a volume of \(175\text{ m}^3\). What is the length of each side of its base?
qs.s: Divide the volume by the height to find the base area: \(s^2 = 175 \div 7 = 25\). Taking the square root gives \(s = 5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism with a square base has a height of \(11\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(2475\text{ cm}^3\). What is the perimeter of the square base?
qs.s: The base area is \(s^2 = 2475 \div 11 = 225\), so each side is \(s = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of the base is \(4 \times 15 = 60\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box with a square base has a height of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(864\text{ cm}^3\). What is the total outside surface area of the box?
qs.s: The base area is \(s^2 = 864 \div 6 = 144\), giving \(s = 12\text{ cm}\). With only one base, the surface area is \(s^2 + 4sh = 144 + 4(12 \times 6) = 144 + 288 = 432\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage tank with a square base has a height of \(6.4\text{ m}\) and a volume of \(4000\text{ m}^3\). What is the side length of the square base?
qs.s: Divide the volume by the height to get \(s^2 = 4000 \div 6.4 = 625\). Taking the square root gives \(s = \sqrt{625} = 25\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two rectangular solids each have a square base and a height of \(5\text{ cm}\). Solid A has a volume of \(720\text{ cm}^3\), and Solid B has a volume of \(1620\text{ cm}^3\). How much longer is the base side length of Solid B than that of Solid A?
qs.s: The base side lengths are \(s_A = \sqrt{720 \div 5} = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}\) and \(s_B = \sqrt{1620 \div 5} = \sqrt{324} = 18\text{ cm}\), so the difference is \(18 - 12 = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a height of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(1152\text{ cm}^3\). What is the total surface area of the rectangular solid?
qs.s: The base area is \(s^2 = 1152 \div 8 = 144\), so \(s = 12\text{ cm}\). The total surface area is \(2s^2 + 4sh = 2(144) + 4(12 \times 8) = 288 + 384 = 672\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The volume of a square pyramid is given by the formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h\), where \(s\) is the side length of the base. If a pyramid has a height of \(8\text{ m}\) and a volume of \(96\text{ m}^3\), what is the side length of its base?
qs.s: Substitute the known values to get \(96 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(8) = \frac{8}{3}s^2\). Multiply both sides by \(\frac{3}{8}\) to find \(s^2 = 36\), which gives \(s = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cone is given by the formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). If a cone has a height of \(7\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(189\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Substitute \(V = 189\pi\) and \(h = 7\) into \(189\pi = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(7)\), so \(\frac{7}{3}r^2 = 189\). Solving for \(r^2\) yields \(r^2 = 81\), so \(r = \sqrt{81} = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cone is given by the formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). If a cone has a height of \(9\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(108\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into the formula to get \(108\pi = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(9) = 3\pi r^2\). Dividing both sides by \(3\pi\) gives \(r^2 = 36\), so \(r = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is given by the formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\). If a cylinder has a height of \(5\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(320\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Substitute into the volume formula to get \(320\pi = \pi r^2(5)\), which simplifies to \(r^2 = 64\). Taking the square root gives \(r = \sqrt{64} = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is given by the formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\). If a cylinder has a height of \(12\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(192\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into the formula to get \(192\pi = 12\pi r^2\). Divide both sides by \(12\pi\) to get \(r^2 = 16\), which gives \(r = \sqrt{16} = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A storage tank shaped like a cylinder has a height of \(18\text{ m}\) and a volume of \(4050\pi\text{ m}^3\). Using the volume formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\), what is the circumference of the circular base of the tank?
qs.s: From \(4050\pi = 18\pi r^2\), we find \(r^2 = 225\), so \(r = 15\text{ m}\). The circumference of the circular base is \(C = 2\pi r = 2\pi(15) = 30\pi\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The volume of a square pyramid is given by the formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h\), where \(s\) is the side length of the base. If a pyramid has a height of \(15\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(720\text{ cm}^3\), what is the perimeter of its base?
qs.s: Substitute into \(720 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(15) = 5s^2\) to find \(s^2 = 144\), which gives base side length \(s = 12\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of the square base is \(P = 4s = 4(12) = 48\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two cones each have a height of \(12\text{ cm}\) and have a combined volume of \(500\pi\text{ cm}^3\). If the volume of the larger cone is four times the volume of the smaller cone, what is the radius of the smaller cone? (The volume of a cone is \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\).)
qs.s: Let the volume of the smaller cone be \(V_1\); then \(V_1 + 4V_1 = 5V_1 = 500\pi\), so \(V_1 = 100\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Using \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(12) = 4\pi r^2 = 100\pi\), we get \(r^2 = 25\), so \(r = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A solid consists of a cylinder and a cone joined at their circular bases, sharing the same radius \(r\). The cylinder has a height of \(4\text{ cm}\) and the cone has a height of \(9\text{ cm}\). If the total volume is given by \(V = \pi r^2 h_{\text{cyl}} + \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h_{\text{cone}}\) and equals \(343\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is the radius \(r\)?
qs.s: Substitute the heights to obtain \(V = 4\pi r^2 + \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(9) = 7\pi r^2\). Setting \(7\pi r^2 = 343\pi\) gives \(r^2 = 49\), so \(r = \sqrt{49} = 7\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cone is given by the formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). If a cone has a height of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(2400\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is the diameter of its base?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(2400\pi = \frac{8}{3}\pi r^2\) to find \(r^2 = 900\), which gives a radius of \(r = 30\text{ cm}\). The diameter is twice the radius: \(d = 2(30) = 60\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube is given by the formula \(S = 6s^2\), where \(s\) is the edge length. If a cube has a total surface area of \(294\text{ m}^2\), what is its edge length?
qs.s: Divide both sides of \(6s^2 = 294\) by 6 to get \(s^2 = 49\). Since \(\sqrt{49} = 7\), the edge length is \(7\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is given by the formula \(S = 4\pi r^2\). If a sphere has a surface area of \(484\pi\text{ in}^2\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Dividing both sides of \(4\pi r^2 = 484\pi\) by \(4\pi\) yields \(r^2 = 121\). Taking the square root gives \(r = 11\text{ in}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is given by the formula \(S = 4\pi r^2\). If a sphere has a surface area of \(324\pi\text{ cm}^2\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Set \(4\pi r^2 = 324\pi\), which simplifies to \(r^2 = 81\). Taking the square root gives \(r = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a cylinder is given by the formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\). If a cylinder has a height of \(5\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(720\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 5\) to get \(5\pi r^2 = 720\pi\), so \(r^2 = 144\). Taking the square root gives \(r = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The curved surface area of a hemisphere is given by the formula \(S = 2\pi r^2\). If a dome-shaped hemisphere has a curved surface area of \(450\pi\text{ m}^2\), what is its radius?
qs.s: Divide both sides of \(2\pi r^2 = 450\pi\) by \(2\pi\) to get \(r^2 = 225\). Thus, \(r = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism with a square base has a volume given by \(V = s^2 h\), where \(s\) is the side length of the base and \(h\) is the height. If the prism has a height of \(6\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(1176\text{ cm}^3\), what is the perimeter of its square base?
qs.s: Dividing the volume by the height gives \(s^2 = 1176 / 6 = 196\), so \(s = 14\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of the square base is \(4s = 4 \times 14 = 56\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube is given by the formula \(S = 6s^2\), where \(s\) is the edge length. If a cube has a total surface area of \(384\text{ cm}^2\), what is the sum of the lengths of all 12 of its edges?
qs.s: Solving \(6s^2 = 384\) yields \(s^2 = 64\), so each edge is \(s = 8\text{ cm}\). Since a cube has 12 edges, their total length is \(12 \times 8 = 96\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two spheres have a combined surface area of \(500\pi\text{ cm}^2\). If the surface area of the larger sphere is 4 times that of the smaller sphere, what is the radius of the larger sphere? (Use \(S = 4\pi r^2\).)
qs.s: Let the smaller area be \(S_1\), so \(S_1 + 4S_1 = 500\pi\) gives \(S_1 = 100\pi\), meaning the larger surface area is \(400\pi\text{ cm}^2\). Solving \(4\pi R^2 = 400\pi\) gives \(R^2 = 100\), so \(R = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a closed cylinder is given by the formula \(S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h\). If the height is three times the radius (\(h = 3r\)) and the total surface area is \(1152\pi\text{ cm}^2\), what is the radius of the cylinder?
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 3r\) into the formula to get \(S = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r(3r) = 8\pi r^2\). Setting \(8\pi r^2 = 1152\pi\) gives \(r^2 = 144\), so \(r = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is given by the formula \(S = 3\pi r^2\), where \(r\) is the radius. If a solid hemisphere has a total surface area of \(1083\pi\text{ mm}^2\), what is its diameter?
qs.s: Divide the total surface area by \(3\pi\) to obtain \(r^2 = 361\), giving a radius of \(r = 19\text{ mm}\). The diameter is \(2r = 38\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: The triangular prism shown has a volume of \(84\text{ cm}^3\). Using the formula \(V = \frac{1}{2}lwh\) and the dimensions in the figure, what is the height \(h\) of the prism?
qs.s: Substitute the known values into the volume formula: \(84 = \frac{1}{2}(7)(4)h = 14h\). Dividing both sides by \(14\) gives \(h = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The rectangular prism shown has a volume of \(168\text{ cm}^3\). Using the formula \(V = l \cdot w \cdot h\), find the missing width \(w\).
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(V = l \cdot w \cdot h\) to get \(168 = 7 \cdot w \cdot 4 = 28w\). Dividing by \(28\) yields \(w = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A right triangular prism has a volume of \(120\text{ cm}^3\). Based on the dimensions in the figure and the formula \(V = \frac{1}{2}lwh\), what is the length \(l\)?
qs.s: Substitute the known dimensions into \(V = \frac{1}{2}lwh\) to obtain \(120 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot l \cdot 3 \cdot 8 = 12l\). Solving gives \(l = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A triangular prism has a volume of \(72\text{ cm}^3\). Using the formula \(V = \frac{1}{2}lwh\) and the labels in the figure, find the width \(w\) of the prism.
qs.s: Substitute the values into the formula: \(72 = \frac{1}{2}(6)(w)(8) = 24w\). Dividing by \(24\) gives \(w = 3\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A right triangular prism has a volume of \(150\text{ cm}^3\). Using the formula \(V = \frac{1}{2}lwh\) and the dimensions on the figure, find the height \(h\).
qs.s: Apply the formula \(V = \frac{1}{2}lwh\): \(150 = \frac{1}{2}(5)(6)h = 15h\). Dividing both sides by \(15\) gives \(h = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder has a height of \(7\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \(175\pi\text{ cm}^3\). Using the formula \(V = \pi r^2 h\) and the figure, find the radius \(r\).
qs.s: Substitute into \(V = \pi r^2 h\): \(175\pi = \pi r^2 (7)\). Dividing both sides by \(7\pi\) yields \(r^2 = 25\), so \(r = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The right pyramid shown has a square base with edge length \(s\) and a height of \(9\text{ cm}\). If the volume is \(108\text{ cm}^3\) and \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h\), what is the base edge length \(s\)?
qs.s: Substitute the given values into \(V = \frac{1}{3}s^2 h\): \(108 = \frac{1}{3}s^2(9) = 3s^2\). Dividing by \(3\) gives \(s^2 = 36\), so \(s = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The right triangular prism shown has a base with two equal legs of length \(x\). If the volume is \(270\text{ cm}^3\) and \(V = \frac{1}{2}x^2 h\), what is the value of \(x\)?
qs.s: Substitute the values into \(V = \frac{1}{2}x^2 h\): \(270 = \frac{1}{2}x^2(15) = 7.5x^2\). Dividing by \(7.5\) yields \(x^2 = 36\), so \(x = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cube has a total surface area of \(294\text{ cm}^2\). Using the formula \(S = 6s^2\), what is its edge length \(s\)?
qs.s: Set the surface area formula equal to \(294\): \(294 = 6s^2\), which simplifies to \(s^2 = 49\). Taking the square root gives \(s = \sqrt{49} = 7\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The prism shown has a square base with side length \(s\) and a height of \(8\text{ cm}\). If its volume is \(200\text{ cm}^3\) and \(V = s^2 h\), what is the base side length \(s\)?
qs.s: Substitute into \(V = s^2 h\) to get \(200 = s^2 \cdot 8\), which simplifies to \(s^2 = 25\). Taking the square root gives \(s = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangle is twice its width. If the area of the rectangle is \(72\text{ cm}^2\), what is the width of the rectangle?
qs.s: The area of the rectangle is \(l \times w = (2w)(w) = 2w^2 = 72\text{ cm}^2\), which simplifies to \(w^2 = 36\). Taking the square root gives the width \(w = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The base of a triangle is twice its height. If the area of the triangle is \(144\text{ cm}^2\), what is the height of the triangle?
qs.s: The area is given by \(\frac{1}{2}bh = \frac{1}{2}(2h)(h) = h^2 = 144\text{ cm}^2\). Taking the square root gives the height \(h = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The base of a triangle is twice its height. If the area of the triangle is \(225\text{ m}^2\), what is the length of the base?
qs.s: The area is \(\frac{1}{2}(2h)(h) = h^2 = 225\text{ m}^2\), so the height is \(h = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ m}\). Since the base is twice the height, the base is \(2(15) = 30\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The base of a triangle is four times its height. If the area of the triangle is \(98\text{ cm}^2\), what is the height of the triangle?
qs.s: The area is \(\frac{1}{2}(4h)(h) = 2h^2 = 98\text{ cm}^2\), which simplifies to \(h^2 = 49\). Taking the square root gives \(h = \sqrt{49} = 7\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangle is twice its width. If the area of the rectangle is \(200\text{ mm}^2\), what is the length of the rectangle?
qs.s: The area is \((2w)(w) = 2w^2 = 200\text{ mm}^2\), so \(w^2 = 100\) and \(w = 10\text{ mm}\). The length is twice the width, so \(l = 2(10) = 20\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: A square and a rectangle have the same area. The rectangle has a width of \(8\text{ cm}\) and a length of \(18\text{ cm}\). What is the perimeter of the square?
qs.s: The area of the rectangle is \(8 \times 18 = 144\text{ cm}^2\), so the side length of the square is \(\sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of the square is \(4 \times 12 = 48\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular garden has a length that is \(1.5\) times its width. If the area of the garden is \(600\text{ m}^2\), what is the perimeter of the garden?
qs.s: The area is \((1.5w)(w) = 1.5w^2 = 600\), giving \(w^2 = 400\) and \(w = 20\text{ m}\). With length \(l = 1.5(20) = 30\text{ m}\), the perimeter is \(2(30 + 20) = 100\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Three identical squares are placed side by side to form a rectangle. If the total area of the rectangle is \(432\text{ cm}^2\), what is the perimeter of the rectangle?
qs.s: The area of each square is \(432 \div 3 = 144\text{ cm}^2\), so each square has side length \(s = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of the rectangle formed by the three squares is \(8s = 8(12) = 96\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangle is five times its width. If the area of the rectangle is \(320\text{ cm}^2\), what is the perimeter of the rectangle?
qs.s: The area is \((5w)(w) = 5w^2 = 320\), so \(w^2 = 64\) and \(w = 8\text{ cm}\). The length is \(5(8) = 40\text{ cm}\), giving a perimeter of \(2(40 + 8) = 96\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The base of a triangle is five times its height. If the area of the triangle is \(490\text{ m}^2\), what is the difference between the length of the base and the height?
qs.s: The area is \(\frac{1}{2}(5h)(h) = \frac{5}{2}h^2 = 490\), so \(h^2 = 196\) and \(h = 14\text{ m}\). The base is \(5(14) = 70\text{ m}\), so the difference is \(70 - 14 = 56\text{ m}\).

exercises.name: Real-Life Word Problems Modelled with Square Roots

qs.q: In a greenhouse, there are four times as many tomato plants as pepper plants. If the product of the number of tomato plants and pepper plants is 64, how many pepper plants are there?
qs.s: Let \(p\) be the number of pepper plants, so the number of tomato plants is \(4p\). Solving \(4p^2 = 64\) gives \(p^2 = 16\), so there are \(p = 4\) pepper plants.

qs.q: Lucas worked twice as many hours this week as Ethan. If the product of the number of hours they worked is 98, how many hours did Lucas work?
qs.s: Let \(h\) be the number of hours Ethan worked, so Lucas worked \(2h\) hours. Then \(2h^2 = 98\), which gives \(h^2 = 49\) and \(h = 7\), so Lucas worked \(2 \times 7 = 14\) hours.

qs.q: A shelf holds twice as many mystery novels as science fiction novels. If the product of the number of mystery novels and science fiction novels is 72, how many mystery novels are on the shelf?
qs.s: Let \(s\) be the number of science fiction novels, so there are \(2s\) mystery novels. Solving \(2s^2 = 72\) gives \(s^2 = 36\), so \(s = 6\), meaning there are \(2 \times 6 = 12\) mystery novels.

qs.q: During track practice, Liam ran three times as many laps as Mason. If the product of the number of laps they ran is 48, how many laps did Liam run?
qs.s: Let \(m\) be the number of laps Mason ran, so Liam ran \(3m\) laps. Then \(3m^2 = 48\), giving \(m^2 = 16\) and \(m = 4\), so Liam ran \(3 \times 4 = 12\) laps.

qs.q: A rectangular computer screen is three times as wide as it is high. If the area of the screen is 108 square inches, how many inches high is the screen?
qs.s: Let the height be \(h\) inches, so the width is \(3h\) inches. Solving \(3h^2 = 108\) gives \(h^2 = 36\), which means the height is \(h = 6\) inches.

qs.q: A factory has three machines: A, B, and C. In one hour, Machine B produces twice as many parts as Machine A, and Machine C produces five times as many parts as Machine A. If the product of the outputs of A and B plus the product of the outputs of A and C is 112, how many parts does Machine C produce in one hour?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the output of A, so B produces \(2x\) and C produces \(5x\). Then \(x(2x) + x(5x) = 7x^2 = 112\), which gives \(x^2 = 16\) and \(x = 4\), so Machine C produces \(5 \times 4 = 20\) parts.

qs.q: A soccer field has a length that is 1.5 times its width. If the area of the field is 5400 m², what is the perimeter of the field, in metres?
qs.s: Let \(w\) be the width, so the length is \(1.5w\). Solving \(1.5w^2 = 5400\) gives \(w^2 = 3600\), so \(w = 60\text{ m}\) and length is \(90\text{ m}\), yielding a perimeter of \(2(60 + 90) = 300\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular hallway has a length that is four times its width. The floor is covered by 72 square tiles, each with an area of 50 cm². What is the width of the hallway, in centimetres?
qs.s: The total area of the floor is \(72 \times 50 = 3600\text{ cm}^2\). Setting \(w(4w) = 3600\) gives \(4w^2 = 3600\), so \(w^2 = 900\) and the width is \(w = 30\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A triangular sail has a base that is four times its height. If the area of the sail is 450 m², what is the sum of its base and height, in metres?
qs.s: The area is \(\frac{1}{2}(4h)(h) = 2h^2 = 450\), giving \(h^2 = 225\) and \(h = 15\text{ m}\). The base is \(4 \times 15 = 60\text{ m}\), so the sum is \(60 + 15 = 75\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A farmer owns two square plots of land that have a combined area of 8000 m². The side length of the larger plot is twice the side length of the smaller plot. What is the perimeter of the larger plot, in metres?
qs.s: Let \(s\) be the side of the smaller plot, so the larger side is \(2s\). The combined area is \(s^2 + (2s)^2 = 5s^2 = 8000\), so \(s^2 = 1600\) and \(s = 40\text{ m}\), giving the larger plot a side of \(80\text{ m}\) and a perimeter of \(4 \times 80 = 320\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The combined area of two squares is \(40\text{ cm}^2\). If the area of the larger square is nine times the area of the smaller square, what is the length of the side of the smaller square?
qs.s: Let the smaller square have area \(A\). Then \(A + 9A = 40\), giving \(10A = 40\) and \(A = 4\text{ cm}^2\), so the side length of the smaller square is \(\sqrt{4} = 2\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A larger square has an area four times that of a smaller square. If the combined area of the two squares is \(500\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of the side of the larger square?
qs.s: Let the smaller square have area \(A\). Then \(A + 4A = 500\), so \(5A = 500\) and \(A = 100\text{ cm}^2\), which means the larger square has area \(400\text{ cm}^2\) and side length \(\sqrt{400} = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A larger square has an area nine times that of a smaller square. If the total area of the two squares is \(160\text{ mm}^2\), what is the length of the side of the larger square?
qs.s: Let the smaller square have area \(A\). Then \(A + 9A = 160\), which gives \(10A = 160\) and \(A = 16\text{ mm}^2\), so the larger square has area \(9 \times 16 = 144\text{ mm}^2\) and side length \(\sqrt{144} = 12\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: A larger square has an area four times that of a smaller square. If the combined area of the two squares is \(45\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of the side of the larger square?
qs.s: Let the smaller square have area \(A\). Then \(A + 4A = 45\), so \(5A = 45\) and \(A = 9\text{ cm}^2\), which means the larger square has area \(36\text{ cm}^2\) and side length \(\sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two squares have a combined area of \(125\text{ m}^2\). If the larger square has an area four times that of the smaller square, what is the length of the side of the smaller square?
qs.s: Let the smaller square have area \(A\). Then \(A + 4A = 125\), which simplifies to \(5A = 125\) and \(A = 25\text{ m}^2\), so the side length of the smaller square is \(\sqrt{25} = 5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A design is made of four identical smaller squares and one larger square. The area of the larger square is nine times the area of each smaller square. If the total area of the design is \(325\text{ cm}^2\), what is the side length of the larger square?
qs.s: Let \(A\) be the area of one smaller square; then \(4A + 9A = 13A = 325\), so \(A = 25\text{ cm}^2\). The larger square has area \(9 \times 25 = 225\text{ cm}^2\), so its side length is \(\sqrt{225} = 15\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The area of a larger square is nine times the area of a smaller square. If the combined area of the two squares is \(250\text{ cm}^2\), what is the difference between the perimeter of the larger square and the perimeter of the smaller square?
qs.s: Let \(A\) be the smaller square's area; then \(A + 9A = 10A = 250\), so \(A = 25\text{ cm}^2\) and side length is \(5\text{ cm}\). The larger square has area \(225\text{ cm}^2\) and side length \(15\text{ cm}\), giving a perimeter difference of \(4(15) - 4(5) = 60 - 20 = 40\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The side length of a larger square is three times the side length of a smaller square. If the combined area of the two squares is \(250\text{ cm}^2\), what is the perimeter of the larger square?
qs.s: Let the smaller square have side length \(s\), so the combined area is \(s^2 + (3s)^2 = 10s^2 = 250\), giving \(s = 5\text{ cm}\). The larger square has side length \(3(5) = 15\text{ cm}\), giving a perimeter of \(4 \times 15 = 60\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two circles have a combined area of \(250\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The radius of the larger circle is three times the radius of the smaller circle. What is the diameter of the larger circle?
qs.s: Let \(r\) be the radius of the smaller circle, so the larger circle has radius \(3r\) and area \(9\pi r^2\). Then \(\pi r^2 + 9\pi r^2 = 10\pi r^2 = 250\pi\), giving \(r = 5\text{ cm}\), so the larger circle's radius is \(15\text{ cm}\) and its diameter is \(2 \times 15 = 30\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A display consists of three squares: small, medium, and large. The medium square has an area four times that of the small square, and the large square has an area four times that of the medium square. If the total area of all three squares is \(336\text{ cm}^2\), what is the length of the side of the largest square?
qs.s: Let the small square have area \(A\), so the medium has area \(4A\) and the large has area \(16A\). Then \(A + 4A + 16A = 21A = 336\), giving \(A = 16\text{ cm}^2\), which makes the large square's area \(256\text{ cm}^2\) and its side length \(\sqrt{256} = 16\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangle has an area 3 times the area of a square. One side of the rectangle is the same length as the side of the square. Find the side length of the square if the total area of the square and the rectangle is \(144\text{ cm}^2\).
qs.s: Let \(A\) be the area of the square, so \(A + 3A = 4A = 144\text{ cm}^2\), which yields \(A = 36\text{ cm}^2\). The side length of the square is \(\sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangle has an area 5 times the area of a square. The shorter side of the rectangle is equal to the side length of the square. What is the length of the longer side of the rectangle if the combined area of the square and the rectangle is \(96\text{ m}^2\)?
qs.s: The total area is \(A + 5A = 6A = 96\text{ m}^2\), giving \(A = 16\text{ m}^2\) for the square. The side length is \(\sqrt{16} = 4\text{ m}\), so the longer side of the rectangle is \(5 \times 4 = 20\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangle has an area 7 times the area of a square. One side of the rectangle has the same length as the side of the square. What is the length of the longer side of the rectangle if the total area of the square and the rectangle is \(200\text{ cm}^2\)?
qs.s: Let \(A\) be the area of the square; then \(A + 7A = 8A = 200\text{ cm}^2\), so \(A = 25\text{ cm}^2\). The side length of the square is \(\sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}\), so the longer side of the rectangle is \(7 \times 5 = 35\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangle has an area 8 times the area of a square. The width of the rectangle is equal to the side length of the square. What is the length of the rectangle if the total area of the square and the rectangle is \(225\text{ mm}^2\)?
qs.s: The combined area is \(A + 8A = 9A = 225\text{ mm}^2\), so the square has area \(A = 25\text{ mm}^2\) and side length \(\sqrt{25} = 5\text{ mm}\). The length of the rectangle is \(8 \times 5 = 40\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: A rectangle has an area 6 times the area of a square. One side of the rectangle is the same length as the side of the square. What is the length of the longer side of the rectangle if the combined area of the square and the rectangle is \(112\text{ in.}^2\)?
qs.s: The combined area is \(A + 6A = 7A = 112\text{ in.}^2\), which gives \(A = 16\text{ in.}^2\) for the square. The side of the square is \(\sqrt{16} = 4\text{ in.}\), making the longer side of the rectangle \(6 \times 4 = 24\text{ in.}\)

qs.q: Two identical squares and a rectangle have a combined area of \(432\text{ cm}^2\). The rectangle has an area 10 times the area of one square, and its width is equal to the side length of a square. What is the length of the rectangle?
qs.s: Let \(A\) be the area of one square; the combined area is \(2A + 10A = 12A = 432\text{ cm}^2\), so \(A = 36\text{ cm}^2\). The side length of each square is \(\sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}\), so the length of the rectangle is \(10 \times 6 = 60\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A right triangle and a square have a combined area of \(256\text{ cm}^2\). The height of the triangle is equal to the side length of the square, and the base of the triangle is 6 times its height. What is the length of the base of the triangle?
qs.s: Let \(s\) be the side length of the square; the triangle's area is \(\frac{1}{2}(6s)(s) = 3s^2\), giving a total area of \(s^2 + 3s^2 = 4s^2 = 256\text{ cm}^2\). Solving yields \(s^2 = 64\), so \(s = 8\text{ cm}\), and the base of the triangle is \(6 \times 8 = 48\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A square and two rectangles have a combined area of \(384\text{ m}^2\). The first rectangle has an area \(3.5\) times the area of the square, and the second rectangle has an area \(1.5\) times the area of the square. Each rectangle has one side equal to the side length of the square. What is the length of the longer side of the first rectangle?
qs.s: The total area is \(A + 3.5A + 1.5A = 6A = 384\text{ m}^2\), giving \(A = 64\text{ m}^2\) and side length \(\sqrt{64} = 8\text{ m}\). The longer side of the first rectangle is \(3.5 \times 8 = 28\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangle has an area 15 times the area of a square. The width of the rectangle is equal to the side length of the square. If the total combined area of the square and the rectangle is \(1600\text{ cm}^2\), what is the perimeter of the rectangle?
qs.s: The total area is \(A + 15A = 16A = 1600\text{ cm}^2\), so the square has area \(A = 100\text{ cm}^2\) and side length \(\sqrt{100} = 10\text{ cm}\). The rectangle has dimensions \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(150\text{ cm}\), giving a perimeter of \(2(150 + 10) = 320\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two circles have a combined area of \(490\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The radius of the larger circle is 3 times the radius of the smaller circle. What is the diameter of the larger circle?
qs.s: Let \(r\) be the radius of the smaller circle; the combined area is \(\pi r^2 + \pi(3r)^2 = 10\pi r^2 = 490\pi\text{ cm}^2\), so \(r^2 = 49\) and \(r = 7\text{ cm}\). The larger circle has a radius of \(3 \times 7 = 21\text{ cm}\), so its diameter is \(2 \times 21 = 42\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The distance, \(d\) in kilometers, that a person can see to the horizon from an altitude of \(h\) meters is given by the formula \(d = \sqrt{13h}\). What is the altitude of an observer who can see a distance of \(26\text{ kilometers}\) to the horizon?
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 26\) to get \(26 = \sqrt{13h}\). Squaring both sides gives \(676 = 13h\), and dividing by 13 yields \(h = 52\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The velocity, \(v\) in meters per second, of an object dropped from a height is given by the formula \(v = \sqrt{20h}\), where \(h\) is the height in meters. What is the height from which the object was dropped if its velocity upon impact is \(30\text{ meters per second}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 30\) into \(30 = \sqrt{20h}\) and square both sides to get \(900 = 20h\). Dividing by 20 yields \(h = 45\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The speed, \(s\) in meters per second, of an ocean wave is modeled by the formula \(s = \sqrt{g \cdot d}\), where \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\) is the acceleration due to gravity and \(d\) is the water depth in meters. What is the depth of the ocean if a wave travels at a speed of \(70\text{ meters per second}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 70\) and \(g = 10\) into \(70 = \sqrt{10d}\). Squaring both sides yields \(4900 = 10d\), which simplifies to \(d = 490\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The electric current, \(I\) in amperes, flowing through an appliance is given by the formula \(I = \sqrt{\frac{P}{R}}\), where \(P\) is power in watts and \(R\) is resistance in ohms. If an appliance has a resistance of \(12\text{ ohms}\) and draws a current of \(5\text{ amperes}\), what is its power?
qs.s: Substitute \(I = 5\) and \(R = 12\) into \(5 = \sqrt{\frac{P}{12}}\). Squaring both sides gives \(25 = \frac{P}{12}\), so \(P = 25 \times 12 = 300\text{ watts}\).

qs.q: The momentum, \(p\) in kilogram-meters per second, of a moving object is given by the formula \(p = \sqrt{2mK}\), where \(m\) is mass in kilograms and \(K\) is kinetic energy in joules. What is the kinetic energy of an object with a mass of \(8\text{ kilograms}\) and a momentum of \(40\text{ kilogram-meters per second}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(p = 40\) and \(m = 8\) to obtain \(40 = \sqrt{16K}\). Squaring both sides gives \(1600 = 16K\), so \(K = 100\text{ joules}\).

qs.q: The velocity, \(v\) in meters per second, of liquid flowing from an opening in a pressurized tank is given by \(v = 4\sqrt{5h + 16}\), where \(h\) is the liquid depth in meters. What is the depth of the liquid if the exit velocity is \(56\text{ meters per second}\)?
qs.s: Divide both sides of \(56 = 4\sqrt{5h + 16}\) by 4 to get \(14 = \sqrt{5h + 16}\). Squaring both sides gives \(196 = 5h + 16\), which leads to \(5h = 180\), so \(h = 36\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The final speed, \(v\) in meters per second, of an accelerating rocket sled is given by the formula \(v = \sqrt{v_0^2 + 2as}\), where \(v_0\) is the initial speed in \(\text{m/s}\), \(a\) is acceleration in \(\text{m/s}^2\), and \(s\) is distance in meters. If the sled accelerates at \(16\text{ m/s}^2\) from an initial speed of \(40\text{ m/s}\) to a final speed of \(120\text{ m/s}\), what distance did it travel?
qs.s: Substitute values into \(120 = \sqrt{40^2 + 2(16)s}\) and square both sides to obtain \(14{,}400 = 1600 + 32s\). Subtracting 1600 gives \(32s = 12{,}800\), so \(s = 400\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The speed, \(v\) in meters per second, of sound in a gas is modeled by the formula \(v = 20\sqrt{T + 273}\), where \(T\) is the temperature in degrees Celsius. At what temperature is the speed of sound equal to \(340\text{ meters per second}\)?
qs.s: Divide both sides of \(340 = 20\sqrt{T + 273}\) by 20 to get \(17 = \sqrt{T + 273}\). Squaring both sides gives \(289 = T + 273\), so \(T = 289 - 273 = 16^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: Electromagnetic force, \(E\) in volts, is determined by the formula \(E = \sqrt{W \cdot R}\), where \(W\) is total power in watts and \(R\) is resistance in ohms. A transmission system operates at an electromagnetic force of \(480\text{ volts}\) with a resistance of \(15\text{ ohms}\). If the total power is generated equally by \(6\) identical generators, how many watts does each generator produce?
qs.s: Squaring both sides of \(480 = \sqrt{15W}\) gives \(230{,}400 = 15W\), so total power is \(W = 15{,}360\text{ watts}\). Dividing equally among the 6 generators yields \(15{,}360 \div 6 = 2560\text{ watts}\).

qs.q: The electric current, \(I\) in amperes, flowing through a resistor is given by \(I = \sqrt{\frac{P}{R}}\), where \(P\) is power in watts and \(R\) is resistance in ohms. A heater has a resistance of \(8\text{ ohms}\). If the current increases from \(5\text{ amperes}\) to \(10\text{ amperes}\), by how many watts does the power increase?
qs.s: Solving for power gives \(P = I^2 R\). The initial power is \(5^2 \times 8 = 200\text{ W}\) and the final power is \(10^2 \times 8 = 800\text{ W}\), so the power increases by \(800 - 200 = 600\text{ watts}\).

qs.q: The time \(t\) in seconds for an object to fall a distance \(d\) in feet is given by the formula \(t = \sqrt{d / 16}\). If an object takes \(5\) seconds to hit the ground, what distance \(d\) in feet did it fall?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 5\) into the formula to get \(5 = \sqrt{d / 16}\). Squaring both sides gives \(25 = d / 16\), so \(d = 25 \times 16 = 400\text{ feet}\).

qs.q: The length of the diagonal \(d\) in centimeters of a square with area \(A\) in square centimeters is given by the formula \(d = \sqrt{2A}\). If the diagonal of a square is \(14\text{ cm}\), what is its area \(A\) in square centimeters?
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 14\) into \(14 = \sqrt{2A}\). Squaring both sides gives \(196 = 2A\), which simplifies to \(A = 196 / 2 = 98\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: The speed \(s\) in miles per hour of a car can be estimated from the length of its skid marks \(d\) in feet using the formula \(s = \sqrt{24d}\). If the speed of the car was \(60\text{ mph}\), what was the length of the skid mark \(d\) in feet?
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 60\) into the formula to get \(60 = \sqrt{24d}\). Squaring both sides gives \(3600 = 24d\), so \(d = 3600 / 24 = 150\text{ feet}\).

qs.q: The velocity \(v\) in meters per second of an object with kinetic energy \(K\) in joules and mass \(m\) in kilograms is given by \(v = \sqrt{2K / m}\). If an object has a mass of \(50\text{ kg}\) and travels at a speed of \(6\text{ m/s}\), what is its kinetic energy \(K\) in joules?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 6\) and \(m = 50\) into \(6 = \sqrt{2K / 50}\), which simplifies to \(6 = \sqrt{K / 25}\). Squaring both sides gives \(36 = K / 25\), so \(K = 36 \times 25 = 900\text{ joules}\).

qs.q: The speed \(v\) in meters per second of a wave traveling along a string is given by the formula \(v = \sqrt{T / m}\), where \(T\) is the tension in newtons and \(m\) is the mass per unit length in kilograms per meter. If the wave speed is \(12\text{ m/s}\) and the mass per unit length is \(3\text{ kg/m}\), what is the tension \(T\) in newtons?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 12\) and \(m = 3\) to obtain \(12 = \sqrt{T / 3}\). Squaring both sides yields \(144 = T / 3\), so \(T = 144 \times 3 = 432\text{ newtons}\).

qs.q: The final velocity \(v\) in meters per second of an accelerating object is given by the formula \(v = \sqrt{u^2 + 2as}\), where \(u\) is the initial velocity in meters per second, \(a\) is the acceleration in \(\text{m/s}^2\), and \(s\) is the distance traveled in meters. If an object accelerates at \(3\text{ m/s}^2\) from an initial velocity of \(8\text{ m/s}\) to a final velocity of \(20\text{ m/s}\), what distance \(s\) in meters did it travel?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 20\), \(u = 8\), and \(a = 3\) to get \(20 = \sqrt{64 + 6s}\). Squaring both sides yields \(400 = 64 + 6s\), so \(6s = 336\), which gives \(s = 56\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The formula \(t = \sqrt{\frac{2(d - 5)}{a}}\) models the time \(t\) in seconds required for an automated cart to travel a net distance \(d\) in meters while accelerating at \(a\text{ m/s}^2\). If the cart accelerates at \(3\text{ m/s}^2\) and the trip takes \(4\text{ seconds}\), what was the distance \(d\) in meters?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 4\) and \(a = 3\) to get \(4 = \sqrt{\frac{2(d - 5)}{3}}\). Squaring both sides gives \(16 = \frac{2(d - 5)}{3}\), so \(48 = 2(d - 5)\), which simplifies to \(d - 5 = 24\), giving \(d = 29\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The current \(I\) in amps flowing through an electrical circuit is given by \(I = \sqrt{P / R}\), where \(P\) is the power in watts and \(R\) is the resistance in ohms. A circuit has a fixed resistance of \(8\text{ ohms}\). How many additional watts of power are required to increase the current from \(6\text{ amps}\) to \(9\text{ amps}\)?
qs.s: The initial power is \(P_1 = 6^2 \times 8 = 288\text{ W}\) and the final power is \(P_2 = 9^2 \times 8 = 648\text{ W}\). The additional power needed is \(648 - 288 = 360\text{ watts}\).

qs.q: The wind speed \(S\) in knots at an offshore weather station is modeled by the formula \(S = 4\sqrt{2h + 7}\), where \(h\) is the wave height in feet. If the recorded wind speed is \(36\text{ knots}\), what is the wave height \(h\) in feet?
qs.s: Divide both sides of \(36 = 4\sqrt{2h + 7}\) by 4 to get \(9 = \sqrt{2h + 7}\). Squaring both sides gives \(81 = 2h + 7\), so \(2h = 74\), which results in \(h = 37\text{ feet}\).

qs.q: The current \(I\) in amps in a circuit with power \(P\) in watts and total resistance \(R\) in ohms is given by \(I = \sqrt{P / R}\). A circuit has a power of \(2400\text{ watts}\) and two resistors connected in series with resistances of \(R_1 = 35\text{ ohms}\) and an unknown resistor \(R_2\), so that \(R = 35 + R_2\). If the current in the circuit is \(5\text{ amps}\), what is the resistance of \(R_2\) in ohms?
qs.s: Substitute \(I = 5\), \(P = 2400\), and \(R = 35 + R_2\) to get \(5 = \sqrt{2400 / (35 + R_2)}\). Squaring both sides gives \(25 = 2400 / (35 + R_2)\), which means \(35 + R_2 = 96\), and solving yields \(R_2 = 61\text{ ohms}\).

qs.q: The maximum safe speed \(v\), in miles per hour, on an unbanked circular exit ramp of radius \(r\), in feet, is modeled by the formula \(v = \sqrt{\frac{5r}{2}}\). If the safe speed for a particular ramp is 40 miles per hour, what is the radius of the ramp, in feet?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 40\) into the formula to get \(40 = \sqrt{\frac{5r}{2}}\). Squaring both sides gives \(1600 = \frac{5r}{2}\), so \(5r = 3200\) and \(r = 640\).

qs.q: The speed \(s\), in miles per hour, of a car before braking can be estimated from the length \(d\), in feet, of its skid marks using the formula \(s = \sqrt{24d}\). If the car was travelling at 60 miles per hour, what was the length of its skid marks, in feet?
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 60\) into the formula to get \(60 = \sqrt{24d}\). Squaring both sides gives \(3600 = 24d\), which solves to \(d = 150\).

qs.q: The electric current \(I\), in amperes, drawn by an appliance is given by the formula \(I = \sqrt{\frac{3P}{25}}\), where \(P\) is the power in watts. If the appliance draws a current of 6 amperes, what is its power, in watts?
qs.s: Substitute \(I = 6\) into the formula to get \(6 = \sqrt{\frac{3P}{25}}\). Squaring both sides gives \(36 = \frac{3P}{25}\), so \(3P = 900\) and \(P = 300\).

qs.q: The maximum theoretical speed \(s\), in knots, of a sailboat is related to its waterline length \(L\), in feet, by the formula \(s = \sqrt{\frac{9L}{5}}\). If a sailboat has a maximum speed of 9 knots, what is its waterline length, in feet?
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 9\) into the formula to get \(9 = \sqrt{\frac{9L}{5}}\). Squaring both sides yields \(81 = \frac{9L}{5}\), which simplifies to \(L = 45\).

qs.q: The velocity \(v\), in meters per second, of an object dropped from a height \(h\), in meters, is given by the formula \(v = \sqrt{20h}\). If an object hits the ground with a velocity of 30 meters per second, from what height was it dropped, in meters?
qs.s: Substitute \(v = 30\) into \(v = \sqrt{20h}\) to get \(30 = \sqrt{20h}\). Squaring both sides yields \(900 = 20h\), which simplifies to \(h = 45\).

qs.q: The speed \(v\), in feet per second, of a cart rolling down a ramp after traveling a distance of \(d\) feet is given by the formula \(v = 8\sqrt{\frac{5d + 20}{3}}\). If the cart reaches a speed of 40 feet per second, what distance \(d\), in feet, has it traveled?
qs.s: Dividing both sides of \(40 = 8\sqrt{\frac{5d + 20}{3}}\) by 8 gives \(5 = \sqrt{\frac{5d + 20}{3}}\), and squaring gives \(25 = \frac{5d + 20}{3}\). Multiplying by 3 gives \(75 = 5d + 20\), which solves to \(5d = 55\), so \(d = 11\).

qs.q: The recommended number of parking spaces \(N\) for a new shopping center is given by \(N = 4\sqrt{2A + 100}\), where \(A\) is the retail floor area in square meters. If the shopping center is designed to have 360 parking spaces, what is its retail floor area, in square meters?
qs.s: Dividing both sides of \(360 = 4\sqrt{2A + 100}\) by 4 gives \(90 = \sqrt{2A + 100}\), and squaring both sides gives \(8100 = 2A + 100\). Solving for \(A\) yields \(2A = 8000\), so \(A = 4000\).

qs.q: The speed of sound \(s\), in meters per second, through dry air is modeled by the formula \(s = 20\sqrt{T + 273}\), where \(T\) is the air temperature in degrees Celsius. If the speed of sound is measured to be 360 meters per second, what is the air temperature in degrees Celsius?
qs.s: Dividing both sides of \(360 = 20\sqrt{T + 273}\) by 20 gives \(18 = \sqrt{T + 273}\). Squaring both sides gives \(324 = T + 273\), so \(T = 324 - 273 = 51\).

qs.q: The rate of water flow \(r\), in liters per minute, draining from a cylindrical tank is given by \(r = 12\sqrt{5h}\), where \(h\) is the water depth in meters. By how many meters must the water depth increase to increase the drainage rate from 60 liters per minute to 120 liters per minute?
qs.s: For \(r = 60\), \(60 = 12\sqrt{5h_1} \implies 5 = \sqrt{5h_1} \implies h_1 = 5\), and for \(r = 120\), \(120 = 12\sqrt{5h_2} \implies 10 = \sqrt{5h_2} \implies h_2 = 20\). The required increase in depth is \(20 - 5 = 15\).

qs.q: On a clear day, the distance \(d\), in miles, that an observer can see to the horizon is given by \(d = \sqrt{\frac{3h}{2}}\), where \(h\) is the observer's eye level above the ground in feet. An observer at a lookout tower can see 18 miles. How many feet higher must an observation deck be built above the tower so that an observer there can see 24 miles?
qs.s: At 18 miles, \(18 = \sqrt{\frac{3h_1}{2}} \implies h_1 = 216\text{ ft}\), and at 24 miles, \(24 = \sqrt{\frac{3h_2}{2}} \implies h_2 = 384\text{ ft}\). The additional height required is \(384 - 216 = 168\text{ ft}\).

exercises.name: Estimating square roots between consecutive whole numbers

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{34}\) lie?
Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{55}\) lie?
Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{85}\) lie?
Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{14}\) lie?
Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{19}\) lie?
Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{350}\) lie?
Between which two consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(5 + \sqrt{48}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36 < 48 < 49 = 7^2\), \(\sqrt{48}\) is between 6 and 7. Adding 5 to both bounds gives \(11 < 5 + \sqrt{48} < 12\).

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(10 - \sqrt{28}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(5^2 = 25 < 28 < 36 = 6^2\), \(\sqrt{28}\) is between 5 and 6. Subtracting these values from 10 gives bounds of \(10 - 6 = 4\) and \(10 - 5 = 5\).

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{175}\) lie?
Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{4^2 + 7^2}\) lie?
qs.s: Evaluating under the radical gives \(4^2 + 7^2 = 16 + 49 = 65\). Since \(8^2 = 64\) and \(9^2 = 81\), \(\sqrt{65}\) lies between 8 and 9.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{43}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36\) and \(7^2 = 49\), and 43 is between 36 and 49, \(\sqrt{43}\) lies between 6 and 7.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{68}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(8^2 = 64\) and \(9^2 = 81\), and 68 is between 64 and 81, \(\sqrt{68}\) lies between 8 and 9.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{11}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(3^2 = 9\) and \(4^2 = 16\), and 11 is between 9 and 16, \(\sqrt{11}\) lies between 3 and 4.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{23}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(4^2 = 16\) and \(5^2 = 25\), and 23 is between 16 and 25, \(\sqrt{23}\) lies between 4 and 5.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{95}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(9^2 = 81\) and \(10^2 = 100\), and 95 is between 81 and 100, \(\sqrt{95}\) lies between 9 and 10.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{330}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(18^2 = 324\) and \(19^2 = 361\), 330 falls between 324 and 361. Therefore, \(\sqrt{330}\) lies between 18 and 19.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(\sqrt{3 \times 50 + 26}\) lie?
qs.s: Calculate the radicand: \(3 \times 50 + 26 = 150 + 26 = 176\). Since \(13^2 = 169 < 176 < 196 = 14^2\), the value lies between 13 and 14.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(\sqrt{7^2 + 4^2}\) lie?
qs.s: Evaluate the expression inside the radical: \(7^2 + 4^2 = 49 + 16 = 65\). Since \(8^2 = 64 < 65 < 81 = 9^2\), the value lies between 8 and 9.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{150}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(12^2 = 144\) and \(13^2 = 169\), 150 falls between 144 and 169. Therefore, \(\sqrt{150}\) lies between 12 and 13.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(20 - \sqrt{48}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36 < 48 < 49 = 7^2\), \(\sqrt{48}\) is between 6 and 7. Subtracting this from 20 yields a value between \(20 - 7 = 13\) and \(20 - 6 = 14\).

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{15}\)?
Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{53}\)?
Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{95}\)?
Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{29}\)?
Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{70}\)?
Between what consecutive whole numbers is the value of \(\sqrt{48} + 5\)?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36 < 48 < 49 = 7^2\), we know \(6 < \sqrt{48} < 7\). Adding 5 to each bound gives \(11 < \sqrt{48} + 5 < 12\).

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{215}\)?
Between what consecutive whole numbers is the value of \(\sqrt{85} - 3\)?
Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{5^2 + 7^2}\)?
qs.s: Evaluate inside the radical: \(5^2 + 7^2 = 25 + 49 = 74\). Since \(8^2 = 64 < 74 < 81 = 9^2\), \(\sqrt{74}\) lies between 8 and 9.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers is \(\sqrt{68 + 45}\)?
qs.s: Simplify the radicand to get \(\sqrt{113}\). Since \(10^2 = 100\) and \(11^2 = 121\), \(\sqrt{113}\) lies between 10 and 11.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{77}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(8^2 = 64\) and \(9^2 = 81\), we have \(64 < 77 < 81\). Taking square roots gives \(8 < \sqrt{77} < 9\), so \(\sqrt{77}\) lies between 8 and 9.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{58}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(7^2 = 49\) and \(8^2 = 64\), we have \(49 < 58 < 64\). Taking square roots gives \(7 < \sqrt{58} < 8\), so \(\sqrt{58}\) lies between 7 and 8.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{42}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36\) and \(7^2 = 49\), we have \(36 < 42 < 49\). Taking square roots gives \(6 < \sqrt{42} < 7\), so \(\sqrt{42}\) lies between 6 and 7.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{32}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(5^2 = 25\) and \(6^2 = 36\), we have \(25 < 32 < 36\). Taking square roots gives \(5 < \sqrt{32} < 6\), so \(\sqrt{32}\) lies between 5 and 6.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{9^2 + 5^2}\) lie?
qs.s: Evaluating inside the radical gives \(9^2 + 5^2 = 81 + 25 = 106\). Since \(10^2 = 100 < 106 < 121 = 11^2\), \(\sqrt{106}\) lies between 10 and 11.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(6 + \sqrt{45}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36 < 45 < 49 = 7^2\), \(\sqrt{45}\) is between 6 and 7. Adding 6 to both bounds gives \(12 < 6 + \sqrt{45} < 13\), so the value lies between 12 and 13.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(15 - \sqrt{30}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(5^2 = 25 < 30 < 36 = 6^2\), \(\sqrt{30}\) is between 5 and 6. Subtracting these bounds from 15 gives \(15 - 6 < 15 - \sqrt{30} < 15 - 5\), so the value lies between 9 and 10.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{180}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(13^2 = 169\) and \(14^2 = 196\), we have \(169 < 180 < 196\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{180}\) lies between 13 and 14.

qs.q: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{280}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(16^2 = 256\) and \(17^2 = 289\), we have \(256 < 280 < 289\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{280}\) lies between 16 and 17.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{54}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(7^2 = 49\) and \(8^2 = 64\), and 54 is between 49 and 64, \(\sqrt{54}\) lies between 7 and 8.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{13}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(3^2 = 9\) and \(4^2 = 16\), and 13 is between 9 and 16, \(\sqrt{13}\) lies between 3 and 4.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{75}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(8^2 = 64\) and \(9^2 = 81\), and 75 is between 64 and 81, \(\sqrt{75}\) lies between 8 and 9.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{45}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36\) and \(7^2 = 49\), and 45 is between 36 and 49, \(\sqrt{45}\) lies between 6 and 7.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{32}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(5^2 = 25\) and \(6^2 = 36\), and 32 is between 25 and 36, \(\sqrt{32}\) lies between 5 and 6.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{300}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(17^2 = 289\) and \(18^2 = 324\), and 300 is between 289 and 324, \(\sqrt{300}\) lies between 17 and 18.

qs.q: A square has an area of \(115\text{ cm}^2\). Between what two consecutive whole numbers of centimeters does its side length lie?
qs.s: The side length is \(\sqrt{115}\text{ cm}\). Since \(10^2 = 100\) and \(11^2 = 121\), \(\sqrt{115}\) lies between 10 and 11.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(\sqrt{5^2 + 8^2}\) lie?
qs.s: Evaluate inside the radical first: \(\sqrt{25 + 64} = \sqrt{89}\). Since \(9^2 = 81\) and \(10^2 = 100\), \(\sqrt{89}\) lies between 9 and 10.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does the value of \(4 + \sqrt{50}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(7^2 = 49\) and \(8^2 = 64\), \(\sqrt{50}\) is between 7 and 8. Adding 4 gives a value between 11 and 12.

qs.q: Between what two consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{150}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(12^2 = 144\) and \(13^2 = 169\), and 150 falls between 144 and 169, \(\sqrt{150}\) lies between 12 and 13.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{83}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(9^2 = 81\) and \(10^2 = 100\), and 83 is between 81 and 100, \(\sqrt{83}\) lies between 9 and 10.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{19}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(4^2 = 16\) and \(5^2 = 25\), and 19 is between 16 and 25, \(\sqrt{19}\) lies between 4 and 5.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{42}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(6^2 = 36\) and \(7^2 = 49\), and 42 is between 36 and 49, \(\sqrt{42}\) lies between 6 and 7.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{55}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(7^2 = 49\) and \(8^2 = 64\), and 55 is between 49 and 64, \(\sqrt{55}\) lies between 7 and 8.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{5 \times 40 + 24}\) lie?
qs.s: Evaluating inside the radical gives \(5 \times 40 + 24 = 200 + 24 = 224\). Since \(14^2 = 196\) and \(15^2 = 225\), \(\sqrt{224}\) lies between 14 and 15.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{450}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(21^2 = 441\) and \(22^2 = 484\), and 450 is between 441 and 484, \(\sqrt{450}\) lies between 21 and 22.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{20^2 - 11^2}\) lie?
qs.s: Evaluating inside the radical gives \(20^2 - 11^2 = 400 - 121 = 279\). Since \(16^2 = 256\) and \(17^2 = 289\), \(\sqrt{279}\) lies between 16 and 17.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{135}\) lie?
qs.s: Since \(11^2 = 121\) and \(12^2 = 144\), and 135 lies between 121 and 144, \(\sqrt{135}\) lies between 11 and 12.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers does \(\sqrt{9^2 + 10^2}\) lie?
qs.s: Evaluating inside the radical gives \(9^2 + 10^2 = 81 + 100 = 181\). Since \(13^2 = 169\) and \(14^2 = 196\), \(\sqrt{181}\) lies between 13 and 14.

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers is the value of \(\sqrt{200} - 3\)?
qs.s: Since \(14^2 = 196\) and \(15^2 = 225\), \(\sqrt{200}\) is between 14 and 15. Subtracting 3 gives a value between \(14 - 3 = 11\) and \(15 - 3 = 12\).

qs.q: Between what consecutive whole numbers is the value of \(\sqrt{9^2 + 5^2}\)?

Given that \(\sqrt{7} \doteq 2.646\) and \(\sqrt{70} \doteq 8.367\), calculate \(\sqrt{700}\) without a calculator.
qs.s: Rewrite \(\sqrt{700} = \sqrt{7 \times 100} = \sqrt{7} \times 10 = 2.646 \times 10 = 26.46\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{2} \doteq 1.414\) and \(\sqrt{20} \doteq 4.472\), calculate \(\sqrt{2000}\) without a calculator.
qs.s: Rewrite \(\sqrt{2000} = \sqrt{20 \times 100} = \sqrt{20} \times 10 = 4.472 \times 10 = 44.72\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{3} \doteq 1.732\) and \(\sqrt{30} \doteq 5.477\), calculate \(\sqrt{0.003}\) without a calculator.
Given that \(\sqrt{5} \doteq 2.236\) and \(\sqrt{50} \doteq 7.071\), calculate \(\sqrt{0.5}\) without a calculator.

Given that \(\sqrt{2} \doteq 1.414\) and \sqrt{20} \doteq 4.472$, calculate without a calculator: \(\sqrt{0.02}\)
Given that \(\sqrt{5} \doteq 2.236\) and \(\sqrt{50} \doteq 7.071\), calculate without a calculator: \(\sqrt{0.5}\)

qs.s: Write \(\sqrt{30000} = \sqrt{3 \times 10000} = 100\sqrt{3} \doteq 100 \times 1.732 = 173.2\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{7} \doteq 2.646\) and \(\sqrt{70} \doteq 8.367\), calculate without a calculator: \(\sqrt{700000} + \sqrt{0.0007}\)
Given that \(\sqrt{6} \doteq 2.449\) and \(\sqrt{60} \doteq 7.746\), calculate without a calculator: \(4\sqrt{600} - \sqrt{6000}\)
qs.s: Since \(\sqrt{600} = 10\sqrt{6} \doteq 24.49\) and \(\sqrt{6000} = 10\sqrt{60} \doteq 77.46\), the expression evaluates to \(4(24.49) - 77.46 = 97.96 - 77.46 = 20.5\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{3} \doteq 1.732\) and \(\sqrt{30} \doteq 5.477\), calculate without a calculator: \(\sqrt{30000} + \sqrt{0.003}\)
Given that \(\sqrt{2} \doteq 1.414\) and \(\sqrt{20} \doteq 4.472\), calculate without a calculator: \(\sqrt{0.02} + \sqrt{0.2}\)
Given that \(\sqrt{5} \doteq 2.236\) and \(\sqrt{50} \doteq 7.071\), calculate without a calculator: \(\sqrt{5000} - \sqrt{500}\)
qs.s: Since \(\sqrt{5000} = 10\sqrt{50} \doteq 70.71\) and \(\sqrt{500} = 10\sqrt{5} \doteq 22.36\), their difference is \(70.71 - 22.36 = 48.35\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{7} \doteq 2.646\) and \(\sqrt{70} \doteq 8.367\), calculate the value of \(\sqrt{7000}\) without a calculator.
qs.s: Since \(\sqrt{7000} = \sqrt{70 \times 100} = 10\sqrt{70}\), we have \(10 \times 8.367 = 83.67\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{6} \doteq 2.449\) and \(\sqrt{60} \doteq 7.746\), calculate the value of \(\sqrt{0.006}\) without a calculator.
Given that \(\sqrt{5} \doteq 2.236\) and \(\sqrt{50} \doteq 7.071\), calculate the value of \(\sqrt{0.05}\) without a calculator.
Given that \(\sqrt{3} \doteq 1.732\) and \(\sqrt{30} \doteq 5.477\), calculate the value of \(\sqrt{0.3}\) without a calculator.
Given that \(\sqrt{7} \doteq 2.646\) and \(\sqrt{70} \doteq 8.367\), calculate the perimeter, in centimeters, of a square with an area of \(0.007\text{ cm}^2\) without a calculator.
qs.s: The side length is \(s = \sqrt{0.007} = \frac{\sqrt{70}}{100} \doteq 0.08367\text{ cm}\). The perimeter is \(4s = 4 \times 0.08367 = 0.33468\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{3} \doteq 1.732\) and \(\sqrt{30} \doteq 5.477\), calculate the value of \(\sqrt{3000} + \sqrt{0.03}\) without a calculator.
qs.s: Evaluating each term gives \(\sqrt{3000} = 10\sqrt{30} \doteq 54.77\) and \(\sqrt{0.03} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{10} \doteq 0.1732\). Adding them together yields \(54.77 + 0.1732 = 54.9432\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{2} \doteq 1.414\) and \(\sqrt{20} \doteq 4.472\), calculate the value of \(\sqrt{0.00002}\) without a calculator.
qs.s: Writing \(0.00002\) with an even power-of-ten denominator gives \(\sqrt{\frac{20}{1\,000\,000}} = \frac{\sqrt{20}}{1000} \doteq \frac{4.472}{1000} = 0.004472\).

qs.q: Given that \(\sqrt{5} \doteq 2.236\) and \(\sqrt{50} \doteq 7.071\), find the value of \(x\) if \(\sqrt{x} \doteq 0.07071\).
Given that \(\sqrt{8} \doteq 2.828\) and \(\sqrt{80} \doteq 8.944\), calculate the value of \(\sqrt{80\,000} - \sqrt{0.8}\) without a calculator.
qs.s: Evaluate each term: \(\sqrt{80\,000} = 100\sqrt{8} \doteq 282.8\) and \(\sqrt{0.8} = \frac{\sqrt{80}}{10} \doteq 0.8944\). Subtracting gives \(282.8 - 0.8944 = 281.9056\).

A square garden has an area of \(8000\text{ m}^2\). Given that \(\sqrt{8} \doteq 2.828\) and \(\sqrt{80} \doteq 8.944\), calculate the perimeter of the garden without a calculator.
qs.s: The side length is \(\sqrt{8000} = 10\sqrt{80} = 89.44\text{ m}\), so the perimeter is \(4 \times 89.44 = 357.76\text{ m}\).
